commands.name: check_asset_circular_dependency
commands.description: Depth-first search of an asset's dependency graph looking for a CYCLE, returning has_circular_dependency plus the actual circular_path that closes the loop and its length -- the diagnosis for cook failures, load-order surprises and Blueprints that will not compile in isolation. Complements get_asset_dependencies (one level out) and get_asset_dependencies_recursive (the whole closure without cycle detection). WARNING: check `search_limit_reached` before trusting a false: the walk stops at max_depth / max_visited, and a cycle beyond those limits reads exactly like no cycle at all.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Exact asset name or full package name; the bare-name fallback scans /Game only and takes the first match

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Maximum recursion depth, default 100. Hitting it sets search_limit_reached and makes a `false` answer inconclusive.

params.name: max_visited
params.description: Maximum total nodes visited, default 10000. Hitting it also sets search_limit_reached.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Filter by dependency kind considered at every DFS step: "hard", "soft", or "all" (case-insensitive), default "all"

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, has_circular_dependency: bool, nodes_visited: int, max_depth_reached: int, search_limit_reached: bool, circular_path: [string] (the cycle itself, its first package repeated at the end), cycle_length: int (packages in the cycle), root_in_cycle: bool, lead_in_path?: [string] (root ... first package of the cycle, when the root only leads into it), suggestion?: string (the edge that closes the cycle), dependency_type: string }

commands.name: diff_blueprint_components
commands.description: Compare the COMPONENT trees of two Blueprints (or of one Blueprint against a components[] array captured earlier from get_blueprint_scs_tree) and report which components were added, removed or changed, where "changed" means the class, attach_parent, attach_socket, source or relative transform (0.01 tolerance) differ. It reuses get_blueprint_scs_tree's full enumeration, so native + own SCS + inherited components are all in scope, most-derived-wins. Use it for "did a reparent or a merge lose a component?" -- feeding a pre-change scs_tree as components_b makes it a before/after check without a second asset. removed = in A only, added = in B only. Read-only. diff_blueprints covers components AND graphs AND variables; get_blueprint_component_overrides goes deeper into ONE component's per-property provenance.

params.name: blueprint_a
params.description: First Blueprint asset path or short name (the "before" / baseline side).

params.name: blueprint_b
params.description: Second Blueprint (the "after" side). Omit if passing components_b.

params.name: components_b
params.description: Alternative to blueprint_b: a prior get_blueprint_scs_tree components array (snapshot). A snapshot without transforms reads every transform as changed.

params.name: include_native
params.description: Include native/CDO components on the live side(s) (default true).

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Include components inherited from ancestor Blueprints (default true).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on components enumerated per live side, 1..10000 (default 2000).

commands.returns: { blueprint_a, a_path, blueprint_b, b_path, side_b_source, added:[record], removed:[record], changed:[{name, class, changes:{class?:{a,b}, attach_parent?:{a,b}, attach_socket?:{a,b}, source?:{a,b}, transform?:{a,b}}}], unchanged_count, counts_a:{native,scs,inherited}, counts_b:{...}, truncated, total_differences }

The focused, far cheaper subset of diff_blueprints for when you already know the single graph you care about (an "AnimGraph", a function, a collapsed composite). Same NodeGuid matching caveat: it compares a fork against its original meaningfully, but two independently authored Blueprints show every node as added/removed. Read-only.

commands.name: diff_blueprints
commands.description: Structural diff of TWO Blueprints (or AnimBlueprints): parent class, SCS components, variables, functions, and per graph a node-by-node diff of what was added, removed and changed, where a changed node reports its title, per-pin default-value and link changes and -- for AnimGraph nodes -- the internal FAnimNode config and property-binding differences. WARNING: nodes are matched by NodeGuid, which duplicating or forking an asset PRESERVES: this is built to compare a fork against its original, and two independently authored Blueprints will show every single node as added/removed, which is noise, not a finding. Read-only. Siblings: diff_blueprint_graphs for ONE named graph, diff_blueprint_components for components only, get_blueprint_component_overrides for per-property provenance, compare_objects for two LIVE UObjects instead of authored structure. Watch `graphs_not_examined[]` -- when the node budget runs out the remaining graphs are listed there instead of being reported as identical.

params.name: blueprint_a

params.name: blueprint_b

commands.name: diff_object_snapshots
commands.description: Compare two snapshots taken by snapshot_object and report which properties were added, removed or CHANGED, at the object level and per component, with both values side by side. The second half of the before/after measurement: capture a baseline, run the action, capture again, and this tells you what actually moved -- instead of trusting the acting call's own success flag. Also the way to diff editor-vs-PIE and, in co-op, SERVER-vs-CLIENT state for the same actor, which is the only proof that a value really replicated. Sides can be given as stored handles, as inline snapshot objects (from snapshot_object(return_snapshot=true)), or as paths to persisted snapshot files; `a_origin`/`b_origin` report which route each side came from. compare_objects is the same idea for two LIVE objects at one instant.

commands.name: find_blueprint_assets_by_class
commands.description: Search a content path for every Blueprint ASSET whose generated class derives from a target UClass, returning asset name, asset path, generated class and the deepest NATIVE parent -- "give me every Blueprint that is a Pawn / a Widget / an ActorComponent" without hand-scanning folders. Use get_blueprint_children when the base is itself a Blueprint rather than a C++ class, list_derived_classes for classes instead of assets, and get_assets_by_tag when you want a registry tag rather than an inheritance test. WARNING: it LOADS every Blueprint under package_path to read its GeneratedClass, so scope the path narrowly on a big project rather than sweeping all of /Game.

params.name: class_name
params.description: UClass short name or /Script/ path (e.g. "Pawn", "/Script/Engine.Pawn"); a bare name is also retried with a "U" prefix. An unresolvable name is an error, not an empty result.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content path to scan, recursive (default "/Game"). Narrow it: every Blueprint underneath gets loaded.

commands.returns: { class_name, target_class, package_path, total, assets:[{ asset_name, asset_path, generated_class, native_parent }] }

commands.name: find_erroring_blueprints
commands.description: Scan a content path for Blueprints and AnimBlueprints sitting in a compile ERROR state and report each one with its status, error/warning counts and its FIRST error message -- the search for the culprit when PIE refuses to start because of an asset nobody was working on. It reads the loaded compile Status and recompiles the erroring ones with a results log to extract that message. WARNING: loading every Blueprint under a broad path is heavy enough to stall the editor on thousands of assets: scope `path` narrowly, and reach for only_loaded=true first -- the Blueprint that aborts PIE is usually still in memory, so that fast in-memory pass normally finds it without a single disk load. Complements validate_assets_in_path and audit_blueprint_health by listing EVERY erroring Blueprint with its first error in one call. WARNING: the scope parameter is named `path`, NOT search_path: pass the wrong name and it is silently ignored, the default /Game applies, and the tool sweeps the whole project while the answer looks scoped to your folder.

params.name: path
params.description: Content path to scan, recursive (default "/Game"). WARNING: this exact name -- a `search_path` key is ignored and you get the full /Game sweep. Scope it narrowly to stay cheap.

params.name: only_loaded
params.description: When true, only inspect Blueprints already loaded in memory (no disk load). Default false.

params.name: include_warnings
params.description: Also report Blueprints with compile WARNINGS (not just errors). Default false.

params.name: compile_all
params.description: Recompile EVERY scanned Blueprint (thorough but heavy); otherwise only recompile ones whose loaded Status is already Error. Default false.

params.name: max_scan
params.description: Max Blueprints to load/inspect (default 5000).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max erroring/warning Blueprints to return (default 500).

commands.returns: { path, scanned, inspected, only_loaded, erroring_count, warning_count, results_truncated, blueprints:[{ asset_path, name, class, status, num_errors, num_warnings, first_error }] }

commands.name: get_asset_dependencies
commands.description: List every package an asset DEPENDS ON (its outgoing edges), each with its class and loaded state -- "what does this asset drag in with it?", the input to a migration or import budget. Direction matters: this is what the asset NEEDS; get_asset_dependents / get_asset_referencers answer who needs IT. Use get_asset_dependencies_recursive for the transitive closure and check_asset_circular_dependency to detect cycles. WARNING: these are PACKAGE-level edges from the Asset Registry: they cannot tell you WHICH node or property creates the edge (that is find_blueprint_node_references), and a name built at runtime or resolved through a DataRegistry produces no edge at all.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Exact asset name or full package name; the bare-name fallback scans /Game only and stops at the FIRST match, without reporting that others existed

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum dependencies to return, 1..50000 (default 5000). Read `results_truncated` for the real answer: `total_dependencies` counts the RAW registry edges before exclude_engine, so it exceeds dependencies_count on almost every asset without anything having been cut.

params.name: exclude_engine
params.description: Skip /Engine and /Script dependencies, default true. Filtered entries do NOT consume the max_results budget, but they ARE counted in total_dependencies.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Filter by dependency kind: "hard", "soft", or "all" (case-insensitive), default "all"

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, dependencies: [object], dependencies_count: int, total_dependencies: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool, exclude_engine: bool, dependency_type: string }

commands.name: get_asset_dependents
commands.description: List every package that REFERENCES an asset (its incoming edges), each with its class and loaded state -- "who breaks if I delete or move this?", addressed by asset NAME. Direction matters: this is who needs IT; get_asset_dependencies is what it needs. Nearly the same query as get_asset_referencers -- prefer THAT one when the name could be ambiguous (it refuses to guess and echoes `resolved_package`, while this one silently takes the first /Game match), and prefer this one when you want the hard/soft split via dependency_type. Package-level edges only: use find_blueprint_node_references to find call sites inside graphs.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Exact asset name or full package name; the bare-name fallback scans /Game only and stops at the FIRST match, without reporting that others existed

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum dependents to return, 1..50000 (default 5000). Read `results_truncated`: `total_dependents` counts the RAW registry edges before exclude_engine, so it can exceed dependents_count with nothing cut.

params.name: exclude_engine
params.description: Skip /Engine and /Script referencers, default true. Filtered entries do NOT consume the max_results budget, but they ARE counted in total_dependents.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Filter by dependency kind: "hard", "soft", or "all" (case-insensitive), default "all"

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, dependents: [object], dependents_count: int, total_dependents: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool, exclude_engine: bool, dependency_type: string }

commands.name: get_asset_referencers
commands.description: List every asset that REFERENCES a target asset -- "who breaks if I delete, move or rename this?" -- wrapping AssetRegistry::GetReferencers over the Package category and returning each referencing package with its primary asset's name, path and class. It accepts an object path, a package path or a bare name, echoes `resolved_package` so you can confirm it queried the package you meant, and REFUSES an ambiguous bare name with the candidate list instead of picking one. Hard references only by default (the "what keeps this loaded" audit); set include_soft_references=true to include TSoftObjectPtr / FSoftObjectPath edges. Its mirror is get_asset_dependencies (what this asset needs); get_asset_dependents answers the same direction as this one from a bare asset name, and find_blueprint_node_references finds call sites INSIDE graphs, which package-level references cannot see.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Target asset: an object path ('/Game/X/DT_ItemRows.DT_ItemRows'), a package path ('/Game/X/DT_ItemRows'), or an unambiguous bare asset name ('DT_ItemRows'). An ambiguous bare name is an error listing the candidates, never a silent pick.

params.name: include_soft_references
params.description: If true, also include soft referencers (default false -> hard-only).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned referencers (1..50000); defaults to 5000.

commands.returns: { asset_path, resolved_package, include_soft_references, total, returned, results_truncated, referencers:[{ package_name, asset_name?, asset_path?, asset_class? }] }

commands.name: get_blueprint_children
commands.description: List every Blueprint asset that inherits from a given Blueprint -- the "what breaks if I change this base class?" blast-radius query, and the inverse of get_blueprint_parent. Use find_blueprint_assets_by_class when the base is a NATIVE C++ class rather than a Blueprint, get_class_hierarchy to walk upwards instead, and get_asset_referencers for references that are not inheritance at all.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset short name (exact) or full package name; an ambiguous bare name resolves to the first hit and lists the rest in `ambiguous_matches`

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum children to return, 1..10000 (default 1000); compare with children_count and results_truncated

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, children: [object], children_count: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool, parent_blueprint_valid: bool, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_blueprint_component_overrides
commands.description: Per-property PROVENANCE on a Blueprint's component templates: which values this Blueprint actually OVERRODE and which it merely inherits. Over the same components as get_blueprint_scs_tree (native CDO + own SCS + inherited chain) it resolves the effective template down the SCS -> child ICH override -> ancestor SCS -> native CDO cascade, never minting an ICH override, and compares each editable property against a baseline -- the archetype by default, or the same-named template in `other_blueprint` for the "fork vs original" question -- with the ENGINE's equality (FProperty::Identical, PPF_DeepComparison) instead of exported text. Each result is CLASSIFIED (identical | real_override | text_localization_metadata_only | object_outer_only | export_text_only | type_mismatch | no_baseline), so FText localization and object-outer noise stop masquerading as edits. WARNING: component templates can go STALE in memory (values can flip just from an editor restart): pass verify_on_disk to cross-check the raw .uasset bytes -- for anything not string-ish it answers found:null / applicable:false, never a misleading false. Read-only. list_instance_overrides asks the same question about a PLACED ACTOR.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name to audit.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional: restrict the audit to this one component (exact variable name).

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional: restrict the audit to this one property (FName or authored name).

params.name: other_blueprint
params.description: Optional: compare against the SAME-NAMED template in this other Blueprint instead of against the archetype (the "fork vs original" question).

params.name: include_native
params.description: Include native/CDO components (default true).

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Include components inherited from ancestor Blueprints (default true).

params.name: include_identical
params.description: Also emit properties that are equal in BOTH the engine comparison and the exported text (default false -- they are the vast majority).

params.name: only_editable
params.description: Only consider CPF_Edit properties (default true). Transient/DuplicateTransient/NonPIEDuplicateTransient/Deprecated are always skipped.

params.name: verify_on_disk
params.description: Cross-check string-ish values against the raw .uasset bytes of the package that owns the template (default false).

params.name: max_components
params.description: Cap on components enumerated, 1..10000 (default 500).

params.name: max_properties_per_component
params.description: Cap on properties examined per component, 1..20000 (default 1000).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, blueprint_path, other_blueprint?, other_blueprint_path?, baseline_mode, components:[{component, resolved, template_name, template_path, scs_variable_name, component_key_guid, matched_by_scs_node, component_class, source, declaring_class, resolved_from_class, authored_here, baseline_source, baseline_path, baseline_class, component_class_mismatch, properties:[{component, property, property_display, value, baseline_value, inherited_value, inherited_value_available, authored_here, declaring_class, resolved_from_class, template_source, baseline_source, kind, differs, identical_deep, export_text_equal, export_text_value, export_text_baseline, note, on_disk?}], properties_reported, properties_examined, properties_truncated}], components_examined, components_truncated, properties_examined, override_count, noise_count, identical_count, no_baseline_count, on_disk:{found,not_found,not_applicable}, templates_may_be_stale, success }

commands.name: get_blueprint_exec_path
commands.description: Report which exec nodes and BRANCHES actually RAN inside a Blueprint at runtime -- which Branch went true, which FunctionResult fired -- read from the editor's Blueprint-debugger trace stack. Unlike trace_blueprint_execution and profile_blueprint_execution, which are STATIC and list every node that exists, this reflects real execution, so it answers "did that path run at all?" when a graph fails silently. WARNING: two-phase by construction: the VM only records the trace for the object currently being DEBUGGED, so call it ONCE with object_path to arm recording (SetObjectBeingDebugged), then drive the PIE scenario, then call it AGAIN to read the recorded path -- a single call returns nothing and that is not a bug. Requires a running PIE session with Blueprint debugging; `world` (including 'server' / 'client' / 'pie:N') selects which instance gets armed, and the response stamps which world it was.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint / AnimBlueprint asset path or short name to filter the trace to.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Optional: only include samples in a function/graph whose name contains this.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Optional live PIE object to set as the debugged instance (arms trace recording).

params.name: set_debug_object
params.description: When object_path is given, call SetObjectBeingDebugged on it. Default true.

params.name: world
params.description: World to resolve object_path in: absent/'editor' (default) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie'/'game'/'runtime' (ambiguous). A fully-qualified PIE object path (...UEDPIE...) resolves regardless of this.

params.name: max_samples

The first question to ask about an unfamiliar Blueprint, and the way to tell whether a library class sneaked into the parent chain. It returns ONE level -- get_class_hierarchy walks the whole ancestor chain of the compiled class, get_blueprint_children lists descendants, and verify_reparent_success checks the chain against an expectation after a reparent. commands.name: get_blueprint_scs_tree
commands.description: Enumerate the COMPLETE component tree of a Blueprint asset -- native components from the C++ CDO, its own SCS nodes, and everything inherited down the ancestor chain -- each classified by source with its class, attach parent/socket and transform, most-derived-wins. The component listing to use by default: get_blueprint_components_list sees ONLY the Blueprint's own SCS and silently omits native and inherited ones. `component_class` filters by class OR ANY SUBCLASS across all three sources, which Actor::GetComponentsByClass cannot do (it only ever sees a constructed instance's OwnedComponents, never SCS templates on a Blueprint nobody instantiated). WARNING: before concluding a component does not exist, read `omitted_total`, NOT results_truncated: null templates and name-shadowed ancestor entries are dropped without setting it, and omitted_duplicate_names[]/omitted_null_templates[] name what disappeared (counted before the component_class filter). `scs_cdo_desync` / `generated_property_exists` flag an SCS that disagrees with the compiled class -- the fingerprint of a half-reverted asset. See diff_blueprint_components to compare two trees, get_actor_components for a live instance.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint or AnimBlueprint asset short name (exact) or full /Game path; an ambiguous bare name resolves to one match without saying which, so pass the path when it matters

params.name: include_native
params.description: Include C++/native components from the CDO (default true)

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Include components inherited from ancestor Blueprint classes (default true)

params.name: component_class
params.description: Optional class filter (short name, /Script/Module.Class, or /Game/... Blueprint path). Matches this class OR ANY SUBCLASS of it (same semantics as the engine's own GetComponentsByClass), evaluated against every source (native CDO, own SCS, inherited SCS) -- unlike Actor::GetComponentsByClass/K2_GetComponentsByClass, which only ever see a live actor's already-constructed OwnedComponents and are blind to SCS node templates on a Blueprint that hasn't been instantiated yet.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on components returned, 1..10000 (default 1000)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_valid: bool, parent_class: string, parent_class_path: string, components: [object], components_count: int, counts: object, has_simple_construction_script: bool, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, component_class_filter: string|null, component_class_resolved: bool, desync_count: int, blueprint_status: string, generated_class_available: bool, omitted_duplicate_names: [{name, source, owner_class, shadowed_by?}], omitted_duplicate_count: int, omitted_null_templates: [{name, source, owner_class}], omitted_null_template_count: int, omitted_total: int } -- each component record also carries generated_property_exists (bool|null) and scs_cdo_desync (bool|null): the compiler mints one FObjectProperty per SCS node with the SAME FName as the node (SCS_Node.h, KismetCompiler.cpp), so a MISSING property means the SCS and the compiled class disagree -- the fingerprint of an asset left half-reverted. This tool emits Node->GetVariableName() VERBATIM; it does NOT normalize a trailing digit.

commands.name: build_animation_state_machine
commands.description: Atomic JSON-spec builder for an Animation Blueprint state machine. Builds (or reuses) the state machine, then iterates states, transitions, and per-transition rules in one idempotent call. Replaces 8+ primitive cmds (add_anim_state_machine + add_anim_state + add_anim_transition + set_anim_transition_rule_*) with a single spec. Re-running with the same spec is a no-op (each primitive is internally idempotent: state-by-name, transition-by-source+target). For repeated invocations that change rule shape, the rule is re-applied on the existing transition.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path

params.name: state_machine_name
params.description: Target state machine name (created if missing via add_anim_state_machine)

params.name: spec
params.description: JSON describing the graph shape. states: [{name: str, animation?: str (/Game/Anim/Foo — optional; load-bearing for the runtime state asset but NOT created here), loop?: bool, pos?: [x, y]}]. transitions: [{from: str, to: str, blend?: number (= crossfade_duration seconds), bidirectional?: bool, priority_order?: int, rule?: object}]. Each rule variant maps 1:1 to an existing primitive cmd: {type: "automatic", enabled?: bool = false, trigger_time?: number = 0.0} | {type: "bool", variable: str (must exist on the AnimBP), invert?: bool = false} | {type: "comparison", variable: str (must be float/double on the AnimBP), operator: "=="|"!="|">"|"<"|">="|"<=", comparison_value: number}. An absent rule leaves the transition inert (no rule wired).

params.name: compile_after
params.description: Optional, default false; if true runs compile_anim_blueprint at the end

commands.returns: { success: bool, anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, machine_already_existed: bool, states_created: int, states_skipped: int, transitions_created: int, transitions_updated: int, transitions_skipped: int, errors: [string], compiled: bool, compiled_after: bool }

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint

commands.returns: { count, state_machines: [{name, graph_name}] }

commands.name: list_warp_targets_on_component
commands.description: List every FMotionWarpingTarget on an actor's UMotionWarpingComponent. Read-only: wraps GetWarpTargets() (TConstArrayView<FMotionWarpingTarget>). Each entry reports the FName, the static location/rotation, the optional component reference (via path or null), the optional bone name, the b_follow_component flag, the location/rotation offsets, and the location_offset_direction enum integer.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full editor path or short name of the actor.

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, warp_target_count: int, warp_targets: array }

commands.name: move_ik_solver_in_stack
commands.description: Move the solver at from_index so that it ends up at to_index (both 0-based positions in the solver stack) of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. An index outside the stack is an error and nothing moves; from_index equal to to_index is not an error but moved false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset

params.name: from_index
params.description: Source 0-based solver index

params.name: to_index
params.description: Target 0-based solver index, below the solver count

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, from_index: int, to_index: int, moved: bool, solver_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: play_animation
commands.description: Play an AnimMontage on a skeletal mesh component with UAnimInstance::Montage_Play at play_rate, then jump to start_section if playback started. Editor world unless the world param says otherwise; the component needs an anim instance. playing/success mean Montage_Play returned a length above 0.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path to the AnimMontage (e.g. '/Game/Animations/MyMontage.MyMontage')

params.name: play_rate
params.description: Playback rate multiplier (optional, default 1.0)

params.name: start_section
params.description: Name of the section to jump to after play starts (optional)

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

commands.returns: { component_name: string, montage_path: string, montage_name: string, playing: bool, play_rate: number, montage_length: number, return_value: number, success: bool, start_section: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: refresh_anim_montage_cache
commands.description: Re-run UAnimMontage::RefreshCacheData on a UAnimMontage in an undo transaction (it sorts the notifies, moves a notify off a missing or overlapping notify track, adding tracks as needed, and rebuilds the branching point markers) and save it. Idempotent: when the refresh rewrites none of those fields the reply is a success with refreshed=false and saved=false, the montage keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

commands.returns: { montage_path, refreshed, sequence_length, slot_count, section_count, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: reimport_anim_sequence
commands.description: Reimport a UAnimSequence, or any reimportable asset (the class is not checked), from source_file_path or its first recorded source via FReimportManager, automated (no dialogs) and unsaved. A missing source is refused before the reimport, which would crash the editor on it, and a reimport the handler reports as failed is a failure too: both make success false with reimported=false, and the missing source a note.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence

params.name: source_file_path
params.description: Absolute path of the file to reimport from on disk (e.g. "D:/Art/Walk.fbx"); defaults to the first source file recorded in the asset import data.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, source_file_path, reimported, source_validated, note? }

commands.name: remove_anim_montage

params.description: Long path of the UBlendSpace1D.

commands.returns: { asset_path, asset_class, package_name, deleted, already_existed, note? }

A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: blendspace_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UBlendSpace.

params.name: index
params.description: Index of the sample to remove.

commands.returns: { blendspace_path, removed, num_samples, samples, saved, save_error, message }

params.name: goal_name

commands.description: Remove the retarget chain with that name from an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. A name no chain has is not an error but removed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset

params.name: chain_name
params.description: Name of the retarget chain to remove

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, chain_name: string, removed: bool, chain_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_ik_solver

params.name: montage_path

params.name: notify_index

params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

commands.name: remove_motion_warping_component
commands.description: Detach the UMotionWarpingComponent from an actor (mirror of add_motion_warping_component). Idempotent: an actor that has no such component returns already_existed:false + removed:false + note, not an error.

params.name: actor_path

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, component_path?: string, removed: bool, already_existed: bool, note?: string }

params.name: asset_path

params.name: curve_name

commands.returns: { pose_asset_path, curve_name, removed_count, removed, num_curves, saved, save_error, message }

params.name: pose_asset_path

params.description: Name of the pose to remove.

commands.returns: { pose_asset_path, pose_name, was_present, removed_count, removed, contains_after, num_poses, pose_names, saved, save_error, message }

params.name: op_index

commands.name: scale_anim_curve
commands.description: Retime a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package: every key TIME becomes (t - origin) * factor + origin, and the key VALUES are left untouched -- this stretches/compresses a curve in time, it does not scale its amplitude. FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. A retime that moves no key (factor 1, no keys, or every key at the origin) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the float curve.

params.name: factor
params.description: Scale factor applied to each key TIME (default 1.0).

params.name: origin
params.description: Time origin the key times are scaled about (default 0.0).

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, origin, factor, num_keys, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_additive_settings
commands.description: Set the additive-animation type and base pose on a UAnimSequence in an undo transaction and save it. Settings the sequence already has are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: additive_anim_type

params.name: ref_pose_type

params.description: Frame index used for the base pose (default 0)

params.name: ref_pose_anim_path
params.description: Object path of the reference UAnimSequence for the base pose (optional)

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, additive_anim_type, ref_pose_type, ref_frame_index, ref_pose_anim_set, changed, success, saved, save_error, message? }

commands.name: set_anim_bone_track_keys
commands.description: Replace the keys of one bone track of a UAnimSequence with the given per-key transforms (translation, rotation, scale: real pose data, not identity), adding the track when it is missing, through its data controller as one undo step, then save the package; num_keys_readback and first_key are read back from the data model. A track that already holds exactly these keys (the stored track data comes out unchanged, measured with the data model GUID) is a success with changed=false and saved=false, the package keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A bone_name the sequence's skeleton does not have is an error and nothing is written; an omitted bone_name targets the root bone. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Identity keys: add_anim_bone_track.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: keys
params.description: Array of per-key transforms: { translation:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll] (deg), scale:[x,y,z] }. translation default [0,0,0], rotation default [0,0,0], scale default [1,1,1].

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Name of a bone of the skeleton of the sequence; omitted or empty means the root bone.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, bone_name, num_keys, num_keys_readback, num_bone_tracks, first_key:{translation,rotation_euler}, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_curve_color
commands.description: Set the editor display color of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (cosmetic: it tints the curve in the editor, it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. The color the curve already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the float curve.

params.name: color
params.description: RGBA color as [r, g, b, a] in 0..1 (default [1,1,1,1]).

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, color, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_curve_comment
commands.description: Set the author comment of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (metadata only; it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. The comment the curve already has (case-sensitive) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the float curve.

params.name: comment
params.description: Comment string to set (default empty).

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, comment, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_curve_interp_mode
commands.description: Replace the curve flags (the EAnimAssetCurveFlags bitmask) of an existing float or transform curve on a UAnimSequence with one flag, in an undo transaction, then save the package. Despite the name it changes no key interpolation or tangents: linear and editable both set Editable; metadata, drive_track and disabled set those flags. interp_mode is required; an unknown mode, curve or sequence is an error, and any curve_type other than transform means float. old_flags and new_flags are the bitmasks before and after; flags the curve already has are a success with applied=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_curve_data reads the flags.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the curve

params.name: interp_mode
params.description: One of "linear|editable|metadata|drive_track|disabled"

params.name: curve_type
params.description: Curve type to target: float (default) or transform

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, interp_mode, old_flags, new_flags, applied, saved, save_error, note? }

commands.name: set_anim_curve_keys
commands.description: Replace every key of an existing float curve on a UAnimSequence with the given [time, value] pairs as linear keys with auto tangents, through its data controller in an undo transaction, then save the package; num_keys is read back. The curve must exist (add_anim_float_curve first) and keys needs at least one valid pair. A transform curve is refused, since its keys are transforms, not [time, value] pairs: rekey it with add_anim_transform_curve. Any other curve_type is an error, and so is a rekey the data controller rejects, with nothing saved. A curve that already holds exactly those keys is a success with applied=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the float curve (e.g. "MyCurve")

params.name: keys
params.description: JSON array of [time, value] pairs, time in seconds, at least one; entries that are not such a pair are skipped, and tangents or interpolation cannot be given.

params.name: curve_type
params.description: Curve type to target: float (default) or transform; transform is refused with an error pointing at add_anim_transform_curve.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, curve_type, num_keys, applied, saved, save_error, note? }

commands.name: set_anim_frame_rate

The rate the data model already has is a success with changed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_sequence_info reads the rate.

params.name: fps
params.description: New frame rate in frames per second, rounded to a whole number that must be at least 1.

commands.returns: { sequence_path, fps, numerator, denominator, changed, saved, save_error, note? }

params.name: actor_name

params.description: Sets bSearchForWindowsInAnimsWithinMontages: when true, motion-warping windows are also searched in animations nested inside montages (required, no default)

commands.returns: { actor_name, previous_search_in_anims: bool, new_search_in_anims: bool, changed: bool }

commands.name: set_motion_warping_target_bone_name

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Engine name of the actor carrying the UMotionWarpingComponent

params.name: warp_target_name
params.description: FName of the existing warp target on the component

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Skeletal bone on the target's Component to anchor to; NAME_None follows the component root

commands.returns: { actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_bone_name: string, new_bone_name: string, changed: bool }

commands.name: set_motion_warping_target_follow_component
commands.description: Set bFollowComponent on an existing component-based warp target of an editor-world actor found by internal name, keeping its Component, BoneName and offsets. A missing target, or one without a Component, is an error. WarpTargets is Transient, so the change is not saved with the level.

params.name: actor_name

params.name: warp_target_name

params.name: follow
params.description: When true the target tracks the Component's live transform each frame; when false it snapshots the current transform (required, no default)

commands.returns: { actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_follow: bool, new_follow: bool, changed: bool }

commands.name: set_motion_warping_target_location
commands.description: Update an existing FMotionWarpingTarget's location (and optionally rotation) by FName -- an idempotent replace-in-place. Choose this over add_warp_target_to_component when the target already exists and you only want to nudge where it points; add_warp_target_to_component is the one that CREATES a target.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Engine name of the actor carrying the UMotionWarpingComponent

params.name: warp_target_name
params.description: FName of the existing target

params.name: location
params.description: [x, y, z] world location

params.name: rotation

commands.returns: { actor_name, warp_target_name, location_set, previous_count, new_count }

commands.name: set_motion_warping_target_location_offset

params.name: warp_target_name

commands.returns: { actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_x, previous_y, previous_z, new_x, new_y, new_z, changed: bool }

commands.name: set_motion_warping_target_rotation
commands.description: Set the rotation of an existing warp target of an editor-world actor (found by internal name), keeping its Location. The target is rebuilt as a plain transform target, so a component-based one loses its Component, BoneName, follow flag and offsets. WarpTargets is Transient: not saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Internal object name of the actor with the UMotionWarpingComponent, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_0"; the outliner label does not match.

params.name: warp_target_name
params.description: FName of the existing warp target on the component

params.name: rotation
params.description: New world rotation in degrees as [pitch, yaw, roll]; omitted means [0, 0, 0].

commands.returns: { actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_pitch, previous_yaw, previous_roll, new_pitch, new_yaw, new_roll, changed: bool }

commands.name: set_pose_asset_base_pose
commands.description: Set which named pose of a UPoseAsset is its base pose (UPoseAsset::SetBasePoseName) in an undo transaction, then save the asset; an empty or None base_pose_name goes back to the skeleton reference pose. A name the asset does not contain is an error before anything changes, and so is a base pose the engine does not take (read back from the asset), with nothing saved. The base pose the asset already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. The base pose only drives evaluation of an additive pose asset, which additive and note report. Edit poses with add_pose_to_pose_asset, rename_pose_in_pose_asset and remove_pose_from_pose_asset.

params.name: pose_asset_path
params.description: Path to the UPoseAsset.

params.name: base_pose_name
params.description: Name of the pose to use as the base; empty/None resets to the reference pose.

commands.returns: { pose_asset_path, base_pose_name, requested_name, applied, base_pose_index, is_reference_pose, additive, note, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_pose_search_database_schema
commands.description: Bind a UPoseSearchSchema to a UPoseSearchDatabase (assigns the Schema field). Use it right after creating a database with no schema, or to rebind an existing one; a database without a schema cannot be indexed.

params.name: database_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase (required).

params.name: schema_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to bind (required).

commands.returns: { database_path, previous_schema_path, new_schema_path, changed: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_pose_search_schema_mirror_data_table
commands.description: Bind (or rebind) the UMirrorDataTable of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under `role` (default role when omitted). Refused when no entry has that role.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required).

params.name: mirror_data_table_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMirrorDataTable to bind under the given role (required).

params.name: role
params.description: Role name (FName) identifying the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry within a multi-character schema (optional; empty = default role).

commands.returns: { asset_path, role, previous_mirror_data_table_path, new_mirror_data_table_path, changed, saved }

commands.name: set_pose_search_schema_properties
commands.description: Author UPoseSearchSchema scalar tunables via reflection (partial merge + clamp). Replaces the 8 former per-field set_pose_search_schema_* setters.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path of the target UPoseSearchSchema (required).

params.name: properties
params.description: Object of UPoseSearchSchema UPROPERTY fields to merge; keys are the C++ property NAMES (case-insensitive), absent keys untouched. Covers: SampleRate(int, ClampMin=1 ClampMax=240), bAddDataPadding(bool), bInjectAdditionalDebugChannels(bool), bDrawInjectAdditionalDebugChannels(bool), NumberOfPermutations(int, ClampMin=1), PermutationsSampleRate(int, ClampMin=1 ClampMax=240), PermutationsTimeOffset(float), DataPreprocessor(enum name: None/Normalize/NormalizeOnlyByDeviation/NormalizeWithCommonSchema). Object-refs (skeleton, mirror_data_table) and the role tag are set via their dedicated commands, not here.

commands.returns: { asset_path, asset_class, settings, applied_keys, changed, saved }

commands.name: set_pose_search_schema_role
commands.description: Rename the role (FName) of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under role_from (default role when omitted). Refused when new_role is already taken by another entry.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required).

params.name: new_role
params.description: New role name (FName) to assign to the entry, identifying it within a multi-character schema (required).

params.name: role_from
params.description: Existing role name (FName) of the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry to rename (optional; empty = default role).

commands.returns: { asset_path, previous_role, new_role, changed, saved }

commands.name: set_pose_search_schema_skeleton
commands.description: Bind (or rebind) the USkeleton of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under `role`. Idempotent by role: if a skeleton is already bound under that role it is REPLACED; if no roled entry exists for that role yet, one is created. Use add_pose_search_roled_skeleton instead when you want to ADD a second character's role without disturbing the first.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required).

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the USkeleton to bind under the given role (required).

params.name: role
params.description: Role name (FName) identifying the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry within a multi-character schema (optional; empty = default role).

commands.returns: { asset_path, role, previous_skeleton_path, new_skeleton_path, changed, saved }

commands.name: set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation
commands.description: Set a bone's rotation offset in the current retarget pose (euler degrees) of an IK Retargeter asset, as one undo transaction, then save the asset; the offset is read back as quat_x..quat_w. Creates a default pose if none is current. bone_name is stored as given, not checked against the skeleton. When the pose to edit is already current and already holds exactly that offset for the bone, changed is false, saved is false, a note says so and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRetargeter asset

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Name of the bone to update

params.name: source_or_target
params.description: Optional "Source" or "Target" scope; defaults to "Target"

params.name: pitch
params.description: Euler pitch in degrees (used when no quat is provided)

params.name: yaw
params.description: Euler yaw in degrees

params.name: roll
params.description: Euler roll in degrees

params.name: quat_x
params.description: Optional quaternion X

params.name: quat_y
params.description: Optional quaternion Y

params.name: quat_z
params.description: Optional quaternion Z

params.name: quat_w
params.description: Optional quaternion W

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional nested {x, y, z, w} quaternion object

params.name: pose_name
params.description: Optional explicit retarget pose name; created if missing

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, bone_name: string, source_or_target: string, retarget_pose: string, quat_x: number, quat_y: number, quat_z: number, quat_w: number, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_retargeter_chain_mapping
commands.description: Make source_chain drive target_chain in an IK Retargeter asset, overwriting the previous mapping, on every op whose chain mapping lists target_chain (or only the op named op_name), in one undo transaction, then save the asset. source_chain is not validated, so a misspelled name is stored as given. set_ok is false when no op lists target_chain; mapped_source is read back from the first matching op. When no op lists target_chain, or every one already maps it to source_chain, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_ik_retargeter_info shows the per-op mappings.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRetargeter asset

params.name: source_chain
params.description: Name of the source retarget chain

params.name: target_chain
params.description: Name of the target retarget chain to map to

params.name: op_name
params.description: Optional op name as get_ik_retargeter_info lists it; omitted, every op whose chain mapping lists target_chain is updated

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, source_chain: string, target_chain: string, mapped_source: string, set_ok: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_retargeter_op_settings
commands.description: Partial-merge a retarget op's live settings struct (only the JSON fields present are written -> idempotent), and optionally toggle the op enabled flag, as one undo transaction, then save the asset.  Settings keys match get_retargeter_op_info (first char lower-cased, e.g. lODThreshold). Numeric ClampMin/ClampMax metadata is enforced after the merge. The optional `enabled` flag is applied via the controller. The payload echoes the read-back settings. When neither is given, or the op already has those settings and that enabled state, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. An out-of-range op_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path
params.description: Content path to the UIKRetargeter asset.

params.name: op_index
params.description: 0-based index of the op in the retargeter's op stack.

params.name: settings
params.description: Partial settings object; only present fields are written (e.g. { lODThreshold: 5 }).

params.name: enabled
params.description: Optional: enable/disable the op (applied via the controller).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, op_index: int, op_name: string, op_type: string, enabled: bool, settings: object, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_rig_control_limits
commands.description: Set a scalar Control Rig control's min/max limits (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer).  Enables the limit array for the control type and sets MinimumValue/MaximumValue type-correctly; once enabled, set_rig_control_value clamps via ApplyLimits. Verified read-back.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset.

params.name: control_name
params.description: Name of an existing control element (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer).

params.name: min
params.description: Minimum value (number).

params.name: max
params.description: Maximum value (number).

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether to enable the limits (optional, default true).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, min: number, max: number, limit_enabled: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_rig_control_settings
commands.description: Edit an existing Control Rig control's shape/gizmo/color/limit-draw settings (the bits add_rig_control can't set afterwards).  Read-modify-write: reads the control's FRigControlSettings, applies the provided fields, writes back via URigHierarchyController::SetControlSettings, recompiles + saves, and returns the verified read-back. Only the supplied fields change.

params.name: control_rig_path

params.name: control_name
params.description: Name of an existing control element.

params.name: display_name
params.description: Optional display name (FName) for the control.

params.name: shape_name
params.description: Optional gizmo shape name (e.g. "Default", "Box", "Sphere", "Circle").

params.name: shape_color
params.description: Optional shape color [R, G, B] or [R, G, B, A] floats (0..1).

params.name: shape_visible
params.description: Optional bool: whether the gizmo shape is visible in 3D.

params.name: draw_limits
params.description: Optional bool: whether to draw the control's limits in debug.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, control_name: string, settings_applied: { display_name, shape_name, shape_color: [float], shape_visible, draw_limits }, applied_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_rig_control_shape_transform
commands.description: Set the local shape (gizmo) transform of an existing Control Rig control.  Reads the current local shape transform, overrides only the supplied location/rotation/scale, writes back via URigHierarchy::SetControlShapeTransform, recompiles + saves, and returns the verified read-back. This positions the manipulator gizmo relative to the control, independent of the control's value.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset.

params.name: control_name
params.description: Name of an existing control element.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] gizmo location.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] gizmo rotation.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] gizmo scale.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, control_name: string, shape_transform: { location: [float], rotation: [float], scale: [float] }, applied_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_rig_control_value
commands.description: Set a Control Rig control's pose value (Initial + Current), type-correct per the control's ERigControlType.  add_rig_control only seeds the identity value. SetControlValue applies the control's limits, so a value outside an enabled min/max is clamped (set limits first with set_rig_control_limits). Verified read-back.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset.

params.name: control_name
params.description: Name of an existing control element.

params.name: value
params.description: The value: bool (Bool), number (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer), or [x,y(,z)] (Vector2D/Position/Scale/Rotator).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, value: any, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_rigvm_pin_default
commands.description: Set the default value of a pin in the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint (URigVMController::SetPinDefaultValue, no undo entry), then compile and save it. success reflects the save even when the write failed: check set, pin_found and current_value, which is read back.

params.name: control_rig_path

params.name: pin_path
params.description: Pin path NodeName.PinName, e.g. SetTransform.bInitial

params.name: value
params.description: Value in UE export-text form, e.g. "true", "1.0" or "(X=0.0,Y=0.0,Z=1.0)"; array pins are resized to the given element count.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, pin_path: string, value: string, set: bool, pin_found: bool, current_value: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_allow_cpu_access
commands.description: Set bAllowCPUAccess on every LOD of a skeletal mesh. Used to keep vertex/skin data resident for FX sampling or other CPU work.

params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset

params.name: b_allow
params.description: New value for the flag (default true)

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, b_allow: bool, applied_lods: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_anim_class
commands.description: Repoint a Blueprint's skeletal mesh component AnimClass to a (fork) AnimBlueprint. Also handles the INHERITED native Character Mesh, which is not in the SCS and which the generic component-property setters cannot reach: it writes the CDO component archetype so spawned instances inherit the new AnimClass. Also sets AnimationMode=AnimationBlueprint.

params.description: Character/Actor Blueprint (name or path), e.g. "BP_MyCharacter".

commands.returns: { blueprint, component, anim_class, previous_anim_class, applied, wrote_cdo_archetype, saved }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_lod_build_settings
commands.description: Change the stored build settings of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset, only the fields you pass, and save the mesh. The mesh is not rebuilt here, so the settings take effect at its next build or reimport; a failed save returns an error. Returns settings_applied.

params.name: recompute_tangents

params.name: use_mikk_t_space

params.name: texture_importance

params.name: shading_importance
params.description: SMOI_* importance of shading quality.

params.name: skinning_importance
params.description: SMOI_* importance of skinning quality.

params.name: max_bones_per_vertex

params.name: welding_threshold

params.name: normals_threshold

params.name: enforce_bone_boundaries

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_lod_screen_size

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_min_lod

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, old_min_lod: int, min_lod: int, lod_count: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: setup_foot_ik

Bones the target skeleton lacks are an error and nothing is written. The node is left unwired: connect it with connect_anim_graph_pins. Idempotent; refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

commands.name: bulk_rename_assets
commands.description: Rename/move multiple assets in one IAssetTools::RenameAssets batch, with per-item disk verification instead of the batch bool. Guards: refuses while PIE is active; refuses paths under readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots setting) on BOTH the source and the destination; pre-detects the native-CDO reference case that makes the engine's FMessageDialog auto-cancel the whole batch (would_block_on_modal) and does NOT call RenameAssets in that case. Also reports referencer packages left DIRTY -- PerformAssetRename discards its FailedPackages list unless UE source control is connected, so a referencer (typically OFPA) can be left unwritten while RenameAssets still returns true.

params.name: assets
params.description: List of rename descriptors: { old_path (required), new_name (optional, default = current name), new_folder (optional, default = current folder) }.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Optional bool (default false). Plan + run every guard and the CDO scan, but never call RenameAssets.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long paths that must not be renamed FROM or INTO (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots setting). Pass [] to disable the guard.

params.name: allow_cdo_referenced
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When false, a native-CDO reference to any asset in the batch refuses the batch instead of letting it silently no-op.

commands.returns: { dry_run: bool, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_explicit: bool, planned_count: int, renamed_count: int, failed_count: int, skipped_count: int, batch_api_result: bool|null, would_block_on_modal: bool, cdo_references: [object], soft_scan_is_approximate: bool, referencer_packages_dirty: [object], results: [object] }
