params.description: Optional [w, h] destination size, defaults to render target dimensions

params.name: color
params.description: Optional [r, g, b, a] tint color, defaults to opaque white

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, texture_path: string, drawn: bool, position: [number], size: [number] }

commands.name: evaluate_curve_at_time
commands.description: Evaluate a curve asset at a given time.  Loads a UCurveFloat / UCurveVector / UCurveLinearColor and evaluates it at the requested time. For multi-channel curves (Vector=3, LinearColor=4) the optional channel selects which component the scalar 'value' field reports; the full component array is always returned in 'values'.

params.name: curve_path
params.description: Object path or package path of the curve asset.

params.name: time
params.description: The time (X) to evaluate at.

params.name: channel
params.description: Optional channel index for multi-channel curves (Vector/LinearColor) to populate 'value'.

commands.returns: { curve_path: string, curve_class: string, time: float, curve_type: string, num_channels: int, channel: int, value: float, values: [float], vector: {x,y,z}, color: {r,g,b,a} }

commands.name: export_render_target
commands.description: Export a render target to an image file on disk: PNG, except an RGBA16f or RGBA32f render target, which writes HDR when filename ends in .hdr and EXR otherwise. exported is measured on disk: the file must exist, hold bytes and have been written by this call. It is false, and the call fails saying why, for a render target without a resource (every render target in a process that cannot render: -nullrhi, a commandlet), an invalid path, a file that cannot be opened for writing, or an image that cannot be read back; an empty file left by a failed export is removed when the call created it.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the render target to export

params.name: output_directory
params.description: Absolute directory path to write into, created if missing

params.name: filename
params.description: Output file name including extension, e.g. RT_Example.png

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, output_directory: string, filename: string, file_path: string, exported: bool, file_exists: bool, file_size_bytes: number }

commands.name: generate_asset_thumbnail
commands.description: Render and cache an asset's thumbnail (or report the existing cached one).  When the editor can render (FApp::CanEverRender() and the RHI is initialized), this generates a fresh thumbnail via ThumbnailTools and caches it into the package's thumbnail map. When rendering is unavailable, or the object type has no thumbnail renderer, it honestly reports the existing cached thumbnail state.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path or package path of the asset.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, object_path: string, asset_class: string, rendered: bool, has_thumbnail: bool, width: int, height: int, compressed_bytes: int, message: string }

commands.name: get_asset_by_name
commands.description: Retrieve ONE asset by exact name and return its identity (name, class, object path, package, is_loaded, file size) plus, with load_full_data, type-specific detail: a Blueprint's parent class / compile status / generated class, a StaticMesh's section-vertex-LOD counts, whether a material is an instance. WARNING: When the name is ambiguous it still resolves to the FIRST match and merely lists the rest in `ambiguous_matches` -- check that field, or use resolve_asset_by_name, which refuses to pick for you. The fallback name scan only covers /Game, so an /Engine or plugin-mount asset must be addressed by its full package name. Use get_assets_by_names for a batch, get_asset_metadata for registry tags, and search_assets_by_pattern when you only know part of the name.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT asset name, or a full package name (which is tried first and is the only form that reaches outside /Game)

params.name: load_full_data
params.description: When true (DEFAULT), LOADS the asset to add type-specific details (Blueprint parent class, mesh sections, ...). Pass false to stay metadata-only and avoid a synchronous load.

commands.returns: { name: string, class: string, path: string, package: string, is_loaded: bool, file_size_bytes?: int, file_size_kb?: number, parent_class?: string, is_compiled?: bool, is_valid?: bool, generated_class?: string, num_sections?: int, num_vertices?: int, num_lods?: int, is_material_instance?: bool, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_asset_dependencies_recursive
commands.description: Recursively walk an asset's package dependencies via the Asset Registry.  Breadth-first, deduplicated, capped at max_depth (default 3). Each returned dependency records the depth at which it was first reached (1 == direct).

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path or package path of the root asset.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Maximum dependency depth to traverse (1..32, default 3).

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Optional "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive, default "all"). Filters every depth level of the walk via the AssetRegistry hard/soft FDependencyQuery split; "all" leaves the walk unfiltered.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, package_name: string, max_depth: int, dependency_type: string, dependencies: [{path, depth}], count: int }

commands.name: get_asset_disk_size
commands.description: Get the on-disk file size of an asset's package (.uasset/.umap).  Resolves the package filename via FPackageName::LongPackageNameToFilename and stats it with IFileManager::FileSize.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path or package path of the asset (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/M_Example').

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, package_name: string, file_path: string, extension: string, size_bytes: number, size_kb: number, size_mb: number, exists_on_disk: bool, message: string }

commands.name: get_asset_file_size
commands.description: Read the ON-DISK size of an asset's .uasset in bytes, KB and MB, plus the absolute file path it resolved to -- the measurement for a disk-budget question ("what is costing the 491 MB in this import?"). WARNING: Size is NOT a proxy for content or integrity: a DataTable that GREW by 5 KB had lost 46 of its 48 references. To measure content use get_data_table_info, read_data_table_row_complex or get_asset_dependencies; for in-memory cost use get_asset_memory_usage. Resolution matches get_asset_by_name (full package name first, then a /Game-only exact-name scan, first hit wins with the rest in ambiguous_matches).

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT asset name, or a full package name (which is tried first and is the only form that reaches outside /Game)

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, file_path: string, file_size_bytes: int, file_size_kb: number, file_size_mb: number, file_exists: bool, asset_class: string, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_asset_import_data
commands.description: Read an asset's UAssetImportData: source filename(s) and import timestamp.  Returns has_import_data, source_file (first resolved filename), the full source_files list (relative + resolved filename + import_time), and source_file_count.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path of the asset, e.g. /Game/Imported/MyTex.MyTex.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, asset_class: string, has_import_data: bool, source_file: string, source_files: [{relative_filename, resolved_filename, import_time}], source_file_count: int, import_time: string }

commands.name: get_asset_last_modified
commands.description: Read the .uasset file's last-modified timestamp (formatted string + Unix epoch) and how old it is in days and hours -- "was this asset actually written to disk when I saved it?", the disk-side oracle for a save whose return value claimed success. WARNING: It is a FILE timestamp: an asset edited in memory but not saved reports its old date, and Unreal does not distinguish creation from modification (the tool reads the same stamp for both). Use list_assets_modified_since to sweep a whole folder by date, and list_dirty_packages for unsaved-in-memory changes. Resolution matches get_asset_by_name (full package name first, then a /Game-only exact-name scan, first hit wins with the rest in ambiguous_matches).

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT asset name, or a full package name (which is tried first and is the only form that reaches outside /Game)

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, file_path: string, last_modified: string, last_modified_timestamp: int, file_exists: bool, asset_class: string, age_days: number, age_hours: number, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_asset_metadata
commands.description: Read an asset's Asset Registry TAGS (the indexed key/value pairs an asset publishes -- parent class, mesh stats, fork-lineage tags, ...) together with its name, class, object path and package. WARNING: its `asset_name` is NOT a name: the tool literally prefixes "/Game/" to whatever you pass, so it must be a path RELATIVE TO /Game ("MyGame/Systems/Foo/BP_Foo.BP_Foo"), never a bare asset name and never an absolute "/Game/..." path -- and it LOADS the asset to resolve it. Use get_assets_metadata_batch for many paths at once, get_asset_by_name for identity from a bare name, and get_assets_by_tag to search BY a tag value instead of reading the tags of one asset.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Path RELATIVE to /Game, with no leading slash (e.g. "MyGame/Systems/Foo/BP_Foo.BP_Foo"); the tool prepends "/Game/" itself, so a bare name or an absolute path both fail to resolve

commands.returns: { name: string, class: string, path: string, package: string, asset_class_path?: string, package_path?: string, tags?: [{ name, value }] }

commands.name: get_asset_metadata_tags
commands.description: Reads all editor metadata tags (UMetaData) of an asset.  Wraps UEditorAssetLibrary::GetMetadataTagValues and returns each tag as a {key, value} pair. (Distinct from get_asset_metadata, which reads asset registry data instead of the asset's stored metadata tags.)

params.name: asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the asset.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, tags: [{ key: string, value: string }], tag_count: number }

commands.name: get_asset_thumbnail
commands.description: Report whether an asset is of a type that CAN carry a thumbnail, alongside its resolved object path, class and loaded state. WARNING: `has_thumbnail` is a CLASS test, not a lookup of stored thumbnail bytes: it is true for any StaticMesh, Material, Texture, Blueprint, SkeletalMesh or Level and false for everything else, whether or not a thumbnail was ever rendered -- and it returns no image data at all. To actually see something rendered, use generate_asset_thumbnail or capture_viewport. Resolution matches get_asset_by_name (full package name first, then a /Game-only exact-name scan, first hit wins with the rest in ambiguous_matches).

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT asset name, or a full package name (which is tried first and is the only form that reaches outside /Game)

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, has_thumbnail: bool, asset_class: string, asset_loaded: bool, asset_class_name?: string, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_assets_by_names
commands.description: Batch variant of get_asset_by_name: resolve N asset names in ONE round-trip instead of N calls, returning per entry a found flag plus that asset's identity (class, object path, package, is_loaded) or the error that stopped it. Delegates to get_asset_by_name literally, so it inherits both its /Game-only fallback scan and its ambiguous_matches transparency -- an ambiguous name still resolves to the first hit, so check that field per entry. Use get_assets_metadata_batch when you want registry TAGS rather than identity.

params.name: asset_names
params.description: Array of exact asset names (or full package names) to resolve (required)

params.name: load_full_data
params.description: When true, adds the type-specific details of get_asset_by_name per asset. Defaults to FALSE here -- the opposite of the single-asset tool -- so a batch call cannot accidentally force N synchronous loads.

commands.returns: { requested_count: int, resolved: [{ asset_name, found: bool, name?, class?, path?, package?, is_loaded?, ambiguous_matches?, ... (same fields as get_asset_by_name when found) }] }

commands.name: get_assets_by_tag
commands.description: Search assets BY an Asset Registry tag (FARFilter::TagsAndValues), server-side and metadata-only -- it never force-loads anything. This is the only tool here that queries by tag rather than by name, path or type: "every asset carrying the fork-origin tag (mcp.forkOrigin by default)", "every Blueprint whose ParentClass tag is X". It is also the general-class search that get_assets_by_type cannot do, since class_filter resolves ANY class (with subclasses) instead of five hardcoded ones. Search by class alone by pairing class_filter with a tag every asset of that class publishes; use get_asset_metadata to read the tags OF one asset rather than search by them.

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Asset Registry tag name to filter on, e.g. "ParentClass" or "mcp.forkOrigin" (required). Read the available tag names off a sample asset with get_asset_metadata.

params.name: tag_value
params.description: When given, only assets whose tag equals this value EXACTLY match; when omitted, matches any asset that HAS the tag with any value

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Root package path to search under; defaults to "/Game", so /Engine, /Water and plugin mounts need their root passed explicitly

params.name: recursive
params.description: When true (DEFAULT), recurse into subfolders

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional class short name or /Script path (e.g. "Blueprint", "/Script/Engine.DataTable") to additionally constrain the match; subclasses match too (bRecursiveClasses)

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. `total_found` is the uncapped count.

commands.returns: { tag_name: string, tag_value: string, folder_path: string, recursive: bool, class_filter: string, assets: [{ name, path, class, package }], count: int, total_found: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_assets_by_type
commands.description: List every asset of a CLASS under a content path, with name, object path, class, package and is_loaded, plus total_found and results_truncated. Takes any resolvable class -- "DataTable", "NiagaraSystem", "LandscapeGrassType", a "/Script/Module.Class" path -- matched WITH its subclasses, plus five shortcuts kept for convenience: "Blueprint", "StaticMesh", "Texture" (Texture2D exactly), "Sound" (SoundWave exactly) and "Material", which is the one that earns its keep by grouping Material + MaterialInstanceConstant + MaterialInstanceDynamic. Searches /Game by default and any mount via package_path (/Engine, /Water, plugin content). Sister tools: get_assets_in_folder to enumerate a directory whatever the class, search_assets_by_pattern to search by NAME, get_assets_by_tag to search by an Asset Registry tag.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: A class name ("DataTable"), a "/Script/Module.Class" path, or one of the shortcuts Blueprint | StaticMesh | Material | Texture | Sound. A name that resolves to no class is an error, not an empty result. WARNING: The shortcuts match those classes EXACTLY (Texture finds Texture2D but not TextureCube); any other name matches the class AND its subclasses.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content root to search, recursively. Defaults to "/Game"; pass "/Engine", "/Water", a plugin mount or a subfolder to look elsewhere.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. `total_found` is the uncapped count.

commands.returns: { assets: [{ name, path, class, package, is_loaded }], count: int, total_found: int, asset_type: string, package_path: string, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_assets_in_folder
commands.description: Enumerate every asset under a content FOLDER (recursively by default), each with name, object path, class, package and is_loaded, plus total_found so you can tell a truncated listing from a complete one. The "what is actually in this directory?" inventory -- metadata only, it never loads an asset. Reaches any mounted content root, not just /Game. Pick this over search_assets_by_pattern when you know WHERE to look rather than what the name contains, over get_assets_by_type when you want everything regardless of class, and over resolve_asset_by_name when you do not have an exact name at all.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Folder to list. A bare/relative name is prefixed with /Game/; a path already starting with "/" (e.g. /Water/Materials, /Engine/..., /<PluginName>/...) is used verbatim, so every mounted content root is reachable.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. Compare `count` against `total_found` (which is NOT capped) to see how much was left out.

params.name: recursive
params.description: When true (DEFAULT), include subfolders; false lists only the assets sitting directly in this folder

commands.returns: { assets: [{ name, path, class, package, is_loaded }], count: int, total_found: int, folder_path: string, recursive: bool, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_assets_metadata_batch
commands.description: Batch variant of get_asset_metadata: read the Asset Registry tags of N assets in ONE round-trip instead of N calls, returning per entry a found flag plus the same fields get_asset_metadata emits (or an error string). It runs get_asset_metadata for each entry, so it inherits its path semantics exactly -- including the trap that each entry is prefixed with "/Game/", so entries must be paths RELATIVE to /Game, never bare names and never absolute "/Game/..." paths. Use get_assets_by_names for identity/type info from bare NAMES instead of tags.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: Array of paths RELATIVE to /Game with no leading slash (e.g. "MyGame/Systems/Foo/BP_Foo.BP_Foo"); each is passed to get_asset_metadata, which prepends "/Game/" itself (required)

params.name: max_results
params.description: Safety cap on how many array entries get processed (1..5000); defaults to 500. Entries past the cap are dropped and results_truncated goes true.

commands.returns: { requested_count: int, processed_count: int, results_truncated: bool, results: [{ asset_path, found: bool, name?, class?, path?, package?, asset_class_path?, package_path?, tags?, error? }] }

commands.name: get_collection_assets
commands.description: List the object paths of the assets directly in one Content Browser collection (child collections are not included), without changing anything. The collection is looked up by collection_name within share_type, default Local; an unrecognized share_type also falls back to Local, and a name not found under that share type is an error. get_collections lists every collection with its share_type. Returns assets and asset_count; change membership with add_asset_to_collection or remove_asset_from_collection.

params.name: collection_name
params.description: Name of the (existing) collection.

params.name: share_type
params.description: ECollectionShareType: "Local", "Private", or "Shared" (optional, default "Local")

commands.returns: { collection_name: string, share_type: string, assets: [string], asset_count: number }

commands.name: get_collections
commands.description: List every Content Browser collection of the project container, of every share type, without changing anything: name and share_type of each (the share_type that get_collection_assets and the other collection tools need), plus collection_count. Errors when the collection manager is unavailable.
commands.returns: { collections: [{ name: string, share_type: string }], collection_count: number }

commands.name: get_reference_path
commands.description: Find the shortest reference CHAIN through the AssetRegistry dependency graph: with `from`, the shortest from -> ... -> target (walking dependencies); without `from`, the shortest chain from a root (a package nothing references) DOWN to target (walking referencers) -- i.e. 'what keeps target alive / why is it undeletable'. get_asset_referencers gives the direct edges; this gives the PATH.

params.name: target
params.description: The asset whose reference chain to trace (object path or /Game package path).

params.name: from
params.description: Optional starting hub/root asset; when set, traces from -> target via dependencies instead of the referencer-root chain.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Max chain depth to search (optional, default 16; clamped 1..64).

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Optional "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive, default "all"). Filters BOTH BFS directions (the from->target dependency walk and the referencer-root walk) and the always-computed direct_referencers list via the AssetRegistry hard/soft FDependencyQuery split; "all" leaves them unfiltered.

commands.returns: { target: string, target_package: string, from: string, dependency_type: string, found: bool, reached_root: bool, chain: [string], chain_length: int, direct_referencers: [string], direct_referencer_count: int, message: string }

commands.name: get_render_target_2d_array_info
commands.description: Read metadata for a UTextureRenderTarget2DArray asset (size, slice count, format). Metadata-only, no pixel readback.

params.name: render_target_path

commands.name: get_render_target_cube_info

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the render target, e.g. /Game/RenderTargets/RTC_Example

commands.returns: { render_target_name: string, asset_path: string, size: int, num_mips: int, pixel_format: string, is_hdr: bool, is_srgb: bool, auto_generate_mips: bool }

commands.name: get_render_target_info
commands.description: Read the metadata of a UTextureRenderTarget2D asset without reading pixels or changing it: width, height, format (RTF_*), pixel_format and is_srgb. For 2D-array or cube render targets use get_render_target_2d_array_info or get_render_target_cube_info; export_render_target writes the image to disk.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the render target, e.g. /Game/RenderTargets/RT_Example

commands.returns: { render_target_name: string, asset_path: string, width: int, height: int, format: string, pixel_format: string, is_srgb: bool }

commands.name: get_static_mesh_info
commands.description: Get detailed info about a static mesh: LODs, verts, materials (with slots), sockets, nanite, collision, bounds.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset.

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, num_lods, num_verts_lod0, num_materials, num_sockets, materials: [{slot_index, slot_name, material_path}], collision_complexity, nanite_enabled, bounds_origin_x, bounds_origin_y, bounds_origin_z, bounds_extent_x, bounds_extent_y, bounds_extent_z, sphere_radius }

commands.name: get_texture_array_info
commands.description: Reads metadata for a UTexture2DArray asset.  texture_array_path accepts short "/Game/MyGame/T_Array" or fully-qualified "...T_Array.T_Array" asset paths.

params.name: texture_array_path

commands.returns: { texture_array_name: string, asset_path: string, width: int, height: int, num_slices: int, format: string, has_source: bool, source_texture_count: int }

params.description: Asset path of the texture (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/T_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/MyGame/T_Example.T_Example")

params.name: file_path

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination content folder, e.g. /Game/Imported.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Optional destination asset name (default = source file stem).

commands.returns: { file_path: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_name: string, width: int, height: int, imported: bool }

commands.name: ingest_external_uassets
commands.description: Copy .uasset/.uexp/.ubulk/.umap from an EXTERNAL Content tree into THIS project, preserving each file's path relative to its Content root, then register the new packages with IAssetRegistry::ScanPathsSynchronous(bForceRescan) and sweep object redirectors under the destination. Fills the gap that migrate_assets only EXPORTS and import_asset is FBX/PNG-only. HEAVY: touches project Content on disk + mutates the registry -- run with confirmation.

params.name: source_dir
params.description: External source directory (its Content ancestor defines the preserved relative path; if none, source_dir itself is the root).

params.name: dest_root
params.description: Destination content mount path (optional, default '/Game'); e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Imported'.

params.name: paths
params.description: Optional list of relative sub-paths (relative to the Content root) to restrict the copy to; empty/absent = whole tree.

params.name: overwrite
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When false, destination files that already exist are skipped.

params.name: fixup_redirectors
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Resolve + leave-fixed object redirectors under dest_root after the copy.

commands.returns: { source_dir: string, content_root: string, dest_root: string, dest_dir: string, files_copied: int, files_skipped: int, files_failed: int, scanned_paths: [string], redirectors_fixed: int, copied: [{src, dest, package_path}], message: string }

commands.name: list_assets_modified_since
commands.description: List package files (.uasset/.umap) under a content path whose ON-DISK mtime is newer than a timestamp -- the `find -newermt` recipe for isolating an UE Migrate set or a session's changes, but returning /Game package names. Enumerates the filesystem (so it catches just-migrated assets the registry may not have indexed yet).

params.name: timestamp

commands.name: resolve_asset_by_name
commands.description: Resolve an exact asset name (or path) to EVERY matching asset and report `match_count` + `unambiguous`, instead of silently picking the first one the way get_asset_by_name, get_blueprint_parent, get_graph_nodes and the rest of the by-name tools do. Run this FIRST whenever you are about to address an asset by bare name: a project can have hundreds of duplicate names (the same name in a vendored pack and in the game's own folders, plus dated backup copies), and `unambiguous:false` is the only warning you will get before another tool hands you a stale backup's contents as if they were the real asset. From there, pass the full path everywhere. match_count:0 with success:true is a valid, informative answer -- it means "no asset with this exact name", which is a real measurement of non-existence (unlike search_assets_by_pattern's count:0, which can just mean the pattern had a wildcard in it).

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT bare asset name or full package/asset path. This is an equality test, not a substring one -- use search_assets_by_pattern when you only know part of the name.

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional class short name or /Script path (e.g. "Blueprint", "DataTable") to constrain the match; matches subclasses too

params.name: search_root

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, search_root: string, class_filter: string, match_count: int, unambiguous: bool, matches: [{ path, package, class }] }

A quick way to compare copies of one asset: an incomplete (stub) copy shows far fewer reference tokens than the complete one. Accepts a disk path OR a /Game|/Engine mount path.

params.name: package_file
params.description: Absolute .uasset/.umap path on disk, or a /Game|/Engine mount path.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Optional regex (ECMAScript); tokens containing a match are counted in the 'matches' fields.

commands.returns: { package_file: string, resolved_path: string, exists: bool, file_size_bytes: number, modified: string, pattern: string, ref_path_unique: int, ref_path_occurrences: number, ref_paths: [{token, count}], match_unique: int, match_occurrences: number, matches: [{token, count}] }

commands.name: search_assets_by_pattern
commands.description: Find assets by NAME, scanning every mounted content root (/Game, /Engine, /Water, plugin mounts, ...) and returning name, object path, class and package per hit. The broad "does anything called <token> exist, and where?" search. It has TWO match modes and picks one automatically, reporting which in `match_mode`: a pattern WITHOUT `*`/`?` is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING test (FString::Contains) -- pass the bare token, this is the common case; a pattern WITH `*` or `?` is a real glob (FString::MatchesWildcard). WARNING: The glob is ANCHORED AT BOTH ENDS -- it matches the WHOLE name, not a substring -- so `Grass*` means "starts with Grass" and `*Grass*` is what reproduces substring behaviour. It only ever looks at the asset NAME, so it cannot find an asset by its folder or by a class it belongs to: use resolve_asset_by_name to check ONE exact name and get every homonym, get_assets_in_folder to enumerate a directory, get_assets_by_type for the 5 built-in type filters, and get_assets_by_tag for an Asset Registry tag.

params.name: search_pattern
params.description: Matched against the asset NAME. Contains no `*`/`?` -> case-insensitive substring (FString::Contains). Contains `*` or `?` -> glob (FString::MatchesWildcard), ANCHORED at both ends: `*` matches any run including empty, `?` matches 0 or 1 character (UE semantics, not exactly 1). Not a regex.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of matched assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. WARNING: Hitting the cap ABORTS the enumeration, so `total_scanned` then counts only the assets visited before the early-out, not the whole registry.

params.name: case_sensitive
params.description: When true, match is case-sensitive; defaults to false

params.name: wait_for_scan
params.description: When true (default), force-completes the AssetRegistry scan before enumerating so a still-loading registry cannot report total_scanned:0. Set false to skip the (possibly blocking) wait.

commands.returns: { assets: [{ name, path, class, package, is_loaded }], count: int, total_scanned: int, scan_was_pending: bool, search_pattern: string, match_mode: "substring"|"wildcard", case_sensitive: bool, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.description: Reads a USoundModulationParameter asset without changing it. Returns parameter_path, parameter_class (the concrete class, e.g. SoundModulationParameterVolume) and its settings value_normalized, clamp_to_normalized_range and value_unit. Change them with set_modulation_parameter_settings.

params.name: parameter_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationParameter

commands.returns: { parameter_path, parameter_class, value_normalized, clamp_to_normalized_range, value_unit }

commands.name: get_sound_attenuation_properties
commands.description: Read every FSoundAttenuationSettings field (shape, falloff, spatialization, LPF, occlusion, reverb send) of a USoundAttenuation asset as one settings object, with the keys set_sound_attenuation_properties takes, plus asset_class. Read-only.

params.name: attenuation_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundAttenuation.

commands.returns: { attenuation_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object }

commands.name: get_sound_class_hierarchy
commands.description: Read one level of the hierarchy of a USoundClass asset: its parent and parent_path (parent "None" for a root), the names of its direct children and child_count. Call it again on a parent or child to walk further. Read-only.

params.name: sound_class_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundClass, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SC_SFX.SC_SFX".

commands.returns: { name: string, sound_class_path: string, parent: string, parent_path: string, children: [string], child_count: int }

commands.name: get_sound_class_properties
commands.description: Read a USoundClass asset: every FSoundClassProperties field that set_sound_class_properties writes (volume, pitch, filters, reverb and routing flags, output_target, loading_behavior) plus its direct parent and direct children by name and path; parent_class is "None" for a root class, and child_count is the number of children listed (null references are skipped). One level only: walk further with get_sound_class_hierarchy on a parent or child. Read-only; it loads the asset by object or package path, and one that does not load as a USoundClass is an error.

params.name: sound_class_path
params.description: Content path of the USoundClass asset.

commands.returns: { sound_class_path: string, volume: float, pitch: float, low_pass_frequency: float, attenuation_distance_scale: float, lfe_bleed: float, voice_center_channel_volume: float, radio_filter_volume: float, radio_filter_volume_threshold: float, default_2d_reverb_send_amount: float, apply_effects: bool, always_play: bool, is_ui_sound: bool, is_music: bool, center_channel_only: bool, apply_ambient_volumes: bool, reverb: bool, output_target: string, loading_behavior: string, parent_class: string, parent_class_path: string, child_classes: [{name, path}], child_count: int }

commands.name: get_sound_concurrency_properties
commands.description: Read every FSoundConcurrencySettings field (maxCount, bLimitToOwner, resolutionRule, retriggerTime, volume scaling, voice stealing) of a USoundConcurrency asset as one settings object, with the keys set_sound_concurrency_properties takes, plus asset_class. Read-only.

params.name: concurrency_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundConcurrency.

commands.returns: { concurrency_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object }

commands.name: get_sound_cue_graph
commands.description: Read the node graph of a USoundCue without changing it: every node in AllNodes with its id (the node_id other sound cue tools take), class, child_ids (-1 for an empty slot), max_child_nodes and editable properties, plus first_node_id (-1 when unset) and node_count.

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Full asset path of the cue

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, asset_path: string, nodes: [object], node_count: int, first_node_id: int, has_first_node: bool }

commands.name: get_sound_modulation_patch_info
commands.description: Reads a USoundModulationPatch asset without changing it. Returns patch_path, bBypass, output_parameter ({ path, class }, or null when unset), inputs (one { bus: { path }, name } per input; name is always empty) and input_count.

params.name: patch_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationPatch

commands.returns: { patch_path, bBypass, output_parameter: { path, class } | null, inputs: [{ bus: { path } }], input_count }

commands.name: get_sound_source_bus
commands.description: Read the routing fields of a USoundSourceBus asset: source_bus_channels (Mono or Stereo), duration in seconds (0 plays indefinitely) and the UAudioBus it outputs to (audio_bus_path and audio_bus_class, empty when none). Read-only. Writer: set_sound_source_bus_audio_bus.

params.name: ssb_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundSourceBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SSB_Radio".

commands.returns: { ssb_path: string, asset_class: string, source_bus_channels: string, duration: float, audio_bus_path: string, audio_bus_class: string }

commands.name: get_sound_wave_properties
commands.description: Read USoundWave tunables (the object's own UPROPERTY fields) from an imported sound wave.

params.name: sound_wave_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundWave.

commands.returns: { sound_wave_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object, looping: bool }

commands.name: get_soundfield_submix_info
commands.description: Read a USoundfieldSubmix asset without changing it: its soundfield_encoding_format and resolved_format, encoding_settings {class, path}, and effect_chain entries {index, class, path, settings_class, settings_path} with chain_length. Adds a note when no concrete soundfield effect class is loaded.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Full path to the USoundfieldSubmix (required).

commands.returns: { submix_path, soundfield_encoding_format, resolved_format, encoding_settings_class, encoding_settings: { class, path }, effect_chain: [{ index, class, path, settings_class, settings_path }], chain_length, note? }

commands.name: get_submix_effect_chain
commands.description: Read the effect chain of a USoundSubmix asset in order: one entry per slot with the name, class and path of its USoundEffectSubmixPreset ("None" for an empty slot), plus chain_length. Read-only; add_submix_effect_to_chain appends to it.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundSubmix, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SM_Master.SM_Master".

commands.returns: { submix_path: string, effects: [object], chain_length: int }

commands.name: list_meta_sound_node_types
commands.description: Enumerate all MetaSound node classes registered with the engine (via Metasound::Frontend::ISearchEngine). Editor-only because ISearchEngine::FindAllClasses is gated by WITH_EDITORONLY_DATA.

params.name: include_unloaded
params.description: If true (default), include classes from assets not yet loaded into memory.

commands.returns: { count, types: [{ class_name, class_path, type, version, is_native }] }

commands.name: list_meta_sound_nodes
commands.description: List every node in the default graph of a MetaSound Source asset with its GUID id, name, class name and input/output counts, plus count. Read-only; pass the id to get_meta_sound_node_info and the other node tools.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted.

commands.returns: { metasound_path, count, nodes: [{ id, name, class_name, input_count, output_count }] }

commands.name: list_meta_sound_references
commands.description: List the packages that reference a MetaSound Source asset, hard or soft, from the Asset Registry, with their count. Read-only; the source is loaded to resolve its package. For assets of any type use get_asset_referencers.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted.

commands.returns: { metasound_path, count, references: [{ package_name }] }

commands.name: list_meta_sounds
commands.description: List all UMetaSoundSource assets under a content path (default /Game).

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content path to filter on (default "/Game").

commands.returns: { package_path, count, sounds: [{ path, name, class }] }

commands.name: list_subtitle_cues
commands.description: Lists all subtitle cues on a USubtitleAssetUserData.  Read-only walk of the Subtitles array, returning cue_count, max_duration (from USubtitleAssetUserData::GetMaximumDuration), and per-cue fields (index, text, start_offset, duration, duration_type, priority, subtitle_type, comment).

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Content path of the USubtitleAssetUserData asset.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, success: bool, count: int, max_duration: float, cues: [{index, text, start_offset, duration, duration_type, priority, subtitle_type, comment}] }

commands.name: metasound_add_interface
commands.description: Adds a registered interface to an existing MetaSound Source's graph.  Obtains a builder for the saved asset via the editor subsystem's FindOrBeginBuilding (the reliable headless path), validates the interface via IsInterfaceRegistered, then calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::AddInterface (which adds the interface's input/output nodes). The asset is saved after the edit.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source (e.g. "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example" or fully-qualified ".MS_Example").

params.name: interface_name
params.description: Name of a registered MetaSound interface to add (required)

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_kind: string, interface_name: string, added: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: metasound_add_node_by_classname
commands.description: Add a real process node to a MetaSound Source graph by its registered class name (e.g. UE/Sine/Audio).  Unlike add_metasound_graph_input (which adds a graph input node), this instantiates a DSP node so you can author a real signal patch headless. Returns the node's GUID (node_id) and its enumerated input/output pins (name + data_type) for follow-up set/connect calls. The asset is saved. NOT idempotent: each call adds a new node instance (delete + recreate the source for a clean run).

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: class_namespace
params.description: Registered node class namespace, e.g. "UE".

params.name: class_name
params.description: Registered node class name, e.g. "Sine".

params.name: class_variant
params.description: Optional class variant, e.g. "Audio" (omit for the default/no-variant class).

params.name: major_version
params.description: Optional major version (default 1).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, class_namespace: string, class_name: string, class_variant: string, inputs: [{name,data_type}], outputs: [{name,data_type}], added: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: metasound_connect_node_to_graph_output
commands.description: Connect a concrete node's output pin to a named graph output, completing a signal patch (e.g. Sine.Audio -> the source's audio output).  Uses ConnectNodeOutputToGraphOutput (idempotent: replaces any existing edge). Reports the honest EMetaSoundBuilderResult.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: node_id
params.description: GUID of the source node (from metasound_add_node_by_classname).

params.name: node_output_name
params.description: Name of the node's output pin (e.g. "Audio").

params.name: graph_output_name
params.description: Name of the target graph output (discover via get_metasound_graph_info).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, node_output_name: string, graph_output_name: string, connected: bool, result: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: metasound_set_input_default
commands.description: Sets the default literal value of a MetaSound Source graph input.  Obtains a builder for the existing asset (FindOrBeginBuilding) and calls SetGraphInputDefault with an FMetasoundFrontendLiteral built from the supplied value, then reads the value back to verify and saves the asset. Provide exactly one of ``value`` (float, default), ``int_value``, ``bool_value`` or ``string_value``.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: input_name
params.description: Name of the graph input whose default to set.

params.name: value
params.description: Float default value (optional, used if no other *_value is provided)

params.name: int_value
params.description: Int32 default value (optional, mutually exclusive with value/bool_value/string_value)

params.name: bool_value
params.description: Bool default value (optional, mutually exclusive with value/int_value/string_value)

params.name: string_value
params.description: String default value (optional, mutually exclusive with value/int_value/bool_value)

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, input_name: string, value_type: string, value_set: bool, verified: bool, value_read_back: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: metasound_set_node_input_default
commands.description: Set the default literal of a named input pin on a concrete node (by node_id from metasound_add_node_by_classname).  Reads the value back to verify and saves. Provide exactly one of ``value`` (float, default), ``int_value``, ``bool_value`` or ``string_value``.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: node_id
params.description: GUID of the node (from metasound_add_node_by_classname).

params.name: input_name
params.description: Name of the node input pin (discover via the node's enumerated inputs).

params.name: value
params.description: Float default (optional, used if no other *_value is provided).

params.name: int_value
params.description: Int32 default (optional, mutually exclusive).

params.name: bool_value
params.description: Bool default (optional, mutually exclusive).

params.name: string_value
params.description: String default (optional, mutually exclusive).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, input_name: string, value_type: string, value_set: bool, verified: bool, value_read_back: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: play_sound
commands.description: Starts the sound already assigned to an audio component of the editor world, matched by object name (case-insensitive) against the first audio component of each actor; components in a running PIE world are not reached. start_time is an offset in seconds into the sound. A component without a sound is an error: assign one with set_audio_sound. Transient: nothing is saved, marked dirty or undoable. was_playing and playing are read just before and just after the call. Stop with stop_sound; to play an asset at a location without a component use play_sound_at_location.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Name of the audio component to play sound on

params.name: start_time
params.description: Optional offset in seconds to start playback at

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, playing: bool, was_playing: bool, sound_name: string, start_time: number, success: bool }

commands.name: play_sound_at_location
commands.description: Plays a sound asset at a specific world location without requiring an audio component.

params.name: sound_path
params.description: Full asset path to the sound (e.g. '/Game/Audio/MySound.MySound')

params.name: location
params.description: [x, y, z] 3D location to play the sound at

params.name: volume
params.description: Optional volume multiplier; defaults to 1.0

params.name: pitch
params.description: Optional pitch multiplier; defaults to 1.0

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation of the sound (it matters to a directional attenuation)

commands.returns: { sound_path: string, sound_name: string, location: { x, y, z }, rotation: { pitch, yaw, roll }, volume: number, pitch: number, success: bool }

commands.name: remove_bus_from_mix
commands.description: Removes every stage that uses a USoundControlBus from a USoundControlBusMix asset and saves the mix; a removal succeeds only when the mix reaches disk. A bus that is not in the mix is already the state asked for: the call succeeds with removed false and already_absent true, and saves nothing. Returns mix_path, bus_path, removed, already_absent, stage_count, saved.

params.name: mix_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus to remove from the mix

commands.returns: { mix_path, bus_path, removed, already_absent, stage_count, saved }

commands.name: remove_metasound_graph_input
commands.description: Removes a graph INPUT (and its node) from a MetaSound Source by name (inverse of add_metasound_graph_input).  Queries GetGraphInputNames first: if the input is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveGraphInput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: input_name
params.description: Name of the graph input to remove.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, input_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_metasound_graph_output
commands.description: Removes a graph OUTPUT (and its node) from a MetaSound Source by name (inverse of add_metasound_graph_output).  Queries GetGraphOutputNames first: if the output is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveGraphOutput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: output_name
params.description: Name of the graph output to remove.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, output_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_metasound_node
commands.description: Removes a node from a MetaSound Source graph by its node_id GUID (inverse of metasound_add_node_by_classname).  Parses the node_id into a node handle and queries ContainsNode first: if the node is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveNode (pruning unused dependencies) and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: node_id
params.description: GUID of the node to remove (from metasound_add_node_by_classname).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_modulation_input_from_patch
commands.description: Removes every input of a USoundModulationPatch asset whose bus has the same asset name as bus_path, then saves the patch; a removal succeeds only when the patch reaches disk. When no input matches, the patch is already the state asked for: the call succeeds with removed false and already_removed true, and saves nothing. Returns patch_path, bus_path, removed, already_removed, input_count, saved.

params.name: patch_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationPatch

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus whose input is removed

commands.returns: { patch_path, bus_path, removed, already_removed, input_count, saved }

commands.name: remove_soundfield_effect
commands.description: Detach the effect at effect_index from a USoundfieldSubmix effect chain (undoable) and save; the effect object stays in the package, an out-of-range index is an error, and a removal succeeds only when the submix reaches disk. Returns removed_effect_class, removed_effect_path and chain_length. With no concrete effect class loaded nothing changes and the call fails, with removed false and a note.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Full path to the USoundfieldSubmix (required).

params.name: effect_index
params.description: Zero-based index into SoundfieldEffectChain (required).

commands.returns: { submix_path, effect_index, removed_effect_class, removed_effect_path, removed: true, already_absent: false, chain_length, saved, save_error? } -- success only when saved; with no concrete effect class loaded the call fails with { submix_path, effect_index, removed: false, saved: false, note } and the chain is not touched.

commands.name: remove_subtitle_cue
commands.description: Remove a single FSubtitleAssetData cue by index. Inverse of add_subtitle_cue; use remove_subtitles_asset to destroy the whole asset instead. Idempotent: an out-of-range index returns removed:false + note, not an error.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the USubtitleAssetUserData.

params.name: cue_index
params.description: 0-based index into Subtitles[].

commands.returns: { asset_path, cue_index, removed, previous_count, new_count }

commands.name: remove_subtitles_asset
commands.description: Destroy a USubtitleAssetUserData asset (mirror of create_subtitles_asset). Typed-delete: it loads the asset and REFUSES to delete it if it is not a USubtitleAssetUserData, so it cannot wipe the wrong asset the way the generic delete_asset can. Idempotent on missing assets.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full /Game/... asset path of the subtitles asset.

commands.returns: { asset_path, deleted, already_existed, asset_class?, note? }

commands.name: set_audio_bus_channels
commands.description: Change the channel layout (AudioBusChannels) of an existing UAudioBus asset and save it; success requires the save. Returns channels, channels_int and num_channels read back from the asset. To make a new bus use create_audio_bus.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAudioBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/AB_Music".

params.name: channels
params.description: EAudioBusChannels: 'Mono' | 'Stereo' | 'Quad' | 'FiveDotOne' | 'SevenDotOne', case-insensitive; FivePointOne, 5.1, SevenPointOne and 7.1 are accepted too.

commands.returns: { bus_path: string, asset_class: string, channels: string, channels_int: int, num_channels: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_audio_sound
commands.description: Sets the sound asset of an audio component of the editor world, matched by object name (case-insensitive) against the first audio component of each actor; components in a running PIE world are not reached. A component that is playing restarts with the new sound unless it allows multiple instances. The change is not saved, marked dirty or undoable. A missing component or a sound that does not load is an error. previous_sound_name names the sound it replaced (None when there was none). Start playback with play_sound.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Name of the audio component to modify

params.name: sound_path
params.description: Full asset path to the sound (e.g. '/Game/Audio/MySound.MySound')

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, sound_path: string, sound_name: string, previous_sound_name: string, sound_duration: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_audio_volume
commands.description: Set VolumeMultiplier (0 to 10, else an error; also resets VolumeModulationMin/Max to 1) on an audio component of the editor world, matched by object name against the first audio component of each actor. No undo, no dirty mark. Returns old_volume, new_volume and volume_set.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Object name of the audio component to modify (e.g. "AudioComponent0"), compared without case; only the first audio component of each actor is searched.

params.name: volume
params.description: Volume multiplier between 0.0 and 10.0

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, old_volume: number, new_volume: number, requested_volume: number, volume_set: bool, volume_message: string, audio_enabled: bool, audio_pitch: number, audio_mobility: string, audio_sound_name: string, audio_3d_attenuation_radius: number, audio_position: { x, y, z }, audio_owner_name: string }

commands.name: set_control_bus_mix_stage_value
commands.description: Sets the stored target value, and optionally the attack and release fade times in seconds, of the stage a USoundControlBus has in a USoundControlBusMix asset, then saves the mix; success requires the save. Only that bus's first stage is edited, inside an undo transaction; a bus that is not in the mix is an error (add it with add_bus_to_mix). It edits the asset, not a live value: push a runtime value with set_control_bus_value. Read the stages with get_control_bus_mix_info.

params.name: mix_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus whose stage is edited

params.name: target_value
params.description: New stage target value (required float)

params.name: attack_time
params.description: Optional attack interpolation time in seconds

params.name: release_time
params.description: Optional release interpolation time in seconds

commands.returns: { mix_path, bus_path, target_value, attack_time, release_time, updated, saved }

commands.name: set_control_bus_value
commands.description: Pushes a runtime value into a USoundControlBus through a global bus mix of the editor world (UAudioModulationStatics::SetGlobalBusMixValue), fading over fade_time. Transient: the asset is not modified or saved, and applied is always true, not read back; read the live value with get_modulation_info.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus

params.name: value
params.description: New runtime bus value to push (required float)

params.name: fade_time
params.description: Fade time in seconds; a negative value reuses the last fade time of the global stage, or 0.1 s if none was set (default -1.0)

commands.returns: { bus_path, value, fade_time, applied }

commands.name: set_meta_sound_node_property
commands.description: Write one field of a MetaSound Source node's Configuration struct by reflection, directly in the document (not through the MetaSound builder), then save the asset. Re-applying a value returns value_changed false but still saves. Succeeds only when the asset reaches disk; a failed save leaves the value in memory only (saved false, save_error).

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted.

params.name: node_id
params.description: Node GUID, as list_meta_sound_nodes returns it in id; a value that is not a GUID is refused.

params.name: property
params.description: FProperty name on the Configuration struct.

params.name: value
params.description: New value for the field as JSON, converted by FJsonObjectConverter: a number, bool, string, array or object (for a struct field); numbers and booleans can also be passed as strings ("0.5", "true").

commands.returns: { metasound_path, node_id, property, set, value_changed, new_value?, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_metasound_preset_parameter
commands.description: Sets a parameter default value on a MetaSound preset.  Loads the preset, obtains a builder via FindOrBeginBuilding, calls SetGraphInputDefault with the appropriate literal type, then BuildAndOverwriteMetaSound to persist.

params.name: preset_path
params.description: Content path of the MetaSound preset asset.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Name of the graph input parameter to set.

params.name: parameter_type
params.description: Literal type for the value: "float" (default), "bool", "int", "string".

params.name: value
params.description: Value to set. Interpreted according to parameter_type.

commands.returns: { preset_path: string, parameter_name: string, success: bool, verified: bool, value_read_back: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_modulation_generator_settings
commands.description: Writes the settings that match the class of a USoundModulationGenerator asset (LFO, ADEnvelope or EnvelopeFollower) and saves it; params of another class are ignored, other generator classes are refused, and the LFO shape cannot be set here. Returns generator_path, generator_class, settings as stored, updated, saved.

params.name: generator_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationGenerator

params.name: frequency
params.description: LFO only: oscillation frequency in Hz (optional float)

params.name: amplitude
params.description: LFO only: output amplitude/gain multiplier (optional float)

params.name: offset
params.description: LFO only: output offset added to the waveform (optional float)

params.name: phase
params.description: LFO only: starting phase in degrees (optional float)

params.name: attack_time
params.description: ADEnvelope/EnvelopeFollower: attack interpolation time in seconds (optional float)

params.name: decay_time
params.description: ADEnvelope only: decay interpolation time in seconds (optional float)

commands.name: audit_widget_accessibility
commands.description: Sweep Widget Blueprints for the accessibility problems that are measurable from what was AUTHORED: text/background contrast against the WCAG 2.x threshold, text smaller than a legible minimum, interactive widgets with no accessible label for a screen reader, and buttons below a minimum touch/focus size. On console this is a CERTIFICATION requirement, not a nicety. READ THE LIMITS BEFORE TRUSTING A PASS: contrast is computed against the FIRST ancestor holding a solid colour -- a UBorder's brush, a UButton's WidgetStyle.Normal, or a flat UImage -- so a background painted by a texture, a material, a video or a sibling drawn underneath is INVISIBLE to this, and those cases come back as background_source:"none" rather than quietly passing, because "could not judge" and "fine" are different answers. A brush only counts when it has no ResourceObject, its TintColor is UseColor_Specified, and its DrawAs actually FILLS the middle: Box, Image or RoundedBox. DrawAs=Border is excluded on purpose (it tiles the sides and leaves the centre empty, which is exactly where the text sits). Colours coming from a CommonUI style asset or a property binding are equally invisible: only authored values are read. What IS exact is the maths -- relative luminance 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B over LINEAR values (which is what an FLinearColor already is) and ratio (Llight+0.05)/(Ldark+0.05), straight from WCAG.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to sweep (default /Game).

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders (default true).

params.name: min_contrast_ratio
params.description: Contrast floor for normal-size text (default 4.5, the WCAG AA rule). Text at or above large_text_size only needs 3.0, applied automatically.

params.name: large_text_size
params.description: Font size from which text counts as "large" for the contrast rule (default 18.0, per WCAG).

params.name: min_font_size
params.description: Smallest legible font size; anything under it is reported (default 12.0).

params.name: min_touch_size
params.description: Minimum width/height in pixels for an interactive widget's authored slot size (default 44.0, the common touch-target guideline). Only checkable when the slot actually carries a size -- an auto-sized slot reports size_known:false instead of a false pass.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max Widget Blueprints to load (default 500).

commands.returns: { folder_path, widget_blueprints_scanned, widgets_examined, issue_count, issues_by_kind: {low_contrast, contrast_unknown, small_text, missing_accessible_text, small_touch_target}, entries: [{ widget_bp_path, widget_name, widget_class, kind, detail, contrast_ratio?, required_ratio?, text_color?, background_color?, background_source?, font_size?, width?, height? }], truncated }

commands.name: audit_widget_style
commands.description: Sweep Widget Blueprints and report every widget whose style DEVIATES from a reference widget -- the "who is off-theme" question, which is the one that scales badly by hand once there are more than a couple of screens. You designate one widget as the truth (reference_bp_path + reference_widget_name), list the property paths that define the style (dotted paths work: "WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor"), and this reports, per matching widget, which of those paths differ and what each side holds. Comparison is on the property's exported text, so it is type-agnostic and reports a real difference rather than a formatting one. Pair it with apply_widget_style_preset, which can copy those same paths off that same reference widget to FIX what this finds.

params.name: reference_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint holding the reference widget (the style source of truth).

params.name: reference_widget_name
params.description: Name of the reference widget inside that Widget Blueprint.

params.name: property_paths
params.description: The paths that define the style, e.g. ["WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor","WidgetStyle.NormalPadding"]. A path that does not resolve on the REFERENCE is an error (the reference must define the style); one that does not resolve on a target is reported as unresolved, not as a deviation.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to sweep for targets (default /Game).

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders (default true).

params.name: target_class
params.description: Only compare widgets of this class, matched with IsA (defaults to the reference widget's own class, which is almost always what you want).

params.name: include_matching
params.description: Also report the widgets that already match (default false).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max Widget Blueprints to load (default 500).

commands.returns: { reference, property_paths, widget_blueprints_scanned, widgets_compared, deviating_count, matching_count, entries: [{ widget_bp_path, widget_name, widget_class, deviations: [{path, actual, expected}], unresolved_paths: [string], matches: bool }], truncated }

commands.name: audit_widget_text
commands.description: Sweep Widget Blueprints and report which player-visible texts are typed INLINE rather than coming from a String Table -- the localization-maintainability question. NOTE: this corrects the intuition most people start with: a text written as a bare string is NOT lost to localization. Unreal assigns it a stable key when the package is saved, and FTextInspector::ShouldGatherForLocalization returns true, so it DOES get collected and translated. What it lacks is a MEANINGFUL identity: the namespace comes out empty and the key is an opaque GUID like 971E3B3B436AEE91028BA1ADB97B3046. That still costs -- translators see no context, and re-authoring the text churns the key, orphaning the translation. So this reports identity_kind per text: string_table (best), explicit (an author-given namespace/key), auto_key (typed inline, key generated on save) and none (never saved, no identity yet). Default output is everything that is NOT string_table or explicit.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to sweep (default /Game). Every UWidgetBlueprint under it is loaded and walked.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders (default true).

params.name: include_all
params.description: Also report the texts that already have a good identity, string_table and explicit ones included (default false).

params.name: include_data_assets
params.description: Also sweep DataTables and DataAssets under the same folder (default false). This is where an AAA game actually keeps its text -- item names, quest descriptions, tooltips -- and it is text the widget walk cannot reach, because there the FTexts sit in nested struct fields rather than on a widget class. Nested structs and arrays of structs are walked too.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max Widget Blueprints to load (default 500). Loading a WBP is not free; a whole-project sweep is a heavy call.

commands.returns: { folder_path, widget_blueprints_scanned, texts_examined, counts_by_identity: {string_table, explicit, auto_key, none}, not_gathered_count, entries: [{ widget_bp_path, widget_name, widget_class, property_name, text, identity_kind, will_be_gathered, namespace, key, string_table }], truncated } -- not_gathered_count is the engine's own ShouldGatherForLocalization saying a text will NOT be collected at all; in a saved asset that is normally 0, and anything above it is a real alarm.

commands.name: capture_pie_state
commands.description: Snapshot of every actor in the ACTIVE PIE world, with every property flagged Replicated or SaveGame (generic -- no judgment call about what is "relevant"). It requires a live PIE session: with none running for pie_client_index it errors cleanly instead of silently snapshotting the EDITOR world, which is what makes it usable as co-op evidence -- point it at a client index to prove a value really replicated. On a large world ALWAYS pass class_filter and/or max_actors. Returns a summary plus a report path; read the detail with read_mcp_audit_file.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Which PIE client's world to snapshot (0 = first/server/standalone). Defaults to 0.

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional actor-class guardrail. Accepts a single class name OR an array of them (the hint is deliberately absent: the type-hint grammar has no union, and `[string|array]` would make this whole @param unparseable, leaving it an EMPTY description in the catalog). Detail: one class name or an array of them, each resolved to a UClass (object/script path, short name, or the Blueprint asset name -- "<Name>_C" is tried too) and matched with IsA, so subclasses match. An entry that does not resolve, or that resolves to a non-AActor class, is a hard ERROR rather than being dropped: dropping it would silently snapshot the whole World Partition world, keeping it would silently return an empty snapshot. Defaults to no filter (every actor).

params.name: max_actors
params.description: Optional cap on how many actors get their properties reflected into the report; 0 (the default) means UNLIMITED, and negative values are clamped to 0. Actors past the cap are still COUNTED (cheap) but not reflected (the expensive part), so total_matching_actors and truncated are exact, not estimated.

commands.returns: { path: string, truncated: bool, summary: { actor_count: int, actors_seen: int, total_matching_actors: int, max_actors: int, truncated: bool, class_filter: [string], replicated_property_count: int, savegame_property_count: int, savegame_filter_status: "active"|"dead_in_this_run" }, report_size_bytes: int, verification: {...}, verification_checks: [...] } -- class_filter lists the resolved class paths; success is false when the report is missing or empty on disk.

commands.name: read_mcp_audit_file
commands.description: Read back the FULL report that an audit_* or capture_pie_state command wrote to disk. Those commands return only a summary plus a path, so this is the second half of every one of them -- without it you never see the per-Blueprint / per-asset / per-actor detail. Restricted to Saved/MCPAudits/: it is not a general file reader.

params.name: path
params.description: Path returned by a prior audit command

commands.returns: the full parsed JSON report object
