params.description: (sight) Peripheral vision half-angle, degrees (Clamp 0..180)

params.name: hearing_range
params.description: (hearing) Hearing range, cm (ClampMin 0)

params.name: detect_enemies
params.description: Optional bool affiliation filter

params.name: detect_neutrals
params.description: Optional bool affiliation filter

params.name: detect_friendlies
params.description: Optional bool affiliation filter

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, sense_type, config_class, <sense fields>, note }

commands.name: add_blueprint_function
commands.description: Create a NEW function graph on a Blueprint, or with override=true a real OVERRIDE of an inherited/interface member (delegated to implement_interface_function, so an event-shape member becomes an event override node and a value-returning one an override graph). It REFUSES rather than guessing: a name that collides with an overridable inherited function errors with a hint instead of silently creating a "<name>_0" shadow, and an EVENT-shape member already shadowed by a local function graph errors telling you to remove that graph first. The new graph does not exist in the generated class until compile_blueprint, so compile BEFORE add_function_parameter or any node that calls it -- otherwise a build_blueprint_graph step fails with "Function not found" and rolls the whole batch back.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name for the new function; with override=true, the EXACT name of the inherited (interface or parent-class) function to override.

params.name: override
params.description: Optional. When true, create an OVERRIDE of an inherited function ('My Blueprint > Override'): resolves the interface/parent-virtual signature and creates the override graph (function-shape) or event override node (event-shape) with the inherited signature + exact name -- NOT a new deduped function. When omitted and the name collides with an inherited overridable function, the call errors with a hint (instead of silently making a '<name>_0' shadow); pass override=false to force a brand-new function anyway.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, function_name: string, graph_name: string, success: bool [, kind, already_existed, node_id, already_exists, is_interface_function, note] } -- with override=true the payload is implement_interface_function's (kind='function'|'event', graph_name or node_id). success:true can come back WITHOUT the graph actually appearing, so confirm with get_blueprint_functions before wiring it.

commands.name: add_blueprint_variable
commands.description: Add a MEMBER variable to a Blueprint (add_function_local_variable is the function-scoped twin), then read/write it with add_graph_node node_type=variable_get/variable_set. TRAP 1: the variable is born NOT editable per instance -- placing the actor and writing that variable fails with "cannot be edited on instances" -- and get_blueprint_variables reports instance_editable:true anyway; fix it with set_bp_variable_metadata(instance_editable=true). TRAP 2: on a class that ALREADY has actors placed in a level, those instances keep the value of the first compile, so a default set afterwards never reaches them -- verify on the instances, not on the CDO.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: New variable name (fails if the name already exists on this Blueprint).

params.name: variable_type
params.description: Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, or the name/path of a struct, enum, class or object (e.g. Vector, /Game/Dir/S_Foo.S_Foo, /Script/Engine.Actor).

params.name: is_array
params.description: When true, make the variable an array container; defaults to false. This is the ONLY array authoring path -- add_function_parameter has no equivalent.

params.name: default_value
params.description: Initial default value for the new variable, in exported-text form; optional

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, variable_type, is_array } -- an echo of the request, NOT a verification: read the variable back with get_blueprint_variables (or the CDO) before relying on it.

commands.name: add_branch_node
commands.description: Add a Branch (if/then/else) node -- pins 'execute', 'Condition', 'then' (true), 'else' (false) -- AND compile the Blueprint as a side effect. add_graph_node node_type="branch" creates the identical node without compiling, which is what you want inside a build_blueprint_graph batch; use this one when a standalone compile is wanted anyway. Leaving 'else' unwired is legitimate and lint_blueprint_graph will not flag it, except inside a function that returns a value (function_exit_without_return).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, Condition, then, else], blueprint_name, graph_name }

commands.name: add_break_struct_node
commands.description: Create a Break Struct node with ONE OUTPUT PIN PER MEMBER of the struct (Blueprint-defined structs included) and return them all, so each field can be read out with connect_pins without a follow-up read. Same node as add_graph_node node_type="break_struct", but reconstructed after creation so the per-member pins are refreshed from the struct. Inverse: add_make_struct_node. Does NOT compile.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: struct_type
params.description: UScriptStruct path (/Game/.../S_Foo.S_Foo), bare name, or engine alias (Vector/Rotator/Transform...).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position (ignored when node_position is set).

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position (ignored when node_position is set).

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y.

commands.returns: { node_id, pins:[...the struct input + one output pin per struct member...], blueprint_name, graph_name, struct_type }

commands.name: add_broadcast_node
commands.description: Add the node that BROADCASTS (fires) an event dispatcher on self -- own or inherited -- with one input pin per signature parameter, so listeners run. Does NOT compile. The dispatcher must already exist in the compiled class (add_event_dispatcher then compile_blueprint), and its parameter pins only appear after set_event_dispatcher_signature. The opposite direction (LISTENING) is add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate" for self, add_object_bound_event for another object's dispatcher.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint that owns (or inherits) the dispatcher

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Exact name of the multicast delegate to broadcast; resolved on the skeleton class, so inherited dispatchers work

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, then, one input per signature param], blueprint_name, graph_name, dispatcher_name } -- an empty parameter list means the dispatcher has no signature yet.

commands.name: add_call_library_function
commands.description: Add a call node for a STATIC library function -- an engine library by name (KismetMathLibrary, KismetSystemLibrary, GameplayStatics, KismetStringLibrary, or any other /Script/Engine class) or a USER BlueprintFunctionLibrary by asset path -- and compile. Prefer add_graph_node node_type="call_function" when the target is a member function of an actor/component. Plan the wiring with get_function_pins, which returns the exact pin names WITHOUT creating anything. TRAP inside build_blueprint_graph: the parameter is 'function_library'; passing 'class_name' fails only THAT step ("Missing required parameter: function_library") while the batch continues, leaving every connection that needed the node reporting "Target node not found".

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: function_library
params.description: A standard engine function library ("KismetMathLibrary", "KismetSystemLibrary", "GameplayStatics", "KismetStringLibrary", with or without the U prefix) OR a user BlueprintFunctionLibrary asset path ("/Game/Dir/BFL_X", "/Game/Dir/BFL_X.BFL_X", or the "..._C" generated class).

params.name: function_name
params.description: Exact UFunction name on that library (e.g. "Abs", "MakeVector", "PrintString"); get_function_pins resolves and previews it first.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...every param pin, already named...], blueprint_name, graph_name, function_library, function } -- pins come back with the node, so connect_pins/set_pin_default_value need no follow-up read.

commands.name: add_cast_node
commands.description: Add an IMPURE Cast To <Class> node (exec in, Cast Succeeded / Cast Failed out) and compile the Blueprint. Same node as add_graph_node node_type="cast", which does NOT compile -- use that one inside a build_blueprint_graph batch. Skip the cast entirely when it only exists to type a GetComponentByClass result: add_get_component_by_class_node returns a ReturnValue pin already typed to the component class.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: target_class_name
params.description: Class to cast to: a name ("Pawn", "Character"), a /Script/Module.Class path, or a Blueprint generated-class path (/Game/Dir/BP_X.BP_X_C).

params.name: target_class
params.description: Alias accepted instead of target_class_name (same meaning); one of the two is required.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...], blueprint_name, graph_name, cast_to } -- the node WITH its pins ('execute', 'Object', 'then'/Cast Succeeded, 'CastFailed', 'As<Class>'), so it can be wired without a follow-up read.

commands.name: add_comment_node
commands.description: Add a resizable comment box (UEdGraphNode_Comment) to a graph. KNOWN BUG: the 'text' parameter is LOST -- the comment is assigned before the node is finalized and the engine's PostPlacedNewNode then overwrites it, so every box created this way reads "Comment"; the returned "comment" field is the oracle and there is no MCP way to fix it (write the rationale in the system's docs instead, and delete the empty box). It also has NO pins, so a pin_defaults entry aimed at it breaks a whole build_blueprint_graph batch.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: text
params.description: Comment text; currently IGNORED (see the bug above), the box always ends up saying "Comment"

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: width
params.description: Comment box width in pixels; defaults to 400

params.name: height
params.description: Comment box height in pixels; defaults to 200

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment } -- no pins array. comment=="Comment" means the requested text was not written.

commands.name: add_component_bound_event
commands.description: Bind a multicast delegate OF ONE OF THIS BLUEPRINT'S OWN COMPONENTS (OnComponentBeginOverlap, OnComponentHit, a vendor component's dispatcher...) to a generated handler event in the event graph -- the editor's component-event flow -- then compile and re-check that the binding registered (bound). ALSO WORKS ON A WIDGET BLUEPRINT: pass the WBP and a WIDGET's name as component_name to wire a Button's OnClicked, a Slider's OnValueChanged, a CheckBox's OnCheckStateChanged -- exactly what the Designer's "+ OnClicked" green button does, and the only headless route to it (bound:true, with a BndEvt__..._OnButtonClickedEvent created). A UMG widget is not an SCS component but IS a property of the generated class, which is all this needs. Idempotent: an identical binding is returned instead of duplicated. The Blueprint must already be compiled, since the component/widget has to exist as a property of the generated class. For a dispatcher on an object that is NOT self and NOT one of its components, use add_object_bound_event; for one on SELF, add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate".

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint OR a Widget Blueprint (already compiled).

params.name: component_name
params.description: SCS component variable name on this Blueprint (e.g. "BodyMesh"), OR -- on a Widget Blueprint -- the name of a widget in its tree (e.g. "Btn_Play"); resolved on the skeleton class, so inherited components and widgets work too.

params.name: delegate_name
params.description: Exact multicast delegate property name on the COMPONENT's class (e.g. "OnComponentBeginOverlap"). On a miss the error names the component class so the right delegate can be looked up.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...the delegate's params as OUTPUT pins...], blueprint_name, graph_name, component_name, delegate, custom_function_name, bound, already_exists? } -- bound is a post-compile re-lookup (the real oracle); already_exists is only present when an existing binding was reused.

commands.name: add_component_to_blueprint
commands.description: Add a component to a Blueprint's SCS (engine class or a Blueprint AC_* class) with an optional relative transform and parent, then compile. TRAP 1: on a CHILD Blueprint whose scene root is INHERITED, a SCENE component can end up written into the PARENT's SCS (source:"inherited", owner_class = the parent) -- which silently edits a vendor/library asset; non-scene ActorComponents land correctly on the child. TRAP 2: a scene component of a BLUEPRINT class, or one given a location, can report success without persisting and then materialize LATER as a duplicate. Both have the same oracle: get_blueprint_scs_tree right after, checking owner_class and source of the new node -- never the return value.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_type
params.description: Component class: a native short name ('StaticMesh', 'Box', 'Sphere'), a /Script path ('/Script/Engine.StaticMeshComponent'), OR a Blueprint component class given as its object path ('/Game/.../AC_Foo.AC_Foo_C'), a bare package path ('/Game/.../AC_Foo'), or a bare '<Name>_C' ('AC_Foo_C').

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name for the new component instance

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative location for scene components

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation for scene components

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative scale for scene components

params.name: transform
params.description: Optional {"location":[x,y,z], "rotation":[p,y,r], "scale":[x,y,z]} alias for scene components; any flat location/rotation/scale arg above wins over the matching axis in here if both are given.

params.name: parent_component_name
params.description: Optional parent for scene components; omit / "root" attaches under the Blueprint's EXISTING scene root (SCS or native) instead of force-adding a second orphan root node. May also name a NATIVE inherited scene component (e.g. ACharacter's "CharacterMesh0"), mirroring attach_blueprint_component. Ignored for non-scene ActorComponents (no transform, no hierarchy to join).

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Optional socket/bone name on the parent (AttachToName)

commands.returns: { component_name: string, component_type: string } -- an ECHO of the request with no owner, no source and no verification. It says nothing about WHERE the node landed: read get_blueprint_scs_tree afterwards.

commands.name: add_custom_event_node
commands.description: Add a NEW Custom Event node (an entry point you invent, not an override of anything) and compile. Idempotent by name: an existing custom event with that name in the graph is returned with already_existed:true, because re-adding one compiles into "more than one function with the same name" and breaks the Blueprint. HARD LIMIT: a custom event cannot be given PARAMETERS -- add_function_parameter answers "Function graph not found" and there is no other route -- so anything that needs arguments (an RPC in particular) must be a function instead. To override an inherited/interface event use override_interface_member.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: event_name
params.description: Name for the custom event (becomes CustomFunctionName). Must not collide with an overridable inherited function or lint_blueprint_graph flags it as custom_event_shadowing_override.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...], blueprint_name, graph_name, event_name, node_title, already_existed } -- the node WITH its pins ('then' and the delegate output), ready for connect_pins. already_existed is only present when an existing event was reused.

commands.name: add_enhanced_input_action_node
commands.description: Add an Enhanced Input action event node (UK2Node_EnhancedInputAction) bound to a UInputAction asset. Unlike add_input_action_event_node -- which creates the LEGACY UK2Node_InputAction that does NOT fire under Enhanced Input -- this node exposes the real ETriggerEvent exec pins (Triggered/Started/Ongoing/Canceled/Completed) that fire from the Enhanced Input pipeline. Use this instead of polling IsInputKeyDown in a timer; it is rebind-aware (bound to the InputAction asset, not a raw key).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor/Pawn Blueprint.

params.name: input_action
params.description: Asset path (or short name) of the UInputAction to bind, e.g. "/Game/Input/IA_Crouch".

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, pins:[{name, direction, type, linked_to, default}], blueprint_name, graph_name, input_action, node_class } -- the created node WITH its freshly-allocated pins: ETriggerEvent exec outputs (Triggered/Started/Ongoing/Canceled/Completed) plus data outputs (ActionValue/ElapsedSeconds/TriggeredSeconds/InputAction). Wire it via connect_pins WITHOUT a follow-up get_graph_nodes.

commands.name: add_event_dispatcher
commands.description: Create an event dispatcher (multicast delegate) on a Blueprint: adds BOTH the delegate member variable and its signature graph, the way the editor's "+ Event Dispatcher" does. It starts with NO parameters -- give it a signature with set_event_dispatcher_signature. Everything downstream needs the class REGENERATED first, so compile_blueprint before add_broadcast_node (to fire it) or add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate" / add_object_bound_event (to listen).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Name of the new event dispatcher; fails if a member variable of that name already exists

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, created } -- created is always true on success; confirm with get_event_dispatchers.

commands.name: add_function_local_variable
commands.description: Add a variable scoped to ONE function graph (interface-override graphs included), instead of a class member like add_blueprint_variable -- use it for scratch state that no other graph should see. Reach it from the graph with add_graph_node node_type=variable_get/variable_set and scope="local" (the default scope="auto" already prefers a local over a member of the same name).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of an existing function graph (FunctionGraphs or an interface-override graph)

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Variable name; the call fails if the name already exists in that function

params.name: variable_type
params.description: Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, or a struct/enum/class/object name or path

params.name: default_value
params.description: Initial default value for the local variable, in exported-text form; optional

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, variable_name, variable_type } -- an echo of the request; local variables do NOT appear in get_blueprint_variables (which lists members), so verify from the graph itself.

commands.name: add_function_parameter
commands.description: Add an input or output (return) parameter to an existing Blueprint FUNCTION graph -- interface-override graphs included -- and reconstruct its Entry/Result node. TWO HARD LIMITS, both silent-ish: it cannot create an ARRAY parameter (there is no is_array; the param comes out SCALAR with success), so redesign the signature to read the array where it lives; and it cannot reach a CUSTOM EVENT ("Function graph not found"), so a Server/Client RPC WITH arguments must be authored as a function plus set_bp_function_rpc. On a Blueprint just given a new function, compile_blueprint between creation and this call.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of an existing function graph (FunctionGraphs or an interface-override graph). A custom event is NOT a function graph and is rejected here.

params.name: param_name
params.description: New parameter name; made unique, so the applied name is the one echoed back in the response.

params.name: param_type
params.description: Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, or a struct/enum/class/object name or path. Arrays are NOT expressible.

params.name: is_output
params.description: When true, add an output/return param (an input pin on the Result node) instead of an input; defaults to false

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, param_name, param_type, is_output } -- param_name is the pin name actually created (uniquified). Verify with get_graph_nodes at compact=false: compact hides the new, still-unlinked pin and makes it look like nothing was created.

commands.name: add_get_component_by_class_node
commands.description: Add a GetComponentByClass node BORN TYPED: the ComponentClass pin is set before the node is reconstructed, so ReturnValue comes out as that component class instead of the generic ActorComponent and no cast is needed. Use it instead of add_graph_node + a pin_defaults entry: inside build_blueprint_graph the defaults are applied AFTER the connections, so a still-generic node fails to connect ("Actor Component Object Reference is not compatible with ...") and, with stop_on_error's default true, takes the whole batch down with it.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint to add the node to

params.name: component_class
params.description: Component class to fetch: short name, /Script/Module.Class, or a /Game Blueprint component path. Must be a UActorComponent subclass or the call errors.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...], blueprint_name, graph_name, component_class, return_pin_type } -- return_pin_type is the ORACLE: if it does not name the requested component class, the pin stayed generic and connecting it will fail.

commands.name: add_graph_node
commands.description: Create ONE node in a Blueprint's event/function graph (node_type selects the kind) and return it WITH its freshly allocated pins, so connect_pins / set_pin_default_value can wire it immediately without a follow-up get_graph_nodes. Use build_blueprint_graph instead when several nodes must be created AND wired in a single undo transaction, and get_function_pins to learn a call_function's pin names BEFORE creating anything. node_type='event' creates a REAL override (the declaring interface/parent class is resolved automatically and bOverrideFunction is set; target_class is ignored here) and fails loudly for a name that is not an overridable event -- an interface method WITH a return value is not an event, use implement_interface_function.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name (resolved under /Game/Blueprints) or full asset path. Pass the FULL path when the short name is ambiguous: a bare name that matches two assets resolves to one of them silently.

params.name: node_type
params.description: One of event, custom_event, call_function, print_string, variable_get, variable_set, branch, sequence, self, cast, spawn_actor (alias spawn_actor_from_class), create_widget, make_struct, break_struct, get_array_item, select, make_array, make_set, make_map, switch_int, switch_string, switch_name, switch_enum, enum_literal, format_text, foreach, foreach_with_break, do_once, gate, flipflop, for_loop, while_loop, is_valid, add_delegate, macro_instance

params.name: event_name
params.description: Event name; required for event and custom_event node types

params.name: function_name
params.description: Function to call; required for call_function node type

params.name: target_class
params.description: Class owning the function or cast/spawn target class. For variable_get/variable_set it names the class that owns the variable, producing a non-self member-access node (with a 'target' pin) instead of a self-context node. For create_widget it names the widget class to construct (e.g. WBP_Foo_C, a full asset path, or the widget Blueprint short name); the node exposes that widget's Expose-On-Spawn pins.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Variable to get/set; required for variable_get and variable_set

params.name: struct_type
params.description: Struct type; required for make_struct and break_struct nodes

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Enum path or name; required for switch_enum and enum_literal nodes

params.name: dispatcher
params.description: Event-dispatcher (multicast delegate) name; required for add_delegate node type. Must already exist in the COMPILED class (add_event_dispatcher + compile_blueprint), and it binds on self only -- for a dispatcher on another class use add_object_bound_event.

params.name: macro_graph_name
params.description: Macro graph name; required for node_type=macro_instance. Resolved against this Blueprint's own MacroGraphs first, then the engine StandardMacros.

params.name: scope

commands.name: add_input_action_event_node
commands.description: Add the LEGACY action-mapping event node (UK2Node_InputAction) bound to an action mapping NAME, and compile. WARNING: this node does NOT fire under Enhanced Input, which is what UE5 projects use -- it compiles clean and simply never runs. For an Enhanced Input action asset use add_enhanced_input_action_node, whose Triggered/Started/Completed pins actually execute. commands.name: add_macro_instance_node
commands.description: Instantiate a macro from a macro LIBRARY asset ("/Game/Lib/ML_X.ML_X:MyMacro", or the library path plus macro_graph) -- the only way to reach a third-party or project macro library, since add_graph_node's macro aliases (foreach, do_once, gate, is_valid...) only look inside the engine StandardMacros. With no library path it falls back to this Blueprint's own MacroGraphs and then StandardMacros. Does NOT compile. Its pins start WILDCARD and only re-type once something is connected, which connect_pins handles by reconstructing the node.

params.name: graph_name

params.name: macro_graph

commands.name: add_make_struct_node
commands.description: Create a Make Struct node with ONE INPUT PIN PER EDITABLE MEMBER of the struct (Blueprint-defined structs included) and return them all, so the struct can be filled with set_pin_default_value / connect_pins without a follow-up read. Same node as add_graph_node node_type="make_struct", but reconstructed after creation so the per-member pins are refreshed from the struct. Inverse: add_break_struct_node. Does NOT compile.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: struct_type
params.description: UScriptStruct path (/Game/.../S_Foo.S_Foo), bare name, or engine alias (Vector/Rotator/Transform...).

commands.name: add_object_bound_event
commands.description: Bind a BlueprintAssignable event dispatcher of an EXTERNAL object (not self, not a component) to a handler custom event -- the editor's right-click "Assign" flow (FEdGraphSchemaAction_K2AssignDelegate). Use this to react to a dispatcher on a widget/actor instance held in a variable (e.g. a UMG widget's "On Radial Menu Item Selected"): it spawns a UK2Node_AddDelegate bound to target_class' dispatcher with its self/target pin LEFT UNCONNECTED (you wire the instance) and a UK2Node_CustomEvent whose OUTPUT pins mirror the dispatcher's params (e.g. the segment-data struct), already wired to the AddDelegate's Delegate pin. Unlike the add_delegate node_type (self-context only), this reaches a dispatcher on a foreign class. Does NOT compile the Blueprint (mirrors the engine action); compile afterward.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint being edited (the object that will bind the event, e.g. the hub component BP).

params.name: target_class
params.description: The EXTERNAL class that owns the dispatcher. Accepts a Blueprint/widget short name, a full asset path, a full class path (/Game/.../WBP.WBP_C), a native /Script path, or the generated "..._C" class name. Prefer a full path or the "_C" class for reliable resolution.

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: The multicast delegate (event dispatcher) property to assign. Matched tolerantly: exact name, spaces stripped, or the display name (so "On Item Selected" resolves to the spaceless FName). On failure the error lists the assignable delegates found on target_class.

params.name: event_name
params.description: Optional desired name for the handler custom event; made unique in the Blueprint. Defaults to "<Dispatcher>_Event".

params.name: graph_name

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, graph_name, target_class, dispatcher, add_delegate_node_id, custom_event_node_id, custom_event_name, wired, node_id, pins:[...] (the AddDelegate node's pins -- wire 'self'/Target = the widget instance and 'execute'/'then' into your exec flow), custom_event:{ node_id, pins:[...] } (hang handler logic off its 'then'/'output_delegate' and read the dispatcher's param output pins) }

commands.name: add_parent_call_node
commands.description: Add a "Parent: <Function>" node that calls the parent-class implementation of an overridden function/event -- the second half of the child-first shape "Event X -> Parent: X -> our logic" that keeps a vendor base class working while the child adds behaviour. Searches the WHOLE ancestor chain, not just the immediate parent. Does NOT compile, and IS allowed inside build_blueprint_graph, so the event + super + logic can be built in one transaction.

params.name: blueprint_name

params.name: function_name

params.name: graph_name

params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, then, the parent's params], blueprint_name, graph_name, function_name, parent_class } -- parent_class names the ancestor that actually declares the implementation being called.

commands.name: add_reroute_node
commands.description: Add a reroute/knot node: pure layout, it re-emits whatever is wired into it and changes no behaviour. Does NOT compile. Note when reading graphs back: get_graph_nodes with compact=true excludes knots by default, so a chain that looks broken there may simply route through one -- re-read with exclude_classes=[].

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: graph_name

params.name: position_x

params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...wildcard in/out until wired...], blueprint_name, graph_name }

commands.name: add_select_node
commands.description: Create a Select node with the RIGHT NUMBER OF OPTION PINS: pass option_count to grow beyond the built-in 2, or an enum in enum_path so one option pin is generated per enum entry and the Index pin becomes that enum. add_graph_node node_type="select" only ever makes the plain 2-option wildcard version. The response names the index pin, the return pin and every option pin, so the branches can be wired without a follow-up read. Its pins stay WILDCARD until something is connected (connect_pins reconstructs the node to re-type them).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

params.name: option_count
params.description: Optional total number of option pins to end up with (default = the node's built-in 2; capped internally at a safe growth loop). Ignored when an enum drives the index.

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Optional enum path/name to drive the Index pin (option pins are then auto-generated per enum entry). An engine enum may live in an unexpected module -- ask the enum itself with static_enum().get_path_name() rather than guessing /Script/Engine.

params.name: index_type
params.description: Alias of enum_path (an enum path/name for the Index pin).

params.name: position_x

commands.returns: { node_id, pins:[...], blueprint_name, graph_name, index_pin, return_value_pin, option_pins:[string], option_count, index_enum? }

commands.name: add_sequence_node
commands.description: Add a Sequence node that fires its outputs in order, spawned with its default two 'Then 0'/'Then 1' pins (there is no parameter to add more), AND compile the Blueprint. add_graph_node node_type="sequence" makes the same node without compiling -- prefer that inside a build_blueprint_graph batch.

params.name: blueprint_name

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, Then 0, Then 1], blueprint_name, graph_name }

commands.name: add_timeline_to_blueprint
commands.description: Add a Timeline to an Actor Blueprint: creates BOTH the UTimelineTemplate variable and its UK2Node_Timeline node in one call, sets a fixed length in seconds, compiles, and verifies the template really registered (timeline_created). Actor-derived Blueprints only. It does NOT author curves or tracks -- the node comes with Play/Stop/Reverse inputs and Update/Finished outputs and nothing driven; a requested name already in use is silently uniquified, so wire the RETURNED timeline_name.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint.

params.name: timeline_name
params.description: Desired variable name for the timeline; if it is taken, a unique one is generated and returned instead.

params.name: length
params.description: Timeline length in seconds (sets fixed-length mode); defaults to 5.0

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...], blueprint_name, graph_name, timeline_name, length, timeline_created, timeline_guid } -- timeline_name is the name ACTUALLY used and timeline_created is a post-compile re-lookup of the template, so false means the variable did not survive.

commands.name: apply_component_property_overrides
commands.description: Re-apply N component-property overrides on ONE Blueprint with a SINGLE compile and a SINGLE save, then verify each value against the POST-COMPILE template (what a fresh instance actually reads). ICH-aware exactly like set_blueprint_component_property: an override on a component inherited from an ancestor Blueprint is routed through this class' InheritableComponentHandler. Built for post-reparent re-authoring, where one call per override means N compiles and N chances for an ICH record not to survive.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name

params.name: overrides
params.description: Array of { component_name, property_name, property_value } objects, applied in the given order

params.name: compile
params.description: Optional bool (default true). false skips the compile: nothing is verifiable, every entry reports matches_requested=false with verification_status='not_verifiable'

params.name: save
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Saves the Blueprint package ONCE, after the compile

commands.returns: { success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, requested_count, applied_count, verified_count, mismatched_count, failed_count, compiled, saved, save_error?, equality_predicate, results: [{ index, component_name, property_name, source, applied, apply_error?, verification_status, matches_requested, post_value, post_source, note? }], verification } }

commands.name: apply_material_to_blueprint
commands.description: Assign a material ASSET to one slot of a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (an OWN SCS node, not a placed actor) -- the persistent counterpart of set_mesh_material_color, which only builds a runtime dynamic instance. Does NOT compile and does NOT save. Actors ALREADY placed in a level keep their serialized material: change the template and the placed instances stay as they were.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; must be a UPrimitiveComponent

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface (material or material instance) to assign; a path that does not load is an error

params.name: material_slot
params.description: Optional material slot index; defaults to 0. It is not range-checked against the mesh's slot count.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, material_path: string, material_slot: int, success: bool } -- an echo: success:true only means the material loaded and SetMaterial was called. Read it back with get_blueprint_material_info.

commands.name: attach_blueprint_component
commands.description: Parent an existing SCS component under another component (or the native root). The parent may be an SCS component of this Blueprint OR a NATIVE inherited scene component from a parent C++ class (e.g. ACharacter's "CharacterMesh0" or the native capsule) -- when the name is not an SCS node and is not the native root, it is resolved from the parent-class CDO and the child is parented to it natively (bIsParentComponentNative=true). This makes sockets on inherited native meshes reachable (e.g. a socket under CharacterMesh0 at "spine_4", or a ChildActor attached at "spine_2").

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the SCS component to attach (the child)

params.name: parent_component_name
params.description: Optional parent component name; omit / "root" / the native root name attaches to the native root component. May also name a NATIVE inherited scene component (e.g. "CharacterMesh0") to parent the child natively to it.

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Optional socket/bone name on the parent (AttachToName)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, parent, parent_is_native, attach_socket, already_attached }

commands.name: build_blueprint_graph
commands.description: Build several nodes, wire their pins, and set pin defaults in one pass, wrapped in a single undo transaction -- the way to author a whole graph shape without create -> get_graph_nodes -> connect round-trips (get_function_pins gives you the pin names up front). THE ORDER IS FIXED AND MATTERS: every node first, then ALL connections, then pin_defaults -- so a node whose TYPE depends on a pin default (a generic GetComponentByClass) is connected while still untyped, fails with "... is not compatible with ..." and, under stop_on_error's default true, takes the whole call down; use add_get_component_by_class_node, which is born typed. add_comment_node has no pins at all, so a pin_defaults entry aimed at one also kills the batch. Self-contained: each sub-step runs its command directly, never through the bridge (only these: add_graph_node, add_custom_event_node, add_timeline_to_blueprint, add_cast_node, add_branch_node, add_sequence_node, add_component_bound_event, add_input_action_event_node, add_enhanced_input_action_node, add_actor_begin_overlap_event, add_call_library_function, add_reroute_node, add_comment_node, add_select_node, add_make_struct_node, add_break_struct_node, add_parent_call_node, add_get_component_by_class_node, add_broadcast_node, add_object_bound_event, add_macro_instance_node). add_component_event is NOT usable here; create it with its own call.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: nodes
params.description: [{id: string, command_type: string, params?: object}, ...] (required, non-empty). 'id' is a caller-chosen local key used to reference the node from 'connections'/'pin_defaults'; 'params' is that command's own param object (blueprint_name/graph_name are auto-filled if omitted). WORKED EXAMPLE (print "hi" on BeginPlay, one call): nodes=[{"id":"beg","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"event","event_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}},{"id":"print","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"print_string"}}], connections=[{"from_node":"beg","from_pin":"then","to_node":"print","to_pin":"execute"}], pin_defaults=[{"node":"print","pin":"InString","value":"hi"}]. Pin names for a call_function node are knowable up front via get_function_pins (so no create->get_graph_nodes->connect round-trips). Child-override canonical shape (call the parent first), one call: nodes=[{"id":"evt","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"event","event_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}},{"id":"super","command_type":"add_parent_call_node","params":{"function_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}}], connections=[{"from_node":"evt","from_pin":"then","to_node":"super","to_pin":"execute"}]. NOTE on add_object_bound_event: it creates TWO nodes; the step's local 'id' resolves to the UK2Node_AddDelegate (wire the external instance into its 'self' pin and the exec flow into 'execute'), while the handler custom event is addressable as "<id>.custom_event" and its real NodeGuid is echoed back as custom_event_node_id.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: connections
params.description: [{from_node, from_pin, to_node, to_pin}, ...]; from_node/to_node may be a local 'id' from 'nodes' (or "<id>.custom_event" for an add_object_bound_event step's handler event) or a pre-existing real NodeGuid.

params.name: pin_defaults
params.description: [{node, pin, value}, ...]; node may be a local 'id' from 'nodes' (or "<id>.custom_event") or a pre-existing real NodeGuid.

params.name: stop_on_error
params.description: Stop (and try to roll back the whole transaction) on the first failing step; defaults to true, unlike batch's default false, since connections/pin_defaults depend on earlier nodes existing. With stop_on_error:false there is NO rollback at all -- the editor's global undo is never touched, every step is attempted, and whatever half-built shape remains is cleaned up with delete_node/disconnect_pin. That is the safer mode when other work is live in the editor's undo buffer.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, graph_name, nodes: [{index, id, command_type, ok, node_id?, custom_event_node_id?, error?}], connections: [{index, ok, error?}], pin_defaults: [{index, ok, error?}], stopped_early, rollback_required, rolled_back, transaction_opened, undo_queue_len_before, undo_queue_len_after, top_transaction_title, rollback_refused_reason?, warning? }. rolled_back reports whether the undo ACTUALLY ran, not the intention: the rollback is refused (rolled_back:false + rollback_refused_reason + warning) whenever the top of the editor's undo stack is not this call's own transaction, because GEditor->UndoTransaction is global and would otherwise revert another agent's or another session's work in memory while the disk stays clean. A payload that fails pre-validation returns instead { success:false, error, validation_errors: [{section, index, id?, error}], transaction_opened:false, blueprint_name, graph_name } and never opens a transaction.

commands.name: compile_blueprint
commands.description: Compile a Blueprint to regenerate its class, returning the REAL outcome (succeeded == zero errors) plus the error/warning counts, and with return_messages=true the per-message log with each message anchored to its node_id/graph. Required after authoring functions, variables or RPCs and before anything calls them. TRAP: num_errors:0 is not a promise the graph works -- an unresolved WILDCARD pin on an array/ForEach node can compile clean and still block PIE, and warnings (a "was pruned" node whose consumers silently read defaults) do not lower it. Read the warnings too, and get_compile_errors as a second opinion.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint. A short name matching two assets compiles ONE of them silently -- pass the full path when in doubt.

params.name: return_messages
params.description: Optional (default false). When true, ALSO returns the per-message compiler results log so callers can see node-anchored errors/warnings. When false/absent the response omits the `messages` array but still reports the REAL compile status.

commands.returns: { name: string, compiled: bool, succeeded: bool, num_errors: int, num_warnings: int } -- `compiled`/`succeeded` reflect the ACTUAL compile outcome (true iff zero errors; warnings still compile). Both the default and return_messages paths return these fields. When return_messages=true additionally { messages: [{severity: 'error'|'warning'|'note', text: string, node_id: string, node_title: string, graph_name: string}] } (node_id/node_title/graph_name are empty strings when the message is not anchored to a graph node)

commands.name: connect_pins
commands.description: Wire one node's OUTPUT pin to another node's INPUT pin inside one Blueprint graph, type-checked by the K2 schema (an incompatible pair is returned as an error, never a silent no-op). Nodes are addressed by NodeGuid, pins by name. Either node that still carries a WILDCARD pin is reconstructed afterwards, so array / ForEach / Select pins really re-type instead of compiling into "The type of Target Array is undetermined" (which compile_blueprint reports as compiled:true). Use validate_pin_connection to test a pair without mutating, and build_blueprint_graph to create+wire in one transaction.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: source_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the source node (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes).

params.name: source_pin
params.description: Output pin name on the source node (e.g. "then", "ReturnValue"). An output pin of that name is preferred; any pin with the name is accepted as a fallback.

params.name: target_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target node.

params.name: target_pin
params.description: Input pin name on the target node (e.g. "execute", "Condition").

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. BOTH nodes must live in this same graph.

commands.returns: { connected, source_node_id, target_node_id } -- connected is always true when the call succeeds; the failure path is an error response, so there is no false to check.

An existing Blueprint at the path is returned unchanged, whatever its parent; a failed save only sets saved false. Returns asset_path, created, already_existed and saved. Refused during PIE unless force.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUA_AlignToFloor".

commands.returns: success or error payload

An existing Blueprint at the path is returned unchanged, whatever its parent; a failed save only sets saved false. Returns asset_path, created, already_existed and saved. Refused during PIE unless force.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/EditorTools"; a trailing slash is ignored.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUA_RenameTextures".

commands.returns: success or error payload

commands.name: create_blueprint
commands.description: Create a new Blueprint asset, optionally as a child of ANY parent class -- native or another Blueprint (pass its "..._C" class or asset path) -- and save it to disk immediately unless PIE is running. Also makes Blueprint Function Libraries and Macro Libraries, which have no Actor parent and which the normal path would reject. It does NOT create interfaces (create_blueprint_interface) nor the framework-class shortcuts (create_game_mode_class_bp, create_player_controller_class_bp, ...). It refuses instead of overwriting when the asset already exists on disk, and it never confirms the parent: read it back with get_blueprint_parent.

params.name: name
params.description: Blueprint name. Either a bare name (created under 'path' or /Game/Blueprints/) OR a full content path ("/Game/MyGame/Systems/World/BP_Foo"); an object-path form ("/Game/.../BP_Foo.BP_Foo") is also accepted.

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Optional parent class. Accepts a native name ("Actor", "Pawn", "Character", "StaticMeshActor", "BlueprintFunctionLibrary"), a "/Script/Module.Class" path, a Blueprint generated-class path ("/Game/.../BP_X.BP_X_C"), or a Blueprint asset path ("/Game/.../BP_X"). Defaults to AActor. Passing "BlueprintFunctionLibrary" makes a Function Library.

params.name: blueprint_type
params.description: Optional Blueprint type override: "normal" (default), "function_library" (a UBlueprintFunctionLibrary of static functions; parent_class is ignored/forced), or "macro" (a Macro Library; keeps parent_class or defaults to Actor). Function-library is also auto-detected from parent_class="BlueprintFunctionLibrary".

params.name: path
params.description: Optional target content folder ("/Game/MyGame/Systems"). Used only when 'name' is a bare name; ignored when 'name' is already a full path.

commands.returns: { name: string, path: string, package_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, blueprint_type: string, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string } -- parent_class here is what was REQUESTED and resolved, not proof the asset carries it: confirm a child's real parent with get_blueprint_parent. saved:false is honest and always carries save_error (PIE was running, or the Blueprint was already resident in memory and left untouched) -- an unsaved Blueprint exists only in the editor and a later compile on it also returns success.

commands.name: create_blueprint_macro
commands.description: Create an EMPTY, Tunnel-terminated macro graph owned by this Blueprint's MacroGraphs (a reusable snippet, not a function: macros inline at compile time and can carry multiple exec outputs). Idempotent -- an existing macro of that name is returned with already_existed:true. Fill it with add_graph_node using graph_name=<macro>, then instantiate it with add_macro_instance_node (add_graph_node node_type="macro_instance" also finds the Blueprint's own macros).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: macro_name
params.description: Name for the new macro graph.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, macro_name, graph_name, already_existed } -- graph_name is what to pass as graph_name / macro_graph downstream.

commands.name: create_editor_utility_blueprint
commands.description: Create, compile and save an Editor Utility Blueprint at package_path/name, parented to parent_class. Returns asset_path, parent_class, created, already_existed and saved; an existing Editor Utility Blueprint there is returned unchanged and parent_class is not applied to it. Refused during PIE unless force.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities"; a trailing slash is ignored.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUB_BatchRename".

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Parent class by name without the U or A prefix, e.g. "EditorUtilityActor", or by path such as "/Script/Blutility.EditorUtilityObject" (default EditorUtilityObject); it must be Blueprintable.

commands.returns: { name, package_path, asset_path, blueprint_class, parent_class, created, already_existed, saved, save_error }

commands.name: create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint
commands.description: Create, compile and save an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint (parent UEditorUtilityWidget) with a CanvasPanel root at package_path/name. Returns asset_path, root_widget, root_widget_class, created, already_existed and saved; an existing one is returned unchanged. Open it as a tab with run_editor_utility_widget. Refused during PIE unless force.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities"; a trailing slash is ignored.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUW_LevelTools".

commands.returns: { name, package_path, asset_path, blueprint_class, parent_class, root_widget, root_widget_class, created, already_existed, root_created, saved, save_error }

commands.name: delete_bp_variable
commands.description: Remove a member variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited/native variables are refused) and report whether it is really gone by re-looking it up. Nodes that still read/write it survive as broken references, so run compile_blueprint + get_compile_errors afterwards. For an event dispatcher use remove_event_dispatcher instead -- this call would drop the delegate variable and strand its signature graph.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, deleted } -- deleted is re-checked after the removal, so false means it is still there.

commands.name: delete_node
commands.description: Delete ONE node from a graph by its NodeGuid, breaking its links; refused for nodes the editor protects (FunctionEntry, Result, tunnels). This is the cleanup for orphan nodes left behind when a build_blueprint_graph batch fails and its rollback is refused, and it is reversible (the .uasset on disk is untouched until save_asset). It does NOT compile -- follow with compile_blueprint + get_compile_errors.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node to delete

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { deleted, node_id }

commands.name: disconnect_pin
commands.description: Break ALL links on one pin of one node (there is no way to drop a single link of a multi-linked pin). Main use: clearing links that point at nodes which no longer exist after a failed or refused build_blueprint_graph rollback -- get_graph_nodes with compact=false shows those as linked_to entries with dead GUIDs. To remove the whole node instead, use delete_node.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes)

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Pin name, in either direction

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { disconnected, node_id, pin_name }

commands.name: find_blueprint_node_references
commands.description: "Find in Blueprints" over MCP: locate every Blueprint NODE that references a symbol -- variable, function, event, custom event, multicast delegate, macro, timeline, cast target, component, or a class/object in a pin default -- across a content path, returning each hit's asset, graph chain, node_id, title, match_kind and RESOLVED declaring class (resolved:false = a name-only guess). READ-ONLY. THE RULE FOR READING A ZERO: matches_found:0 only measures NON-EXISTENCE when `assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match` comes back EMPTY -- if it names assets, the symbol's string IS in those packages, so either the real name is spelled differently or the reference lives outside a graph (component template, property default). Check coverage_complete too: a truncated, timed-out or capped scan proves nothing. Blind by construction: Level Script Blueprints inside a .umap, and C++ callers.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Required (unless component_name is given): the name to look for, matched EXACTLY (variable/function/event/macro/class/component name). A misspelling returns 0 with a full-coverage report -- see assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match before believing it.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional: search for an actor COMPONENT by name; implies mode="component" and, with owner_blueprint, also matches GetComponentByClass/Cast pins that target the component's class.

params.name: owner_blueprint
params.description: Optional: Blueprint that DECLARES component_name (asset name or path); required to resolve the component's class for the class-pin matching.

params.name: mode
params.description: Optional (default "auto"): auto|all|variable|function|event|delegate|macro|component|class|pin_default. Filters which match kinds are returned; an unrecognized value returns everything and sets mode_recognized=false.

params.name: path
params.description: Optional (default "/Game"): content path root to scan.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Optional (default true): recurse into subfolders of path.

params.name: exclude_paths
params.description: Optional: array of package-path prefixes to skip (e.g. ["/Game/VendorPack/Demo"]).

params.name: include_paths
params.description: Optional: array of package-path prefixes to restrict the scan to (applied after path).

params.name: prefilter
params.description: Optional (default true): byte-scan the .uasset name map before loading. Turning it OFF loads every Blueprint under path (slow, but the ground truth to compare against).

params.name: case_sensitive
params.description: Optional (default false): case-sensitive symbol matching (both the byte prefilter and the node classifier).

params.name: include_pin_defaults
params.description: Optional (default true): also report pin defaults / pin types that name the symbol, on nodes with no structural match.

params.name: include_node_json
params.description: Optional (default false): embed the full NodeToJson serialization of each matching node.

params.name: include_pins
params.description: Optional (default false): when include_node_json is on, include the node's pins.

params.name: max_assets
params.description: Optional (default 20000): hard cap on candidate assets examined.

params.name: max_matches
params.description: Optional (default 200): stop after this many matches (sets truncated=true).

params.name: max_seconds
params.description: Optional (default 60): wall-clock budget; on expiry the scan stops and timed_out=true.

commands.returns: { symbol, mode, mode_recognized, path, recursive, prefilter_enabled, component_class, component_declared_in, assets_in_path, assets_scanned, assets_prefiltered_out, assets_prefilter_unavailable, assets_prefilter_bypassed_dirty, assets_loaded, assets_load_failed, assets_with_matches, graphs_visited, nodes_visited, foreign_subgraphs_skipped, matches_found, truncated, timed_out, coverage_complete, elapsed_ms, assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match:[string], notes:[string], matches:[{asset_name, asset_path, package_name, graph, graph_chain, graph_kind, node_id, node_class, node_title, match_kind, member_name, declaring_class, resolved, is_component_ref, is_interface_call, exact, detail, pin, pin_value, node?}], success }

commands.name: fork_class_chain
commands.description: One-call thin-fork + optional reparent + verify: collapses the create->reparent->verify pattern into a single call. It creates a NEW thin child Blueprint of base_class at fork_name (the seam you insert between a shared-library base and your own class), optionally tags it with the fork-origin metadata tag (project setting ForkOriginTag), saves it, and then -- only if reparent_target is given -- reparents that existing Blueprint onto the new fork through the guarded reparent_blueprint_safe path (snapshot + compile flags + post-check + rollback) and reports its verification. WARNING: no durable backup is taken -- the rollback is in-memory only, so call backup_asset yourself first if you want a rollback-to-disk safety net.

params.name: fork_name
params.description: Name or full /Game path for the NEW thin child Blueprint to create.

params.name: base_class
params.description: Parent class for the new fork (native /Script, /Game/.../BP.BP_C, or a BP asset path).

params.name: path
params.description: Optional folder for fork_name when it is a bare name (default /Game/Blueprints).

params.name: fork_origin
params.description: Optional: value stored in the fork's fork-origin metadata tag (project setting ForkOriginTag, default 'mcp.forkOrigin'), recording its fork lineage.

params.name: reparent_target
params.description: Optional: an existing Blueprint to reparent onto the new fork.

params.name: auto_rollback
params.description: Optional (default true): forwarded to the safe reparent of reparent_target.

params.name: rename_colliding_vars
params.description: Optional (default false): forwarded to the safe reparent of reparent_target.

commands.returns: { fork_name, fork_path, fork_generated_class, base_class, already_exists, fork_origin_set, saved, save_error?, reparent:{...safe-reparent result...}|null, verification, verification_checks, error?, success }

commands.name: get_actor_material_info
commands.description: List the material slots of an actor PLACED IN THE EDITOR WORLD, one row per slot per StaticMeshComponent, with the material actually assigned (name, path, class) or "None". Scope limits worth knowing: it only walks UStaticMeshComponents (a skeletal mesh's slots are invisible here) and only the EDITOR world (no PIE selector), and the actor is matched by its object NAME, not its outliner label. The Blueprint-template twin is get_blueprint_material_info.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name of the actor in the EDITOR world (GetName(), not the display label shown in the outliner)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, material_slots: [{ slot, component, material_name, material_path, material_class }], total_slots: int } -- total_slots 0 means no StaticMeshComponent had slots, NOT that the actor has no materials.

commands.name: get_ai_perception_senses
commands.description: Read back the senses configured on an AIPerceptionComponent TEMPLATE of a Blueprint: for each one its config class plus the fields that matter (sight radius / lose-sight radius / peripheral angle, or hearing range) and the three affiliation filters. This is the verification step for add_ai_perception_sense. It reads the OWN SCS template, so an AIPerception component inherited from a parent Blueprint is not found, and a config class other than Sight or Hearing comes back with sense_type "unknown" and no fields.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint owning the component

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS AIPerceptionComponent node; another component type is an explicit error

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, senses: [ { config_class, sense_type, sight_radius|hearing_range, ... , detect_enemies, detect_neutrals, detect_friendlies } ], sense_count } -- sense_count 0 means the template has no configured sense, which is also what an AI that never perceives anything looks like.

commands.name: get_available_materials
commands.description: Enumerate material assets under a content path and return each one's name, object path, package and class -- the object path is what apply_material_to_blueprint / set_actor_material expect. One Asset Registry query on UMaterialInterface and all its subclasses (materials, material instances, project or plugin material classes); nothing is loaded, so a wide path is cheap. For one known name prefer resolve_asset_by_name.

params.name: search_path
params.description: Optional content path filter (e.g. "/Game/Materials"); empty/absent means the whole project and is reported back as "/Game/"

params.name: include_engine_materials
params.description: When true, also include /Engine/ materials; defaults to true, so the list is large unless a search_path narrows it

commands.returns: { materials: [{ name, path, package, class }], count: int, search_path_used: string } -- there is no truncation flag: count is everything that matched.

commands.name: get_blueprint_component_object_path
commands.description: Resolve a Blueprint component's TEMPLATE archetype and return its object path, so get_property_value/set_property_value/call_function can target that component directly.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name/path of the Blueprint that owns the component.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component variable name. Resolves an OWN SCS component (the _GEN_VARIABLE archetype on USCS_Node::ComponentTemplate) or an INHERITED/native component (the like-named subobject on the generated-class CDO).

commands.returns: { object_path: string, class: string, source: 'scs'|'inherited' } -- object_path is GetPathName() (feed it to get/set_property_value); class is the component class' full path.

commands.name: get_blueprint_component_property
commands.description: Read the EFFECTIVE default of a property on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE, resolving components INHERITED from a parent/grandparent Blueprint. Read-only twin of set_blueprint_component_property: it NEVER mints an ICH override. Resolution order: own SCS template -> existing child InheritableComponentHandler override -> ancestor's declaring SCS template -> native CDO subobject. Omit property_name to dump ALL properties of the resolved template.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component variable name (own or inherited)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property to read; omit to return ALL properties of the resolved template

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Also resolve inherited/ICH/native components (default true); when false only this Blueprint's own SCS components are considered

params.name: group_by_field
params.description: Optional. Only with property_name pointing at a TArray of STRUCTS: group the elements by this struct member and report duplicate_groups[]/empty_key_indices[]/has_duplicates. Two elements sharing a key is invisible in a plain value dump, yet when that array feeds a TMap the LAST one silently wins (Map.Add overwrites) -- this is the guardrail for exactly that class of bug.

params.name: report_duplicates
params.description: Optional bool. Implied true when group_by_field is given; pass true WITHOUT group_by_field to group by the WHOLE element value instead of one member.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, source: 'scs'|'inherited-ich'|'inherited-scs'|'inherited-native', resolved_from_class: string, property_name: string, value: any (single-property mode), properties: object, property_count: int (all-properties mode), duplicate_analysis?: { grouped_by, element_count, distinct_keys, duplicate_groups: [{key, count, indices[]}], empty_key_indices: [int], has_duplicates: bool, keys: [string] } }

commands.name: get_blueprint_components
commands.description: List the components this Blueprint DECLARES in its own SCS, with type, relative transform and the real hierarchy linkage (in-tree parent from the ChildNodes tree, parent_is_native for a native/inherited parent, attach_socket, children). SCOPE: own SCS only -- components inherited from a parent Blueprint or declared natively are NOT here, so a small count is not proof the actor is small. For the full picture including ancestors use get_blueprint_scs_tree (which reports what it deduplicates), and cross-check the CDO when a component must be proven to exist.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, components: [{ name, type, is_scene_component, parent, parent_is_native, attach_socket, children:[name], location?, rotation?, scale? }], component_count: int } -- "parent" is the in-tree SCS parent, falling back to the inherited/native parent name when the node is parented outside this SCS; location/rotation/scale only appear for scene components.

commands.name: get_blueprint_functions
commands.description: List the callable graphs of a Blueprint. Enumerates the FULL graph set (UBlueprint::GetAllGraphs), not just Blueprint->FunctionGraphs: an INTERFACE override graph lives in ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs, which FunctionGraphs alone misses (a function that exists would read as "missing"). Each entry carries graph_type so the caller can tell a plain function from an interface override, a macro or a delegate signature.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint. Pass the FULL path: a short name that matches two assets (a backup copy shares the original's name) resolves to one of them SILENTLY, and the listing then describes the wrong asset.

params.name: include_ubergraphs
params.description: Optional bool (default false): also list the EventGraph/ubergraph pages (graph_type='ubergraph'). Off by default so 'functions' stays function-shaped.

params.name: include_subgraphs
params.description: Optional bool (default false): also list nested/collapsed sub-graphs reached by GetAllGraphs but owned by no top-level list (graph_type='subgraph')

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, functions: [{ name, node_count, graph_type, is_interface, interface_name?, is_user_constructed }], function_count: int, own_function_graph_count: int, interface_graph_count: int, macro_graph_count: int, delegate_graph_count: int, ubergraph_count: int, subgraph_count: int, graphs_total: int } -- graph_type is function|interface|macro|delegate_signature|ubergraph|subgraph; is_user_constructed is just node_count>2, i.e. "someone wrote something beyond the auto Entry/Result terminators", because implementing an interface pre-creates empty graphs. subgraph_count>0 with include_subgraphs off is the warning that collapsed graphs exist and are not listed.

commands.name: get_blueprint_info
commands.description: One cheap overview of a Blueprint: parent class, compile status, and the counts + names of its OWN components, variables, function graphs and ubergraph pages. Everything here is what THIS asset declares -- nothing inherited, and interface-override graphs are not listed. So use it to orient, and the specialists to decide: get_blueprint_scs_tree for the real component set including ancestors, get_blueprint_functions for interface/macro/delegate graphs, get_blueprint_variables for variable flags, get_graph_nodes to read a graph.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, parent_class: string, components: [{ name, type }], component_count: int, variables: [{ name, type }], variable_count: int, functions: [{ name }], function_count: int, graphs: [{ name, type }], graph_count: int, has_event_graph: bool, event_graph_name?: string, status: string } -- parent_class is a short NAME (ambiguous between an engine class and a same-named project one), variable "type" is only the pin CATEGORY (no struct/class), and status is UpToDate/Error/Unknown.

commands.name: get_blueprint_material_info
commands.description: Read the material slots of ONE StaticMeshComponent TEMPLATE in a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node), with the material assigned to each slot or "None". This is the verification step after apply_material_to_blueprint / set_static_mesh_properties. The slot count comes from the assigned static mesh's LOD 0 sections, so with no mesh assigned it returns ZERO slots and has_static_mesh:false -- which is a missing mesh, not a missing material. For a placed actor use get_actor_material_info.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; it must be a UStaticMeshComponent (any other type is an error)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, material_slots: [{ slot, component, material_name, material_path, material_class }], total_slots: int, has_static_mesh: bool } -- read has_static_mesh FIRST: total_slots:0 with has_static_mesh:false means no mesh was assigned, so the array says nothing about materials.

commands.name: get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info
commands.description: Read ONE variable's full detail: its default value, the structured type (category, sub-category object and container kind -- not just the pin category get_blueprint_variables gives you), and every checkbox of the variable Details panel -- is_instance_editable / is_expose_on_spawn / is_blueprint_read_only / is_expose_to_cinematics / is_replicated / replication_condition / save_game. This is the headless oracle for "does this variable really persist into a .sav?", which otherwise costs a co-op PIE session plus a binary grep of the slot file. save_game is reported from BOTH places the flag lives, because they disagree until you compile: `save_game` is CPF_SaveGame as AUTHORED (FBPVariableDescription::PropertyFlags, exactly what the editor checkbox writes) while `save_game_generated` is the same flag on the FProperty of the GENERATED class, which is the one the save archive consults -- so save_game:true + save_game_generated:false means MARKED BUT NOT COMPILED, and nothing will persist yet; `save_game_matches` says it in one field. Read is_replicated FIRST: replication_condition is always populated (COND_None by default) and only means anything when replication is on. `default_value` is read from the CDO when the class is compiled (`default_value_source:"cdo"`), so it does not come back EMPTY for arrays, maps and every variable of an already-compiled Blueprint. Booleans of this family are contrasted, not believed -- audit_replication is the ground truth for replication.
