params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (e.g. "MyFloat"); inherited variables are not covered

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, variable_name: string, default_value: string, default_value_source: "cdo"|"blueprint_description", default_value_serialized: string, var_type: string, property_type: string, var_type_detail: {category, sub_category, sub_category_object, sub_category_object_path, container}, is_instance_editable: bool, is_expose_on_spawn: bool, is_blueprint_read_only: bool, is_expose_to_cinematics: bool, is_replicated: bool, replication_condition: string, save_game: bool, save_game_generated: bool, save_game_generated_found: bool, save_game_matches: bool }

commands.name: get_blueprint_variables
commands.description: List the variables this Blueprint DECLARES (its NewVariables): name, pin category, editor category and three flags. Inherited variables, function locals and components are NOT here. THE THREE FLAGS ARE UNRELIABLE, read off the stored variable description rather than the compiled property: instance_editable checks CPF_Edit and ignores CPF_DisableEditOnInstance, so it says true for variables the editor refuses to edit per instance; expose_on_spawn checks a property flag while set_bp_variable_metadata writes the ExposeOnSpawn METADATA, so it says false for variables that DO show up as SpawnActor pins; and expose_to_cinematics is hardcoded false. Oracles: write the placed instance for editability, the spawn node's pins for exposure, get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info for type/replication.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, variables: [{ name, type, category, instance_editable, expose_on_spawn, expose_to_cinematics }], variable_count: int } -- "type" is only the pin CATEGORY (e.g. "struct", "object"), not the struct or class; the three booleans are the unreliable ones described above.

commands.name: get_event_dispatchers
commands.description: List a Blueprint's event dispatchers (multicast delegates) WITH each one's full parameter signature (name, C++ type, is_output) and whether it is inherited. Read from the SKELETON class, so it reflects edits made since the last full compile. Use it before add_broadcast_node / add_object_bound_event / set_event_dispatcher_signature, whose pins mirror this signature; only the dispatchers this Blueprint DECLARES can have their signature edited.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Also include dispatchers inherited from parent classes; default false = only the ones this Blueprint declares (i.e. the editable ones)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, dispatchers: [ { name: string, is_inherited: bool, param_count: int, params: [ { name: string, type: string, is_output: bool } ] } ], dispatcher_count: int }

commands.name: get_function_pins
commands.description: Preview the EXACT pins a call_function / add_call_library_function node WOULD expose for a UFunction WITHOUT creating anything: owner_class, is_pure, is_static, exec_input/exec_output ("execute"/"then", null when pure), self_pin (null when static), input_params, output_params and return_value. This is what lets a whole build_blueprint_graph (nodes + connections + pin_defaults) be written in ONE call instead of create -> get_graph_nodes -> connect round-trips. It answers "what pins would it have", NOT "can a Blueprint call it": some engine functions resolve and preview here and are still rejected by the compiler, so the oracle for callability is compile_blueprint + get_compile_errors.

params.name: function_name
params.description: UFunction name, matched EXACTLY against the reflected name (e.g. "PrintString", "K2_GetActorLocation", or a Blueprint function graph's own name, which may contain spaces like "Emit Noise At Location"). A guessed name that does not exist just errors -- it never returns an empty preview.

params.name: target_class
params.description: Optional class searched FIRST: native name ("KismetSystemLibrary"), "/Script/Module.Class", a Blueprint class path ("/Game/...X_C"), or a user BFL. Also always searched: the blueprint's own class + KismetSystem/GameplayStatics/KismetMath.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Optional Blueprint whose generated class joins the search (for self / BP-local functions).

commands.returns: { function_name, owner_class, is_pure, is_static, exec_input, exec_output, self_pin, input_params:[{name,type}], output_params:[{name,type}], return_value:{name,type}|null, note }

commands.name: get_graph_nodes
commands.description: Read one Blueprint graph: every node with its node_id (NodeGuid), class, title, position, comment and pins (name, direction, type, linked_to, default) -- the read that feeds connect_pins / set_pin_default_value / delete_node, and the way to see what a graph actually DOES. TRAP: compact=true drops per-pin type metadata AND omits every pin that is unlinked and default-less (plus knots and comment boxes), so a pin missing from a compact listing is NOT proof the pin does not exist -- re-read with compact=false before concluding anything about pins. Also: a bare blueprint_name that matches two assets picks one silently (pass the full path), and reading a graph under a read-only vendor root leaves that package DIRTY in memory (reload_asset_package with on_dirty="discard" cleans it).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path. Prefer the FULL path: a short name with more than one match resolves silently to one of them, and stale backup copies share the original's name.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. Also resolves a collapsed composite subgraph by its title (e.g. 'In Game HUD') and accepts a path form ('EventGraph > In Game HUD').

params.name: expand_composites
params.description: When true, inline the nodes of collapsed composite subgraphs recursively; each node gains a "graph" tag naming the graph it came from. Macro-library graphs are never inlined. (Optional, default false)

params.name: compact
params.description: Token-lean listing: drops pin types, positions and comments, and skips pins that are unlinked AND have no default. Also excludes K2Node_Knot + EdGraphNode_Comment unless exclude_classes is given. Good for reading topology, WRONG for checking whether a pin exists. (Optional, default false)

params.name: exclude_classes
params.description: Array of leaf node class names to skip, matched against each node's "class" field (e.g. ["K2Node_Knot"]). Pass [] to include everything even in compact mode. Absent + compact=true means knots and comments are excluded; absent + compact=false excludes nothing.

params.name: max_nodes
params.description: Cap on the number of nodes emitted (<=0 or absent = unlimited); the response still counts every non-excluded node in total_node_count and sets truncated=true.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, graph_name, nodes:[{node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment, pins:[...], subgraph?}], node_count, compact, total_node_count, excluded_count, truncated } -- node_count is what was EMITTED, total_node_count what exists; a node owning a nested graph (composite / macro instance) carries "subgraph" with the name to pass back as graph_name.

commands.name: get_node_pin_info
commands.description: Dump ONE node's full pin detail -- every pin's name, direction, type, linked_to and default -- plus its class, title, position and comment, addressed by NodeGuid. Use it instead of get_graph_nodes when the node is already known: the listing is always FULL fidelity (get_graph_nodes with compact=true hides unlinked default-less pins) and costs a fraction of the tokens of a whole graph.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes)

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. Also resolves collapsed composite subgraphs by title or a path form ('EventGraph > In Game HUD').

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment, pins:[{name, direction, type, linked_to, default}] }

commands.name: get_property_access_path
commands.description: Read a UK2Node_PropertyAccess node's binding Path -- the anim-Blueprint property binding (InAnimInstance.Foo, InDeltaTime...) that no ordinary pin read exposes -- as segments plus its display text_path, and say whether the leaf actually RESOLVED (a still-wildcard Value pin means the path points at nothing). Read-only; errors on any node that is not a K2Node_PropertyAccess. Writer twin: set_property_access_path.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path (usually an Animation Blueprint).

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the property-access node (from get_graph_nodes).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

commands.returns: { node_id, graph_name, path:[string], text_path, resolved, resolved_pin:{name,direction,type,...} } -- resolved:false (Value pin still wildcard) is the signal that the binding is broken.

commands.name: implement_interface
commands.description: Add a Blueprint Interface to a Blueprint's implemented list (asset path or class name). NOT idempotent: an interface already implemented comes back as an error, unlike remove_interface. It only registers the contract -- the graphs that IMPLEMENT each member are created by implement_interface_function / override_interface_member, which are also the only correct route for interface EVENTS.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: interface_path
params.description: Blueprint interface asset path (e.g. /Game/Dir/BPI_Foo.BPI_Foo), or a resolvable interface class name/path

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, interface, implemented } -- implemented is always true on success; failure is an error response. Confirm the member set with get_blueprint_functions (interface graphs live in ImplementedInterfaces, not FunctionGraphs).

commands.name: implement_interface_function
commands.description: Create or resolve the graph that IMPLEMENTS an interface member (or a parent virtual) and return a graph_name you can immediately wire with get_graph_nodes / connect_pins / set_pin_default_value. It picks the right shape by itself: a member WITH a return value gets a real FUNCTION graph in ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs -- where add_blueprint_function refuses it ("Function already exists") and an event node would be a useless return-less stub -- while an event-shape member (no return value) gets a genuine event OVERRIDE node in the event graph, with its node_id returned. Idempotent in both branches. override_interface_member is the same logic under a friendlier name/response.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path (must already implement the interface / inherit the virtual; implement_interface first).

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the interface or overridable function (e.g. "CanInteract", "GetInteractText").

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, graph_name, kind: "function"|"event", already_existed: bool, node_id? } -- kind "function": graph_name is an editable function graph, ready to wire with get_graph_nodes / connect_pins; kind "event": the member returns nothing, so an event OVERRIDE node was created (or reused) in the event graph that graph_name names, and node_id is that node, to wire with connect_pins.

commands.name: lint_blueprint_graph
commands.description: Read-only lint of a Blueprint's graphs for four authoring bugs that COMPILE CLEAN and only show up in play: eclipsed_interface_event and custom_event_shadowing_override (a node that looks like an override and is not, so the base contract never runs), unreachable_exec_node (a node no exec chain reaches from any entry) and function_exit_without_return (a live exec path that falls off the end of a value-returning function, so the caller silently gets false/0/None). Scans ALL ubergraph + function + macro graphs by default. HONESTY LIMIT: findings:[] is NOT a clean bill of health -- by deliberate design it never flags a merely unconnected exec output, so a Branch or Is Valid with dangling outputs can pass; check linked_to yourself with get_graph_nodes (compact=false) or get_node_pin_info.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint to analyze.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Optional single graph to analyze; when omitted, scans ALL ubergraph (event) pages + function graphs + macro graphs owned by this Blueprint. Interface-override graphs are NOT in that default set -- name one explicitly to lint it.

commands.returns: { findings: [ { kind, node_id, node_title, graph_name, why, fix_hint, pin? } ] } -- kind is one of eclipsed_interface_event, custom_event_shadowing_override, unreachable_exec_node, function_exit_without_return (this one also reports the offending exec pin in "pin"); "why" carries a best-effort pointer at the likely upstream break. No counters and no coverage flags: an empty array only means these four rules found nothing.

commands.name: list_editor_utility_widgets
commands.description: List the Editor Utility Widget Blueprint assets under a content folder and its subfolders, read from the Asset Registry without loading them. Returns search_path, count and widgets [{name, asset_path, package_name, package_path}]; open one as an editor tab with run_editor_utility_widget.

params.name: path
params.description: Content folder to search recursively, without a trailing slash, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities" (default /Game).

commands.returns: { name, asset_path, package_name, package_path, search_path, count, widgets }

commands.name: list_overridable_functions
commands.description: Enumerate the functions/events that a Blueprint deriving from a class could override. Works on an EXISTING Blueprint (blueprint_name) or on ANY class (class_name) so the override surface can be inspected BEFORE the child exists. Gated with UEdGraphSchema_K2::CanKismetOverrideFunction -- the same predicate add_blueprint_function(override=true) enforces -- so discovery and authoring agree (a bare NativeEvent||FUNC_BlueprintEvent filter lets a parent Blueprint's *__DelegateSignature through as "overridable"). Each entry reports where the member is DECLARED and where it is last IMPLEMENTED, with is_stub, which is what distinguishes a concrete ancestor from its `_Abstract` sibling.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name/path of an existing Blueprint. Its ParentClass is the override surface.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Alternative to blueprint_name: any class ("Actor", "/Script/Engine.Pawn", "/Game/.../BP_X.BP_X_C", or a Blueprint asset path). The override surface is THAT class, i.e. what a new child would get. Ignored when blueprint_name is given.

params.name: include_non_overridable
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true also lists the entries a NativeEvent||FUNC_BlueprintEvent filter passes but CanKismetOverrideFunction rejects (delegate signatures, BlueprintInternalUseOnly, deprecated), each flagged can_kismet_override=false. Nothing is lost silently.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name?, class_name?, source_mode, resolved_class, base_class, ancestors: [string], count, functions: [{ function_name, display_name, declaring_class, is_native_event, is_event, is_interface, interface_name?, kind, can_kismet_override, has_override_graph, has_user_logic, is_implemented, parent_impl_kind, parent_impl_owner_class, parent_impl_graph, parent_impl_node_count, is_stub, is_stub_basis }] }

commands.name: list_scripted_action_utilities
commands.description: List Editor Utility Blueprints that are scripted Asset/Actor Action Utilities

params.name: path
params.description: Optional content path to search under (default /Game)

commands.returns: { name, path, package_name, kind, parent_class, search_path, count, utilities }

commands.name: list_widget_bound_events
commands.description: List every event-dispatcher BINDING wired in a Blueprint, across the three node kinds that make one in practice: UK2Node_AddDelegate (from add_object_bound_event / add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate"), UK2Node_ComponentBoundEvent (from add_component_bound_event -- a component's dispatcher OR a UMG widget's, e.g. a Button's OnClicked) and UK2Node_ActorBoundEvent (a level actor's, bound from the Level Blueprint). Each entry reports which kind it is (binding_kind), what it is bound ON (bound_to: the component/widget variable, or the actor), the delegate's owner class and name, and the handler on the other end. Despite the name it works on ANY Blueprint -- but it only walks Ubergraph pages and FunctionGraphs, so a binding inside a macro or interface graph is out of scope. Run it BEFORE add_object_bound_event / add_component_bound_event: double-binding one delegate to two handlers compiles fine and silently runs BOTH. A reader that cannot see what the writer wrote is worse than no reader: a 0 reads as "not wired" and sends you to re-wire what is already there.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path (Actor Blueprint, Widget Blueprint or Level Blueprint).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, bindings:[{ graph_name, node_id, binding_kind, bound_to, delegate_owner_class, delegate_name, delegate_resolved, wired, custom_event_name, custom_event_node_id }], binding_count, kind_counts:{add_delegate,component_bound_event,actor_bound_event} } -- binding_kind names the node class behind the entry. bound_to is the component/widget variable name (component_bound_event), the actor name (actor_bound_event), or empty for add_delegate, whose target pin is left unconnected by design. delegate_resolved=false means the delegate no longer resolves live (renamed/removed). wired=false is a DANGLING add_delegate bind (its Delegate pin has no handler); the two *BoundEvent kinds ARE their own handler, so they are always wired and custom_event_name is the generated BndEvt__ function.

commands.name: move_node
commands.description: Move a node to a new [x, y] canvas position. Purely cosmetic layout: no pin, link, default or type changes, and no compile. Returns the position actually applied.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node to move

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, pos_x, pos_y }

commands.name: override_interface_member
commands.description: Override a Blueprint interface member or parent virtual by name: an event override node (kind="event", node_id) when it returns nothing, else a function-override graph (kind="function", graph_name). Idempotent (was_already_overridden); leaves the Blueprint needing a compile, unsaved. Prefer it to hand-placed interface event nodes, which can compile yet never fire.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path (must implement the interface / inherit the virtual).

params.name: member_name
params.description: Name of the interface or overridable function to override (e.g. "CanInteract").

params.name: interface_path
params.description: Ignored: the member is resolved by member_name alone, implemented interfaces first, then parent classes.

params.name: node_position
params.description: Optional [x, y] canvas position applied to a freshly created event-override node.

params.name: position_x
params.description: Ignored by this tool: the new node is only moved when node_position is given, and node_position then wins.

params.name: position_y
params.description: Ignored by this tool: the new node is only moved when node_position is given, and node_position then wins.

commands.returns: { kind: "event"|"function", created: bool, was_already_overridden: bool, graph_name, node_id? } -- kind "event": an event OVERRIDE node was created or reused in the event graph that graph_name names, and node_id is that node; kind "function": graph_name is an editable function-override graph, ready to wire.

commands.name: recombine_blueprint_pin
commands.description: Collapse a previously split struct pin back into ONE pin (inverse of split_blueprint_pin), which is what set_pin_default_value needs before it will write a struct literal. Accepts either the parent pin's name or any of its sub-pin names; links on the sub-pins are dropped by the engine as part of recombining.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin.

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Name of the parent pin OR of any of its sub-pins.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { recombined } -- always true on the success path; a pin that is not split is an error response instead.

commands.name: reconcile_function_signature
commands.description: Repair a LOCAL function graph's parameter pins so they match a parent UFUNCTION -- for an override whose signature went stale after a reparent -- WITHOUT nuking the graph's downstream nodes, which is what re-creating the override by hand costs you. It diffs the parent's parameters against the function's entry/result pins: mode='add_missing' (the default) only ADDS the missing pins, so it is non-destructive and safe to run blind; mode='remove_extra' / 'mirror' also DROP pins the parent lacks, which can sever downstream connections, and are therefore gated behind force_remove=true -- without it the extra pins are merely REPORTED (partially_implemented=true).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path owning the function.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the local function graph to reconcile.

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Optional: class whose UFUNCTION defines the target signature (default: the Blueprint's current ParentClass).

params.name: mode
params.description: Optional (default 'add_missing'): 'add_missing' | 'remove_extra' | 'mirror'.

params.name: force_remove
params.description: Optional (default false): actually remove extra pins for 'remove_extra'/'mirror' (may drop connections).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, parent_class, mode, added:[{name,direction}], removed:[{name,direction}], extra_pins:[{name,direction}], missing_pins:[{name,direction}], removal_performed, partially_implemented, note, success }

commands.name: remove_blueprint_component_node
commands.description: Remove one or MORE SCS component nodes in a single batch (ONE compile for the whole lot), optionally promoting their children, and report the double census (flat AllNodes vs a walk of RootNodes) so descendants that go missing or become unreachable are NAMED instead of silently dropped. Same engine work as remove_component_from_blueprint; the difference is the contract for a component that is not there: this one is IDEMPOTENT (already_removed:true, no error), while remove_component_from_blueprint treats "nothing matched" as a caller error. Prefer this one in scripts that may re-run.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the SCS component node to remove (single form)

params.name: component_names
params.description: Optional array of SCS component node names removed in ONE batch with a SINGLE compile. Chaining single-node calls is what causes collateral deletions; prefer this for lots. Merged with component_name when both are given.

params.name: promote_children
params.description: Optional bool (default true); true keeps descendants (RemoveNodeAndPromoteChildren), false orphans/deletes them (RemoveNode)

commands.returns: { success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, component_name, promote_children, removed, already_removed, requested[], removed_components[], also_removed[], unexpected_losses[], not_found[], still_present[], node_count_before, node_count_after, reachable_before, reachable_after, orphans_before[], orphans_after[], root_nodes_before[], root_nodes_after[], root_nodes_changed, compiled, compile_count, verification } }

commands.name: remove_blueprint_function
commands.description: Delete a function graph OWNED BY the Blueprint (Blueprint->FunctionGraphs) by name. WARNING: It resolves more graphs than it can delete: name lookup goes through FindGraph (all graphs, interface overrides and macros included) but the delete only touches FunctionGraphs and only when bAllowDeletion is true, so an INTERFACE OVERRIDE resolves and cannot be removed. That case is a hard error naming the reason -- to change an interface override, author the signature on the INTERFACE and re-create it (add_function_parameter on the BPI_ -> compile_blueprint -> implement_interface_function). Not idempotent: a name that does not resolve is an error. TRAP when deleting to re-create: the class is NOT regenerated here, so an immediate add_blueprint_function with the same name fails with "is an inherited overridable function (declared on <this very class>)" because the stale UFunction is still in the generated class -- put a compile_blueprint BETWEEN the two calls. Callers of the removed function are left broken until the next compile.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function graph to remove; must exist, be owned by this Blueprint and be deletable, or the call errors

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, removed_function: string, success: bool } -- success:true means the graph is gone from Blueprint->FunctionGraphs (re-read after the delete), not merely that the call ran.

commands.name: remove_component_from_blueprint
commands.description: Remove one or more component nodes from a Blueprint's SCS, with a DOUBLE CENSUS (flat AllNodes vs a walk of RootNodes) so collateral losses are reported instead of hidden: also_removed names descendants that went with their parent and unexpected_losses names nodes left in AllNodes but unreachable from any root. Batch-capable and that is the point -- chaining SINGLE-node calls on the same Blueprint is exactly the pattern that deletes components nobody asked for, so pass component_names and take ONE compile for the lot. A re-added component comes back with its CLASS defaults: per-instance overrides are gone and do not come back on save. "Nothing matched" is an ERROR here; remove_blueprint_component_node is the idempotent twin that reports already_removed instead.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name/path of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the component to remove (single form; matches the variable name or the _GEN_VARIABLE internal name)

params.name: component_names
params.description: Optional array of component names removed as ONE batch with a SINGLE compile. Chaining single-node calls is the pattern that causes collateral deletions. Merged with component_name when both are given.

params.name: promote_children
params.description: Optional bool, default true: keep descendants by re-parenting them (RemoveNodeAndPromoteChildren). Pass false for plain RemoveNode, which orphans the whole subtree.

commands.returns: { success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, removed_component, requested[], removed_components[], also_removed[], unexpected_losses[], not_found[], still_present[], node_count_before, node_count_after, reachable_before, reachable_after, orphans_before[], orphans_after[], root_nodes_before[], root_nodes_after[], root_nodes_changed, promote_children, compiled, compile_count, success, verification } }

commands.name: remove_event_dispatcher
commands.description: Remove an event dispatcher, dropping BOTH artifacts add_event_dispatcher created: the delegate member variable AND its signature graph (delete_bp_variable removes only the variable and strands the graph, which is why this exists). Idempotent -- when neither artifact is present it returns removed:false instead of erroring. Broadcast/bind nodes that referenced it are left broken: compile_blueprint + get_compile_errors after.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Name of the event dispatcher to remove (must be one this Blueprint owns; inherited ones have no local artifacts)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, removed } -- removed:false means nothing was there (no-op), not a failure.

commands.name: remove_interface
commands.description: Remove an implemented Blueprint Interface (inverse of implement_interface) and, unless preserve_functions is set, DELETE the graphs that implemented it -- work is lost, so pass preserve_functions=true to keep them as ordinary Blueprint functions. Idempotent, unlike implement_interface: an interface that is not implemented returns removed:false instead of erroring.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: interface_path
params.description: Blueprint interface asset path (or class name) to remove

params.name: preserve_functions
params.description: When true, keep the interface's function graphs as normal Blueprint functions instead of deleting them; defaults to false

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, interface, removed } -- removed:false means it was not implemented (no-op), not a failure.

commands.name: remove_unused_variables
commands.description: Delete EVERY variable the engine considers unused from a Blueprint in one shot (GatherUnusedVariables + RemoveUnusedVariables) and report which ones went. Destructive and non-selective -- "unused" means no graph node reads or writes it, so a variable only touched from C++, a DataTable, a save game or a runtime name lookup counts as unused and is deleted. Preview it by comparing get_blueprint_variables before/after, or delete a specific one with delete_bp_variable.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, removed_count: int, removed_variables?: [string] } -- removed_variables is the list gathered BEFORE the removal and removed_count what the engine reported removing; when they disagree, trust neither and re-read get_blueprint_variables.

commands.name: rename_bp_variable
commands.description: Rename a member variable DECLARED on this Blueprint, KEEPING everything the delete+re-add workaround throws away: the VarGuid, the type, the default value, the category, the tooltip and the replication flags -- and, crucially, RE-WIRING every Get/Set node that reads it, in this Blueprint and in every dependent one. This is the only correct way to rename an authored variable in place (e.g. to translate its name). WARNING: it refuses a variable that has a RepNotify function: the engine's own rename opens a MODAL dialog for that case (FSuppressableWarningDialog, which does NOT honour unattended mode) and would hang the editor waiting for a click -- clear the RepNotify with set_bp_variable_replication, rename, then set it back. WARNING: dependent Blueprints are only repaired if they are LOADED: this command loads the ones the Asset Registry reports as referencers first, and reports them in `referencers_loaded`, but an asset that references it in a way the registry does not see keeps the old name silently. It does NOT create CoreRedirects, so a saved game, a DataTable cell or a Python set_editor_property that names the variable as text is NOT fixed -- grep for those. Run compile_blueprint afterwards and save_asset on this Blueprint AND on every referencer.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path owning the variable.

params.name: old_name
params.description: Current name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint; inherited/native ones are refused.

params.name: new_name
params.description: New name. Must be a legal identifier and free across the WHOLE class chain (the engine does not check this and would happily create a duplicate). Case-only changes are allowed.

params.name: load_referencers
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Load the Blueprints the Asset Registry lists as referencers BEFORE renaming, so the engine's reference fixup reaches them; it only ever sees what is already in memory.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, old_name, new_name, renamed (re-read: true only if new_name exists and old_name is gone), referencers_loaded: [string], repnotify_cleared: bool, warning? }

commands.name: rename_function_parameter
commands.description: Rename a PARAMETER of a Blueprint function graph -- the parameter counterpart of rename_bp_variable, and the only headless way to do it: add_function_parameter only ADDS, there is no remove_function_parameter, so "delete and re-add" is not even available. It renames the pin on the Entry node and on EVERY Result node of the graph, and registers a CoreRedirect so that call sites re-map themselves. That redirect is not a nicety: it is what stops this from being a PHANTOM PIN FACTORY. With the redirect, the call site's pin takes the new name AND KEEPS ITS LITERAL VALUE; renamed WITHOUT one, the old pin stays alive and ORPHANED on the caller. WARNING: that orphan is silent: it survives compiles that report num_errors:0 -- so `compile_blueprint` is NOT the oracle here. The oracle is get_graph_nodes(compact=false) on the callers, checking that NO pin still carries the old name. The redirect matches on `Class.Function.Param`, so it reaches callers that merely CALL the function (K2Node_Message included) without implementing its interface, and dependents that are not even loaded -- both of which rename_bp_variable cannot reach. It does NOT rename anything that names the parameter as TEXT (a DataTable cell, a saved game, Python). Run compile_blueprint afterwards and save_asset on this Blueprint AND on every caller. AND THE COMPILE IS NOT THE END OF IT: what reaches the .uasset is UserDefinedPins, not the EdGraphPins you read back -- a rename checked only on the latter can report renamed:true, compile at num_errors:0, be saved and COMMITTED, and still come back as the OLD name the next time the editor starts. So it also reports entry_user_pins_after/result_user_pins_after (the serialized side, legitimately EMPTY on an interface-override graph) and refuses to claim success while any UserDefinedPin still carries the old name. The end-to-end oracle is still disk: save_asset -> reload_asset_package -> get_function_pins.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path owning the function graph.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function graph (an interface's own function graph and an interface-override graph both work).

params.name: old_name
params.description: Current parameter name, matched on the Entry node and on every Result node. A name present on only one of them is fine.

params.name: new_name
params.description: New parameter name. Must be free on the terminal nodes; a collision is refused up front via the engine's own dry-run, before anything is touched.

params.name: write_redirect
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Also PERSIST the redirect as a +PropertyRedirects line in Config/DefaultEngine.ini, so it survives a restart and reaches the other machine. With false the redirect is registered in memory only and the rename EVAPORATES for anyone who opens the project later.

params.name: load_referencers
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Load the Blueprints the Asset Registry lists as referencers BEFORE renaming, so their nodes reconstruct in this session instead of the next one.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, old_name, new_name, renamed: bool, terminals_renamed: [string], entry_pins_after: [string], result_pins_after: [string], entry_user_pins_after: [string], result_user_pins_after: [string], redirect_registered: string, redirect_persisted_to: string|null, referencers_loaded: [string], must_compile_and_save: [string], warning: string } -- the *_user_pins_after pair is the SERIALIZED side (UserDefinedPins): empty on an interface-override graph is normal, but the old name appearing there is the rename that will revert on restart.

commands.name: reparent_blueprint
commands.description: Change a Blueprint's parent class and recompile with the editor's own reparent compile flags (delta serialization + skip-new-variable-defaults, whose absence crashes the reinstancer on Blueprints holding class-typed variables). NO snapshot and NO rollback here -- reparent_blueprint_safe adds those, and even its rollback is only PARTIAL (it restores the parent but leaves SCS components RENAMED), so after ANY failed attempt restore the .uasset with git checkout BEFORE measuring again or the leftovers read as pre-existing damage. Errors when the parent is already that class.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: new_parent_class
params.description: New parent class: /Script/Module.Class, a Blueprint's generated class path (/Game/Dir/BP_X.BP_X_C), or a resolvable class name

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, old_parent, new_parent, reparented } -- reparented is set unconditionally on the success path; the real oracles are get_blueprint_parent, the component overrides (apply_component_property_overrides re-authors them) and git status of the .uasset.

commands.name: reparent_blueprint_safe
commands.description: Guarded, rollback-capable Blueprint reparent -- PREFER THIS OVER the raw reparent_blueprint, which has none of these guards. It adds: a pre-flight snapshot (parent chain, own-variable count, CDO component count); an OPTIONAL variable de-collision rename (rename_colliding_vars) for own variables whose name collides with a member the NEW parent already declares, which a plain reparent would otherwise clobber; the delta-serialization compile flags, without which a Blueprint with more than ~10 type-pinned variables CRASHES the editor during reinstancing; the same SCS-root reconciliation the Blueprint editor itself does, so a silently renamed component ("Mesh" -> "Mesh1") is reported instead of hidden; an invariant post-check (parent matches, no compile error, own-variable count did not shrink); and, on failure, an in-memory auto_rollback that restores the original parent, restores the component names and recompiles. It never saves to disk. This is a genuinely destructive multi-step transaction: run it with dry_run=true first on any real fork -- that reports the plan and the would-rename set without mutating anything.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path to reparent.

params.name: new_parent_class
params.description: New parent class name or path (native /Script, /Game/.../BP.BP_C, or a BP asset path -> its GeneratedClass).

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Optional (default false): analyze + report the plan (snapshot, would-rename vars, component collisions) without mutating.

params.name: rename_colliding_vars
params.description: Optional (default false): before reparenting, rename own NewVariables that collide by name with a member on the new parent.

params.name: auto_rollback
params.description: Optional (default true): on post-check failure, restore the original parent, restore the SCS node names and recompile.

params.name: reconcile_scene_root
params.description: Optional (default true): run the editor's own post-reparent conform pass -- ValidateSceneRootNodes + PrepareToConformSparseClassData + a second pass after the compile. Setting it FALSE disables all three; it exists only as a bisect escape hatch.

params.name: treat_component_renames_as_regression
params.description: Optional (default false): count a silently renamed SCS component as a post-check regression (which triggers auto_rollback).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, blueprint_path, old_parent, new_parent, dry_run, reparented, renamed_variables:[{from,to}], pre_variable_count, post_variable_count, pre_component_count, post_component_count, pre_scs_node_count, post_scs_node_count, scene_root_reconciled, scene_root_reconciled_post_compile, default_scene_root_removed, sparse_class_data_conform_prepared, compile_messages:[{severity,text}], compile_error_count, compile_warning_count, renamed_components:[{guid,from,to,matched_by}], removed_components:[{guid,name}], components_without_guid, colliding_components:[{name,own_class,parent_class}], child_only_components:[{name,class}], compile_status, parent_match, compile_ok, variables_intact, components_intact, post_check_ok, rolled_back, rollback_complete, rollback_restored_components:[{guid,name}] (snapshotted nodes whose name MATCHES again after the rollback), rollback_unrestored_components:[{guid,expected_name,actual_name}], rollback_compile_messages:[{severity,text}], regressions:[string], saved_to_disk (always false -- this tool never saves), persistence_note, verification, verification_checks, success }

commands.name: run_asset_action_utility
commands.description: Run (or introspect) a scripted action on an Asset/Actor Action Utility

params.name: utility_path
params.description: Object path of the utility blueprint, e.g.

params.name: function_name
params.description: CallInEditor action to run (default first action)

commands.returns: { utility_path, kind, generated_class, action_functions, function_name, function_found, invoked, note }

commands.name: run_editor_utility_widget
commands.description: Spawn and register an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint as an editor tab

params.name: widget_blueprint_path
params.description: /Game path of the Editor Utility Widget Blueprint

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_path, asset_path, tab_id, registration_name, registered, tab_exists, widget_spawned }

commands.name: set_blueprint_component_array_element
commands.description: Author ONE element of a TArray property on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (own SCS, or ICH-aware for a component inherited from an ancestor Blueprint): patch named struct members of an existing element, insert a new element at an index, or remove one. Every OTHER element is exported before and after and compared, so a whole-array rewrite that quietly loses the empty/None gaps cannot pass itself off as a targeted edit. There is deliberately NO 'move' operation.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component variable name (own or inherited)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Name of the TArray property on the component template

params.name: index
params.description: 0-based element index. set_fields/remove need an existing index; insert accepts 0..Num (Num appends)

params.name: operation
params.description: 'set_fields' (default), 'insert' or 'remove'

params.name: fields
params.description: Object of { StructMemberName: value } applied to the element. Used by set_fields, and by insert when the element type is a struct

params.name: element
params.description: Whole-element JSON value. Used by insert for NON-struct element types (or instead of 'fields' for a struct)

params.name: compile
params.description: Optional bool (default true): compile so the edited template reinstances

params.name: save
params.description: Optional bool (default true): save the Blueprint package after the compile

commands.returns: { success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, component_name, property_name, source, operation, index, inner_type, num_before, num_after, fields_applied[], field_errors[], siblings_unchanged, siblings_changed[], element_value, post_compile_num, post_compile_element, compiled, saved, save_error?, verification } }

commands.name: set_blueprint_component_collision
commands.description: Set collision on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (own SCS or inherited via ICH), not on a spawned actor, applying in this order: `profile` through SetCollisionProfileName (which expands the profile into the FBodyInstance response array -- a raw reflection write would set the string and leave BodyInstance inconsistent, and that is the whole reason this is a separate tool), then `collision_enabled`, then per-channel `responses`. Use it instead of set_blueprint_component_property for anything collision-shaped. Unknown channel, response or collision_enabled names are hard errors, never a silent default. Note the ORDER: a later profile would reset the per-channel responses, so responses always win here.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or name (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component to modify (required); must resolve to a UPrimitiveComponent or the call errors with "no collision to set"

params.name: profile
params.description: Collision profile name, e.g. "BlockAll" (optional). Applied FIRST, so it does not undo the per-channel responses below.

params.name: collision_enabled
params.description: ECollisionEnabled value name: NoCollision, QueryOnly, PhysicsOnly or QueryAndPhysics (optional). Any other string is an error.

params.name: responses
params.description: Object mapping channel -> response, e.g. {"Visibility":"Ignore","ECC_Pawn":"Overlap"} (optional). Channels accept the friendly display name or an ECC_* token (custom project channels included); responses are Ignore, Overlap or Block. An unknown channel is refused rather than defaulting to WorldStatic.

params.name: compile
params.description: Optional bool (default FALSE): compile the Blueprint afterwards so the FBodyInstance change reinstances on the next spawn/PIE. Without it the edit stays in the uncompiled template.

params.name: return_messages
params.description: No effect here: it is only read by the compile this tool may run internally, whose message log is discarded. Call compile_blueprint directly if you want the messages.

commands.returns: { success, data: { blueprint_name, component_name, source ("scs" | "inherited-ich" | "inherited-native": which template was written), profile?, collision_enabled?, responses_applied: [{channel, response}], compiled } } -- responses_applied lists ONLY the per-channel writes; profile and collision_enabled appear as their own fields only when they were given. Nothing is re-read: verify with get_blueprint_component_property or get_collision_info.

commands.name: set_blueprint_component_property
commands.description: Set the DEFAULT of a property on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE, including components INHERITED from an ancestor Blueprint (routed through this class' InheritableComponentHandler) or native inherited subobjects; only FRESH instances read the new value. THREE TRAPS, all with the same shape (a green return over a different reality): (1) it can drop an entire OTHER component from the Blueprint IN MEMORY while disk and git stay clean -- count get_blueprint_components before and after, and reload_asset_package(on_dirty="discard") is the cure; (2) on an OBJECT-REFERENCE property it can write None and report override_persisted:true, wiping the inherited default -- check with get_blueprint_component_overrides; (3) actors ALREADY PLACED in a level keep their serialized value, so only runtime-spawned ones change. Read the effective value with get_blueprint_component_property (the read-only twin, which never mints an override), and use apply_component_property_overrides for several writes at once.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component variable name (own or inherited)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property to set on the component template

params.name: property_value
params.description: New value (any JSON type; same importer as set_component_property). An array value REWRITES THE WHOLE ARRAY, including the empty/None gaps -- set_blueprint_component_array_element edits one element and proves the siblings did not move.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, property_name, component_class, source, override_persisted } -- source tells you which template was hit (scs / inherited-ich / inherited-scs / inherited-native) and override_persisted only guards the ICH case; NEITHER field re-reads the value, so they are not proof the write landed.

commands.name: set_blueprint_function_pure
commands.description: Mark a Blueprint function as PURE (or back to impure), the editor's "Pure" checkbox: a pure function has no exec pins and is re-evaluated wherever its output is read. REQUIRED to finish a UMG property binding -- FDelegateEditorBinding::IsBindingValid refuses any function that is not FUNC_BlueprintPure or const, so add_widget_property_binding will report valid:false until this has been run on the function. The counterpart reader is get_blueprint_functions_list's is_pure, which reads the same flag off the same UK2Node_FunctionEntry. WARNING: Turning a function pure REMOVES its exec pins: any existing wire into or out of them is dropped by the reconstruct, so do this BEFORE building the function's body, not after.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint owning the function.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function GRAPH (not an event; events cannot be pure).

params.name: is_pure
params.description: true to mark pure (default true), false to make it impure again.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, is_pure, was_pure, changed, function_flags } -- is_pure is RE-READ from the entry node after the compile, so it is evidence and not an echo.

commands.name: set_bp_class_replication
commands.description: Set class-level ACTOR replication on a Blueprint's CDO (bReplicates, optionally bAlwaysRelevant), compile, and read the values back off the RE-FETCHED post-compile CDO. Actor Blueprints only: a component Blueprint is refused (component replication is set_component_replication). Related reader trap: audit_replication's class_replicates reads the ACTOR flag, so it reports false for every component Blueprint whatever its CDO says.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint (must be compiled at least once).

params.name: replicates
params.description: Whether the Actor class replicates to network clients. Required.

params.name: always_relevant
params.description: Sets the Actor's bAlwaysRelevant flag; only applied when the field is present

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, replicates, always_relevant_set, always_relevant } -- values re-read from the CDO after compiling; always_relevant is only present when it was requested.

commands.name: set_bp_function_rpc
commands.description: Turn a Blueprint FUNCTION into an RPC (rpc_type Server / Client / NetMulticast, or NotReplicated to undo it, plus reliable), then compile and read the FUNC_Net* flags back off the entry node. This is the ONLY headless way to author an RPC THAT TAKES ARGUMENTS: add_function_parameter cannot reach a custom event, so build the RPC as add_blueprint_function -> compile_blueprint -> add_function_parameter -> here. Engine limits that follow: a replicated function cannot return a value and cannot host latent nodes (put a Delay in a separate, parameterless custom event).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of an existing FUNCTION graph on the Blueprint (a custom event has no entry node here and is refused).

params.name: rpc_type
params.description: One of "NotReplicated", "Server", "Client", "NetMulticast" (case-insensitive).

params.name: reliable
params.description: Mark the RPC reliable; ignored (and cleared) when rpc_type is NotReplicated; defaults to false

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, rpc_type, is_net, reliable, function_flags } -- re-read from the entry node's flags after compiling; rpc_type is the RESOLVED type, so compare it with what you asked for. Proof that the call really crosses the wire is not here: drive it in PIE and read the resulting state on the OTHER side.

commands.name: set_bp_variable_default
commands.description: Set the default value of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint: writes the live CDO and mirrors the result back into the serialized variable description so it survives save/reload. LIMIT (not a lie, a hard boundary): it CANNOT touch an INHERITED variable -- it answers "Variable 'X' is not declared on this blueprint" -- so the "child that only overrides a parent default" pattern needs the CDO route (execute_python + set_editor_property + compile_blueprint + save). And on a class with actors already placed in a level, the placed instances keep their serialized value: verify on the instances, never on the CDO.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint (inherited ones are refused)

params.name: value
params.description: New default in exported-text form, parsed into the variable's type; empty allowed. A value the type cannot parse is an error AND the previous value is restored (the engine's struct import zeroes the target before parsing, so a failed parse wipes the CDO).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, default_value, roundtrip_verified } -- default_value is re-exported from the CDO after the write, so it is the real stored value. WARNING: roundtrip_verified:false means the exported text does NOT re-import into the type (e.g. FGameplayTagContainer): the CDO holds the right value and the compiler's property copy carries it, but the serialized description was deliberately left empty because feeding an unparseable string back through a Full compile ZEROES the default. Verify that variable on the CDO after compiling, and prefer wiring it in the graph if it must survive a fresh regeneration.

commands.name: set_bp_variable_metadata
commands.description: Set the editor-facing checkboxes and text of an existing Blueprint variable: instance_editable (per-instance editability), save_game (CPF_SaveGame -- whether the variable goes into a .sav), expose_on_spawn (adds the variable as a pin on SpawnActor), category and tooltip. Only the fields present are touched; passing none is an error. This is the fix for a variable created by add_blueprint_variable, which is born NOT instance-editable while the readers report it as editable. Variable must be declared on THIS Blueprint; on a library variable the answer is a child class of your own, not this call. WARNING: this call does NOT compile: it structurally-modifies the Blueprint, which regenerates the SKELETON only, so a save_game just written is authored but NOT yet on the generated class the save archive reads -- the response says so in save_game_needs_compile, and the loop that finishes the job is compile_blueprint -> save_asset -> get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info and check save_game_generated.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint (inherited ones are refused).

params.name: instance_editable
params.description: true = editable on each placed actor. Verify by WRITING the placed instance and reading it back; the reporting field is unreliable for every variable.

params.name: save_game
params.description: true = tick "SaveGame" (CPF_SaveGame), so a SaveGame archive (ArIsSaveGame) serializes this variable; false unticks it. The only headless way to set this flag -- set_property_value, Python, set_bp_variable_replication and BlueprintEditorLibrary all refuse it. Needs a compile to reach the generated class.

params.name: expose_on_spawn
params.description: true = the variable shows up as an input pin on SpawnActorFromClass. Verify on the NODE's pins, not on get_blueprint_variables' expose_on_spawn, which reports false for variables that ARE exposed.

params.name: category
params.description: Category to group the variable under in the editor

params.name: tooltip
params.description: Tooltip text shown for the variable

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, updated, save_game?, save_game_generated?, save_game_needs_compile? } -- updated:true only means at least one field was applied, not that it persisted. The three save_game_* fields appear only when save_game was passed, and are READ BACK after the write: save_game off the variable descriptor, save_game_generated off the FProperty of the generated class.

commands.name: set_bp_variable_replication
commands.description: Set a Blueprint variable's replication mode -- None / Replicated / RepNotify (RepNotify also creates the OnRep_<Variable> function graph if missing) -- then compiles and reads CPF_Net/CPF_RepNotify back. TRAP: the full green report can come back WITHOUT the flag surviving into the generated class (a variable reported is_replicated:true that never replicates; re-running this same call fixes it). The ground truth is audit_replication (its payload's replicated_variables list), then compile and re-audit -- never this return, and never one client alone.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited/native variables are refused).

params.name: mode
params.description: One of "None", "Replicated", "RepNotify" (case-insensitive). "None" also clears the RepNotify function and resets the lifetime condition.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, mode, is_replicated, is_rep_notify, rep_notify_func, property_flags } -- read back from the variable's flags after compiling, which is necessary but NOT sufficient (see the trap above).

commands.name: set_component_replication
commands.description: Set bReplicates on ONE SCS component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (the archetype, not a spawned actor's instance), compile, and read it back off the template. It governs the component's own PROPERTY replication; note that a component declared in the SCS already routes its RPCs through its stable network name WITHOUT this flag (a component added at RUNTIME does not, and loses them). For the owning actor use set_bp_class_replication.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: component_name
params.description: SCS component variable name on this Blueprint (inherited-only components have no local SCS node and are not found).

params.name: replicates
params.description: Whether the component should replicate. Required.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, replicates } -- replicates is re-read from the template after compiling.

commands.name: set_event_dispatcher_signature
commands.description: Add to (mode="add", the idempotent default) or rewrite (mode="replace") the parameter list of a dispatcher this Blueprint OWNS -- inherited dispatchers have no local signature graph and are refused with the list of owned ones. Every requested type is resolved BEFORE anything is mutated, so a bad type aborts cleanly. The parameters become the OUTPUT pins of every bound handler and the INPUT pins of add_broadcast_node; existing nodes keep stale pins until compile_blueprint reconstructs them.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path that OWNS the dispatcher (inherited dispatchers cannot be edited here).

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Name of an existing event dispatcher (created by add_event_dispatcher or the editor).

params.name: params
params.description: Array of parameter specs to add: [ { name: string, type: string } ]. Dispatcher params are input-only; 'type' accepts the same strings as add_function_parameter (bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, Array<T>, an object/class/struct/enum name or path).

params.name: mode
params.description: "add" (default, idempotent: skip a param whose name already exists) or "replace" (clear the existing signature first, then add the given params).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, mode, added: [string], params: [ { name, type } ], param_count }

commands.name: set_mesh_material_color
commands.description: Tint one material slot of a Blueprint component template by creating a DYNAMIC material instance (MID) over the current or given material, setting one vector parameter, and assigning the MID to the slot. A MID is a RUNTIME object, so this is a quick preview, NOT the way to author a change that must survive save/reload -- for a persistent tint make a MaterialInstanceConstant and assign it with apply_material_to_blueprint. A parameter_name the material does not declare is accepted silently and simply does nothing.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; must be a UPrimitiveComponent

params.name: color
params.description: RGBA color [R, G, B, A] as floats, each clamped to 0.0-1.0; exactly 4 values are required

params.name: material_slot
params.description: Optional slot index; defaults to 0

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Optional vector parameter name; defaults to "BaseColor". A name the material does not declare is NOT reported as an error -- it just has no visible effect.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Optional material asset path to use as the MID's parent; without it the component's current slot material is used, falling back to /Engine/BasicShapes/BasicShapeMaterial

commands.returns: { component: string, material_slot: int, parameter_name: string, color: [number, number, number, number], success: bool } -- success:true only means the MID was created and assigned; re-read with get_blueprint_material_info after a save/reload to see whether anything persisted.

commands.name: set_physics_properties
commands.description: Set simulate-physics, mass override, linear and angular damping on ONE primitive component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node only -- inherited components are not found here, and it is the template, not a placed actor). Only the fields present are touched. It does NOT compile and does NOT save. For any other property of a component template use set_blueprint_component_property, which is ICH-aware and reaches inherited components.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; must resolve to a UPrimitiveComponent or the call errors

params.name: simulate_physics
params.description: Optional bool to toggle physics simulation

params.name: mass
params.description: Optional mass override in kg (applied as SetMassOverrideInKg, not a scale)

params.name: linear_damping
params.description: Optional linear damping coefficient

params.name: angular_damping
params.description: Optional angular damping coefficient

commands.returns: { component: string } -- just the component name back. NOTHING is read back, so verify with get_blueprint_component_property on each property you set.

commands.name: set_pin_default_value
commands.description: Write the literal default of an UNCONNECTED input pin and return the value read BACK off the pin. Struct pins are canonicalized: a bare GameplayTag name becomes (TagName="X") and an UNREGISTERED tag is rejected up front instead of silently landing as an empty tag; value_json nativizes any struct (and is the only way to put SEVERAL tags in a GameplayTagContainer). Array/set/map pins are refused (use a MakeArray/MakeSet/MakeMap node) and so are pins currently split into sub-pins (recombine_blueprint_pin first). A plain string is fine for an FText pin. TRAP: on a FormatText "Format" pin the literal IS written but the {argument} pins are NOT created, leaving a valid, useless node -- build the string with Concat_StrStr / Conv_StringToText instead.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Pin name; an INPUT pin of that name is preferred, any pin with the name is the fallback

params.name: value
params.description: Literal default in the pin's exported-text form; empty string allowed (clears it). For a struct pin, "()" clears and a leading "(" is passed through untouched.

params.name: value_json
params.description: Optional JSON object nativized into the struct's export-text form, for STRUCT pins only. For an FGameplayTagContainer it must carry a "GameplayTags" array (["A","B"] or [{"TagName":"A"}]) and every tag is validated; takes precedence over 'value'.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { node_id, pin_name, default_value } -- default_value is re-read from the pin AFTER the write, so it is the oracle for what actually landed (a rejected value shows up as the old one).

commands.name: set_property_access_path
commands.description: Rewrite a UK2Node_PropertyAccess node's binding Path and reconstruct the node so the leaf property re-resolves and the Value pin re-types, then return the path READ BACK -- so resolved:true is real evidence the new binding points at something. It does NOT recompile: follow with compile_blueprint + get_compile_errors. reconstructed:false means the PropertyAccessEditor feature was unavailable: the path WAS written but text_path/resolved_pin stay stale until the graph reopens.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path (usually an Animation Blueprint).

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the property-access node; any other node class is refused by name.

params.name: path
params.description: The new path: either an array of segment strings (["InAnimInstance","Foo"]) OR a dotted string ("InAnimInstance.Foo"). An empty result is an error, never a cleared binding.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

commands.returns: { node_id, graph_name, reconstructed, path:[string], text_path, resolved, resolved_pin, note? } -- path/text_path/resolved are re-read AFTER the reconstruct, so they are the oracle rather than an echo.

commands.name: set_replication_condition
commands.description: Set the ELifetimeCondition (COND_OwnerOnly, COND_SkipOwner, COND_InitialOnly...) that decides WHICH clients get a replicated variable, then compile. It is the second half of set_bp_variable_replication, which decides WHETHER it replicates at all: on a variable that is not Replicated/RepNotify the condition is stored and completely INERT, and the response says so through is_replicated:false plus a "note". Blueprint-declared variables only.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited ones are refused).

params.name: condition
params.description: ELifetimeCondition name, with or without the COND_ prefix (e.g. "OwnerOnly" or "COND_OwnerOnly"); an unknown name is an error.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, condition, is_replicated, note? } -- condition is the canonical COND_ name that was stored; is_replicated:false means the setting has no effect yet.

commands.name: set_static_mesh_properties
commands.description: Assign a static mesh asset and/or a slot-0 material to a mesh component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node, not a placed actor), in one call. Does NOT compile and does NOT save. Use apply_material_to_blueprint when only a material is changing or the slot is not 0, and get_blueprint_material_info to read the resulting slots back.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS mesh component

params.name: static_mesh
params.description: Optional asset path of the UStaticMesh to assign

params.name: material
params.description: Optional asset path of the UMaterialInterface for slot 0

commands.returns: { component: string } -- name only, no verification: read the result with get_blueprint_material_info / get_blueprint_component_property.

commands.name: spawn_blueprint_actor
commands.description: Spawn an instance of a Blueprint class as an actor and report WHICH world took it and whether the actor has AUTHORITY. The default (world absent or 'editor') places it in the EDITOR level, not in play. For anything that must exist for every player during PIE use world='server'; world='pie' is ambiguous and can land on the CLIENT, where the actor has no authority, no AI controller and no server-side existence while looking identical in the payload. The actor is NOT saved into the map: save_level afterwards for an editor-world spawn.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label applied to the spawned actor (SetActorLabel); it is not the object name and is not made unique

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) spawns into the editor level | 'server' spawns into the PIE world WITH AUTHORITY (what you want for anything that must exist for every player: an actor spawned into the client world has no authority and no server-side existence) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context -- can land on the CLIENT) | 'game' (alias of 'pie')

commands.returns: { actor JSON via DescribeActorObject, world: string, has_authority: bool (AActor::HasAuthority() read off the spawned actor), local_role: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: split_blueprint_pin
commands.description: Split a struct-typed pin (Vector, Rotator, Transform...) into its scalar sub-pins and return their names, so each component can be wired or defaulted on its own instead of writing the whole struct literal. Refused when the schema says the pin is not splittable. Note the interaction: set_pin_default_value REFUSES a pin that is currently split -- recombine_blueprint_pin first if you want to write the struct as one value.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin.

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Name of the struct pin to split (either direction).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { split, sub_pins:[string] } -- sub_pins are the names to pass to connect_pins / set_pin_default_value from now on (e.g. "NewLocation_X").

commands.name: validate_pin_connection
commands.description: Dry-run the K2 schema's verdict on a pin pair WITHOUT touching the graph: returns valid plus the schema's own message (which names the incompatible types) and its raw response code. connect_pins runs the same check and then connects, so use this one to test a plan before committing a build_blueprint_graph batch whose rollback can be refused, or to find out WHY a connection was rejected without leaving anything behind.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: source_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the source node.

params.name: source_pin
params.description: Output pin name on the source node (falls back to any pin with that name).

params.name: target_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target node; must be in the same graph as the source.

params.name: target_pin
params.description: Input pin name on the target node (falls back to any pin with that name).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { valid, message, response_code } -- valid is false only for an outright DISALLOW; a response that would connect WITH a conversion node or by breaking an existing link still reports valid:true, and "message" is where that shows.

commands.name: add_camera_component
commands.description: Add a UCameraComponent to an actor placed in the editor world, found by name or label, optionally attaching it to a SpringArm (or any other USceneComponent) on the same actor; if the actor already has a camera component, that first one is configured instead, whatever its name, overwriting only the fields you pass. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved. post_process_settings takes FPostProcessSettings property names, and each value it sets also turns on its bOverride_ flag so that it takes effect. An invalid projection_mode or a rejected post_process_settings (a key that names no property included) is an error and nothing is created or written.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the target actor.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional name for a new component (defaults to "Camera"); a name another object of the actor already has gets a unique variant, returned in component_name. Ignored when the actor already has a camera component, which is configured whatever its name.

params.name: parent_component
params.description: Optional name of a USceneComponent on the same actor to attach to (e.g. "SpringArm"). Default = actor root component.

params.name: field_of_view
params.description: Optional float. Horizontal FOV in degrees (1..170).

params.name: aspect_ratio
params.description: Optional float. Aspect ratio (e.g. 16/9). 0 = auto.

params.name: ortho_width
params.description: Optional float. Orthographic width (only used when projection_mode = "Orthographic").

params.name: projection_mode
params.description: Optional string. "Perspective" or "Orthographic".

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] relative location vs parent.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] relative rotation vs parent.

params.name: b_use_controller_view_rotation
params.description: Optional bool. Match pawn control rotation.

params.name: b_use_pawn_control_rotation
params.description: Optional bool. Alias for b_use_controller_view_rotation — sets UCameraComponent::bUsePawnControlRotation.

params.name: b_lock_to_hmd
params.description: Optional bool. Lock orientation to the HMD.

params.name: post_process_settings
params.description: Optional object of FPostProcessSettings fields by property name, e.g. {"BloomIntensity": 2}; each value also turns on its bOverride_ companion unless the object sets that companion itself; a key that names no property is an error.

params.name: post_process_blend_weight
params.description: Optional float. Weight of post-process (0..1). 0 means post-process disabled.

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, parent_component, already_existed, applied_count, field_of_view, aspect_ratio, projection_mode, location: [x,y,z], rotation: [pitch,yaw,roll], post_process_blend_weight }

commands.name: add_camera_node_child
commands.description: Populates the Children of a composite rig node (the rig RootNode must be a UArrayCameraNode ("Sequence"); set it via set_camera_rig_root_node node_type=ArrayCameraNode). Creates a new UCameraNode of child_node_type outered to the rig and appends it, in one undo step, then saves the rig. Idempotent via optional index: index<Children.Num() REPLACES that slot instead of appending. added is the read-back of the new child in its slot; a failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory. Gameplay Camera System is EXPERIMENTAL (plugin GameplayCameras).

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset whose composite RootNode is edited (required)

params.name: child_node_type
params.description: A concrete UCameraNode subclass name for the new child, e.g. "OffsetCameraNode", "FieldOfViewCameraNode" (required)

params.name: index
params.description: Optional child slot. If given and < current child count, REPLACES that slot (deterministic re-runs); otherwise appends.

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, child_node_type, child_class, child_index, children_count, added, replaced, saved, save_error }

commands.name: add_gameplay_camera_component
commands.description: Adds a UGameplayCameraComponent to an actor and points it at a UCameraAsset. Idempotent. Note: activation needs a running game/PIE and is out of scope here.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor (required)

params.name: camera_asset_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraAsset to reference (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, already_existed, camera_asset_path, camera_set }

commands.name: add_spring_arm
commands.description: Add a USpringArmComponent (camera boom) to an actor placed in the editor world, found by name or label; if the actor already has a spring arm, that first one is configured instead, whatever its name, overwriting only the fields you pass. A new arm becomes an instance component attached to the root. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved. Negative lengths, sizes and speeds clamp to 0; an unknown probe_channel is an error and nothing is created or written. Attach a camera with add_camera_component (parent_component = the returned component_name); for a Blueprint asset use add_component_to_blueprint.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the target actor in the editor world.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional name for a new component (defaults to "SpringArm"); a name another object of the actor already has gets a unique variant, returned in component_name. Ignored when the actor already has a spring arm, which is configured whatever its name.

params.name: target_arm_length
params.description: Optional float. Natural length of the spring arm (uu). Default 300.

params.name: socket_offset
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] relative offset applied at the spring-arm tip.

params.name: target_offset
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world-space offset applied at the start of the spring.

params.name: probe_size
params.description: Optional float. Collision probe radius.

params.name: probe_channel
