params.description: Optional string name of ECollisionChannel (e.g. "Camera", "Visibility"). Default "Camera".

params.name: b_do_collision_test
params.description: Optional bool. Enable camera collision probe.

params.name: b_use_pawn_control_rotation
params.description: Optional bool. Use the parent pawn's view rotation.

params.name: b_inherit_pitch
params.description: Optional bool. Inherit pitch from parent.

params.name: b_inherit_yaw
params.description: Optional bool. Inherit yaw from parent.

params.name: b_inherit_roll
params.description: Optional bool. Inherit roll from parent.

params.name: b_enable_camera_lag
params.description: Optional bool. Enable positional lag.

params.name: b_enable_camera_rotation_lag
params.description: Optional bool. Enable rotational lag.

params.name: camera_lag_speed
params.description: Optional float. Positional lag speed (units/sec).

params.name: camera_rotation_lag_speed
params.description: Optional float. Rotational lag speed (deg/sec).

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, already_existed, applied_count, target_arm_length, socket_offset: [x,y,z], target_offset: [x,y,z], probe_size, probe_channel, b_do_collision_test, b_use_pawn_control_rotation, b_inherit_pitch, b_inherit_yaw, b_inherit_roll, b_enable_camera_lag, b_enable_camera_rotation_lag, camera_lag_speed, camera_rotation_lag_speed }

commands.name: build_camera_rig
commands.description: Builds a UCameraRigAsset (UCameraRigAsset::BuildCameraRig) and reports the resulting build status.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset (required)

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, built, build_status }

commands.name: create_camera
commands.description: Spawn a new ACameraActor in the editor world (never in PIE) at an optional location and rotation, with camera_name as its outliner label. Labels need not be unique, so address the camera later by the returned actor_name. Each location axis must be within +-100000, otherwise an error. The level is marked dirty, not saved. location_set, rotation_set and label_set compare what the spawned actor reports with the request. Move or re-aim it with set_camera_transform; spawn_actor places a CameraActor in PIE too; add_camera_component puts a camera on an existing actor.

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Name to assign to the new camera actor.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location for the new camera (defaults to origin)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] world rotation for the new camera (defaults to zero)

commands.returns: { camera_name: string, camera_created: bool, actor_name: string, location_set: bool, rotation_set: bool, label_set: bool, actual_label: string, actual_location: [number, number, number] }

commands.name: create_camera_asset
commands.description: Create a UCameraAsset (Gameplay Camera System, Experimental plugin) at package_path/name and save it; one already there is returned unchanged (already_existed:true), another asset class there is an error. Returns asset_path and saved. Next: set_camera_asset_director, then add_gameplay_camera_component.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the UCameraAsset to create, e.g. "CA_Player"; also the last segment of its path

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content folder (default "/Game/Cameras")

commands.returns: { name, asset_path, asset_class, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_camera_rig_asset
commands.description: Creates a UCameraRigAsset (Gameplay Camera System, Experimental). Idempotent (returns the existing asset).

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (required)

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content folder (default "/Game/Cameras")

commands.returns: { name, asset_path, asset_class, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_camera_rig_crane
commands.description: Spawn an unrotated CameraRig_Crane actor in the editor world with the given pitch, yaw and arm length; it is always labelled "CameraRigCrane_MCP", so address it later by the returned internal_name. Returns location and the read-back crane values; the level is not saved.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin; each axis within -100000 to 100000)

params.name: crane_pitch
params.description: Crane pitch angle in degrees (optional, default 0)

params.name: crane_yaw
params.description: Crane yaw angle in degrees (optional, default 0)

params.name: arm_length
params.description: Crane arm length (optional, default 500.0, valid 0-100000)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, internal_name: string, location: [number, number, number], crane_pitch: number, crane_yaw: number, arm_length: number, success: bool }

commands.name: create_camera_rig_rail
commands.description: Spawn an unrotated CameraRig_Rail actor in the editor world; with more than 2 points the rail is rebuilt as a straight 500-unit line along local X. Always labelled "CameraRigRail_MCP", so address it by the returned internal_name, e.g. in set_camera_rig_rail_position. Not saved.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin; each axis within -100000 to 100000)

params.name: num_spline_points
params.description: Number of spline points on the rail (optional, default 2, valid 2-100)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, internal_name: string, location: [number, number, number], num_spline_points: number, success: bool }

commands.name: create_camera_shake_blueprint
commands.description: Create a Blueprint asset parented to UCameraShakeBase, compile and save it.  UCameraShakeBase is abstract but Blueprintable; the generated Blueprint subclass is concrete. Idempotent: if the asset already exists it is loaded and returned.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. BP_ExplosionShake)

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/Blueprints")

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_camera_shake: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: get_camera_asset_info
commands.description: Reports a UCameraAsset's director and, for a SingleCameraDirector, the rig it runs. Read-only.

params.name: camera_asset_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraAsset (required)

commands.returns: { camera_asset_path, has_director, director_class, camera_rig_path }

commands.name: get_camera_fov
commands.description: Retrieve the current field of view (FOV) of a camera.

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Name of the camera to query (matches actor name or label).

commands.returns: { camera_name: string, fov: number }

commands.name: get_camera_post_process
commands.description: Read the overridden PostProcessSettings off a camera actor's camera component: only the fields whose bOverride_* companion is on are returned (those actually contributing). Mirrors set_camera_post_process's field set. Pure reader.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the camera actor to query.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, post_process_blend_weight: number, overridden_count: int, settings: object (overridden field -> value; scalars as numbers, wheels as [R,G,B,master], scene_color_tint as [R,G,B,A]) }

commands.name: get_camera_rig_nodes
commands.description: Reports a camera rig's RootNode class and its camera-parameter fields (name + value), plus, for a composite ArrayCameraNode root, its Children (index + class). Read-only.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset (required)

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, has_root_node, root_node_class, parameters:[{name, value}], children:[{index, class}] }

commands.name: get_camera_transform
commands.description: Read the world location and rotation of a camera actor (ACameraActor or CineCameraActor) in the editor world, found by object name or label (case-insensitive, first match). Returns location [X, Y, Z] and rotation [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] in degrees; set_camera_transform is the writer.

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Name of the camera to query (matches actor name or label).

commands.returns: { camera_name: string, location: [number, number, number], rotation: [number, number, number] }

commands.name: get_cameras
commands.description: List all camera actors in the editor world with their transform and FOV.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum number of cameras to return (optional, default 1000, valid 1-10000)

commands.returns: { cameras: [{ name: string, label: string, is_valid: bool, location: [number, number, number], rotation: [number, number, number], fov: number? }], total_count: number, max_results: number, truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_cine_camera_settings
commands.description: Read the full cine-camera configuration off a CineCameraActor's CineCameraComponent: filmback (sensor size/offsets/aspect + preset), lens (focal/f-stop range, squeeze, blades, preset), focus (method/manual distance/offset/smoothing) and the current focal length / aperture / focus distance. Pure reader; mutates nothing.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the CineCameraActor to query.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, filmback: { sensor_width, sensor_height, sensor_horizontal_offset, sensor_vertical_offset, sensor_aspect_ratio, preset_name }, lens: { min_focal_length, max_focal_length, min_fstop, max_fstop, minimum_focus_distance, squeeze_factor, diaphragm_blade_count, preset_name }, focus: { method, manual_focus_distance, focus_offset, smooth_focus_changes, focus_smoothing_interp_speed }, current_focal_length, current_aperture, current_focus_distance, horizontal_fov, vertical_fov, note }

commands.name: list_camera_node_types
commands.description: Lists all concrete UCameraNode subclasses usable in a camera rig. Read-only reflection (GetDerivedClasses).
commands.returns: { base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }

commands.name: set_camera_asset_director
commands.description: Wires a new USingleCameraDirector on a UCameraAsset, pointing it at a UCameraRigAsset (the "one rig" director) and replacing any director it had, then saves the asset. One undo step. director_set is the GetCameraDirector read-back; a failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory.

params.name: camera_asset_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraAsset (required)

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset the director runs (required)

commands.returns: { camera_asset_path, camera_rig_path, director_class, director_set, saved, save_error }

commands.name: set_camera_fov
commands.description: Set the field of view (degrees, above 0 up to 180) of the camera component of an ACameraActor or CineCameraActor in the editor world, found by object name or label. No undo transaction and nothing is saved. Returns previous_fov, actual_fov and fov_set; get_camera_fov reads it.

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Name of the camera to modify (matches actor name or label).

params.name: fov
params.description: Field of view in degrees. Must be between 0.0 and 180.0.

commands.returns: { camera_name: string, requested_fov: number, previous_fov: number, actual_fov: number, fov_set: bool, camera_valid: bool }

commands.name: set_camera_node_parameters
commands.description: Sets parameters on a camera rig's RootNode by reflection, all or nothing: every property is parsed first, and an unknown property or a value that does not fit fails the call, naming each one in failed, with nothing written or saved. FXxxCameraParameter props take the raw value, a bool or a number (a whole one for an integer), written to the nested .Value; other props set directly. Otherwise all of them are written in one undo step and the rig is saved; applied reads the stored values back. Values the root node already holds are a success with changed false, saved false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset whose RootNode is edited (required)

params.name: properties
params.description: JSON object { PropertyName: value, ... } (e.g. {"FieldOfView": 90})

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, node_class, changed, set:[name], failed:[{name, error}], applied:{name: stored_value_text}, saved, save_error, note }

commands.name: set_camera_post_process

params.name: bloom_threshold

params.name: vignette_intensity

params.name: film_grain_intensity
params.description: Optional film grain intensity 0..1 (number).

params.name: exposure_bias

params.name: exposure_min_brightness
params.description: Optional auto-exposure minimum brightness (number).

params.name: exposure_max_brightness
params.description: Optional auto-exposure maximum brightness (number).

params.name: exposure_speed_up
params.description: Optional auto-exposure adaptation speed up (number).

params.name: exposure_speed_down
params.description: Optional auto-exposure adaptation speed down (number).

params.name: ambient_occlusion_intensity
params.description: Optional ambient occlusion intensity 0..1 (number).

params.name: ambient_occlusion_radius
params.description: Optional ambient occlusion radius (number).

params.name: color_saturation
params.description: Optional color saturation wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_contrast
params.description: Optional color contrast wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_gamma
params.description: Optional color gamma wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_gain
params.description: Optional color gain wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_offset

params.name: scene_color_tint
params.description: Optional scene color tint [R,G,B,A] (array).

params.name: white_temp
params.description: Optional white balance temperature (number).

params.name: white_tint
params.description: Optional white balance tint (number).

params.name: depth_of_field_fstop
params.description: Optional depth-of-field f-stop (number).

params.name: depth_of_field_focal_distance
params.description: Optional depth-of-field focal distance in cm (number).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, applied_count: int, applied: object (field -> value read back), post_process_blend_weight: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_camera_rig_rail_position
commands.description: Set the camera position along a CameraRig_Rail (0.0 = start, 1.0 = end).

params.name: rig_actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the CameraRig_Rail actor.

params.name: position
params.description: Normalised position on the rail, 0.0 to 1.0.

commands.returns: { rig_actor_name: string, position: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_camera_rig_root_node
commands.description: Replace the RootNode of a Gameplay Cameras UCameraRigAsset with a new, default-valued node of node_type; the previous root and everything under it (children, parameter values) is dropped. Runs in an undo transaction and saves the rig; a failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory. Does not build the rig (build_camera_rig does). Valid node_type names come from list_camera_node_types; configure the new root with set_camera_node_parameters, give an ArrayCameraNode root children with add_camera_node_child, and read it back with get_camera_rig_nodes.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset (required)

params.name: node_type
params.description: A concrete UCameraNode subclass name, e.g. "FieldOfViewCameraNode", "OffsetCameraNode", "ArrayCameraNode" (required)

commands.name: add_chooser_column_to_table
commands.description: Add a column of column_type, its input left unbound, to a UChooserTable asset as one undo step, then compile and save the table; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. Each call adds a new column, even of a type the table already has, except Randomize: a table holds at most one, so an existing Randomize column is returned with already_existed=true and nothing changes. The column goes where the Chooser editor puts it: a filter column before the first output or Randomize column, so filters stay ahead of them; an output column at the end but before a trailing Randomize column; a Randomize column last. The columns after it move up one index; column_index is where the new column went. The new column gets one cell, its DefaultRowValue, per row already in the table, so columns and rows stay in step whichever is added first. Besides the types listed under column_type it accepts OutputFloat, OutputBool, OutputName, OutputEnum, ObjectClass, Name, MultiEnum and Randomize.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: column_type
params.description: Column struct to add: "FloatRange", "Bool", "Enum", "Object", or "OutputObject".

params.name: column_name
params.description: Label echoed back in the reply only; it is not stored on the column.

commands.returns: { table_path: string, column_index: int, column_name: string, column_type: string, already_existed: bool, row_count?: int, saved?: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_chooser_row
commands.description: Add one implicit row to a UChooserTable. Grows every column's RowValues by one (using each column's DefaultRowValue where available) and grows ResultsStructs by one, as one undo step, then compiles and saves the table; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

commands.returns: { table_path: string, row_index: int, row_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_chooser_table
commands.description: Create (or load if it already exists) a UChooserTable asset under the given package path. A new table is compiled and saved. On an existing table only the result_type and output_object_class the call gives are applied, as one undo step, and the table is compiled and saved only when that changes it (saved false otherwise). success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. An unknown result_type, or an output_object_class that does not load as a UClass, is an error checked before the asset is created or loaded.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset short name (e.g. "MyChooser"); becomes the package short name.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Long package root (default "/Game/MCP"); full asset path = <package_path>/<name>.

params.name: result_type
params.description: EObjectChooserResultType: "Object" (default), "Class", or "NoPrimaryResult".

params.name: output_object_class
params.description: UClass path used as OutputObjectType (default UObject), loaded via LoadObject<UClass>; a path that does not load is an error.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, already_existed: bool, result_type: string, output_object_class: string|null, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: delete_chooser_table
commands.description: Destroy a UChooserTable asset at a /Game path (mirror of create_chooser_table). Typed-delete: it loads the asset and REFUSES to delete it if it is not a UChooserTable, so it cannot wipe the wrong asset the way the generic delete_asset can; that refusal, and a delete the engine does not carry out, make success false with deleted false. Idempotent on missing assets.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full /Game/.../Chooser asset path.

commands.returns: { table_path, deleted, already_existed, asset_class?, note? }

commands.name: evaluate_chooser_table
commands.description: Actually RUN a UChooserTable and get the SINGLE chosen result -- the way to test a chooser you just authored without opening the editor. Headless-safe: it is a pure runtime API, so it needs no PIE and no render. Pass context_object_path (any UObject in the editor world) to seed the evaluation context. A table with no columns, or one where no context property matches, falls through to the table's FallbackResult (reported as fallback_used); a table that matches nothing and has no fallback returns null. Use evaluate_chooser_table_multi when you want EVERY matching result instead of the first.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: context_object_path
params.description: Optional UObject path used to seed the evaluation context.

params.name: object_class
params.description: Optional UClass path for the expected result type (default = /Script/Engine.Object).

commands.returns: { table_path, evaluated, result_object_path, result_object_class, fallback_used, note? }

commands.name: evaluate_chooser_table_multi
commands.description: Actually RUN a UChooserTable and get EVERY matching result, not just the first: the multi-result mirror of evaluate_chooser_table, which is what you want when the chooser is meant to select a set. Headless-safe pure runtime API -- no PIE, no render. object_class defaults to /Script/CoreUObject.Object and is never null, since results are post-filtered with IsA; null entries the engine interleaves in its array are skipped, so result_count is the count of REAL results.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: context_object_path
params.description: Optional UObject path used to seed the evaluation context.

params.name: object_class
params.description: Optional UClass path for the expected result type (default = /Script/CoreUObject.Object).

commands.returns: { table_path, evaluated, result_count, results: [{ result_object_path, result_object_class }], fallback_used, column_count }

commands.name: get_chooser_column_values
commands.description: Read ONE COLUMN ACROSS ALL ROWS of a UChooserTable, plus that column's DefaultRowValue -- the column-wise counterpart of get_chooser_row_values (one row across all columns), with the same typed cell shapes. The per-column default is EDITOR-ONLY: outside an editor build it comes back null with a note, while the row values themselves always resolve. column_index out of range is an honest error. Read-only: no compile, no save.

commands.name: get_chooser_row_values
commands.description: Read ONE ROW ACROSS ALL COLUMNS of a UChooserTable, as typed cells -- the row-wise counterpart of get_chooser_column_values (one column across all rows) and finer-grained than inspect_chooser_table. Cell shapes by column type: FloatRange {min,max,b_no_min,b_no_max}; Bool {cell_value}; Enum {comparison,value}; Object {comparison,asset_path}; OutputObject {asset_path}. row_index out of range is an honest error. Read-only -- no compile, no save -- and it works headless, since row data is not editor-only.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: row_index
params.description: 0-based row index to read across all columns.

commands.returns: { table_path, row_index, row_count, cells: [{ column_index, column_type, <typed fields> }] }

commands.name: remove_chooser_column
commands.description: Remove a column from a UChooserTable by index (inverse of add_chooser_column_to_table). The column's per-row cells go with it -- a column owns its own RowValues, so nothing needs re-syncing across the other columns and the row COUNT is unchanged (use remove_chooser_row for that). The removal is one undo step; the table is then compiled and saved, and success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. A table with no columns is left as it is (note, saved false). Omit column_index (or pass -1) to remove the LAST column, matching remove_chooser_row's default.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: column_index
params.description: Optional 0-based column index (default -1 = last column).

commands.returns: { table_path, removed_column_index, previous_column_count, new_column_count, column_type, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: remove_chooser_row
commands.description: Remove one implicit row from a UChooserTable (inverse of add_chooser_row). A chooser row is not a real object: this shrinks EVERY column's RowValues array by one -- at row_index if given, else the last row -- and shrinks ResultsStructs to match, as one undo step, then compiles and saves the table like add_chooser_row; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. A table with no rows is left as it is (note, saved false). Use remove_chooser_column to drop a column instead.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: row_index
params.description: Optional 0-based row index to remove (default: last row).

commands.returns: { table_path, removed_row_index, previous_row_count, new_row_count, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: set_chooser_column_default
commands.description: Set the DefaultRowValue of one UChooserTable column, the cell value rows appended by add_chooser_row inherit; set it before adding rows. The fields that apply depend on the column type (see the params); others are ignored. A change is one undo step and is compiled and saved, and success is false, with save_error, when the save fails; a value the column already holds changes nothing (already_existed true, saved false).

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: column_index
params.description: 0-based column index to update.

params.name: min
params.description: FloatRange column: default lower bound of the row's float range.

params.name: max
params.description: FloatRange column: default upper bound of the row's float range.

params.name: b_no_min
params.description: FloatRange column: when true, disables the lower bound (row matches any value <= max).

params.name: b_no_max
params.description: FloatRange column: when true, disables the upper bound (row matches any value >= min).

params.name: default_value
params.description: Bool column: "MatchFalse", "MatchTrue" or "MatchAny"; OutputFloat: a number; OutputBool: a bool; OutputName: a name string; Randomize: a probability weight. Ignored by other column types.

params.name: comparison
params.description: Enum and Name columns: "MatchEqual", "MatchNotEqual", "MatchAny" or "Modulus"; ObjectClass column: "Equal", "NotEqual", "SubClassOf" (default), "NotSubClassOf" or "Any". Case-insensitive.

params.name: value
params.description: Enum and OutputEnum columns: enum ordinal (clamped to 0-255); Name column: the name string to compare; MultiEnum column: the bitmask as an integer.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object/OutputObject column: long package path of the UObject bound as the default row value.

params.name: class_path
params.description: ObjectClass column: path of the UClass to match (e.g. "/Script/Engine.Pawn" or "/Game/BP_Enemy.BP_Enemy_C"), used with comparison (default SubClassOf).

commands.returns: { table_path, column_index, column_type, default_value?, asset_path?, comparison?, already_existed, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_chooser_row_outcome
commands.description: Set the FAssetChooser outcome (UObject reference) for a specific row in a UChooserTable, as one undo step, then compile and save the table; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. params.name: table_path

commands.name: diff_project_config
commands.description: Diff THIS project's Config/Default*.ini against ANOTHER project's, aligned by section+key (pure file read via FConfigFile::Read; no world, no editor state). Surfaces settings that differ or failed to migrate: custom collision channels (GameTraceChannel/ObjectChannel under [/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile]), input mappings, enabled plugins ([Plugins]/[/Script/...]), and every other key. Perspective is THIS -> OTHER: 'added' = present in OTHER but not THIS; 'removed' = present in THIS but not OTHER; 'changed' = present in both with different value(s). Multi-value keys (array-of-struct like +Channels/+ActionMappings) are compared as sorted value lists so hash-ordering never yields a false diff.

commands.name: rerun_construction_scripts
commands.description: Run AActor::RerunConstructionScripts() on a level actor: destroys every construction-script-generated component and rebuilds it, exactly as dragging the actor in the editor would. This is the ONLY way to reach that function from MCP -- it is ENGINE_API and public but NOT a UFUNCTION, so reflection, call_function and execute_python cannot see it. Use it to find out what a property edit really survives, or to re-apply a Blueprint's construction logic after editing the instance. Reports the before/after component sets instead of a bare success.

commands.name: set_component_property
commands.description: Set the value of any property on a level actor's component via the canonical JSON->property importer (mcp_common::SetObjectProperty). Handles every FProperty kind: object/soft-object/class/soft-class refs (by "/Game/..." path string), enums (by name), FGameplayTag/FGameplayTagContainer (registry-validated), nested structs, arrays, sets and maps -- not just scalars, FVector, FRotator and FLinearColor. WARNING: it writes the EDITOR world BY DEFAULT even while PIE is running, and that is deliberate, not a bug: it is the only MCP route to a property Python's set_editor_property refuses (CPF_DisableEditOnInstance), and because the edit lands in the editor instance the NEXT PIE session already starts with it. The flip side is that a value written mid-PIE does NOT reach the running actor -- so to hit the live one you must ask for it: world='server' | 'client' | 'pie:N'. The reply stamps world_name/world_package/world_type/net_mode/pie_instance, so success:true says WHICH world was written (world_package is the field carrying the UEDPIE_N prefix -- in a World Partition map the UWorld keeps the map's own name).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name of the actor containing the component. Matched against the actor's OBJECT name (GetName) only -- not its editor label.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the component

params.name: property_name
params.description: Name of the property to set

params.name: property_value
params.description: New value. Any JSON type: a bare string (e.g. "/Game/Foo.Foo" object path, "Movable" enum name, "A.B.C" gameplay tag, "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)" struct text), a number/bool, or nested JSON (a struct object, an array for array/set/tag-container props, an object for map props). Strings still import via ImportText_Direct so prior callers keep working.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' is the DEFAULT -- it writes the editor world even with PIE running, which is what persists into the next PIE and what makes CPF_DisableEditOnInstance reachable; 'server' (the live PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' write the RUNNING actor instead; 'pie' is the ambiguous resolution and 'game' its alias. An unrecognised value FAILS with a message naming what was asked for and listing the worlds that exist -- it never falls back to another world in silence.

params.name: verify_persistence
params.description: Optional bool, default false. When true, run AActor::RerunConstructionScripts() and re-read the property to find out whether the value SURVIVES the User Construction Script. Without this, value_changed:true is measured BEFORE the UCS runs, so a property the UCS recomputes (the classic case: RelativeScale3D on a spline/box the UCS rescales) reports as changed and is silently reverted a moment later. Costs a full component rebuild of that actor, and it re-runs in whichever world you selected.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, property_name: string, property_type: string (FProperty class name), old_value: string, new_value: string (== final applied value), final_value: string (real value read back off the component), success: bool, value_changed: bool, component_class: string, component_is_active: bool, component_is_registered: bool, world: string (the selector actually used), world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }. With verify_persistence=true it also returns { construction_scripts_rerun: bool, has_non_trivial_user_construction_script: bool, post_construction_value: string, survives_construction_script: bool, persistence_note: string, verification: object, verification_checks: [object] }. On failure returns { success:false, error: <precise reason from the importer, or from the world resolver> }.

commands.name: add_data_table_row
commands.description: Create a new row in a DataTable (upsert -- it overwrites if the key exists), passing columns as a plain JSON object. Values go through reflection, so scalars, enums by name, nested structs and arrays all work. It fails the WHOLE write when any column cannot be imported, rather than committing a half-filled row with silent defaults, and lists anything it did not recognise in unknown_columns -- read that array, a typo'd column name is dropped, not an error. GameplayTag and GameplayTagContainer columns are the ones that reject a bare string: pass them in ExportText form, e.g. (TagName="A.B"). Use set_data_table_row to require the row to exist, or set_data_table_row_fields for a partial per-column update with before/after evidence.

commands.returns: success or error payload

commands.name: create_composite_data_table
commands.description: Create (or re-converge) a UCompositeDataTable whose row map is the merge of its parent DataTables, so a fork can EXTEND an upstream table instead of replacing it. The parent list is SET, not appended (re-running with a different list rewrites it), the row struct of every parent is validated BEFORE assignment (a mismatch or a cyclic parent chain would make the engine open a modal dialog and hang the editor), and the merge is verified by re-reading the live row map.

params.name: table_name
params.description: Name of the composite DataTable asset to create or converge.

params.name: include_row_sources
params.description: Optional bool (default false): also return the winning parent for EVERY merged row. Expensive on large tables.

commands.returns: { table_name, package_path, table_path, table_class, row_struct, created, already_existed, requested_parent_tables, missing_parents, parents_applied, saved, save_error, parent_tables, parent_count, contributing_parent_count, merged_row_count, sum_parent_row_counts, expected_merged_row_count, merged_row_count_matches_parents, parent_row_struct_mismatch, shadowed_rows, shadowed_row_count, row_sources_included, row_sources? }

commands.name: get_data_table_column
commands.description: Read one column across every row of a DataTable as ExportText strings, so TMaps, soft references and tags come out flat and intact; read-only. Returns row_struct, row_count and values as {row_name: text}. Use it to verify cell edits; an unknown column is an error.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable.

params.name: column
params.description: Name of the column (a field of the row struct, by property or display name) to read across every row

params.name: data_table
params.description: Alias of table_path: pass one of the two.

commands.returns: { table_path, column, row_struct, row_count, values:{ rowName: exporttext-string } }

commands.name: get_data_table_info
commands.description: Retrieves detailed information about a DataTable, including all row names. When the asset is a UCompositeDataTable (see table_class) the reported row_count is the ALREADY-MERGED map, so the response additionally explains where those rows come from: parent_tables[] in precedence order, merged_row_count vs sum_parent_row_counts, shadowed_rows[] with the winning parent, and parent_row_struct_mismatch[] for parents the engine silently skips.

params.name: table_path
params.description: The full asset path to the DataTable.

params.name: include_row_sources
params.description: Composite tables only. Optional bool (default false): also return the winning parent for EVERY merged row. Expensive on large tables.

commands.returns: { table_path, table_name, table_class, row_struct, row_count, row_names, columns:[{ name, type, is_map, is_soft, is_tag }] } plus, for a UCompositeDataTable: { parent_tables:[{ index, path, name, table_class, row_struct, row_count, row_struct_matches, contributes, null_entry }], parent_count, contributing_parent_count, merged_row_count, sum_parent_row_counts, expected_merged_row_count, merged_row_count_matches_parents, parent_row_struct_mismatch:[], shadowed_rows:[{ row_name, winner, winner_parent_slot, shadowed_by_winner:[] }], shadowed_row_count, row_sources_included, row_sources? }

commands.name: get_data_table_row
commands.description: Read ONE row of a DataTable by key and get every column as JSON . Reads the row memory untyped (FindRowUnchecked), so it works on Blueprint / user-defined row structs that are not FTableRowBase children, where the typed lookup reports "Row not found" for rows that exist; a miss here really is a missing key. Serializes TMap, nested struct and GameplayTag columns. When you need the byte-exact ExportText of a column (to copy a vendor row, or to tell an empty enum from an unwritten one) use read_data_table_row_complex instead, and get_data_table_rows when you want the enum DISPLAY names.

params.name: table_path
params.description: The full asset path to the DataTable.

params.name: row_name
params.description: The name of the row to retrieve.

commands.returns: { table_path, row_name, row_data } where row_data is the fully serialized row struct (TMap / nested struct / FGameplayTag columns included)

commands.name: get_data_table_row_as_json
commands.description: Export ONE DataTable row through UE's own DataTable JSON writer, returning both the verbatim native JSON string and a parsed object -- the exact format set_data_table_row_from_json consumes, so it is the read half of a copy/duplicate/round-trip. Use it over get_data_table_row when the value has to go back INTO the engine (it emits GameplayTagContainers in the ExportText form the importer accepts). The round trip is not lossless for multi-word user-defined enums, so re-read what you wrote.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable

params.name: row_name
params.description: Name (key) of the row

commands.returns: { table_path, row_name, row_struct, row_json (verbatim native JSON string), row_data (parsed) }

commands.name: get_data_table_rows
commands.description: Dump EVERY row of a DataTable as an array, with the row count -- for browsing or diffing a whole table of items, recipes, quests or loot. The reader to pick when a column is a user-defined ENUM: it emits the enumerator's DISPLAY NAME, whereas the ExportText readers return "" for the index-0 enumerator, which is indistinguishable from a column that was never written. Whole-table sized, so for one row use get_data_table_row and for one column across rows use get_data_table_column.

params.name: table_path
params.description: The full asset path to the DataTable.

commands.returns: { table_path, row_name, rows, row_count }

commands.name: get_string_table_entries
commands.description: Lists every entry of a UStringTable asset without changing it. Returns string_table_name, string_table_id, namespace, count and entries, each with key, source (the source string) and its metadata as an id to value object with metadata_count. Edit entries with set_string_table_entry.

params.name: string_table_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UStringTable

commands.returns: { string_table_path: string, string_table_name: string, string_table_id: string, namespace: string, entries: [object], count: int }

commands.name: get_string_table_metadata
commands.description: Read all metadata (id->value) attached to a UStringTable entry (FStringTable::EnumerateMetaData).  The reader that pairs with set_string_table_metadata.

params.name: string_table_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UStringTable.

params.name: key
params.description: Entry key to read metadata from.

commands.returns: { string_table_path: string, key: string, entry_exists: bool, metadata: object, metadata_count: int, namespace: string }

commands.name: import_data_table_csv
commands.description: Bulk-load a DataTable from a CSV string -- the fast path for authoring or restoring many rows at once. DESTRUCTIVE: it REPLACES the table's rows, so any row not in the CSV is gone; export first (export_data_table_as_csv) if you meant to merge. Always read the problems array and problem_count: the native importer reports per-cell failures there while still succeeding overall, and enum values whose display name contains spaces are cut at the first space and silently land on the index-0 enumerator. For a handful of rows prefer set_data_table_rows_from_json, which reports per-row results.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable

params.name: csv_string
params.description: CSV content (header row + one row per data row)

commands.returns: { table_path, row_struct, rows_imported, row_count, problem_count, saved, problems, row_names }

Reads UDataRegistry::DataSources[] via reflection (the UDataRegistrySource base class does not have a public SourceTable accessor; the UDataRegistrySource_DataTable subclass does, and we read it via FProperty lookup so this stays portable across DataTable source variants).

commands.description: Remove a DataTable source from a UDataRegistry asset (the true inverse of add_data_registry_source).  Does a reflective RemoveAt on the registry's protected DataSources[] array and saves the asset. Select the source either by data_table_path (matched against each DataTable source's SourceTable) or by source_index. Does NOT unregister from the subsystem. Idempotent: if the source is not present it returns removed:false with an unchanged count.

params.name: registry_path
params.description: Content path to the UDataRegistry asset.

params.description: Content path of the source DataTable to remove (matched against SourceTable). Provide this OR source_index.

commands.description: Remove the entry key, with all its metadata, from a UStringTable asset inside an undo transaction, then mark the asset dirty and save it. Idempotent: a key that is not in the table is already the state asked for, so the call succeeds with removed false and already_absent true and changes and saves nothing. A missing table is an error, and so is a failed save, which keeps the removal in memory. Use remove_string_table_metadata to drop only metadata, set_string_table_entry to add or change an entry, get_string_table_entries to list them.

params.description: Full asset path to the UStringTable

params.name: key
params.description: Entry key to remove

commands.returns: { string_table_path: string, key: string, removed: bool, existed: bool, already_absent: bool, verified: bool, namespace: string, entry_count: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_string_table_metadata

params.name: key
params.description: Entry key the metadata is attached to.

params.name: metadata_id
params.description: Metadata id (an FName, e.g. 'Comment') to remove.

commands.returns: { string_table_path: string, key: string, metadata_id: string, existed: bool, removed: bool, still_exists: bool, entry_exists: bool, metadata: object, metadata_count: int, namespace: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: rename_curve_table_row
commands.description: Rename a row (curve) in a UCurveTable.  UCurveTable::RenameRow silently no-ops if the source is missing or the target name already exists, so those cases are reported via the boolean flags (not errors).

params.description: Full asset path to the UCurveTable.

params.name: row_name
params.description: Current name of the row to rename.

params.name: new_row_name
params.description: New name for the row.

commands.returns: { curve_table_path: string, row_name: string, new_row_name: string, source_existed: bool, target_existed: bool, renamed: bool, old_still_exists: bool, new_exists: bool, row_count: int, curve_table_mode: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: rename_data_table_row
commands.description: Rename a DataTable row key, copying its value byte-exact (safer than delete plus re-add, which can drop GameplayTags), then save and verify the swap (new_exists, old_removed). Refuses a case-only rename, and an existing new_name unless overwrite=true. Row handles that reference the old name are not updated.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable (data_table also accepted)

params.name: old_name
params.description: Existing row key to rename (error if it does not exist)

params.name: new_name
params.description: New row key (error if it already exists unless overwrite=true)

params.name: overwrite
params.description: When true, allow new_name to replace an existing row; when false (default) a pre-existing new_name is an error

params.name: data_table
params.description: Alias of table_path (the DataTable asset path, e.g. "/Game/Data/DT_Items"); table_path wins when both are given

commands.returns: { table_path, old_name, new_name, row_struct, success, overwrote_existing, new_exists, old_removed, saved, row_count }

commands.name: set_active_culture
commands.description: Set the editor's active culture/locale (FInternationalization::SetCurrentCulture). Honest error if the culture name isn't recognized.

params.name: culture_name
params.description: Required culture identifier, e.g. "en", "es-ES", "ja".

commands.returns: { culture_name: string, success: bool }

commands.name: set_data_asset_property
commands.description: Write ONE reflected property on a DataAsset from a text value and verify it by reading back, returning old_value and new_value so the reply proves the change instead of merely claiming it. Values use UE text form: structs as "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)", object references as a full asset path, GameplayTags as (TagName="A.B"). One property per call, so loop for several; get_data_asset_info dumps them all.

params.name: data_asset_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataAsset.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Name of the UPROPERTY to set (class property name).

params.name: value
params.description: New value as a string (numbers/bools accepted); structs use UE text form e.g. "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)"; object refs use a full asset path.

commands.returns: { data_asset_path: string, property_name: string, property_type: string, old_value: string, new_value: string, applied: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_data_table_cell
commands.description: Set one element of an array column in a DataTable row (a field of a struct element, or a scalar element) by direct ImportText, bypassing the JSON/CSV importer, and save. Returns before_value, after_value, write_verified; an unregistered GameplayTag still becomes None (write_verified:false) and is saved anyway.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable (data_table also accepted)

params.name: row_name
params.description: Name (key) of the row to edit

params.name: column_name
params.description: Name of the row-struct field holding the array (display name or authored/internal name both accepted, same fallback as get_data_table_column)

params.name: row_index
params.description: Index into that array to edit (0-based; errors honestly if out of range, never a silent OOB read/write)

params.name: value
params.description: ExportText/ImportText string to write (e.g. "Material.Bone" for a bare FGameplayTag value, or an enum's internal OR display name)

params.name: cell_property
params.description: Name of the sub-field on the array element STRUCT to set (display or authored name); omit/empty for a scalar array (e.g. TArray<FGameplayTag>/TArray<FName>) to edit the element itself

params.name: data_table
params.description: Alias of table_path (the DataTable asset path, e.g. "/Game/Data/DT_Items"); table_path wins when both are given

commands.returns: { table_path, row_name, column_name, row_index, cell_property, resolved_property, array_length, before_value, after_value, changed, already_set, import_succeeded, write_verified, success, warning?, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_data_table_row
commands.description: Update an EXISTING DataTable row, erroring if the key is absent -- that guard is the only difference from add_data_table_row, and it is what stops a typo'd row name from quietly creating a second row. Columns you omit keep their current values; the write fails as a whole if any provided column cannot be imported, and unrecognised names come back in unknown_columns. Pass GameplayTag columns in ExportText form, e.g. (TagName="A.B"). For per-column before/after evidence use set_data_table_row_fields; for one cell use set_data_table_cell.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable

params.name: row_name
params.description: Name (key) of the existing row to update

params.name: row_data
params.description: Object of {column_name: value} to apply over the current row

commands.returns: success or error payload

commands.name: set_data_table_row_fields
commands.description: Write only the named cells of one DataTable row via the native JSON importer, deep-merged onto the current row so untouched columns and struct sub-fields survive, then save. Returns changed_columns, unchanged_despite_request, unknown_columns (skipped) and the row as ExportText. For many rows use set_data_table_rows_from_json.

params.name: data_table
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable (table_path also accepted)

params.name: row_name
params.description: Name (key) of the row to write

params.name: fields
params.description: Object of {column_name: value} to overlay onto the current row (only these cells are written); a TMap<Enum,SoftClass> value must be an object of {EnumName: bare-class-path} (e.g. {"MyEnumValue":"/Game/...ABP_x_C"}) -- passed through verbatim, never wrapped

params.name: create_if_missing
params.description: When true, create the row (from defaults) if it does not exist; when false (default) a missing row is an error

params.name: table_path
params.description: Alias of data_table (the DataTable asset path, e.g. "/Game/Data/DT_Items"); data_table wins when both are given

commands.returns: { table_path, row_name, row_struct, success, saved, created, updated_existing, written_fields:[..], changed_columns:[..], unchanged_despite_request:[..], unknown_columns?:[..], problems:[..], row_after_exporttext:{column:exporttext} }

commands.name: set_data_table_row_from_json
commands.description: Write a whole DataTable row from a native-format JSON object (the shape get_data_table_row_as_json emits), with merge=true to overwrite only the columns you supply. The route for copying a row between tables or authoring a complex row in one call. ALWAYS read the problems array: success:true routinely coexists with columns that never landed -- a GameplayTagContainer passed as a JSON array is rejected and left empty (give it as the string "(GameplayTags=((TagName=\"A.B\")))"), a sub-field whose internal name differs from the display name you used stays at its struct default, and a user-defined enum whose display name has spaces is cut at the first space and lands on the index-0 enumerator (write the internal NewEnumeratorN name instead). Confirm with read_data_table_row_complex.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable

params.name: row_name
params.description: Name (key) of the row to write

params.name: row_json
params.description: A JSON object of {column:value} (as produced by get_data_table_row_as_json)

params.name: merge
params.description: When true and the row exists, only the caller-provided columns are overwritten

commands.returns: success or error payload

commands.name: set_data_table_rows_from_json
commands.description: Upsert many DataTable rows with one native JSON import and one save, each deep-merged onto its current values like set_data_table_row_fields; missing rows are created from defaults. Returns per-row results and a summary. A failed row does not fail the call: check summary.failed and saved.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the DataTable (data_table also accepted)

params.name: rows
params.description: Object of { row_name: {column:value} }, or that object as a JSON string; each fields object is overlaid non-destructively (a value that is a JSON object deep-merges into the existing struct member, scalars/arrays replace)

params.name: save
params.description: When true (default) save the package once after all rows are written; when false leave it dirty in memory

params.name: data_table
params.description: Alias of table_path (the DataTable asset path, e.g. "/Game/Data/DT_Items"); table_path wins when both are given

commands.returns: { table_path, row_struct, results:{ row_name:{ success, created, updated_existing, changed_columns:[..], unchanged_despite_request:[..], unknown_columns?:[..], error? } }, summary:{ total, created, updated, failed }, saved, row_count, problems:[..] }

commands.description: Attach a new component of a given class to an actor ALREADY PLACED in the level (an instance-level component, not a change to its Blueprint -- for that use add_component_to_blueprint, which affects every instance).
