params.description: Name of the placed actor to add the component to (editor world).

params.name: component_type
params.description: Component class name (e.g., 'StaticMeshComponent', 'BoxComponent', 'UStaticMeshComponent')

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name to assign to the new component

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative location (for scene components)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation (for scene components)

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative scale (for scene components)

params.name: idempotent
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When true, if the actor already has a component of this class, return it instead of adding a duplicate (already_existed:true). Use for single-instance components.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, object_path: string, requested_component_name: string, component_type: string, already_existed: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: add_enum_entry
commands.description: Append one enumerator to a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum) and give it a display name.  Idempotent (an entry whose display/internal name already exists reports already_existed with added=false, leaving the enum unchanged -- the engine itself does NOT dedup). The new entry lands at the end, before the hidden _MAX sentinel.

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum).

params.name: entry_name
params.description: Display name for the new enumerator.

commands.returns: { enum_path: string, entry_name: string, added: bool, already_existed: bool, entry_count: int, entries: [string] }

commands.name: add_message_log_entry
commands.description: Add one message to a named editor Message Log listing (for example "PIE", "MapCheck" or a new name, created on demand) at Info, Warning or Error severity; an unrecognised severity becomes Info, and a missing log_name or message is an error. Entries stay in memory for the editor session and are never saved. Use it for diagnostics meant for Window > Message Log; print_to_output_log writes to the Output Log instead. message_count is the listing's message count after the add. Read entries back with get_message_log_entries, show the window with open_message_log, empty the listing with clear_message_log.

params.name: log_name
params.description: The message log listing name (e.g. "PIE", "MapCheck", or a custom name).

params.name: message
params.description: The message text to add.

params.name: severity
params.description: EMessageSeverity token: "Info" (default), "Warning", "Error".

commands.returns: { added: bool, log_name: string, message: string, severity: string, message_count: int }

commands.name: add_struct_member
commands.description: Add a field to a Blueprint (user-defined) struct: the way to grow a data shape -- a DataTable row struct, a save record, a component's payload -- without opening the struct editor. Honest on collisions: if the new name is invalid or already used it ROLLS BACK the auto-named member it had to create first and returns an error, instead of reporting success under the engine's MemberVar_N name and leaving orphans behind. Adding a field to a struct a DataTable already uses changes every row (new field at its default), so re-read the table afterwards. get_struct_members lists what is there; rename_struct_member and remove_struct_member are the edits.

params.name: struct_path
params.description: Full asset path of the struct (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyStruct).

params.name: member_name
params.description: New member name.

params.name: member_type
params.description: Type string resolved through the Blueprint pin-type resolver: scalars (bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte), plus struct/enum/class/object types addressed by name or asset path. An unresolvable string is an error, not a silent default.

commands.returns: { struct_path, member_name, member_type, member_count }

commands.name: align_actors
commands.description: Snap two or more editor-world actors onto a shared location, rotation and/or scale taken from a reference (the first, the last, their average, or a named actor). Use it to straighten a hand-placed row or make a set of props share an orientation, in one undoable step; batch_set_actor_transform is the tool when each actor needs a DIFFERENT transform. WARNING: aligning "location" collapses them onto the same point -- for a row, align only rotation/scale and set positions yourself.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Array of at least 2 INTERNAL actor names (GetName) in the editor world; fewer is an error, and editor labels do not resolve.

params.name: align_type
params.description: "location" (default), "rotation", "scale" or "all" -- which transform components get copied from the reference.

params.name: reference
params.description: Where the target values come from: "first" (default), "last", "average" (the componentwise mean of all of them), or the internal name of one of the listed actors.

commands.returns: { aligned_count: int, align_type: string, reference: string, aligned_actors: [actor JSON] }

commands.name: backup_asset
commands.description: Duplicate an asset into a timestamped /Game/MCP_Backups/ folder.  Call this before destructive operations (delete, reparent, overwrite). Accepts a package path or a full object path.

params.name: path
params.description: Source asset path (package path like /Game/Foo/Foo or full object path .Foo)

commands.returns: { source: string, backup_path: string }

commands.name: batch_delete_actors
commands.description: Delete several editor-world actors at once through the editor's own delete path, in ONE undoable transaction (a single undo brings them all back), returning the count and the JSON of each actor captured before deletion. WARNING: matches INTERNAL names only -- editor labels do not resolve -- names it cannot find are skipped silently, so compare deleted_count against how many you asked for; and if NONE resolve it errors with "No actors found to delete". Editor world only, and the removal is in memory until save_level writes the .umap.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Array of internal actor names (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Unmatched entries are dropped without an error; resolve labels first with find_actors_by_name.

commands.returns: { deleted_count: int (compare against your input length), deleted_actors: [actor JSON captured before the delete] }

commands.name: batch_place_actors_on_terrain
commands.description: Ground many actors on the landscape in one call by sampling the heightmap at each actor's XY (no line trace; scatter without per-point python). Same grounding math as place_actor_on_terrain, applied per actor.

params.name: actors
params.description: Array of { name (Actor->GetName()) OR label (Actor->GetActorLabel()), z_offset? (per-actor override), align? ('mesh_bbox_bottom'|'actor_origin', per-actor override) }

params.name: align
params.description: Optional default align for entries without their own; 'mesh_bbox_bottom' (default; drops the lowest mesh point) or 'actor_origin'

params.name: z_offset
params.description: Optional default extra world-Z above the sampled ground for entries without their own; defaults to 0

commands.returns: { placed: [ { name, label, previous_z, new_z, landed_z, in_bounds, align, align_used, z_offset } ], failed: [ { name?, label?, error } ], placed_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, landscape_actor_name: string, world_name: string }

commands.name: batch_set_actor_transform
commands.description: Move/rotate/scale MANY actors in a single undoable transaction, each with its own optional location/rotation/scale, reporting success_count, failure_count and the names that did not resolve. Cheaper and atomically undoable versus N set_actor_transform calls. Calls Modify() per actor so their OFPA packages dirty and save_level actually writes them. Takes the same `world` selector as set_actor_transform, so it reaches a live PIE world too. WARNING: resolves the INTERNAL name only (no editor labels, unlike set_actor_transform); a name it cannot find is counted in failure_count, not raised as an error -- read that number.

params.name: actor_transforms
params.description: Array of objects {actor_name: internal GetName; location?: [x,y,z] array only; rotation?: [pitch,yaw,roll] or the safer {pitch,yaw,roll}; scale?: [x,y,z] array only}. Omitted components keep their current value; an entry with no actor_name just increments failure_count, and a malformed vector silently reads as zero.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional: "editor" (default) | "pie" | "server" | "client" | "pie:N". The response stamps which world answered.

commands.returns: { success_count: int, failure_count: int (unresolved or malformed entries -- check it), updated_actors: [actor JSON re-read after the write], failed_actors?: [string], world_name, world_package, ... }

commands.name: begin_transaction
commands.description: Open one undoable transaction so a whole batch of edits collapses into a SINGLE undo entry: every Modify() between this and end_transaction joins it, and cancel_transaction rolls the lot back without leaving anything on the stack. Use it to make a multi-step edit atomically reversible; the returned transaction_index is what end_transaction / cancel_transaction need. already_open:true means one was already running -- transactions do not nest here.

params.name: description
params.description: Label shown in the editor's undo history (e.g. 'MCP: retag turrets'). Make it recognisable; it is what get_transaction_history and next_undo report.

params.name: primary_object_path
params.description: Optional object path recorded as the transaction's PrimaryObject, so the undo entry is attributable to one asset/actor.

commands.returns: { description: string, transaction_index: int, already_open: bool, undo_count: int }

commands.name: bulk_delete_assets
commands.description: GUARDED batch asset deletion. ***dry_run DEFAULTS TO TRUE*** (deliberate: it is the most destructive command in the plugin, `bulk_delete_assets(["/Game/VendorPack"], recursive=true)` would be a valid unconfirmed call, and agent allowlists may run mutating tools with no prompt). Four independent gates REFUSE per item instead of skipping silently: readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots), protect_paths (wildcards -- the only gate that saves a zero-referencer asset), the currently-open editor world, and the OPT-IN require_zero_referencers gate whose referencer count EXCLUDES referencers that are themselves in this batch (so a self-contained dead subgraph can still be deleted whole). Deletion is a single ObjectTools::ForceDeleteObjects over the whole eligible batch -- resolving each object here via StaticFindObject/StaticLoadObject rather than through UEditorAssetSubsystem::DeleteAsset, whose UE::EditorAssetUtils::LoadAssetFromPath/EnsureAssetsLoaded preamble is a known crash site ("Array index out of bounds", deterministic on corrupted leftovers). deleted_count counts ONLY items that passed BOTH post-delete probes -- the package file is gone (FPackageName::DoesPackageExist) AND the object no longer resolves at its original path (StaticFindObject) -- never the API's own return value. Both are required because for a never-saved, registry-visible asset the disk probe is vacuously true (it was never on disk), so residency is the only real evidence; each failure names which probe still sees the item.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: List of asset paths (or folder paths when recursive is true). Required, non-empty.

params.name: recursive
params.description: If true, expand folder paths to all contained assets. Default false.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Default TRUE. Nothing is deleted; would_delete reports what WOULD go, with each item's gate verdict. Pass false to actually delete.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Content roots that may never be deleted from. Default: the project's Read Only Content Roots; pass [] to disable the gate entirely. Matches are REFUSED (refused_readonly_root), never silently skipped. (Read via mcp_common::ParseReadonlyRoots, so the type is declared here.)

params.name: protect_paths
params.description: Wildcard patterns (FString::MatchesWildcard, case-insensitive, `*` spans '/') matched against both the package name and the object path. Default [] (gate off). Matches are REFUSED (refused_protected).

params.name: require_zero_referencers
params.description: Default FALSE. When true, an asset with at least one referencer OUTSIDE this batch is refused. The per-item external_referencer_count is reported either way.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Referencer filter for the count above: "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive), default "all".

commands.returns: { requested_count, expanded_count, recursive, dry_run, readonly_roots: [string], protect_paths: [string], require_zero_referencers: bool, dependency_type: string, expanded_folders: [{folder, asset_count}], eligible_count, would_delete: [{path, package_name, external_referencer_count, external_referencers: [string], on_disk}], deleted: [{path, package_name, deleted, still_loaded, error?}], deleted_count, failed_count, force_delete_reported_count, refused_readonly_root: [{path, matched_root}], refused_protected: [{path, matched_pattern}], refused_referenced: [{path, external_referencer_count, external_referencers: [string]}], refused_open_world: [{path, reason}], refused_count, results: [{path, success, error}], note, verification: {...} }

commands.name: can_redo
commands.description: Cheap yes/no on whether anything can be re-applied, plus the LABEL of the entry redo would restore. can_redo:false right after an undo normally means a new edit has since wiped the redo stack. Prefer get_undo_state for the whole picture in one call.
commands.returns: { can_redo: bool, label: string (title of the transaction redo would restore), reason?: string (why not, when can_redo is false) }

commands.name: can_undo
commands.description: Cheap yes/no on whether anything is undoable right now, plus the LABEL of the entry undo would revert -- read that label before undoing so you do not roll back someone else's edit. Prefer get_undo_state when you also want counts and the redo side in the same call.
commands.returns: { can_undo: bool, label: string (title of the transaction undo would revert), reason?: string (why not, when can_undo is false) }

commands.name: cancel_transaction
commands.description: Abort the transaction opened by begin_transaction: the edits made inside it are rolled back and NO entry is written to the undo stack (undo_count is unchanged). The escape hatch when a multi-step edit goes wrong halfway -- cleaner than committing with end_transaction and then calling undo, which leaves history behind.
commands.returns: { success: bool, transaction_index: int (the one that was cancelled), undo_count: int (unchanged -- nothing was recorded) }

commands.name: capture_viewport
commands.description: Screenshot the active editor viewport to a PNG (forcing a fresh draw first), optionally resized and optionally returned inline as base64. Use it to SHOW a result -- proof that something looks right, an image to hand to a human. Do NOT use it to diagnose: an image costs far more context than a command and is read far less reliably than one, so for "is the actor there / did the value change / did it move" prefer get_actor_bounds, get_component_properties, raycast_scene or a property read, which answer exactly and cheaply. Captures the EDITOR viewport, not a PIE window; high_res_screenshot is the higher-resolution sibling.

params.name: width
params.description: Optional target width to downscale/upscale to (omit to keep native viewport size).

params.name: height
params.description: Optional target height (only used when width is also supplied).

params.name: filename
params.description: Optional output filename (default MCP_Capture_<timestamp>.png); ".png" extension is added if missing.

params.name: return_base64
params.description: bool, also include image_base64 + image_format in the response (default false).

commands.returns: { file_path: string, width: int, height: int, byte_size: int, image_base64: string, image_format: string }

commands.name: clear_message_log
commands.description: Clear all messages from a named engine Message Log listing.

params.name: log_name
params.description: The message log listing name (e.g. "PIE", "MapCheck", or a custom name).

commands.returns: { cleared: bool, log_name: string, cleared_count: int, messages_after: int }

commands.name: clear_undo_barriers
commands.description: Remove ALL undo barriers at once so undo can traverse the whole buffer again -- including barriers another session or the human placed to protect their work, so prefer remove_undo_barrier for just your own. Nothing is undone by this; it only lifts the floor. WARNING: `success` is hardcoded true: `had_barrier` is the oracle, false meaning there was nothing to clear.
commands.returns: { success: bool (hardcoded), had_barrier: bool (THE oracle -- false = honest no-op), undo_count: int, queue_length: int }

commands.name: consolidate_assets
commands.description: Redirect every reference to the source assets onto the target with UEditorAssetSubsystem::ConsolidateAssets, which DELETES the sources (leaving redirectors) and saves what it changed. Only class-compatible sources are used; others are listed in skipped_incompatible and unloadable ones are dropped silently. dry_run=true only reports.

params.name: target_asset_path
params.description: The asset to keep, all references point here

params.name: source_asset_paths
params.description: Assets to consolidate into the target

params.name: dry_run
params.description: If true, skip ConsolidateAssets entirely and only report what would happen, default false

commands.returns: dry_run=true: { target_asset_path, target_class, dry_run: true, would_consolidate: [string], skipped_incompatible: [{path,class}], compatible_count: int, incompatible_count: int }; dry_run=false (default): { target_asset_path, target_class, dry_run: false, consolidated_count: int, source_count: int, success: bool, skipped_incompatible: [{path,class}], incompatible_count: int }

commands.name: copy_actors
commands.description: Put editor-world actors on the editor CLIPBOARD (edactCopySelected), either by name or whatever is currently selected, so paste_actors can drop them back -- the way to clone a group while keeping their relative layout, which duplicate_actor (one actor, in place) does not do. WARNING: naming them REPLACES the current selection as a side effect, and matching is by INTERNAL name only. One of actor_names or copy_selected=true is required.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Optional array of internal actor names (GetName) to copy; supplying it re-selects exactly those actors first.

params.name: copy_selected
params.description: Optional bool. True (with actor_names omitted) copies whatever is selected right now, leaving the selection alone.

commands.returns: { copied_count: int, success: bool (hardcoded; verify with paste_actors' pasted_count) }

commands.name: create_blueprint_interface
commands.description: Create a Blueprint Interface asset: a contract of function signatures that unrelated classes can implement, so callers talk to the contract instead of a concrete class. The right tool when several different kinds of actor must answer the same request (interactable, damageable, workable) and you do not want a shared base class -- one interface replaces N-by-M hard-wired cases. Created empty: add functions with add_blueprint_function, then implement_interface on each class and implement_interface_function per class.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (no path)

params.name: path
params.description: Target content path for the new asset (default /Game/Blueprints)

commands.returns: { name, path, type }

commands.name: create_directory
commands.description: Make a content-browser folder at a UE long path (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Systems/Foo). Idempotent: an existing folder is not an error, it comes back already_existed:true. Use it to lay out a system's folders before creating assets there; a path that does not start with '/' is rejected.

params.name: path
params.description: UE long path of the folder to create, e.g. /Game/MyGame/Systems/Foo. Must start with '/', not a disk path.

commands.returns: { path: string, already_existed: bool (true = nothing was created, and that is a success) }

commands.name: create_enum
commands.description: Create a Blueprint enum asset from an ordered list of enumerator DISPLAY names -- states, categories and types that Blueprints and DataTable columns switch on. Errors if the asset already exists (not idempotent). Beware the display/internal split that follows: the engine stores enumerators internally as NewEnumerator0, NewEnumerator1, ... and writers into DataTables must use those internal names, because a display name containing spaces is cut at the first space by the text importer and silently lands on index 0. So keep single-word display names, or expect to write NewEnumeratorN. add_enum_entry / rename_enum_entry / reorder_enum_entry edit it afterwards.

params.name: name
params.description: Enum asset name.

params.name: entries
params.description: Ordered list of enumerator display-name strings.

params.name: path
params.description: Target content path for the new asset (default /Game/Blueprints)

commands.returns: { name, path, entry_count }

commands.name: create_file_media_source
commands.description: Create a UFileMediaSource asset at package_path/name that points at a movie file path, register it and save it; the file does not need to exist. An existing asset is returned unchanged (file_path is not applied). Returns asset_path, the stored file_path, created and saved.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the file media source asset to create.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Movie file on disk, absolute or "./"-relative to the project Content folder, e.g. "./Movies/Intro.mp4"; a path inside Content is stored in that relative form.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Media)

commands.returns: { media_source_name, asset_path, created, already_exists, file_path, saved, save_error }

commands.name: create_functional_test
commands.description: Create a Blueprint subclass of AFunctionalTest (the canonical UE pattern for a multiplayer-friendly, Blueprint-scriptable test actor) and save it.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Name for the new Functional Test BP asset.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content folder; defaults to /Game/MCP.

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Optional AFunctionalTest-derivative parent (default "FunctionalTest").

commands.returns: { asset_name, asset_path, package_class, parent_class, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_media_player
commands.description: Create a UMediaPlayer asset at package_path/name with PlayOnOpen and looping set, optionally with a linked UMediaTexture named "<name>_T" beside it, and save both. An existing player is returned unchanged (flags not applied). Returns asset_path, play_on_open, loop, media_texture_path, saved and texture_saved.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the media player asset to create.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Media)

params.name: create_output_texture
params.description: Also create a UMediaTexture "<name>_T" next to the player and link it (default true).

params.name: play_on_open
params.description: Set the player's PlayOnOpen flag (default true)

params.name: loop
params.description: Set the player to loop via SetLooping (default false)

commands.returns: { media_player_name, asset_path, created, already_exists, play_on_open, loop, texture_created, media_texture_path, saved, texture_saved, save_error, texture_save_error }

commands.name: create_media_texture
commands.description: Create a UMediaTexture asset at package_path/name (AutoClear on, no player linked) and save it; an existing texture is returned unchanged, with its linked player if any. Link a player with link_media_texture_to_player. Returns asset_path, created, has_media_player and saved.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the media texture asset to create.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Media)

commands.returns: { media_texture_name, asset_path, created, already_exists, has_media_player, media_player_path, saved, save_error }

commands.name: create_struct
commands.description: Create a Blueprint Struct (UUserDefinedStruct). Idempotent by reset+rebuild: a stale struct already at the path is deleted and recreated fresh (reset_stale:true); a same-path asset of a different type is an honest error.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (no path)

params.name: path
params.description: Target content path for the new asset (default /Game/Blueprints)

commands.returns: { name, path, reset_stale }

commands.name: delete_actor
commands.description: Remove one actor from the EDITOR level through the editor's own delete path (select + edactDeleteSelected), so it is transacted and undoable, and echo back the deleted actor's JSON. WARNING: two edges that bite: it matches the INTERNAL name only -- unlike set_actor_transform, an editor LABEL will not resolve -- and it clears the current selection as a side effect. It cannot touch PIE actors (editor world only), and the deletion lives in memory until save_level writes the .umap. Use batch_delete_actors for several at once.

params.name: name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName), case-insensitive but WHOLE-string. Editor labels are NOT accepted here; resolve one first with find_actors_by_name.

commands.returns: { deleted_actor: actor JSON captured before the delete }

commands.name: delete_directory
commands.description: DESTRUCTIVE: removes a content-browser folder AND every asset inside it, recursively, with no dry-run and no referencer check (unlike bulk_delete_assets, which defaults to dry_run and refuses vendored roots). Driven through UEditorAssetSubsystem, which is the pair that works headless. Idempotent: an already-absent folder answers already_absent:true. Verify afterwards with `git status` on the corresponding Content/ path -- never with the `deleted` flag alone.

params.name: path
params.description: UE long path of the folder to delete, e.g. /Game/Scratch. Must start with '/'. Everything under it goes.

commands.returns: { path: string, already_absent: bool, deleted: bool }

commands.name: deselect_actors
commands.description: Drop specific actors from the editor selection, or clear it entirely with deselect_all. The counterpart of select_actors; use the clear-all form to leave the editor in a known state before a tool that acts on the selection (copy_actors, move_actors_to_level) so it does not pick up leftovers. Editor world only; matches INTERNAL names.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Optional array of internal actor names (GetName) to remove from the selection. One of actor_names or deselect_all=true is required.

params.name: deselect_all
params.description: Optional bool. True clears the whole selection; it wins over actor_names when both are sent.

commands.returns: { deselected_all: bool, deselected_count: int }

commands.name: disable_plugin
commands.description: Turn a plugin off in the .uproject and save the project file to disk. WARNING: `enabled:false` is hardcoded on the write succeeding and the modules stay LOADED for this session -- the plugin's classes keep working until the editor restarts, so a still-functioning feature is not evidence the call failed. WARNING: disabling a plugin whose assets are referenced leaves those references broken on the next start; check get_plugin_status and the referencers first.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Plugin name exactly as in its .uplugin file, not a path.

commands.returns: { plugin_name: string, enabled: bool (hardcoded false when the .uproject write succeeded), project_saved: bool, note: string about the required restart }

commands.name: duplicate_actor
commands.description: Copy one editor-world actor in place through the editor's duplicate path, keeping its component overrides, and return both the new actor's JSON and the original's. Undoable; it changes the editor SELECTION as a side effect. Matches the INTERNAL name only (no editor labels). The clone exists in memory until save_level writes the .umap -- and a save that answers success while `git status` stays clean means the .umap is read-only (e.g. a Git LFS `lockable` file you have not locked), not that the duplicate failed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Editor labels are NOT accepted; resolve one with find_actors_by_name first.

commands.returns: { duplicated_actor: actor JSON (its auto-assigned name lives here), original_actor: actor JSON }

commands.name: enable_plugin
commands.description: Turn a plugin on in the .uproject and save the project file to disk. WARNING: `enabled:true` is hardcoded on the write succeeding, and the plugin's MODULES are not loaded by this call -- the editor has to be restarted before its classes, assets or MCP tools actually exist. So do not treat a following "class not found" as a failure of this command; check project_saved and then restart. Use get_plugin_status to read the current state and disable_plugin for the inverse.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Plugin name exactly as in its .uplugin file (e.g. 'PythonScriptPlugin'), not a path.

commands.returns: { plugin_name: string, enabled: bool (hardcoded true when the .uproject write succeeded), project_saved: bool, note: string about the required restart }

commands.name: end_transaction
commands.description: Close the transaction opened by begin_transaction and COMMIT it, so everything done inside becomes one entry on the editor's undo stack (undo_count grows by one). Pair it with every begin_transaction -- leaving one open makes later edits silently join it. Use cancel_transaction instead when you want the batch thrown away rather than kept.
commands.returns: { success: bool, transaction_index: int (the one that was closed), undo_count: int after the commit }

commands.name: execute_console_command
commands.description: Run a console command through the EDITOR (GEditor->Exec against the editor world): cvars, `stat` overlays, `r.*` toggles, engine commands. WARNING: it does NOT reach a running PIE session's PlayerController, so player cheats like `BugItGo` come back handled:false -- to move or cheat a PIE pawn use execute_python against the anchored PIE world. `handled` is the engine's own "some Exec claimed this string", not proof of an effect: verify with the state (get_cvar, a property read), never with this bool.

params.name: command
params.description: Console command line, e.g. 'stat fps', 'r.ScreenPercentage 50', 'ShowFlag.Grid 0'. Editor-side only.

commands.returns: { command: string, handled: bool (an Exec handler claimed the string -- not evidence the effect happened) }

commands.name: execute_python
commands.description: Execute Python code inside the running Unreal Editor. DO NOT GUESS A FIELD NAME: most of this tool's errors are "object has no attribute" -- and the field usually EXISTS, just not where you reached for it: `HitResult().impact_point` raises, `get_editor_property` cannot find it, and only `to_dict()` returns it (Transform.translation is the reverse). The engine's own stub and Epic's web docs list it either way, so neither settles it -- ask the object (dir(x), x.to_dict(), x.get_editor_property(...)). PIE TRAP -- this tool is the ONE HOLE in the plugin's PIE guard: the commands that compile a Blueprint or write to disk are REFUSED while Play-in-Editor is live (McpPieSafety.gen.h), but arbitrary Python cannot be classified statically, so a script that reaches compile/save through unreal.* (BlueprintEditorLibrary.compile_blueprint, EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset, save_loaded_asset, anything that dirties a Blueprint) RUNS ANYWAY. With PIE live that ends either in a DEAD EDITOR -- the compiler's UREINST_* trampoline retains a world and CheckForWorldGCLeaks is Fatal, taking every unsaved edit with it -- or in a save that reports success without writing a byte (Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0). So: call is_play_in_editor_active FIRST whenever your script compiles, saves, or mutates a Blueprint, and stop PIE before running it. READING the live world during PIE is safe and is exactly what this tool is for -- do not avoid it for that. BEFORE writing a loop, check what already answers it in ONE call: scripts that re-implement something a tool already does fail far more often than scripts doing something genuinely new -- hand-rolled scaffolding is where the errors are, and a bug in the scaffold reads exactly like a finding about the game. enumerate actors of a class -> get_actors_by_class. enumerate them AND read their properties, filtered by class or editor label, drilling into one component, with the answering world STAMPED on the result (this tool cannot tell you which world answered) -> get_actor_properties_by_class. read properties off ONE known object -> get_properties / get_property_value. list an actor's components -> get_actor_components. one line trace -> raycast_scene. sample a property across a whole PIE session ARMED BEFORE BeginPlay -- a window a post-tick callback cannot reach at all -> watch_pie_property. But do NOT read this as "always prefer the specific tool": only a minority of scripts are replaceable end-to-end. Python remains the right answer when the script does what those cannot: several classes in one round trip, walking components AND calling a method, filtering by name substring, correlating two values in the same tick, or anything that mutates. Do not trade one call for twelve. WARNING: `log_output` IS NOT THE LOG OF THE CALL -- it is Python's own prints only (UE fills it from a delegate broadcast solely by unreal.log/log_warning/log_error), so every UE_LOG the ENGINE emits during your script is absent from it. Read `engine_log` instead: it is the GLog slice bracketed to this call, Warning+Error by default. Example: build_meta_human can run, return None, write zero assets and report a clean `log_output` while "LogMetaHumanCoreTechLib: Error: Texture Synthesis has not been initialized" sits in GLog. When a call reports success and NOTHING HAPPENED, `engine_log` is the first place to look; widen with engine_log_level=Log, or pass `log_cursor_before` to get_output_log_lines(since_sequence_id=...) for the unfiltered rest.

params.name: command
params.description: Python code to run (single or multi-line).

params.name: capture_output
params.description: Run as a file and collect captured log (default true)

params.name: mode
params.description: Execution mode: ExecuteFile, ExecuteStatement, or EvaluateStatement (default ExecuteFile)

params.name: engine_log_level
params.description: Minimum severity of ENGINE log to return in `engine_log`: Error, Warning (default), Display, Log/All.

params.name: engine_log_max
params.description: Max lines in `engine_log` (default 50, 0 disables, hard cap 4096).

commands.returns: { command, python_success, execution_mode, command_result, output, log_output, log_line_count, engine_log, engine_log_count, engine_log_truncated, log_cursor_before }

commands.name: execute_python_file
commands.description: Execute a Python (.py) file inside the running Unreal Editor. PIE TRAP: same hole as execute_python -- arbitrary Python is NOT covered by the plugin's PIE guard, so a script that compiles a Blueprint or saves an asset runs even with Play-in-Editor live, where compiling can KILL the editor (UREINST_* retains a world, CheckForWorldGCLeaks is Fatal) and saving reports success without writing (Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0). Check is_play_in_editor_active first when the file compiles, saves or mutates a Blueprint; reading the live world during PIE is safe. WARNING: `log_output` IS NOT THE LOG OF THE CALL -- it is Python's own prints only (UE fills it from a delegate broadcast solely by unreal.log/log_warning/log_error), so every UE_LOG the ENGINE emits during your script is absent from it. Read `engine_log` instead: it is the GLog slice bracketed to this call, Warning+Error by default. Example: build_meta_human can run, return None, write zero assets and report a clean `log_output` while "LogMetaHumanCoreTechLib: Error: Texture Synthesis has not been initialized" sits in GLog. When a call reports success and NOTHING HAPPENED, `engine_log` is the first place to look; widen with engine_log_level=Log, or pass `log_cursor_before` to get_output_log_lines(since_sequence_id=...) for the unfiltered rest.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute path to a .py file accessible from the editor host.

params.name: engine_log_level
params.description: Minimum severity of ENGINE log to return in `engine_log`: Error, Warning (default), Display, Log/All.

params.name: engine_log_max
params.description: Max lines in `engine_log` (default 50, 0 disables, hard cap 4096).

commands.returns: { file_path, python_success, command_result, output, log_output, log_line_count, engine_log, engine_log_count, engine_log_truncated, log_cursor_before }

commands.name: export_assets
commands.description: Export assets to files via IAssetTools::ExportAssets (preferred format, FBX/PNG/EXR first), each written to export_path/<package path without its leading slash>.<extension>, e.g. D:/Exports/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.FBX. What was written is measured per asset on disk: exported lists each asset with its file, and not_exported the ones that did not load, have no exporter or failed to write. Succeeds only when every requested asset was written.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: Asset object or package paths to export (e.g. ["/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock"]); empty strings are ignored.

params.name: export_path
params.description: Destination directory on disk (e.g. "D:/Exports"), created if missing; each file lands in subfolders named after its package path.

commands.returns: { exported_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, export_path: string, exported: [{ asset_path: string, file: string }], not_exported: [string] }

commands.name: find_actors_by_name
commands.description: Locate actors by a SUBSTRING of their internal name and/or their editor label, returning name, label, class and transform for each hit. This is the one to use when you know what a thing is CALLED but not its class -- get_actors_by_class needs an exact class name, and this one alone can search labels (match='label'), which is where hand-assigned names live. Plain case-INSENSITIVE substring, no wildcards and no regex: 'turret' matches BP_Turret_C_2, and '*' matches literally nothing. Its world selector is the canonical one: 'editor' (default), 'pie'/'game', 'server', 'client' and 'pie:N' all resolve for real, an unrecognised value FAILS instead of falling through to the editor world, and the reply stamps world_package/world_type/net_mode/pie_instance so you can tell which world answered.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Substring to look for, case-insensitive, no wildcards or regex. Cannot be empty.

params.name: match
params.description: Optional 'name' | 'label' | 'both' (default 'both'). 'name' = internal object name only; 'label' = the editor label from the outliner; 'both' = a hit on either. An unknown value is a clean error.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional cap on hits (default 1000); results_truncated says whether the scan stopped early.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority, GetNetMode() != NM_Client) | 'client' | 'pie:N' (the PIE context whose PIEInstance is N). Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world.

commands.returns: { matching_actors: [ { name, actor_name, label, class, location, rotation, scale, is_loaded } ], matching_actors_count: int, search_pattern: string, match: string, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (in World Partition the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: find_duplicate_assets
commands.description: Find groups of assets sharing the same base name under a folder tree (e.g. same name existing under both a vendored library tree and a first-party fork)

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to scan, default /Game

params.name: recursive
params.description: If true, scan subfolders, default true

params.name: min_group_size
params.description: Minimum number of same-named assets to report as a duplicate group, default 2

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional list of class short names (e.g. "StaticMesh","Material"); only assets whose AssetClassPath short name case-insensitively matches one of these are considered

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on the number of duplicate GROUPS returned (not raw assets), clamped 1..20000, default 2000

commands.returns: { folder_path, recursive, class_filter, min_group_size, group_count, total_duplicate_assets, assets_scanned, max_results, results_truncated, groups: [{ name, count, classes: [string], assets: [{path, package, class}] }] } (groups sorted by count descending)

commands.name: find_unused_assets
commands.description: Find assets in a folder with zero referencers, and annotate each survivor with the reasons it should be KEPT anyway. "Zero referencers" is not the same as "safe to delete": there are three common ways an asset stays alive with an empty referencer set -- it is explicitly protected, a Config/Default*.ini names it, or it is a fork descending from a vendored base library. Each becomes a keep_reason string on the entry; deletion_candidates lists only the entries with NO keep_reason. Nothing is ever removed from unused_assets by these flags (hiding a genuinely unreferenced asset would be the same lie in the other direction). NOTE: there is deliberately no `is_world` -- it is already visible in class_name ("World").

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to scan, e.g. /Game/Unused

params.name: recursive
params.description: If true, scan subfolders, default true

params.name: exclude_classes
params.description: Optional list of class name fragments to skip

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Referencer filter: "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive), default "all" (identical behavior to omitting it)

params.name: protect_paths
params.description: Wildcard patterns (FString::MatchesWildcard, case-insensitive, `*` spans '/') matched against the package name and the object path. Default [] . A match adds keep_reason "protected_path".

params.name: include_lineage_reasons
params.description: Default FALSE because it LOADS every candidate Blueprint. When true, a Blueprint whose super chain reaches a class owned by one of base_libraries gets keep_reason "descends_from_base_library" -- the only signal that saves a fork carrying no fork-origin tag (project setting Fork Origin Tag).

params.name: base_libraries
params.description: Vendored-library content roots for the lineage check. Default: the project's Read Only Content Roots (same default as audit_class_purity).

commands.returns: { folder_path, folder_exists, recursive, dependency_type, protect_paths: [string], include_lineage_reasons, base_libraries: [string], unused_assets: [{path, class_name, size_kb, keep_reasons: [string], keep_reason_detail: {...}}], unused_count, total_scanned, deletion_candidates: [string], deletion_candidate_count, assets_with_keep_reason, keep_reason_counts: {protected_path, referenced_by_config, descends_from_base_library}, config_scan: {files_scanned: int, files: [string]}, lineage_scan: {attempted, blueprints_loaded, skipped_non_blueprint, load_failures} }

commands.name: fixup_redirectors
commands.description: Clean up the redirectors a rename/move left behind, under a folder: load each referencing package (which repoints it) and re-save it, optionally force-deleting redirectors whose referencers all saved. Hand-rolled on purpose -- IAssetTools::FixupReferencers HARD-CRASHES on World-Partition/OFPA projects -- and heavily railed: it REFUSES while PIE is active, never writes under readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots), never outside /Game, and never loads or saves map or OFPA packages, handing the resident ones back in skipped_current_world for you to save_level instead. Deletions are DISK-verified (a redirector whose .uasset survives lands in redirectors_delete_failed, not in the count). WARNING: redirectors_found/deleted count OBJECTS: one renamed Blueprint leaves THREE in a single package -- read redirector_packages_found for files.

params.name: path
params.description: Long path to scan, defaults to /Game

params.name: delete_redirectors
params.description: Optional bool (default false). After a successful repoint, force-delete the redirectors whose every non-redirector referencer was saved. Left in place by default (a redirector is ~2 KB and harmless).

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long-path prefixes that must NEVER be written (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots, i.e. the vendored library roots). Referencers under them are reported in skipped_readonly instead of being saved.

commands.returns: { path: string, redirectors_found: int, redirector_packages_found: int, referencers_repointed: int, packages_saved: int, packages_failed: [{ package: string, error: string }], skipped_readonly: [string], skipped_current_world: [string], redirectors_deleted: int, redirector_packages_deleted: int, redirectors_delete_failed: [{ package: string, reason: string }], redirectors_fixed: int, message: string }

commands.name: get_actors_in_level
commands.description: Dump EVERY actor of a world (name, class, transform), capped by max_results at 5000, with total_actors_in_level and results_truncated so you know if you saw all of it. The unfiltered census: reach for get_actors_by_class when you know the class, find_actors_by_name for a name/label substring, get_actors_in_radius for a place. Its world selector is the canonical one: 'editor' (default), 'pie'/'game', 'server', 'client' and 'pie:N' all resolve for real, an unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist instead of quietly answering from the editor world, and every reply carries world_package/world_type/net_mode/pie_instance so you can see WHICH world answered rather than assuming.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional cap on returned actors (default 5000). Must be > 0. Truncation is reported, never silent.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority, GetNetMode() != NM_Client) | 'client' | 'pie:N' (the PIE context whose PIEInstance is N). Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world.

commands.returns: { actors: [actor JSON], actors_count: int, total_actors_in_level: int, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (in World Partition the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: get_allow_cinematic_control
commands.description: Read whether the active editor viewport allows cinematic control (Sequencer possession)
commands.returns: { allows_cinematic_control: bool }

commands.name: get_automation_test_results
commands.description: Returns the cached result of the last synchronous test completed through run_automation_test or start_gauntlet_run, without running anything: test_name, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings and entries. Skipped or multi-tick tests leave the cache unchanged; fails when no test has completed this editor session.
commands.returns: { test_name, started, completed, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings, entries:[{type,message,context,filename,line}], entry_count }

commands.name: get_compile_errors
commands.description: WARNING: despite the get_ prefix this COMPILES the Blueprint (silently) and then returns its error/warning count and every message with severity -- it is a mutation, not a read: compiling dirties the package, can cascade into other packages, and can knock a Blueprint's placed OFPA instances out of the world in memory (get_actors_by_class then returns 0 in editor AND PIE; load_level of the same map brings them back). Use it as the honest oracle for "does this BP build" -- num_errors and the message list are real, read off the compiler results log -- and reach for check_blueprint_errors / find_erroring_blueprints when a compile is not what you want.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or full asset path (e.g. BP_MyActor or /Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyActor).

commands.returns: { name: string, num_errors: int, num_warnings: int, succeeded: bool (num_errors == 0), messages: [{ severity: 'error'|'warning'|'info', message: string }] }

commands.name: get_current_level
commands.description: Which map a world is sitting on: level_name, its package_name (/Game/... or /Engine/...), the resolved disk filename, whether the package is dirty, and a live actor count. package_name is the discriminator that catches the classic mistake -- if it starts with /Engine/ you are on an engine template (what new_level leaves behind) and a save_level without `filename` would overwrite the ENGINE's own map. Defaults to the EDITOR world; it also takes the standard `world` selector, so during PIE you can ask the play world ('pie'/'server'/'client'/'pie:N') instead of being told about the authoring map and having no way to know it.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default -- the authoring map even while PIE runs) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N'. Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world.

commands.returns: { level_name: string, package_name: string (the /Game or /Engine path -- read this one), filename: string, is_dirty: bool, actor_count: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string ("Editor" | "PIE" | ...), net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: get_cvar
commands.description: Reads a console variable's live value, help text, and flags.

params.name: name
params.description: Console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage".

commands.returns: { name: string, value: string, string_value: string, int_value: int, float_value: float, bool_value: bool, help: string, flags: int, set_by: string }

commands.name: get_engine_ini_value
commands.description: Read one key from the merged in-memory config (GConfig) of an INI such as Engine or Game. Read-only; returns value and found (false, with an empty value, when the section or key is missing). Pass config_file without .ini. Writer: set_engine_ini_value.

commands.name: get_level_blueprint
commands.description: Get (or, with create=true, bring into being) the current level's Level Blueprint and return the blueprint_path that the graph tools need -- its event graph is always called "EventGraph", so add_graph_node / connect_pins can target it directly with graph_name="EventGraph". Read-only by default: with create=false and no blueprint present it answers exists:false + success:true rather than failing.

commands.description: Read back the messages currently in a named engine Message Log listing (IMessageLogListing::GetFilteredMessages), each resolved back to the actor/component the engine attached to it. The reader that pairs with add_message_log_entry/clear_message_log.

commands.name: get_output_log_lines
commands.description: Read the single per-editor-session log buffer UEAgent attaches to GLog (general editor output, not PIE-only -- Serialize() captures every category/verbosity that passes through GLog, regardless of PIE state; usable for PIE Functional Test / wait_for_pie_completion orchestration too). commands.description: Read the editor's undo buffer as a list, most-recent-first: each entry's title, context, primary object and whether it has already been undone. Read this instead of chaining can_undo + can_redo, and read it BEFORE undo/undo_multiple so you know what you are about to revert.
commands.returns: { can_undo, can_redo, undo_count (entries undo can still revert), redo_count (undone entries redo can restore), next_undo, next_redo, transaction_open, transaction_index }

commands.name: high_res_screenshot
commands.description: Capture a high-resolution (supersampled) screenshot and write it to a PNG SYNCHRONOUSLY. Prefers the Play-In-Editor game view when PIE is active (captured_pie=true); otherwise the active editor viewport. Drives FViewport::TakeHighResScreenShot() + FViewport::Draw(), which renders at resolution_multiplier x the viewport size and blocks (via ProcessScreenShots) until the file is on disk. The "HighResShot" exec path defers the write to the next render frame, which never runs headless, so it writes nothing. Requires a real RHI (errors honestly under -nullrhi) and a live viewport. Note: the supersampled path re-renders the scene, so the UMG/Slate HUD is NOT included; use capture_pie_screenshot for a HUD-inclusive PIE shot.

commands.name: import_asset
commands.description: Import an IMAGE file from disk into a content folder as a Texture2D, driving the texture factory inline (it deliberately avoids IAssetTools::ImportAssets, which asserts when re-entered from the engine tick) and returning the created object path. It always overwrites an asset of the same name -- `replace_existing` is accepted and ignored. Images ONLY -- png/jpg/jpeg/bmp/tga/dds/exr/hdr/tif/tiff/psd/pcx: any other extension is a clean error naming the dedicated handler to use instead (import_texture_file for images, import_sound_file for .wav, import_landscape_heightmap for terrain, interchange_import_asset for FBX/glTF meshes). A missing source file or a destination that is not a /Game long path also errors before anything is touched.

params.name: source_file_path
params.description: Absolute path to the image on disk; its existence is checked before any work starts.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: UE long path of the target content folder, e.g. /Game/Imported. Must start with '/'.

params.name: replace_existing
params.description: ACCEPTED AND IGNORED: the tool reads this flag and never uses it. The underlying import suppresses the overwrite dialog and re-imports over an existing asset of the same name regardless of what you pass, so neither value changes anything.

commands.returns: { source_file_path: string, destination_path: string, imported_object_paths: [string] }

commands.name: import_font_file
commands.description: Import a .ttf/.otf/.ttc/.otc font from disk as a UFontFace, and optionally the companion UFont that a FSlateFontInfo needs to actually render text. This is the only way to get a typeface into the project headlessly: import_asset is images-only on purpose, and nothing else in the toolset touches fonts. Drives UFontFileImportFactory inline (never IAssetTools::ImportAssets, which asserts when re-entered from the engine tick, same reason import_asset avoids it) and ALWAYS sets BatchCreateFontAsset explicitly -- left at its default the factory pops a MODAL DIALOG asking whether to create the UFont, which would hang the editor on a click that is never coming. Once imported, point a widget at it with set_widget_property on the dotted path "Font.FontObject" (a UFont) plus "Font.TypefaceFontName", or "Font.Size" for the size.

params.name: source_file_path
params.description: Absolute path on disk to the .ttf/.otf/.ttc/.otc file. A missing file, or any other extension, is a clean error before anything is touched.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: UE long path of the destination content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame/UI/Fonts.

params.name: name
params.description: Optional asset name; defaults to the source file's base name.

params.name: create_font_asset
params.description: Also create the companion UFont asset (default true). A UFontFace alone is a raw typeface: a FSlateFontInfo's FontObject wants a UFont. Pass false to import only the face, e.g. to add it as another typeface entry of an existing font.

commands.returns: { source_file_path, destination_path, imported_object_path, font_face_created, create_font_asset, message }

commands.name: list_dirty_packages
commands.description: What is UNSAVED in the editor right now: every dirty package with its disk path, split into map / OFPA-external / asset, and -- the reason to run it -- readonly_dirty_count, the single go/no-go number telling you a vendored root like /Game/VendorPack would be REWRITTEN by the next bulk save. Run it before closing the editor, before compiling, and before any save; it also resolves OFPA hashes to actor labels so /__ExternalActors__/AB/CD/EF12 becomes a name. Strictly read-only: never marks dirty, never saves. WARNING: it reports IN-MEMORY state only -- a package clean here can still differ from HEAD on disk, so `git status` stays the disk authority. And do NOT use its pie_active field as the PIE gate: it can answer false with PIE running; the oracle is is_play_in_editor_active.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long-path prefixes treated as vendored/upstream (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). Only used to CLASSIFY (under_readonly_root / readonly_dirty_count); nothing is ever written. Pass [] to switch the classification off.

params.name: path_prefix
params.description: Optional long-path prefix filter, e.g. /Game/VendorPack, to ask "is anything of THEIRS dirty". Empty (default) lists everything; what it excluded is counted in filtered_out.

params.name: include_objects
params.description: Optional bool (default false). Also list every object carried by each dirty package. One object-hash walk per package -- a dirty map can hold thousands, so leave it off unless you need the contents.

commands.name: load_level
commands.description: Open a map in the editor (by /Game path or disk .umap), replacing the current world. Also the repair for actors that VANISHED from a world in memory after compile_blueprint: reloading the same map brings the placed OFPA instances back with their per-instance config -- never re-place them. REFUSES up front when any other UWorld is still resident in memory, because the engine's world-leak check turns that into a Fatal error that kills the editor process and every unsaved edit with it; the refusal lists the resident worlds and the remedy. Run list_dirty_packages first: a reload discards unsaved work.

params.name: filename
params.description: Disk path to a .umap, OR a /Game asset path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Foo) resolved to the on-disk map file

params.name: load_as_template
params.description: When true, loads the level as a template; defaults to false

params.name: force
params.description: Skip the resident-world preflight and call LoadMap anyway. With resident worlds alive this PROBABLY KILLS THE EDITOR: the engine raises a Fatal error ("World Memory Leaks"), the process dies and every unsaved in-memory edit is lost. Defaults to false.

commands.returns: { success: bool, error?: string, refused?: bool, load_attempted?: bool, resident_world_count?: int, resident_worlds?: [{ package: string, world_name: string, world_type: string, has_world_context: bool, is_load_target: bool }], remedy?: string, data?: { loaded_filename: string, target_package: string, level_name?: string, world_name?: string, resident_world_count: int, forced_past_resident_worlds: bool, resident_worlds?: [...] } }

commands.name: migrate_assets
commands.description: Copy assets, and their dependencies unless ignore_dependencies, into another project's Content folder with IAssetTools::MigratePackages, with no prompt and skipping files that already exist there. The engine first saves every dirty package of this editor, and migrates nothing if one of them fails to save. What was copied is measured from the migration's own package list against the disk: migrated lists each package written (dependencies included), skipped_existing the requested ones the destination already had, failed the requested ones neither written nor skipped. Succeeds when nothing requested failed. destination_path must be a Content folder with a .uproject (or one .uplugin) next to it, or the engine migrates nothing and the call fails.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: Asset object or package paths to migrate (e.g. ["/Game/Props/SM_Crate"]); each is reduced to its package name.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: Target content folder, e.g. D:/OtherProject/Content

params.name: ignore_dependencies
params.description: When true only the listed packages are copied, without their dependencies (default false).

commands.returns: { migrated_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, destination_path: string, ignore_dependencies: bool, migrated: [{ package: string, file: string }], skipped_existing: [string], failed: [string], note: string? }

commands.name: move_actors_to_level
commands.description: Relocate existing editor-world actors into another sub-level (persistent or a loaded streaming level) -- it rescues actors that got spawned into the wrong level, which set_current_level only prevents going forward. Idempotent: actors already there come back in already_in_level instead of being touched. WARNING: it is clipboard-backed, so the editor SELECTION is mutated as a side effect, and the destination must be loaded AND unlocked. Both levels' packages get dirty: save_level after.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Array of actor names OR editor labels in the editor world (this one does accept labels, unlike delete_actor/batch_delete_actors).

params.name: target_level
params.description: "persistent" or the short name of a loaded streaming sub-level

params.name: move_all_or_fail

commands.returns: { requested: int, moved_count: int, already_in_level: [string], target_level: string, success: bool, note: string }

commands.name: new_level
commands.description: Loads the ENGINE default template map into the editor. It does NOT create a level and the level is NOT empty (~45 actors: Floor, PlayerStart, DirectionalLight, SkyLight, SkyAtmosphere, fog); `level_name` is accepted but IGNORED. After this the editor sits on an /Engine map, so a save_level without `filename` would write over the engine's own .umap. Like load_level it REFUSES to run while other UWorlds are resident in memory, because this is a LoadMap and the engine's world-leak check turns that into a Fatal error that kills the editor process (see force).

params.name: level_name
params.description: IGNORED. Accepted for wire compatibility only; the loaded map is always /Engine/Maps/Templates/Template_Default. When you pass one, the response echoes it in requested_level_name and sets level_name_ignored=true.

params.name: force
params.description: Skip the resident-world preflight and call LoadMap anyway. With resident worlds alive this PROBABLY KILLS THE EDITOR: the engine raises a Fatal error ("World Memory Leaks"), the process dies and every unsaved in-memory edit is lost. Defaults to false.

commands.returns: { success: bool, error?: string, refused?: bool, load_attempted?: bool, requested_filename?: string, target_package?: string, resident_world_count?: int, resident_worlds?: [{ package: string, world_name: string, world_type: string, has_world_context: bool, is_load_target: bool }], resident_world_is_load_target?: bool, remedy?: string, data?: { template_package: string, level_name_ignored: bool, requested_level_name?: string, resident_world_count: int, forced_past_resident_worlds: bool, resident_worlds?: [...], level_name?: string, world_name?: string, loaded_package?: string, is_engine_template?: bool, warning?: string, message?: string } }

commands.name: redo
commands.description: Re-apply the transaction that undo just reverted and report what remains, including next_redo. WARNING: `success` is ALWAYS true even with an empty redo stack -- read `applied` instead. Note the redo stack is discarded as soon as any NEW edit is made after an undo, so a redo that answers applied:false usually means something was changed in between, not that the command failed.
commands.returns: { applied: bool (THE oracle), undo_count: int, can_redo: bool, next_redo: string (label of the next redoable entry) }

commands.name: redo_multiple
commands.description: Re-apply N undone transactions in one call, stopping early when the redo stack runs out rather than erroring. WARNING: compare actually_redone against requested -- that gap is the only honest signal. Remember any new edit made after an undo wipes the redo stack, so this can legitimately redo nothing.

params.name: count
params.description: How many transactions to redo (>= 1). Silently capped at what the redo stack holds.

commands.returns: { requested: int (your input), actually_redone: int (compare against it), undo_count: int }

commands.name: reload_asset_package
commands.description: Re-read already-loaded packages FROM DISK, non-interactively (it never opens the modal that would freeze a headless editor), either preserving or permanently discarding their in-memory edits. This is the repair for the situation list_dirty_packages flags: a vendored package left dirty by a compile cascade is cleaned with on_dirty="discard" (was_dirty:[...] -> still_dirty:[]), so the next bulk save cannot write it. Also the way to throw away a bad in-memory edit without touching disk. It reports before/after evidence per package, and skips what it cannot safely reload (not loaded, OFPA, worlds) instead of pretending. WARNING: on_dirty="discard" is irreversible for unsaved work -- check what is dirty first.

params.name: package_names
params.description: Array of long package names (or object paths) to reload, e.g. ["/Game/VendorPack/.../DT_ItemRows"].

params.name: package_name
params.description: Convenience single-name alias for package_names.

params.name: on_dirty
params.description: Optional "abort" (default) or "discard". "abort" -> EReloadPackagesInteractionMode::AssumeNegative: a package with unsaved in-memory edits is NOT reloaded and its edits are kept. "discard" -> AssumePositive: UPackageTools clears the dirty flag and reloads, PERMANENTLY THROWING AWAY those in-memory edits.

commands.returns: { requested: [string], on_dirty: string, interaction_mode: string, attempted: [string], reloaded: [string], was_dirty: [string], still_dirty: [string], failed: [string], skipped_not_loaded: [string], skipped_ofpa: [string], skipped_world: [object], skipped_invalid: [object], api_returned: bool, api_error: string, verify: { before: [object], after: [object] }, message: string }

commands.name: save_asset
commands.description: Write ONE .uasset to disk by package path (a Blueprint, DataTable, material...) and VERIFY the effect: still_dirty_after_save:false plus file_on_disk:true is the oracle, not `saved`. Use save_level for the .umap and reload_asset_package to undo an in-memory edit instead. PIE: this is REFUSED while Play-in-Editor runs (it never stops or touches your session) -- the engine guard Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0 rejects the write before attempting anything, so a save during play would report success without writing a byte. Stop PIE and retry, or pass force=true. WARNING: when it answers success:false with PIE down, a common cause is the file being READ-ONLY on disk (e.g. a Git LFS `lockable` file that has not been `git lfs lock`ed). You do not have to check that by hand: `file_read_only` is measured on every call and the error message states whether a read-only file IS or is NOT the explanation. WARNING: it writes exactly one package, so it cannot stop a compile cascade from dirtying a vendored asset that a LATER bulk save then rewrites -- list_dirty_packages before, `git status` after.

params.name: path
params.description: Full asset path to save, e.g. /Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyActor (an .Object suffix is tolerated). Must already exist or the call errors.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long-path prefixes treated as vendored/upstream (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). A save under one of them is REFUSED by default; see refuse_readonly. Pass [] to disable the classification entirely.

params.name: refuse_readonly
params.description: Optional bool. When true, a save whose package falls under one of readonly_roots is REFUSED (success:false, saved:false, refused_readonly:true) instead of performed. Default = the process-wide switch (mcp_common::IsReadOnlyRootSaveEnforcementEnabled(), true unless `mcp.ReadOnlyRootEnforcement 0`); when false the write happens and is only reported + ledgered.

commands.returns: { path: string, package_name: string, saved: bool, success: bool, under_readonly_root: bool, readonly_root_matched: string, refused_readonly: bool, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_defaulted: bool, still_dirty_after_save: bool, file_on_disk: bool, file_read_only: bool (measured on disk -- true means the file is read-only, e.g. an unlocked Git LFS `lockable` file), verification: object, verification_checks: [object], error?: string }

commands.name: save_level
commands.description: Write the editor's current level (.umap) to disk; it REFUSES while PIE is running (the engine guard rejects the write anyway) and derives `success` from the file being on disk afterwards, never from the save call's own bool. WARNING: it also REFUSES when the target .umap is READ-ONLY on disk, which in an LFS repo means a `lockable` path you have not `git lfs lock`ed: that write cannot succeed, and answering over HEAD's still-untouched bytes would report success:true having written nothing. The refusal names the file and the fix (`git lfs lock <file>`) -- take the lock, do not retry. WARNING: on a file that ALREADY existed, `file_exists_on_disk` alone still cannot tell "I wrote it" from "it was already there": the field that proves the write is `file_mtime_changed`. It is deliberately NOT gating `success`, because a save with nothing dirty to write also leaves the mtime alone and that is not a failure. WARNING: with `filename` this is a SaveAs that DUPLICATES: the editor stays on the old map, the new one becomes a resident world (which then makes load_level refuse), and a SECOND save to the same filename opens a modal that freezes the editor -- treat filename as one-shot per name per session.

params.name: filename
params.description: Optional. A /Game asset path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Foo) or a disk .umap path; both accepted and resolved. Omit it to save the level in place -- that is the branch that just works. Passing one is a SaveAs: duplicate + resident world + the one-shot rule above.

params.name: save_as
params.description: Accepted for wire compatibility and IGNORED: the branch is chosen by whether `filename` was given. It comes back inside `requested` to mark it as your input, not a measurement.

commands.returns: { success: bool, error?: string, data?: { saved_filename?: string, saved_package?: string, saved_disk_path?: string, level_name?: string, file_exists_on_disk: bool, file_size_bytes: int, file_existed_before: bool, file_mtime_changed: bool (the write itself -- see the read-only note above), save_call_returned: bool, rescued_with_save_packages: bool, pie_was_stopped: bool, orphan_world_risk?: bool, requested?: { filename?: string, save_as?: bool } } }

commands.name: search_cvars

params.name: term
params.description: Substring to search (case-insensitive)

params.name: max

commands.name: set_actor_transform
commands.description: Move, rotate and/or scale ONE actor (omitted components are left as they are) and return the actor's re-read transform plus the identity of the world that was written. Undoable, and it calls Modify() first -- which matters, because moving an actor from Python does NOT dirty its OFPA package and then save_level reports success while writing nothing. Takes a `world` selector, so it also reaches a LIVE PIE pawn (an editor-only lookup would answer "Actor not found" for an actor that exists in another world). Use batch_set_actor_transform for many actors, place_actor_on_terrain to drop one onto the landscape.

params.name: world

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional new WORLD scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. A malformed value silently becomes 0,0,0 and the actor disappears.

commands.returns: { actor JSON via DescribeActorObject, transform RE-READ off the actor after the write }

commands.name: snap_actor_to_ground
commands.description: Drop ONE editor-world actor straight down until its bounds bottom rests on whatever is below -- meshes, BSP or the landscape. It line-traces first and, because headless traces routinely MISS the landscape, falls back to sampling the heightmap so the actor still lands; sampled_from tells you which path answered. Use place_actor_on_terrain when the ground is definitely the landscape and you want no trace at all, batch_place_actors_on_terrain for many actors.

params.description: Name of the actor to snap (editor world).

params.description: Optional downward trace distance in cm; defaults to 10000

params.description: When true, rotate actor to match the surface normal (trace hits only; the heightmap fallback has no normal); defaults to false

params.description: When true (default) and the downward line trace misses (headless traces routinely miss the landscape), fall back to sampling the landscape heightmap at the actor's XY (same sampler as place_actor_on_terrain) so the actor still lands. Set false to require a real trace hit.

commands.returns: { actor: actor JSON, hit: bool, landed: bool, sampled_from: 'trace'|'heightmap', hit_actor?: string, hit_distance?: number }

commands.name: spawn_actor
commands.description: Place a BUILT-IN engine actor (StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, CameraActor) into the editor level or a live PIE world, at an optional location/rotation/scale, and return the created actor's JSON. Only these types: for a Blueprint class use spawn_blueprint_actor. Refuses when an actor of that name already exists, and the spawn is undoable. It creates the actor in MEMORY only -- save_level (with the .umap writable) is what puts it on disk. WARNING: with 2+ PIE clients world='pie' can land in the CLIENT world, producing an actor the authority never sees -- ask for world='server' instead, and check the reply's world_package/net_mode to see where the actor actually went.

params.name: type
params.description: One of StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, CameraActor. Anything else is a clean error; Blueprints go through spawn_blueprint_actor.

params.description: Internal name for the new actor; must be unused in the target world or the call is refused.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional world location, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. An object or a shorter array is silently read as the origin.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional world rotation as the array [pitch, yaw, roll] -- note index 2 is ROLL, not yaw -- or, unambiguously, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..}, which is the recommended form. Defaults to zero.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional world scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Defaults to 1,1,1; a malformed value silently becomes 0,0,0 (an invisible actor).

params.description: Optional UStaticMesh asset path, only honoured for type=StaticMeshActor (e.g. /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector for WHERE the actor is spawned: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- what you want for anything replicated) | 'client' | 'pie:N'. Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent spawn into the editor world.

commands.returns: { actor JSON via DescribeActorObject: name, class, location, rotation, scale, plus world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: start_gauntlet_run
commands.description: Drive the in-process FAutomationTestFramework as the in-editor equivalent of a Gauntlet test run. We run synchronously (single game-thread callback) and report the execution info (errors / warnings / duration). Multi-tick tests (PIE / load-map / latent waits) are abandoned honestly with completed=false (StopTest asserts on a non-empty latent queue).

params.description: Name of the test to run (e.g. "Project.NetworkStress" or any registered automation test).

commands.returns: { test_name, gauntlet_started: true, gauntlet_subprocess: false, automation_equivalent: true, started, completed, errors, warnings, duration_s, verdict: "pass"|"fail"|"skipped", note }

commands.name: undo
commands.description: Step the editor's undo stack back by one transaction and report what is left, including next_undo (the label of the entry now on top). WARNING: `success` is ALWAYS true, including when there was nothing to undo -- the real oracle is `applied`, and the honest verification is re-reading whatever you changed. Use undo_multiple for N steps and get_undo_state to look before you leap; an undo barrier will stop it.

commands.name: undo_multiple

WARNING: compare actually_undone against requested: a smaller number is the honest signal that the stack ran out, and it is the only oracle here.

params.name: count
params.description: How many transactions to undo (>= 1). Silently capped at what the stack actually holds.

commands.returns: { requested: int (your input), actually_undone: int (compare against it), undo_count: int remaining }
