commands.name: editor_status
commands.description: Prove the Unreal editor is alive and TICKING: a no-argument game-thread liveness/health probe, and the first call to make when the MCP bridge goes quiet. It runs on the GAME THREAD via the bridge's command drain, so a reply proves the game thread is pumping -- unlike a transport-only ping, which a wedged editor still answers. After a "Connection reset" use it to tell an editor CRASH (this errors, the reconnect refuses) from a mere tool TIMEOUT (this returns alive=true); call it twice and diff frame_counter to rule out a deadlock, since a frozen game thread replies once but never advances the frame. Also reports whether PIE is running (pie_active / is_simulating) and the open editor world, without starting or stopping anything. Read-only and cheap; safe to call any time.
commands.returns: { alive: bool, gis_running: bool, exit_requested: bool, is_editor: bool, frame_counter: number, pie_active: bool, is_simulating: bool, editor_world: string, world_context_count: int }

Sibling: get_game_instance_info adds the GameInstance class; editor_status is the cheaper "is the editor alive" probe.

commands.name: get_engine_settings

commands.returns: { max_fps: number, screen_percentage: number }

commands.name: get_game_instance_info
commands.description: Read the live UGameInstance (name, class, object path) plus every engine world context (world_name + world_type: Editor/PIE/Game/EditorPreview/Inactive). A UGameInstance only exists while PIE or a game world is running, so at rest exists=false with empty strings is the NORMAL answer, not an error -- use it to answer "is a game session up, and which GameInstance class did it pick?". Pick this over get_engine_info when you care about the GameInstance itself; get_engine_info answers the same world-context question without it.
commands.returns: { exists: bool, game_instance_name: string, game_instance_class: string, game_instance_path: string, world_context_count: int, worlds: [object] }

commands.name: activate_game_feature_plugin

Idempotent: if already active, no-ops with already_active=true.

params.description: Name of the Game Feature Plugin (resolved to a URL via the subsystem registry). Provide this OR plugin_url.

commands.name: unload_game_feature_plugin

A name the class already has is skipped and listed in skipped_attribute_names; success is false when an added attribute is missing from the compiled class or did not get its default_value. A running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before anything is created or added; a call that adds nothing to an existing set is not refused and saves nothing (saved false). A failed save makes success false, with saved false and save_error, and the added attributes stay in memory only.

commands.returns: { world_name: string, subsystem_available: bool, subsystem_class: string }

commands.name: list_behavior_configs
commands.description: Enumerate every UGameplayBehaviorConfig asset under a package path via AssetRegistry.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Optional path filter (default "/Game"). Pass "" to scan all.

commands.returns: { package_path, total, configs:[{ config_path, config_name, behavior_class }] }

commands.name: remove_behavior_config
commands.description: Destroy a UGameplayBehaviorConfig data asset (mirror of create_behavior_config). Typed-delete: it loads the asset and REFUSES to delete it if it is not a UGameplayBehaviorConfig, so it cannot wipe the wrong asset the way the generic delete_asset can. Idempotent on missing assets.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Full /Game/... asset path of the config.

commands.returns: { config_path, deleted, already_existed, asset_class?, note? }

commands.name: set_behavior_class
commands.description: Set the BehaviorClass of a UGameplayBehaviorConfig (via reflection; the field is protected in 5.7).

params.name: config_path
params.description: Content path of the UGameplayBehaviorConfig.

params.name: behavior_class
params.description: UGameplayBehavior subclass name (with or without "U" prefix).

commands.returns: { config_path: string, behavior_class: string, set: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: trigger_behavior_on_actor
commands.description: Start the behavior of a UGameplayBehaviorConfig on a Pawn found by label in the editor world: the config supplies its UGameplayBehavior, whose Trigger runs on the pawn, and the world UGameplayBehaviorSubsystem tracks it until it ends or end_behavior_on_actor stops it. triggered=false means the behavior refused. Runtime only: nothing is saved or undoable. A config without BehaviorClass (see set_behavior_class), no subsystem in the editor world (see get_behavior_subsystem_info), a missing actor or a non-Pawn is an error.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Content path of the UGameplayBehaviorConfig.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the Pawn actor in the editor world to receive the behavior.

commands.returns: { config_path: string, actor_label: string, behavior_class: string, triggered: bool }

commands.name: register_gameplay_debugger_category
commands.description: Registers (or reconfigures, idempotently) a named GameplayDebugger category backed by a single generic data-driven FGameplayDebuggerCategory (GameplayDebugger.h IGameplayDebugger::RegisterCategory). FGameplayDebuggerCategory has 0 BlueprintCallable surface, so this is the only path to author a custom debugger category from MCP. Toggle visibility in-game with the console command "showdebug <category_name>".

params.name: category_name
params.description: Unique name for this debugger category (required)

params.name: specs
params.description: [{actor_class?: string, property_name: string, color?: string ("white"|"red"|"green"|"yellow"|"cyan"...), label?: string}] -- which properties to print for the current debug-actor, and how

commands.returns: { category_name: string, spec_count: int, registered: bool, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: unregister_gameplay_debugger_category
commands.description: Unregisters a named GameplayDebugger category created by register_gameplay_debugger_category (GameplayDebugger.h IGameplayDebugger::UnregisterCategory, the exact inverse of RegisterCategory). Also drops the category's stored specs. Idempotent: unregistering a category that register_gameplay_debugger_category did not create is an honest no-op reporting already_absent:true.

params.name: category_name
params.description: Name of the debugger category to unregister (required)

commands.returns: { category_name: string, unregistered: bool, already_absent: bool }

commands.name: add_gameplay_tag_redirect
commands.description: Add an entry to UGameplayTagsSettings::GameplayTagRedirects (the persistent redirect config), then call FGameplayTagRedirectors::RefreshTagRedirects() so the runtime map picks it up. Idempotent (same Old->New pair returns already_present=true). Requires a ConfigRestartRequired=true flag — UGameplayTagsSettings flags it as such; callers should note that the running game still resolves Old to itself until next process restart in Shipping, but in the editor the redirect is live immediately.

params.name: old_tag_name
params.description: Source tag name (FName).

params.name: new_tag_name
params.description: Destination tag name (FName).

commands.returns: { old_tag_name, new_tag_name, added: bool, already_present: bool, total_redirects: int, needs_restart: bool }

commands.name: add_gameplay_tag_to_table
commands.description: Add one tag (with an optional developer comment) as a row in a gameplay tag DataTable, verifying the write by read-back. The team-friendly way to declare tags: it touches only this asset instead of rewriting the shared DefaultGameplayTags.ini the way create_gameplay_tag does. The trade-off is that a tag added here is not registered LIVE, so it may not resolve until the table is reloaded -- if you must use it in the same session, check with find_gameplay_tag first.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the gameplay tag data table

params.name: tag
params.description: The gameplay tag string used as both row Tag and row name

params.name: dev_comment
params.description: Optional developer comment for the row

commands.returns: { table_path: string, tag: string, row_name: string, dev_comment: string, verified: bool, saved: bool, row_count: int, success: bool, message: string }

commands.name: add_tag_to_object
commands.description: Grant a gameplay tag to an object that implements IGameplayTagAssetInterface -- the way to put an actor into a state (stunned, wet, on fire, alerted) so that tag-driven systems react without any of them knowing about each other. Reports already_present and echoes the resulting tag list, so the reply is its own oracle. Register the tag first (find_gameplay_tag / create_gameplay_tag): an unregistered string resolves to an empty tag and is added as nothing.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to add the tag to

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the tag to add

commands.returns: { object_path: string, tag_name: string, success: bool, already_present: bool, message: string, tags: [string] }

commands.name: count_gameplay_tag_references
commands.description: DOES NOT COUNT ANYTHING: reference_count is ALWAYS 0, plus a note saying why. Declared engine gap -- there is no public GetTagReferenceCount API (the manager tracks refcounts internally, for debug tooling only), so all this returns honestly is whether the tag is valid. Never read the 0 as "nobody uses this tag" and never delete a tag on its evidence. To actually find users: find_blueprint_node_references with include_pin_defaults, plus a binary grep of Content/ and Config/ for the tag string.

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Single tag name (only its validity is really evaluated).

commands.returns: { tag_name, valid: bool, reference_count: 0, note: "..." }

commands.name: create_gameplay_tag
commands.description: Add a new gameplay tag to the project's DefaultGameplayTags.ini AND register it LIVE in this editor session -- that live half is why you must call this before writing the tag into a DataTable row or a property, since an unregistered tag string is silently reset to None by the importers. But it REWRITES THE WHOLE INI: the list comes back alphabetised, every comment block is deleted, and other tags' DevComments are re-serialised and normalised, so adding one tag can produce a diff full of unrelated insertions and deletions. Copy the ini first; the oracle is `git diff --stat` showing your N insertions and ZERO deletions, and if not, git checkout the ini and re-insert only your line (the tag stays registered live either way -- confirm with find_gameplay_tag).

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the gameplay tag to create or check

params.name: dev_comment
params.description: Optional developer comment for the tag

params.name: source_name
params.description: Optional explicit source INI name

commands.returns: { tag_name: string, success: bool, tag_string: string, message: string }

commands.name: create_gameplay_tag_table
commands.description: Create a DataTable of gameplay tags (row struct FGameplayTagTableRow) -- the alternative to declaring tags in DefaultGameplayTags.ini, and the better choice for a large or team-owned tag set: rows merge and diff like data instead of fighting over one ini that the create_gameplay_tag path rewrites end to end. The table must be registered in the project's gameplay tag settings to be loaded. Fill it with add_gameplay_tag_to_table and check it with validate_gameplay_tag_table.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name for the new data table, e.g. GT_MyTags

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/GameplayTags

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, table_path: string, row_struct: string, success: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: find_gameplay_tag
commands.description: Does this exact tag string exist and resolve right now? Returns found plus the resolved tag string. The precondition to check BEFORE using a tag anywhere: an unregistered tag is not an error in UE, it silently becomes an empty/None tag, and a query made with an empty tag fails exactly like a valid tag that does not match -- so the control case and the case under test become indistinguishable. Also the confirmation that create_gameplay_tag registered live even if you restored the ini. Exact lookup: use query_gameplay_tags for prefix/pattern search, get_gameplay_tag_source to see where it is defined.

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the gameplay tag to find

commands.returns: { tag_name: string, found: bool, tag_string: string }

commands.name: get_all_gameplay_tags
commands.description: Dump EVERY gameplay tag registered in the project, with a count -- the full vocabulary the game can reason about, including tags contributed by plugins and vendor content. Large by nature (projects run to thousands), so use query_gameplay_tags to search a branch and find_gameplay_tag to test one string; keep this for a full inventory or a naming audit.
commands.returns: { tags: [object], count: int }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tag_info
commands.description: Read one gameplay tag's detail, including its PARENT tag -- how you walk the hierarchy that makes tags useful (Material.Wood.Oak answers to Material.Wood). Worth knowing before writing a match: hierarchy matching is ASYMMETRIC, HasAny(A, B) only succeeds when a tag of A is B or a DESCENDANT of B, so putting a family where a leaf is expected quietly fails. get_gameplay_tag_source says where the tag is defined; find_gameplay_tag just tests existence.

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the gameplay tag to get info for

commands.returns: { tag_name: string, tag_string: string, tag_name_string: string, parent_tag: string }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tag_redirects
commands.description: List every entry configured in UGameplayTagsSettings::GameplayTagRedirects (the persistent Old->New redirect config). Read-only reader counterpart of add_gameplay_tag_redirect / remove_gameplay_tag_redirect; does NOT mutate or save.
commands.returns: { redirects: [{ old_tag_name, new_tag_name }], count: int }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tag_source
commands.description: Where does this tag come from: native C++, DefaultGameplayTags.ini, a tag DataTable, or transient (registered live this session and NOT on disk) -- plus its comment and its native / restricted / explicit flags. The call that tells you whether a tag will survive an editor restart and which file to edit to change it, and the one that distinguishes YOUR tags from a vendor's or the engine's before you rename or remove anything.

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Single tag name.

commands.returns: { tag_name, valid, source, comment, is_native: bool, is_restricted: bool, is_explicit: bool, allow_non_restricted_children: bool }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tag_table_rows
commands.description: List every tag declared in a gameplay tag DataTable, with its developer comment -- what this table contributes to the project vocabulary, as opposed to get_all_gameplay_tags which returns the merged live registry from all sources. Use it to audit one team's or one module's tags, and validate_gameplay_tag_table to catch malformed or duplicated rows.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the gameplay tag data table

commands.returns: { table_path: string, row_struct: string, rows: [object], row_count: int }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tags_manager
commands.description: One-line health check of the gameplay tag system: the manager singleton's validity and the TOTAL number of registered tags. Cheap sanity probe before a tag frontier -- a plausible total confirms the registry loaded, and comparing the count before and after create_gameplay_tag shows the registration took. Counts only; for the tags themselves use get_all_gameplay_tags or query_gameplay_tags.
commands.returns: { manager_name: string, is_valid: bool, total_tags: int }

commands.name: get_object_tags
commands.description: Read the gameplay tags an object currently owns -- what the game believes this actor or asset IS (states, factions, damage types, item categories). Requires the object to implement IGameplayTagAssetInterface; anything else returns nothing, which is a fact about the interface, not about the object's data. Reads the LIVE container, so during PIE tags added at runtime appear here. has_tag / has_any_gameplay_tags answer a specific question instead of listing everything.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to get tags from

commands.returns: { object_path: string, tags: [string], tag_count: int }

commands.name: has_all_gameplay_tags
commands.description: Does the object own EVERY tag in the list (AND) -- the multi-condition gate: alive AND armed AND not restrained. Hierarchy-aware, and the direction is asymmetric: a requested tag matches when an owned tag IS it or DESCENDS from it, so asking for a family accepts its children but asking for a leaf does not accept the family. It also returns owned_tags, so a false answer is diagnosable in the same call. has_any_gameplay_tags is the OR, has_none_gameplay_tags the negation.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path of the UObject to inspect.

params.name: tags
params.description: Non-empty array of tag-name strings (e.g. ["Combat.Hit","Character.State.Alive"]).

commands.returns: { object_path, requested: [string], has_all: bool, owned_tags: [string] }

commands.name: has_any_gameplay_tags
commands.description: Does the object own AT LEAST ONE of these tags (OR) -- the "is it any kind of X" gate: any Damage.*, any Status.*, any Team.*. Hierarchy matching is ASYMMETRIC and this is where it bites: a requested FAMILY accepts its descendants, a requested LEAF does not accept the family, so swapping the two silently turns an always-true gate into an always-false one. When in doubt request leaf tags, which match either way. Unlike has_all_gameplay_tags it does not echo the owned tags, so pair a false with get_object_tags.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path of the UObject to inspect

params.name: tags
params.description: Non-empty array of tag-name strings (e.g. ["Combat.Hit","Character.State.Alive"])

commands.returns: { object_path, requested: [string], has_any: bool }

commands.name: has_none_gameplay_tags
commands.description: Does the object own NONE of these tags -- the blocker/immunity check: not stunned, not already burning, not on the excluded-faction list. Computed as !HasAny (there is no public HasNone), so it inherits the same asymmetric hierarchy matching: listing a FAMILY blocks all of its descendants, listing a LEAF blocks only that leaf. Beware the double negative -- a true here means "clear to proceed", not "has them".

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path of the UObject to inspect

params.name: tags
params.description: Non-empty array of tag-name strings to test for absence

commands.returns: { object_path, requested: [string], has_none: bool }

commands.name: has_tag
commands.description: Does this object own this gameplay tag: the single-tag state check (is it stunned, is it alerted, is it a valid target) as a plain bool. The cheapest of the tag predicates -- has_any_gameplay_tags / has_all_gameplay_tags / has_none_gameplay_tags take a list, get_object_tags returns everything. Verify the tag exists first (find_gameplay_tag): an unregistered string becomes an empty tag and returns false exactly like a genuine miss.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to check

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the tag to check for

commands.returns: { object_path: string, tag_name: string, has_tag: bool }

commands.name: query_gameplay_tags
commands.description: Search the registered gameplay tags for everything matching a pattern -- the discovery call for "what tags exist under Material.Wood" or "is there already a tag for this". Pick it over get_all_gameplay_tags, which dumps the entire project registry, and over find_gameplay_tag, which only answers about one exact string. Sees the LIVE registry, so a tag added this session by create_gameplay_tag shows up even if the ini was restored, and one that only exists as text in a file does not.

params.name: query_tag
params.description: The query tag pattern to match against all tags

commands.returns: { query_tag: string, matching_tags: [object], count: int }

commands.name: remove_gameplay_tag
commands.description: Delete a gameplay tag from its ini source list. Two cautions. Nothing tells you who was using it -- count_gameplay_tag_references always answers 0 by construction, so audit with find_blueprint_node_references and a binary grep of Content/ first, and add_gameplay_tag_redirect if anything still points at it. And like create_gameplay_tag this rewrites DefaultGameplayTags.ini wholesale, reordering it and dropping comments, so the oracle is `git diff` on the ini, not the success flag.

params.name: tag
params.description: Gameplay tag string to remove, e.g. MyGame.Temp

commands.returns: { tag: string, success: bool, was_present: bool, delete_returned: bool, removed: bool, message: string }

commands.name: remove_gameplay_tag_from_table
commands.description: Remove a gameplay tag row (by tag, the row name) from a FGameplayTagTableRow data table.  Idempotent: a missing row reports already_absent without error.  The remove counterpart of add_gameplay_tag_to_table.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the gameplay tag data table.

params.name: tag
params.description: The gameplay tag string identifying the row to remove (used as the row name).

commands.returns: { table_path: string, tag: string, row_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, row_count: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_gameplay_tag_redirect
commands.description: Delete the gameplay tag redirect(s) that rewrite a given old tag name -- cleanup once every asset has been resaved and nothing references the old name any more. Removing it too early silently breaks whatever still points at the old tag, since an unresolved tag becomes empty rather than an error. If the same old name was rewritten more than once over time there will be several entries: remove_all=true clears them all, and removed_count tells you how many went.

params.name: old_tag_name
params.description: Source tag name to unmap.

params.name: remove_all
params.description: If true (default false), remove every redirect with that OldTagName.

commands.returns: { old_tag_name, removed_count: int, already_absent: bool, total_redirects: int }

commands.name: remove_tag_from_object
commands.description: Take a gameplay tag off an object implementing IGameplayTagAssetInterface -- clearing a state (no longer stunned, no longer burning) so the systems keyed on it stop reacting. The was_present flag distinguishes "removed it" from "it was never there", and the reply echoes the remaining tags. Exact match only: removing a parent tag does not remove its children.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to remove the tag from

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the tag to remove

commands.returns: { object_path: string, tag_name: string, success: bool, was_present: bool, message: string, tags: [string] }

commands.name: validate_gameplay_tag_table
commands.description: Walk every row of a UDataTable (whose RowStruct is FGameplayTagTableRow). For each tag name, verify the tag is actually registered in the manager. Returns the list of missing tags so the user can fix the table or register the missing tags. Does NOT mutate anything.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Asset path to the UDataTable.

commands.returns: { table_path, valid: bool, row_count: int, missing_tags: [{ tag_name, row_name }] }

commands.name: append_mesh_primitive
commands.description: Append a Box, Sphere, Cylinder or Cone to the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, keeping the geometry already there: size is the box edge or the diameter and height of the round shapes, centred at location in mesh-local space. Each call adds another copy as one undo step: undo puts the mesh back as it was. Nothing is saved to an asset. An unknown actor or primitive is an error that leaves the mesh as it was; appended is true when the triangle count grew. To merge another actor's mesh use append_mesh_to_dynamic_mesh; to persist the result, copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: primitive
params.description: Box, Sphere, Cylinder, or Cone, default Box

params.name: size
params.description: Dominant dimension in cm, default 100

params.name: location
params.description: Optional local [x, y, z] offset for the primitive

params.name: dimensions
params.description: Fallback alias for size when size is omitted (cm)

params.name: material_id
params.description: Optional MaterialID stamped on the appended triangles (default 0). Non-zero enables the mesh MaterialID attribute first, so a later copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh (bUseSectionMaterials=true) emits this piece as its own section/material slot. This is how one dynamic mesh becomes a multi-slot static mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, primitive: string, size: number, material_id: int, triangle_count: int, triangles_added: int, vertex_count: int, appended: bool }

commands.name: append_mesh_to_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Merge another UDynamicMesh into the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshBasicEditFunctions::AppendMesh. One undo step puts the target mesh back as it was; the source mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor (the receiver)

params.name: source_actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the DynamicMeshActor whose dynamic mesh will be merged in

params.name: append_transform
params.description: Optional [x,y,z] world-space transform applied to the source mesh before merging (default identity)

commands.returns: { actor_name, source_actor_name, triangles_before, triangles_after, triangles_added, vertex_count_after, appended: bool } -- appended is false when the source mesh has no triangles

commands.name: apply_adaptive_remesh
commands.description: Adaptive-remesh a DynamicMeshActor's dynamic mesh using a target edge length and optional weight map. One undo step restores the mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: max_edge_length
params.description: Target edge length for adaptive remesh (sets TargetType=TargetEdgeLength + TargetEdgeLength). Required.

params.name: min_edge_length
params.description: Soft floor for adaptive edge length (default 1.0). NOTE: FGeometryScriptAdaptiveRemeshOptions has no explicit min field — this is echoed back in the result for traceability but is NOT consulted by the engine call.

params.name: relative_density
params.description: Density adjustment in [-2.0, 2.0] passed to FGeometryScriptAdaptiveRemeshOptions::RelativeDensity (default 0.0).

params.name: weight_map_name
params.description: Optional name of an existing vertex weight map (resolved via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshQueryFunctions::GetWeightMapHandle). If omitted or the mesh does not have such a layer, the engine runs adaptive remesh without a weight map (its default invalid handle).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, min_edge_length: number, max_edge_length: number, relative_density: number, weight_map_name: string, weight_map_resolved: bool, target_type: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, remeshed: bool }

commands.name: apply_mesh_boolean
commands.description: Apply a CSG boolean (Subtract by default, Union or Intersect) between the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world and a temporary primitive tool: other_primitive (Sphere by default) of size cm, offset by location in mesh-local space. The target is changed in place as one undo step that restores it, nothing is saved, and each call cuts or merges again. An unknown actor, operation or primitive is an error. When the engine refuses the result (an empty one, such as subtracting from an empty mesh) the mesh is left unchanged, boolean_applied is false and the call fails. To use another actor's mesh as the tool call apply_mesh_boolean_actor_to_actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: operation
params.description: Union, Subtract, or Intersect, default Subtract

params.name: other_primitive
params.description: Tool primitive shape, default Sphere

params.name: size
params.description: Tool primitive size in cm, default 100

params.name: location
params.description: Optional tool [x, y, z] offset

params.name: dimensions
params.description: Fallback alias for size when size is omitted (cm)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, operation: string, other_primitive: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, boolean_applied: bool }

commands.name: apply_mesh_boolean_actor_to_actor
commands.description: Apply a CSG boolean using a second DynamicMeshActor as the cutting tool. Unlike apply_mesh_boolean (which builds a transient primitive tool), the tool geometry is the live dynamic mesh of source_actor_name. The target mesh is mutated in place as one undo step that restores it; the source mesh is left untouched. NOT idempotent: re-running keeps cutting/merging the same tool against the already-modified target. When the engine refuses the result (an empty one) the target is left unchanged, boolean_applied is false and the call fails.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor (the receiver, mutated in place)

params.name: source_actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the DynamicMeshActor whose live dynamic mesh is used as the boolean tool

params.name: operation
params.description: Union, Subtract, or Intersect, default Subtract

params.name: use_world_transforms
params.description: Optional bool, default true. When true the tool is positioned by the relative world transform (source relative to target) so the boolean respects the actors' placement; when false the tool is applied at identity (co-located).

params.name: fill_holes
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshBooleanOptions.bFillHoles (default true)

params.name: simplify_output
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshBooleanOptions.bSimplifyOutput (default true)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, source_actor_name: string, operation: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, boolean_applied: bool }

commands.name: apply_mesh_morphology
commands.description: Apply an SDF-based morphology op (dilate/contract/close/open) to a DynamicMeshActor's dynamic mesh. Replaces the mesh with an SDF-based offset mesh approximation. One undo step restores the original mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: operation
params.description: Required. One of: dilate, contract, close, open.

params.name: distance
params.description: Required positive float. Offset distance in cm (SDF-based).

commands.returns: { actor_name, operation, distance, triangle_count, triangle_count_before, vertex_count, morphed }

commands.name: apply_mesh_solidify
commands.description: Voxel-wrap a DynamicMeshActor's dynamic mesh (replaces the mesh with a voxelised-and-meshed approximation). One undo step restores the original mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: winding_threshold
params.description: Optional [0..1], default 0.5. Space with generalised winding number above this is considered inside.

params.name: extend_bounds
params.description: Optional positive float, default 1.0. Bounds extension applied to the default input-mesh-based bounds.

params.name: surface_search_steps
params.description: Optional int >= 1, default 3. Marching-cubes vertex search steps.

params.name: thicken_shells
params.description: Optional bool, default false. Thicken open shells into closed solids (expensive on large meshes).

params.name: shell_thickness
params.description: Optional positive float, default 1.0. Offset distance for shell thickening.

commands.returns: { actor_name, triangle_count, triangle_count_before, vertex_count, solidified }

commands.name: apply_uniform_remesh
commands.description: Remesh the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world into evenly sized triangles, aiming at target_edge_length (cm) or target_tri_count: exactly one is required, else an error. The mesh changes in place as one undo step that restores it, and the actor's package is marked dirty, not saved. smoothing_type picks uniform, UV-preserving or mixed smoothing; an unknown value is an error. The reply echoes the settings the engine was given. remeshed is true when the triangle or vertex count changed. For variable density use apply_adaptive_remesh; to only reduce triangles, simplify_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: target_edge_length
params.description: Target uniform edge length in mesh units (sets TargetType=TargetEdgeLength). Mutually exclusive with target_tri_count; at least one is required.

params.name: target_tri_count
params.description: Approximate target triangle count (sets TargetType=TriangleCount). Mutually exclusive with target_edge_length.

params.name: preserve_sharp_edges
params.description: Approximate 'preserve sharp edges' by enabling bPreventNormalFlips on the shared RemeshOptions (default true; UE's FGeometryScriptUniformRemeshOptions has no explicit preserve-sharp flag, so the closest equivalent is the shared RemeshOptions.bPreventNormalFlips).

params.name: smoothing_type
params.description: One of 'uniform' | 'uv_preserving' | 'mixed' (default 'mixed'); maps to EGeometryScriptRemeshSmoothingType on the shared RemeshOptions.

params.name: auto_compact
params.description: Auto-compact the index space after remesh on the shared RemeshOptions (default true).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, target_edge_length: number, target_tri_count: int, preserve_sharp_edges: bool, smoothing_type: string, auto_compact: bool, target_type: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, remeshed: bool }

commands.name: auto_generate_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Compute a real UV UNWRAP for the whole mesh via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshUVFunctions::AutoGeneratePatchBuilderMeshUVs or AutoGenerateXAtlasMeshUVs. This is what sits behind the editor's "Auto UV" button. Use it when a projection is not enough (organic or mixed-orientation geometry); for plank-and-post shapes set_mesh_uvs_from_projection with box is usually cleaner and far cheaper. Both methods PACK the result into standard UV space by default, so island layout is handled too. SLOW on dense meshes: this is a solver, not a projection. A UV channel the mesh does not have, or an empty mesh, is an error; applied is false, and the call fails, leaving the UVs as they were, when the solver reports an error (xatlas needs a compact mesh: run compact_mesh first). One undo step restores the previous UVs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: method
params.description: 'patch_builder' (default, the editor's Auto UV) or 'xatlas'.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel to write (default 0).

params.name: initial_patch_count
params.description: patch_builder: how many patches to seed (default 100). More patches = less distortion, more seams.

params.name: min_patch_size
params.description: patch_builder: minimum triangles per patch (default 2).

params.name: merging_threshold
params.description: patch_builder: patch merging metric threshold (default 1.5). Higher merges more aggressively, giving fewer islands.

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: patch_builder: max angle in degrees between merged patches (default 45).

params.name: respect_polygroups
params.description: patch_builder: seed patches from the existing polygroups instead of curvature (default false). Useful right after append_mesh_primitive, where each appended face is already its own group.

params.name: auto_pack
params.description: Pack the resulting islands into standard UV space (default true).

params.name: max_iterations
params.description: xatlas: solver iterations (default 2). Higher is slower and slightly tighter.

commands.returns: { actor_name, method, uv_channel, triangle_count: int, uv_channel_count: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: build_mesh_bvh
commands.description: Build a BVH (bounding volume hierarchy) for the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world with BuildBVHForMesh, and read it back with IsBVHValidForMesh. The plugin keeps no BVH between calls: this one is dropped on return, and the spatial-query tools (find_nearest_point_on_mesh, find_nearest_ray_intersection_with_mesh, is_point_inside_mesh) build their own on every call, so they never need this first. It checks that a BVH can be built for the mesh as it is now: built is true when the engine reported no error and the BVH reads back as valid; the call fails otherwise. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: b_only_if_invalid
params.description: Optional bool, default true; it has no effect, since no earlier BVH is kept and every call builds a new one.

commands.returns: { actor_name, built: bool, b_only_if_invalid: bool, bvh_valid: bool, vertex_count, triangle_count } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; b_only_if_invalid echoes the request; the counts are those of the mesh the BVH was built for.

commands.name: clear_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Empty a DynamicMeshActor's live UDynamicMesh in place (keep the actor, drop the geometry). One undo step restores the geometry; an already empty mesh adds no undo step.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the DynamicMeshActor to clear (required).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count_before: int, triangle_count_after: int, vertex_count_before: int, vertex_count_after: int, cleared: bool }

commands.name: compact_mesh
commands.description: Compact vertex and triangle ID lists on a DynamicMeshActor's dynamic mesh, removing the gaps that deletes leave; the vertex and triangle counts stay the same. compacted is true when any ID moved. One undo step restores the previous IDs; an already compact mesh adds no undo step.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, compacted: bool }

commands.name: copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh
commands.description: Write the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor INTO an EXISTING /Game UStaticMesh asset's LOD via UGeometryScriptLibrary_StaticMeshFunctions::CopyMeshToStaticMesh (7-arg V2, bUseSectionMaterials=true; engine-default options). Editor-only (the engine function is WITH_EDITOR-gated and touches GEditor + FlushRenderingCommands). Idempotent: overwrites the target LOD in place, no duplication. HONEST GATES: the target asset must already exist (create it first, e.g. via create_editable_static_mesh) and must NOT live under /Engine/ (the engine refuses to modify built-in engine assets). A lod_index outside 0 to 7 (a static mesh has at most 8 LODs) is an error checked before anything changes; one past the asset's last LOD adds the LODs in between, which the engine sets up to be reduced from an earlier LOD.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the source DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: target_static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of an EXISTING /Game UStaticMesh to overwrite.

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional target LOD index, 0 to 7 (default 0); a negative index or one of 8 or more is refused.

params.name: materials
params.description: Optional ordered list of UMaterialInterface content paths, one per MaterialID (index 0 = MaterialID 0). Supplying it flips bReplaceMaterials on, so the target asset gets exactly these material slots. WITHOUT this the asset keeps its existing slots and a multi-MaterialID mesh collapses into whatever slots already existed — this is the parameter that makes per-triangle MaterialIDs visible on the saved asset.

params.name: material_slot_names
params.description: Optional slot names matching materials 1:1 (default: the engine names them). Ignored when materials is absent.

commands.returns: { actor_name, target_static_mesh_path, lod_index, outcome_success: bool, source_triangle_count, material_count: int, replaced_materials: bool, wrote: bool }. NOTE: this marks the target package dirty (transaction) but does NOT save to disk — persistence requires a separate save (e.g. via save_asset).

commands.name: copy_mesh_uv_channel
commands.description: Copy UV data from one UV channel to another on the same mesh. A dest_channel the mesh does not have yet is added first (the channel count only grows, and channels added in between have no UVs set); a source_channel the mesh does not have, or a dest_channel of 8 or more, is an error checked before anything changes. copied is false, and the call fails, when the engine reports an error; the same channel for both is a no-op that succeeds with copied false and a note. One undo step restores the channels, a failed copy leaves the mesh as it was, and nothing is saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: source_channel
params.description: Source UV channel index (required)

params.name: dest_channel
params.description: Destination UV channel index, 0 to 7 (required, added to the mesh when it does not have it yet)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, source_channel: int, dest_channel: int, copied: bool, num_uv_channels_after: int, note?: string } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; copied is false when source_channel equals dest_channel, and note says so or that the mesh grew new channels to reach dest_channel.

commands.name: copy_static_mesh_to_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Copy the geometry of a UStaticMesh asset INTO the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor via UGeometryScriptLibrary_StaticMeshFunctions::CopyMeshFromStaticMesh (engine-default options: build settings applied, tangents on). Destructive replace of the actor's current mesh. Idempotent-ish: re-running re-extracts the same source geometry (result depends only on the source asset + LOD). Reads the MaxAvailable LOD (LODIndex clamped to the asset's available LODs) so it is robust across meshes with fewer LODs. One undo step restores the previous mesh, and a failed copy leaves it as it was.

params.name: source_static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the source UStaticMesh (e.g. "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube").

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor whose GetDynamicMesh() receives the geometry.

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional source LOD index (default 0). LODType is MaxAvailable, so the index is silently clamped to the asset's LOD count.

commands.returns: { source_static_mesh_path, actor_name, lod_index, outcome_success: bool, triangle_count, vertex_count, copied: bool }

commands.name: delete_selected_triangles_from_mesh
commands.description: Delete the listed triangle IDs from a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world; IDs that do not exist are skipped, so compare num_deleted with requested_count. One undo step restores the triangles, and a call that deletes none adds no undo step; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: triangle_ids
params.description: Non-empty array of non-negative integer triangle IDs, e.g. [0, 5, 12]; any negative or non-numeric entry fails the call.

commands.returns: { actor_name, num_deleted, requested_count, triangle_count, previous_triangle_count }

commands.name: delete_triangle_from_mesh
commands.description: Delete one triangle by ID from a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world; a missing ID is not an error, deleted just comes back false and no undo step is added. One undo step restores a deleted triangle; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: triangle_id
params.description: Non-negative integer ID of the triangle to delete.

commands.returns: { actor_name, triangle_id, deleted, triangle_count, previous_triangle_count }

commands.name: find_nearest_point_on_mesh
commands.description: Find the nearest point on the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor to a 3D query point via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshSpatial::FindNearestPointOnMesh. Every call builds a fresh BVH from the mesh as it is now (the plugin keeps none), then queries it, so the answer always reflects the latest mesh edits. found is false when no triangle lies within max_distance, or the mesh is empty. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: query_point
params.description: [x, y, z] query point in the mesh's local space.

params.name: max_distance
params.description: Optional float; max search distance (0 = unlimited).

params.name: allow_unsafe_modified
params.description: Optional; maps to bAllowUnsafeModifiedQueries (default false). It has no effect: the BVH is built fresh on every call, so it always matches the mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name, found: bool, valid: bool, triangle_id, position_x/y/z, bary_coords_x/y/z } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label.

commands.name: find_nearest_ray_intersection_with_mesh
commands.description: Cast a ray against the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor and return the nearest hit via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshSpatial::FindNearestRayIntersectionWithMesh. Every call builds a fresh BVH from the mesh as it is now (the plugin keeps none), so the answer always reflects the latest mesh edits. The engine normalizes ray_direction, so ray_parameter is the distance from ray_origin to the hit. A ray_direction that cannot be normalized (all zeros, a non-finite value, or not an array of three numbers) is refused before anything else runs. hit is false when nothing is hit within max_distance. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: ray_origin
params.description: [x, y, z] origin point of the ray in mesh-local space.

params.name: ray_direction
params.description: [x, y, z] direction of the ray; the engine normalizes it, so its length does not matter, but a zero or non-finite direction is an error.

params.name: max_distance
params.description: Optional float; max search distance (0 = unlimited).

params.name: allow_unsafe_modified
params.description: Optional; maps to bAllowUnsafeModifiedQueries (default false). It has no effect: the BVH is built fresh on every call, so it always matches the mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name, hit: bool, ray_parameter, hit_triangle_id, hit_position_x/y/z, hit_bary_coords_x/y/z } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; ray_parameter is a distance along the normalized direction.

commands.name: generate_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Planar-project UVs for the whole live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world into channel uv_channel, overwriting it: the projection runs down mesh-local Z with 1 UV unit per cm, not fitted to 0-1. A missing channel is added first (the channel count only grows, so higher channels such as a lightmap UV1 are kept). uv_channel 8 or more, or an empty mesh, is an error checked before anything changes; uvs_generated is false (the call fails, leaving the mesh as it was) when the engine reports an error. Idempotent, nothing saved: one undo step restores the previous UVs and channel count. For box, cylinder or region projections use set_mesh_uvs_from_projection; for a real unwrap, auto_generate_mesh_uvs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV set index to write, 0 to 7, default 0

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, uv_channel: int, uv_channel_count: int, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, uvs_generated: bool }

commands.name: get_dynamic_mesh_info
commands.description: Read geometry stats off a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_internal_name: string, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, is_closed: bool, is_empty: bool }

commands.name: get_is_dense_mesh
commands.description: Return true if the mesh's triangle IDs are dense (no gaps after deletions).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name, is_dense }

commands.name: get_mesh_bounding_box
commands.description: Read the local-space axis-aligned bounding box of a static mesh via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshQueryFunctions::GetMeshBoundingBox.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset (e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Cube")

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional LOD index to query (default 0, MaxAvailable)

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, lod_index, min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z, extent_x, extent_y, extent_z, center_x, center_y, center_z }

commands.name: get_mesh_components_detail
commands.description: Enumerate the connected components (physical pieces) of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh via UE::Geometry::FMeshConnectedComponents, reporting for EACH island its triangle count, its local-space bounding box, its triangle_id range and which MaterialIDs it carries. Read-only (unlike the engine's SplitMeshByComponents, which consumes the mesh). This is the map of a mesh in ONE call, and the tool to reach for BEFORE painting anything: get_mesh_material_ids says how many triangles carry each material, and this says what those triangles physically ARE. HONEST GATE: it names nothing — it gives you sizes and positions, and which island is which part is still a human call; what it prevents is deriving that from a triangle-count assumption.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: max_components
params.description: Cap on how many islands to return (default 64). components_truncated says whether the cap cut the list; component_count is always the real total.

params.name: include_triangle_ids
params.description: Also return each island's full triangle ID list (default false; use the reported id_min/id_max range instead unless the island is non-contiguous).

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_count: int, components_truncated: bool, components: [ { index, triangle_count, id_min, id_max, id_contiguous: bool, material_ids: [int], bounds: { min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z, center_x, center_y, center_z, size_x, size_y, size_z }, triangle_ids: [int] } ] }

commands.name: get_mesh_connected_components
commands.description: Count the number of topologically separate connected components (islands) in a static mesh via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshQueryFunctions::GetNumConnectedComponents.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional LOD index to query (default 0)

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, lod_index, connected_components }

commands.name: get_mesh_has_attribute_set
commands.description: Return true if the mesh has at least one attribute set registered.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name, has_attribute_set }

commands.name: get_mesh_is_closed

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional LOD index to query (default 0)

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, lod_index, is_closed }

commands.name: get_mesh_material_ids
commands.description: Read the per-triangle MaterialID distribution of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshMaterialFunctions::GetMaxMaterialID + GetAllTriangleMaterialIDs. Read-only. This is the ORACLE for every MaterialID write: it returns a per-ID triangle histogram, so "did the paint actually land?" is answerable with a read instead of trusting a success flag. IMPORTANT: has_material_ids=false means the mesh has no MaterialID attribute at all, which is exactly the state in which writes are silently dropped by the engine.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

commands.description: Resolve a region into a selection and report its local-space BOUNDING BOX via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshSelectionQueryFunctions::GetMeshSelectionBoundingBox. Read-only. This is what turns a bisection answer ("the piece is somewhere in X>0") into actual numbers: centre and size, which is what lets you tell a 150x100x40 slab from a 14x230x75 rail without opening the editor.

commands.name: is_bvh_valid_for_mesh
commands.description: Report whether a BVH built for the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world is valid for it, via BuildBVHForMesh then UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshSpatial::IsBVHValidForMesh. The plugin keeps no BVH between calls (build_mesh_bvh and rebuild_mesh_bvh drop theirs, and the spatial-query tools build their own on every call), so no kept BVH can go stale after a mesh edit and that staleness is not tracked: this builds a BVH for the mesh as it is now and checks it, as each spatial query does. bvh_valid false means no valid BVH could be built for the mesh. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
