commands.name: is_point_inside_mesh
commands.description: Test whether a 3D point is inside the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor using Fast Winding Number via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshSpatial::IsPointInsideMesh. Every call builds a fresh BVH and fast winding tree from the mesh as it is now (the plugin keeps none), so the answer always reflects the latest mesh edits. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: query_point
params.description: [x, y, z] point in the mesh's local space.

params.name: winding_threshold
params.description: Optional float; default 0.5 (standard parity test). Higher values shrink the "inside" region.

params.name: max_distance
params.description: Optional float; it has no effect on this query, whose winding-number test uses no search distance.

params.name: allow_unsafe_modified
params.description: Optional; maps to bAllowUnsafeModifiedQueries (default false). It has no effect: the BVH is built fresh on every call, so it always matches the mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name, is_inside: bool, containment_outcome: string } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label.

commands.name: rebuild_mesh_bvh
commands.description: Build a BVH for the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor with RebuildBVHForMesh and read it back with IsBVHValidForMesh. The BVH is a temporary that is not kept: the spatial-query tools build their own on every call, so this only checks that a BVH can be built for the mesh as it is now. bvh_rebuilt is true when the engine reported no error and the BVH reads back as valid; the call fails otherwise. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: b_only_if_invalid
params.description: Optional, default true; it has no effect, since every call starts from an empty temporary BVH that the engine always rebuilds

commands.returns: { actor_name, bvh_rebuilt: bool, b_only_if_invalid, bvh_valid } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label.

commands.name: recompute_mesh_normals
commands.description: Recompute the normals of the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, overwriting the values of its existing normal overlay while keeping its hard-edge splits; a mesh without normals first gets per-vertex normals. Face contributions are weighted by area and by corner angle (both on by default; both off gives a plain average). Idempotent, nothing saved: one undo step restores the previous normals, and a recompute that changes nothing adds no undo step. An empty mesh is an error, and recomputed is false (the call fails, leaving the mesh as it was) when the engine reports an error. Use it when shading looks wrong after geometry edits; copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh persists the result.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: angle_weighted
params.description: Weight contributing face normals by corner angle, default true

params.name: area_weighted
params.description: Weight contributing face normals by face area, default true

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, angle_weighted: bool, area_weighted: bool, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, recomputed: bool }

commands.name: recompute_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Recompute UVs on a UV channel using the configured flatten method. A channel the mesh does not have, or an empty mesh, is an error; recomputed is false, and the call fails, when the engine refuses (for example polygroups on a mesh without polygroups); a failed call leaves the UVs as they were. One undo step restores the previous UVs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel index (default 0)

params.name: island_source
params.description: "uv_islands" | "polygroups" | "existing_groups" | "selection" (default "uv_islands")

params.name: method
params.description: flatten method: "spectral_conformal" (default), "conformal" or "exp_map"

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, island_source, method, recomputed }

commands.name: remap_material_ids
commands.description: Renumber MaterialIDs on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh. Two modes: pass from_material_id + to_material_id to merge one ID into another (UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshMaterialFunctions::RemapMaterialIDs), or pass compact=true with the material list to close gaps left by deleted/merged IDs (CompactMaterialIDs) and get back the compacted list to hand to copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh. Gaps matter: MaterialIDs index into that list positionally, so an unused ID in the middle costs a wasted material slot on the baked asset. The materials list may be shorter than the IDs in use (or absent): the missing entries count as no material. When no triangle carries from_material_id, or from and to are the same ID, the mesh is left unchanged and the call succeeds with applied false, triangles_remapped 0 and a note. Otherwise applied is measured (remap: the triangles that carried from_material_id no longer do; compact: the engine reported no error) and the call fails when it is false, leaving the MaterialIDs as they were. One undo step restores the previous MaterialIDs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: compact
params.description: Compact mode: renumber IDs to be contiguous from 0 (default false).

params.name: from_material_id
params.description: Remap mode: the MaterialID to replace. Required unless compact is true.

params.name: to_material_id
params.description: Remap mode: the MaterialID to replace it with. Required unless compact is true.

params.name: materials
params.description: Compact mode: ordered UMaterialInterface content paths, one per current MaterialID. The compacted list is returned in compacted_materials, in the new ID order.

params.name: remove_duplicate_materials
params.description: Compact mode: also merge IDs that point at the SAME material asset (default false).

commands.returns: { actor_name, mode: string, from_material_id: int, to_material_id: int, triangles_remapped?: int, max_material_id_after: int, distinct_material_ids_after: int, compacted_materials: [string], applied: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_dynamic_mesh_actor
commands.description: Destroy a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, found by label or object name, inside an undoable transaction. Returns the label, internal name and triangle_count_before of the destroyed actor; fails if the name matches no DynamicMeshActor. Create one with spawn_dynamic_mesh_actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the DynamicMeshActor to destroy.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_internal_name: string, destroyed: bool, triangle_count_before: int, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_unused_vertices
commands.description: Remove the vertices no triangle references from a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world and refresh its render data. Remaining vertex IDs are not renumbered and a clean mesh is a no-op that adds no undo step; otherwise one undo step restores the mesh. Returns vertex_count_before, vertex_count, vertices_removed and removed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, vertex_count_before: int, vertices_removed: int, removed: bool }

commands.name: repack_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Pack existing UV islands on a UV channel into standard UV space. A channel the mesh does not have, or an empty mesh, is an error checked before anything changes. A channel with no UVs set has no islands to pack: the call succeeds with repacked false and a note, leaving the mesh unchanged. Otherwise repacked is false, and the call fails, leaving the UVs as they were, when the engine reports an error. One undo step restores the previous UVs, nothing saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel index (default 0)

params.name: target_image_width
params.description: target image width in pixels (default 512)

params.name: optimize_island_rotation
params.description: whether to optimize island rotation (default true)

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, target_image_width, optimize_island_rotation, num_uv_islands, repacked, note? }

commands.name: repair_mesh_self_intersections
commands.description: Boolean-union a DynamicMeshActor's dynamic mesh with itself to repair self-intersections, remove internal/floating geometry and resolve non-manifold overlaps (UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshBooleanFunctions::ApplyMeshSelfUnion). Convergent: the first pass mutates the mesh, but a second pass on the already-cleaned mesh is a no-op (repaired reports false). One undo step restores the mesh, and a pass that changes nothing adds no undo step. NOTE: the engine impl ignores its internal success flag and always returns the target mesh, so success is measured by comparing the triangle count, not by the return value.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor (mutated in place)

params.name: fill_holes
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.bFillHoles (default true)

params.name: trim_flaps
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.bTrimFlaps (default true)

params.name: simplify_output
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.bSimplifyOutput (default true)

params.name: winding_threshold
params.description: Optional [0..1] float override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.WindingThreshold (default 0.5). Space with generalised winding number above this is considered inside.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, is_closed: bool, repaired: bool }

commands.name: rotate_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Rotate every vertex of the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world about the mesh-local origin, baking the rotation into the geometry; the actor transform is not touched. Rotations accumulate: each call turns the current mesh again, as one undo step that restores it; nothing saved. An empty mesh is an error; a zero rotation succeeds with applied false and a note, leaving the mesh unchanged. Use transform_dynamic_mesh to move, rotate and scale in one call, set_actor_transform to turn the actor itself, rotate_mesh_uvs to rotate UVs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: rotation
params.description: [pitch, yaw, roll] Euler rotation in degrees, applied on top of the current mesh

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, rotation_pitch: number, rotation_yaw: number, rotation_roll: number, applied: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: rotate_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Rotate all UVs of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world by an angle in degrees around a UV-space pivot; 0 degrees changes nothing (rotated false) and adds no undo step. One undo step restores the UVs; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index; a channel the mesh does not have fails the call.

params.name: rotation_angle_deg
params.description: Rotation angle in degrees; 0 leaves the UVs untouched.

params.name: rotation_origin_u
params.description: U coordinate of the rotation pivot (default 0).

params.name: rotation_origin_v
params.description: V coordinate of the rotation pivot (default 0).

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, rotation_angle_deg, rotation_origin: {u, v}, rotated: bool }

commands.name: scale_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Scale the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshTransformFunctions::ScaleMesh, as one undo step that restores the mesh. A scale that is not three numbers, or an empty mesh, is an error. A scale of 1,1,1 succeeds with applied false and a note, leaving the mesh unchanged.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: scale
params.description: [x, y, z] scale factor (1.0 = no change)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, scale_x: number, scale_y: number, scale_z: number, applied: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: scale_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Scale all UVs of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world by separate U and V factors; zero factors are refused and 1, 1 changes nothing (scaled false) and adds no undo step. One undo step restores the UVs; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index; a channel the mesh does not have fails the call.

params.name: scale_u
params.description: Scale factor along U; must be non-zero (1 keeps U unchanged).

params.name: scale_v
params.description: Scale factor along V; must be non-zero (1 keeps V unchanged).

params.name: scale_origin_u
params.description: U coordinate of the point the scaling is centred on (default 0).

params.name: scale_origin_v
params.description: V coordinate of the point the scaling is centred on (default 0).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, uv_channel: int, scale_u: number, scale_v: number, scale_origin: { u, v }, scaled: bool }

commands.name: select_mesh_triangles
commands.description: Resolve a region into a triangle selection and REPORT it, without modifying anything. Read-only companion of set_mesh_material_id_in_region: same region parameters, same resolver, so a region previewed here paints exactly those triangles there. Use it to avoid the failure mode where a mis-specified box selects 0 triangles and the paint call still returns success. Coordinates are LOCAL to the dynamic mesh, not world.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: region
params.description: 'all' (default) | 'box' | 'sphere' | 'plane' | 'normal_angle' | 'material_id' | 'polygroup' | 'connected_component' (one physical PIECE, by the island index that get_mesh_components_detail reports).

params.name: center
params.description: Local [x,y,z] centre. Used by box/sphere, and as the plane origin.

params.name: extent
params.description: Local [x,y,z] HALF-size in cm. Required by region='box'.

params.name: radius
params.description: Radius in cm. Required by region='sphere'.

params.name: normal
params.description: [x,y,z] direction. Plane normal for region='plane', facing direction for 'normal_angle'. Default [0,0,1].

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: Max angle from normal in degrees for region='normal_angle' (default 15).

params.name: source_material_id
params.description: MaterialID to select when region='material_id'.

params.name: polygroup_id
params.description: Polygroup to select when region='polygroup'.

params.name: polygroup_layer
params.description: Optional extended polygroup layer index for region='polygroup'.

params.name: component_index
params.description: Island index when region='connected_component'. Get it from get_mesh_components_detail, which reports each piece's size and bounding box.

params.name: min_triangle_points
params.description: How many of a triangle's 3 points must be inside for it to count, 1-3 (default 3 = fully contained).

params.name: invert
params.description: Invert the spatial selection (default false).

params.name: include_triangle_ids
params.description: Also return the resolved triangle IDs (default false; they can be thousands). The returned array is what set_mesh_material_id scope='triangles' consumes.

params.name: max_triangle_ids
params.description: Cap on how many IDs to return when include_triangle_ids is on (default 1000). When the cap truncates, triangle_ids_truncated is true — the count in triangles_selected is still the real one.

commands.returns: { actor_name, region, triangles_selected: int, mesh_triangle_count: int, is_empty: bool, triangle_ids: [int], triangle_ids_truncated: bool }

commands.name: set_dynamic_mesh_material
commands.description: Assign a UMaterialInterface asset to a slot on a DynamicMeshActor's UDynamicMeshComponent, in an editor transaction. applied is the slot read back after the assignment; the call fails when it does not hold the material.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor (required).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface (e.g. /Engine/EngineMaterials/DefaultMaterial) (required).

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Material slot to assign. Default 0 (the dynamic mesh only uses slot 0).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, material_path: string, material_name: string, slot_index: int, applied: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: set_mesh_material_id
commands.description: Stamp a MaterialID onto triangles of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh. scope='all' repaints every triangle (UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshMaterialFunctions::ClearMaterialIDs); scope='triangles' repaints the listed triangle IDs (SetMaterialIDOnTriangles). Calls EnableMaterialIDs first, because on a mesh without that attribute the engine drops the write. An ID in triangle_ids that is not a triangle, or an empty mesh, is an error checked before anything is painted. The targeted triangles are read back: applied is true when all of them carry material_id, and the call fails otherwise, leaving the MaterialIDs as they were. One undo step restores the previous MaterialIDs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: material_id
params.description: MaterialID to write (>= 0). Index into the material list later passed to copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: scope
params.description: 'all' (default) or 'triangles'.

params.name: triangle_ids
params.description: Required when scope='triangles': array of triangle IDs to repaint (e.g. from select_mesh_triangles).

commands.returns: { actor_name, material_id, scope, triangles_targeted: int, triangles_painted: int, max_material_id_after: int, distinct_material_ids_after: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_mesh_material_id_in_region
commands.description: Stamp a MaterialID onto every triangle inside a region, via the engine's SelectMeshElements* family + SetMaterialIDForMeshSelection. Use this when polygroups are not usable: after a boolean, appended pieces are fused and set_polygroup_material_id cannot address them separately. Coordinates are LOCAL to the dynamic mesh, not world. Preview any region with select_mesh_triangles before painting: a region that selects 0 triangles still returns success, and adds no undo step. One undo step restores the previous MaterialIDs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: material_id
params.description: MaterialID to write (>= 0).

params.name: region
params.description: 'all' (default) | 'box' | 'sphere' | 'plane' | 'normal_angle' | 'material_id' | 'polygroup' | 'connected_component' (one physical PIECE, by the island index that get_mesh_components_detail reports).

params.name: center
params.description: Local [x,y,z] centre. Used by box/sphere, and as the plane origin.

params.name: extent
params.description: Local [x,y,z] HALF-size in cm. Required by region='box'.

params.name: radius
params.description: Radius in cm. Required by region='sphere'.

params.name: normal
params.description: [x,y,z] direction. Plane normal for region='plane', facing direction for 'normal_angle'. Default [0,0,1].

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: Max angle from normal in degrees for region='normal_angle' (default 15).

params.name: source_material_id
params.description: The MaterialID to SELECT when region='material_id'. Separate from material_id, which is the one being written, so 'repaint 1 as 2' is expressible.

params.name: polygroup_id
params.description: Polygroup to select when region='polygroup'.

params.name: polygroup_layer
params.description: Optional extended polygroup layer index for region='polygroup'.

params.name: component_index
params.description: Island index when region='connected_component'. Get it from get_mesh_components_detail, which reports each piece's size and bounding box.

params.name: min_triangle_points
params.description: How many of a triangle's 3 points must be inside for it to count, 1-3 (default 3 = fully contained). Only used by the spatial regions.

params.name: invert
params.description: Invert the spatial selection (default false).

commands.returns: { actor_name, material_id, region, triangles_selected: int, max_material_id_after: int, distinct_material_ids_after: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_mesh_uv_element_position
commands.description: Set the (u, v) of one element of a UV channel overlay on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world; an invalid element ID writes nothing, adds no undo step and returns is_valid_element false, not an error. One undo step restores the element; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index; a channel the mesh does not have fails the call.

params.name: element_id
params.description: ID of the element in the UV overlay of that channel, not a vertex, edge or triangle ID.

params.name: u
params.description: New U coordinate of the element.

params.name: v
params.description: New V coordinate of the element.

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, element_id, new_position: {u, v}, is_valid_element, set: bool }

commands.name: set_mesh_uvs_from_projection
commands.description: Replace the UVs of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world with a box, plane or cylinder projection, optionally only inside a region. Box suits plank-and-post geometry (each face takes the axis it faces), plane only flat pieces, cylinder wrapped shapes. One undo step restores the previous UVs. Returns triangles_affected and applied.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: projection
params.description: 'box' (default) | 'plane' | 'cylinder'.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel to write (default 0).

params.name: location
params.description: Local [x,y,z] origin of the projection shape (default the mesh origin).

params.name: rotation
params.description: [pitch, yaw, roll] of the projection shape (default none). For 'plane', this is what chooses which way the plane faces.

params.name: scale
params.description: [x,y,z] size of the projection shape (default [100,100,100]). THIS IS THE UV DENSITY KNOB: bigger scale = texture repeats fewer times. A tileable material that reads too big or too small is fixed here, not in the material.

params.name: min_island_tri_count
params.description: box only: islands smaller than this are merged into a neighbour (default 2).

params.name: split_angle
params.description: cylinder only: angle in degrees at which the wrap is split (default 45).

params.name: region
params.description: Optional region to limit the projection to; same vocabulary as select_mesh_triangles (default 'all').

params.name: component_index
params.description: Island index when region='connected_component'.

params.name: center
params.description: Region parameter (box/sphere centre, plane origin).

params.name: extent
params.description: Region parameter: box HALF-size.

params.name: radius
params.description: Region parameter: sphere radius.

params.name: normal
params.description: Region parameter: plane/normal_angle direction.

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: Region parameter for region='normal_angle'.

params.name: source_material_id
params.description: Region parameter for region='material_id'.

params.name: polygroup_id
params.description: Region parameter for region='polygroup'.

params.name: polygroup_layer
params.description: Region parameter for region='polygroup': extended polygroup layer index (default the mesh's default polygroup layer).

params.name: min_triangle_points
params.description: Region parameter, 1-3.

params.name: invert
params.description: Select the complement of a box, sphere, plane or normal_angle region (default false); the other regions ignore it.

commands.returns: { actor_name, projection, uv_channel, region, triangles_affected: int, uv_channel_count: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_num_extended_polygroup_layers
commands.description: Set the number of extended polygroup layers on the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshPolygroupFunctions::SetNumExtendedPolygroupLayers. Idempotent: the engine dedups (only reshapes attributes when the count actually differs from the current one), so re-setting the same count is a no-op. The layer count is read back AFTER the set via GetNumExtendedPolygroupLayers: applied is true when it equals the request, and the call fails, leaving the mesh as it was, when it does not. One undo step restores the previous layers.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: num_layers
params.description: Desired number of extended polygroup layers (>= 0).

commands.returns: { actor_name, requested_num_layers, num_polygroup_layers, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_num_uv_channels
commands.description: Set how many UV channels the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world has: added channels start without UVs, and channels from num_uv_channels upward are discarded with their UVs (note says so). The current count is a no-op (changed false). The engine allows at most 8, so a count above 8 is an error; num_uv_channels is the count read back after the call, and the call fails, leaving the mesh as it was, if it differs from the request. One undo step restores the previous channels with their UVs, nothing saved; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label. Fill a channel with copy_mesh_uv_channel or generate_mesh_uvs; clear_uv_channel works on static mesh assets.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: num_uv_channels
params.description: Desired count, 0 to 8 (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, num_uv_channels: int, previous_num_uv_channels: int, changed: bool, note?: string } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; num_uv_channels is read back; note when channels were removed, whose UV data is dropped.

commands.name: set_polygroup_material_id
commands.description: Stamp a MaterialID onto every triangle of one polygroup via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshMaterialFunctions::SetPolygroupMaterialID. This is usually the cheapest way to paint a part: append_mesh_primitive lays primitives down with PerFace polygroups, so each appended piece is already its own group. HONEST GATE: the engine reports whether the polygroup ID actually existed, and that flag is surfaced as polygroup_id_valid: a false there means nothing was painted, even though the call succeeded, and no undo step is added. One undo step restores the previous MaterialIDs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: polygroup_id
params.description: Polygroup ID to repaint.

params.name: material_id
params.description: MaterialID to write (>= 0).

params.name: polygroup_layer
params.description: Optional extended polygroup layer index. Omit for the default layer.

commands.returns: { actor_name, polygroup_id, material_id, polygroup_id_valid: bool, max_material_id_after: int, distinct_material_ids_after: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: simplify_mesh
commands.description: QEM-simplify a DynamicMeshActor's dynamic mesh to a target triangle count. One undo step restores the mesh; a call that changes nothing adds no undo step.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: target_triangle_count
params.description: Target triangle count to simplify down to (must be > 0)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, target_triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, triangle_count_after: int, vertex_count: int, simplified: bool }

commands.name: spawn_dynamic_mesh_actor
commands.description: Spawn an empty ADynamicMeshActor into the editor world (not PIE) at an optional location and rotation, ignoring collisions, in an undoable transaction. Returns the label of the new actor as actor_name, its internal name and triangle_count (0). Remove it with remove_dynamic_mesh_actor.

params.name: location
params.description: World location [x, y, z] in cm (default the world origin).

params.name: rotation
params.description: World rotation in degrees as [pitch, yaw, roll] (default no rotation).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_internal_name: string, actor_class: string, has_dynamic_mesh_component: bool, has_dynamic_mesh: bool, triangle_count: int, spawned: bool }

commands.name: transform_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Apply a full FTransform (translation + rotation + scale) to the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshTransformFunctions::TransformMesh, as one undo step that restores the mesh. A location or scale that is not three numbers, or an empty mesh, is an error. An identity transform succeeds with applied false and a note, leaving the mesh unchanged.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] translation; default (0,0,0)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation; default (0,0,0)

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] scale; default (1,1,1)

commands.name: translate_dynamic_mesh

commands.name: build_hlod
commands.description: Triggers a world HLOD build for the current editor world.  This is a HEAVY/async operation that requires a World Partition world plus the WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder commandlet / a long-running editor build job, so it cannot be driven synchronously from a single request. The tool does the headless-safe part for real (resolves the editor world, detects World Partition) and returns an honest result: build_started is false with a note explaining why (not a World Partition map, or async/commandlet-only).
commands.returns: { world: string, is_world_partition: bool, build_started: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: create_hlod_layer
commands.description: Creates and saves a new UHLODLayer (World Partition HLOD layer) asset.  Idempotent on re-run. Sets default streaming-grid cell_size=25600, loading_range=51200. Layer type accepts 'Instancing', 'MeshApproximate' (also 'Custom'/'CustomHLODActor'). Defaults to 'Instancing'.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new HLOD layer asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder; defaults to /Game/HLOD

params.name: layer_type
params.description: Optional EHLODLayerType string; defaults to "Instancing"

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, layer_type: string, cell_size: int, loading_range: number, created: bool, already_exists?: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: get_hlod_layer_actors
commands.description: Enumerate which LOADED actors in the current editor world are assigned to a given UHLODLayer (read-side of set_hlod_layer_actors). Two limits worth knowing before you trust an empty result: it only sees actors currently loaded, and it is WORLD PARTITION ONLY -- on a non-WP world it returns not_applicable=true with a note instead of a list, because there the assignment would not survive a Generate anyway.

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Full /Game path of the UHLODLayer asset (matches against AActor::HLODLayer::GetPathName()).

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path, world, is_world_partition, not_applicable, note?, total: int, actors: [{actor_name, actor_path, actor_label}] }

commands.name: get_hlod_layer_info
commands.description: Reads layer type and streaming-grid settings of a UHLODLayer.

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the HLOD layer asset

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path: string, asset_path: string, name: string, layer_type: string, cell_size: int, loading_range: number, is_spatially_loaded: bool }

commands.description: Lists all UHLODLayer assets under a content path via the AssetRegistry.

params.name: path
params.description: Optional content path; defaults to /Game

commands.returns: { path: string, hlod_layers: [{ name, path, layer_type }], count: int }

commands.name: remove_hlod_layer
commands.description: Destroy a UHLODLayer asset at a /Game path (mirror of create_hlod_layer). Typed-delete: it loads the asset and REFUSES to delete it if it is not a UHLODLayer, so it cannot wipe the wrong asset the way the generic delete_asset can. Idempotent on missing assets.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full /Game/.../LayerName asset path.

commands.returns: { asset_path, deleted, already_existed, layer_type?, note? }

commands.name: set_hlod_layer_actors
commands.description: Assign a UHLODLayer to a BATCH of loaded actors in the current editor world -- or clear it from them by passing hlod_layer_path="". WORLD PARTITION ONLY: on a non-WP world it returns not_applicable=true and changes nothing. Idempotent per actor: one that already has that layer is not touched at all and comes back counted as unchanged, so the changed/unchanged/cleared split tells you exactly what really moved.

params.name: actor_paths
params.description: JSON array of actor paths (long package paths or object paths) to assign.

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Full /Game path of the UHLODLayer asset. Pass empty string ("") to clear.

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path, world, is_world_partition, not_applicable, note?, requested: int, changed: int, unchanged: int, cleared: int, not_found: [paths], changed_actors: [{actor_path, old_hlod_layer, new_hlod_layer}] }

commands.name: set_hlod_layer_parent
commands.description: Sets (or clears) the parent UHLODLayer of a UHLODLayer and saves it.  The parent chain drives nested HLOD generation (a layer's HLOD becomes an input to its parent's HLOD). Send parent_layer_path="" to clear the parent to null; omit parent_layer_path to leave it untouched. Idempotent: if the parent is already the requested value, nothing is modified/saved (changed_parent=false). Validates against self-parent and circular parent chains (the engine's guard is editor-only and does not run headless).

commands.name: set_hlod_layer_settings
commands.description: Sets streaming-grid settings / layer type on a UHLODLayer and saves it.  Partial update: only the fields you send are touched. Sending cell_size or loading_range also enables the layer spatially loaded. Layer type accepts 'Instancing'|'MeshApproximate'|'Custom'|'CustomHLODActor'.

params.description: Optional streaming-grid loading range

params.description: Optional EHLODLayerType string

commands.name: add_input_modifier
commands.description: Reshape the VALUE a key sends before the action sees it: append a modifier (Negate to flip an axis, Swizzle to remap X/Y/Z, DeadZone for stick drift, Scalar for sensitivity) to a key mapping in a mapping context. This is how one Axis2D action serves WASD -- S is W negated, not a second action. Modifiers change the value, triggers change when it fires (add_input_trigger); list_input_modifier_types enumerates the classes, remove_input_modifier undoes it by index. The context is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputMappingContext.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputAction.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name of the mapping the modifier is attached to.

params.name: modifier_type
params.description: One of "Negate", "Swizzle", "DeadZone", "Scalar".

params.name: context_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Mapping Context

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: key_name
params.description: Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom)

commands.returns: { context_name, action_name, key, modifier_type, modifier_class, index, modifier_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: add_input_trigger
commands.description: Decide WHEN a key fires its action: append a trigger (Down / Pressed / Released / Hold / Tap / Pulse / ChordAction) so a key can mean tap-to-do-X and hold-to-do-Y instead of consuming two keys. Targets either one key mapping inside a mapping context (pass context + key) or, with no context and no key, the InputAction asset's own Triggers array -- the difference decides whether the rule applies to that binding or to the action everywhere, so a key without a context is refused rather than read as the action. The edited asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Tune it afterwards with set_input_action_trigger_behavior; list_input_trigger_types enumerates the classes.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputAction.

params.name: trigger_type
params.description: One of "Down", "Pressed", "Released", "Hold", "Tap", "Pulse", "ChordAction".

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputMappingContext. Omit it (and context_path) to append the trigger to the InputAction asset's own Triggers array instead of one of its key mappings.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name of the mapping the trigger is attached to: required with a context, and refused when there is no context.

params.name: context_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Mapping Context, instead of context_name.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: key_name
params.description: Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom)

commands.returns: Context target: { context_name, action_name, key, trigger_type, trigger_class, index, trigger_count, saved, save_error? }; Action target: { action_name, action_path, trigger_type, trigger_class, index, trigger_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: add_mapping_to_context
commands.description: Bind a key to an InputAction in a saved Enhanced Input mapping context, addressing both by SHORT ASSET NAME (IMC_Foo / IA_Bar) instead of full paths -- otherwise the same operation as map_input_action, which takes paths. Returns the mapping index, which is what add_input_trigger / add_input_modifier / list_input_triggers address. A context that already maps that key to that action keeps its mapping (added false, already_mapped true, not saved); a new mapping succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Other actions on the same key are not checked: use find_free_input_key first.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputMappingContext (e.g. IMC_Example).

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputAction (e.g. IA_Example).

params.name: key
params.description: Key name to map (e.g. "SpaceBar", "W", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom").

params.name: context_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Mapping Context

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: key_name
params.description: Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom)

commands.returns: { context_name, context_path, action_name, key, index, mapping_count, added, already_mapped, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: create_force_feedback_effect
commands.description: Create a UForceFeedbackEffect data asset (NewObject + save).  Seeds the effect with one default FForceFeedbackChannelDetails so it is a meaningful, non-empty asset. Idempotent: if the asset already exists it is loaded and returned.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. FFE_Rumble)

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/Gameplay")

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, channel_detail_count: number, is_force_feedback_effect: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: create_input_action
commands.description: Create an Enhanced Input InputAction asset (IA_): the verb half of a keybinding -- what the player does, independent of which key does it. Pick value_type up front (Bool for a button, Axis1D for a trigger/scroll, Axis2D for a stick or WASD, Axis3D), then bind it to a key inside a mapping context with map_input_action or add_mapping_to_context. Changing the type later is set_input_action_value_type; behaviour flags are set_input_action_flags. The asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Name of the new InputAction.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Input).

params.name: path
params.description: Fallback for package_path when package_path is absent.

params.name: value_type
params.description: Value type Bool (default), Axis1D, Axis2D, or Axis3D.

commands.returns: { action_name, action_path, value_type, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: create_input_mapping_context
commands.description: Create an Enhanced Input mapping context asset (IMC_): the container that binds keys to InputActions and can be pushed and popped as a set. Prefer a context per MODE (driving, swimming, building, menu) over one key per verb -- pushing a context re-purposes the existing keys instead of consuming another global one. Empty on creation: fill it with map_input_action / add_mapping_to_context, and check the keys are free first with find_free_input_key. The asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Name of the new InputMappingContext.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Input).

params.name: path
params.description: Fallback for package_path when package_path is absent.

commands.returns: { context_name, context_path, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: discover_input_types
commands.description: One-call inventory of what Enhanced Input offers in this build: every value type plus every concrete modifier and trigger subclass, including any the project or a plugin added. Run it before add_input_trigger / add_input_modifier so you pass a class that actually exists instead of guessing a name. Superset of list_input_modifier_types and list_input_trigger_types, which return the same lists one at a time. Read-only.
commands.returns: { modifier_count, trigger_count, modifier_types: [...], trigger_types: [...] }

commands.name: find_free_input_key
commands.description: Which keys are still FREE: lists every input key not bound by any Enhanced Input mapping context or legacy mapping, filterable by category (keyboard / gamepad / mouse / touch) and substring. The complement of list_all_input_mappings and the tool to run before binding a new keyboard shortcut, since a collision compiles silently and only shows up in play. Trustworthy where the Python route is not: InputMappingContext.mappings is deprecated and returns empty, which makes every taken key look available.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring matched against the key name or display name.

params.name: category
params.description: Optional key category filter: one of 'keyboard', 'gamepad', 'mouse', 'touch'. Absent = all categories.

params.name: bindable_only
params.description: When true (default), only keys where FKey::IsBindableInBlueprints() is true are considered (skips AnyKey/gestures/etc.).

commands.returns: { free_keys:[{key,display_name,is_gamepad,is_mouse,is_analog}], free_key_count, bound_key_count, bound_keys:[...] }

commands.name: get_action_mappings
commands.description: List the project's LEGACY action key mappings only (action_name + key + shift/ctrl/alt/cmd), with a count. Narrower than get_input_settings, which returns actions and axes together, and blind to Enhanced Input mapping contexts -- an empty list does not mean the game has no buttons bound. Use list_all_input_mappings when the question is "is this key already taken".
commands.returns: { action_name, key, shift, ctrl, alt, cmd, action_mappings, count }

commands.name: get_available_keys
commands.description: List the input key NAMES the engine knows (keyboard, mouse, gamepad, touch), with an optional substring filter -- how you find the exact spelling a binding call needs ("SpaceBar", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom", "LeftMouseButton") instead of guessing. "Available" here means the engine defines it, NOT that it is unbound: for keys that are actually free use find_free_input_key, and for what is already taken list_all_input_mappings.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to filter key names

commands.returns: { count, keys: [...] }

commands.name: get_axis_mappings
commands.description: List the project's LEGACY axis key mappings only (axis_name + key + scale), with a count -- the analog/movement half of the legacy input system. Blind to Enhanced Input mapping contexts, so an empty list is not proof that movement is unbound; get_input_settings returns actions and axes together, and list_all_input_mappings covers both systems.
commands.returns: { axis_name, key, scale, axis_mappings, count }

commands.name: get_input_action
commands.description: Read one Enhanced Input InputAction asset in full: its value type (Bool / Axis1D / Axis2D / Axis3D), its accumulation behaviour, all the consume/pause/reserve flags, and the triggers and modifiers attached to the ACTION itself. The read-back oracle for create_input_action, set_input_action_value_type and set_input_action_flags, and the place to check b_consume_input -- an action left consuming input can swallow a key for the whole game. Triggers listed here are the action's own; the ones on a specific key binding live in the mapping context (list_input_triggers).

params.name: action_path
params.description: Full path to the InputAction asset (e.g., /Game/Input/IA_Jump).

params.name: action_name
params.description: Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent (short asset name).

commands.returns: { action_path, action_name, value_type, accumulation_behavior, b_consume_input, b_trigger_when_paused, b_consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, b_reserve_all_mappings, trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys, action_description, b_tap, triggers, modifiers }

commands.name: get_input_action_state
commands.description: Read the live Enhanced Input state of one InputAction for a local player in a running PIE or game session: is_tracked, trigger_events, value, last_triggered_world_time and the mapping contexts that carry it, applied or not. It is the oracle for whether an input fired, since inject_key_input and trigger_input_action succeed either way: read it before and after, and an advancing last_triggered_world_time is the proof. is_mapped_in_applied_context false means no applied context maps it (removed on mounting, in a vehicle or a menu); is_tracked false means the engine is not evaluating it, typically an unpossessed pawn. In co-op, world picks which local player is read.

params.name: action
params.description: InputAction to read: full object path or short asset name. Aliases: action_path, action_name.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Local player index (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: World selector: 'pie' (default) | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game'.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Alias of action, read when action is absent or empty: InputAction object path or short asset name.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Alias of action, read only when action is absent or empty and action_path is absent: InputAction object path or short asset name.

commands.returns: { action_path: string, action_name: string, value_type: string, is_enhanced_input: bool, is_tracked: bool, is_mapped_in_applied_context: bool, trigger_event: number, trigger_events: array, value: array, elapsed_seconds: number, triggered_seconds: number, last_triggered_world_time: number, world_time_seconds: number, contexts_mapping_action: array, contexts_mapping_action_count: number, applied_context_count: number, player_index: number, player_controller: string, player_input_class: string, world: string, note: string }

commands.name: get_input_mapping_context
commands.description: Read ONE Enhanced Input mapping context asset (IMC): every action-to-key mapping it declares. An IMC asset stores no priority -- that is given when the context is added to a player (AddMappingContext), so it is not reported here. The per-asset reader, and the reliable one -- the Python property InputMappingContext.mappings is deprecated and hands back an EMPTY list without failing, so a scan built on it reports a fully-bound context as empty. Use list_all_input_mappings for the project-wide "which keys are taken / which conflict" question.

params.name: context_path
params.description: Full path to the InputMappingContext asset (e.g., /Game/Input/IMC_Default).

commands.returns: { context_path, context_name, mappings: [{ action_name, key (display name), key_name (the FKey name map_input_action takes) }], mapping_count }

commands.name: get_input_settings
commands.description: Read the project's LEGACY input mappings from UInputSettings: named action mappings (key + shift/ctrl/alt/cmd modifiers) and axis mappings (key + scale), in one call. Legacy only -- it does NOT see Enhanced Input mapping contexts, so on an Enhanced Input project it can return almost nothing while the game is fully bound. For the complete picture across both systems use list_all_input_mappings; for one Enhanced Input context use get_input_mapping_context.
commands.returns: { action_name, key, shift, ctrl, alt, cmd, action_mappings, axis_name, scale, axis_mappings }

commands.name: get_player_input
commands.description: Read what a player is pressing RIGHT NOW: resolves the PlayerController for a local player index and returns it plus the currently pressed keys. Runtime state, so it needs a live PIE/game session -- an empty pressed_keys outside PIE means nothing. For which keys are BOUND (a static question) use list_all_input_mappings instead; to make an action fire use trigger_input_action.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Player controller index to query (default 0).

commands.returns: { player_controller, pressed_keys }

commands.name: list_all_input_mappings
commands.description: Which keys are already TAKEN, and which ones CONFLICT: aggregates every key-to-action binding across ALL Enhanced Input mapping context assets plus the legacy InputSettings action/axis mappings, and flags any key bound to more than one distinct action. Run it BEFORE claiming a new key -- a keybinding collision does not fail to compile, it surfaces weeks later inside another system. This is the aggregate you can trust: the Python route (InputMappingContext.mappings) is deprecated and returns an EMPTY list, which reads as "every key is free" even when every letter is taken. Use find_free_input_key for the complement (what is still unbound), get_input_mapping_context for one context.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring on the key name to narrow the returned key_bindings.

params.name: conflicts_only
params.description: When true, return only keys flagged as conflicts (more than one distinct action on the same key). Default false.

commands.returns: { contexts:[{context_path,context_name,mapping_count}], context_count, key_bindings:[{key,display_name,bindings:[{action,source,context_path}],binding_count,distinct_action_count,conflict}], bound_key_count, conflicts:[...], conflict_count, legacy_action_mapping_count, legacy_axis_mapping_count }

commands.name: list_input_modifier_types
commands.description: List the concrete input modifier classes available in this build (Negate, Swizzle, DeadZone, Scalar and any project/plugin ones) -- the valid values for add_input_modifier. Read-only. Use discover_input_types to get modifiers, triggers and value types in a single call.
commands.returns: { count, types: [...] }

commands.name: list_input_trigger_types
commands.description: List the concrete input trigger classes available in this build (Down, Pressed, Released, Hold, Tap, Pulse, ChordAction and any project/plugin ones) -- the valid values for add_input_trigger. Read-only. Use discover_input_types to get triggers, modifiers and value types in a single call.
commands.returns: { count, types: [...] }

commands.name: list_input_triggers
commands.description: List the triggers attached to ONE key mapping inside an Enhanced Input mapping context, addressed by mapping_index, with each trigger's class and index. The read-back for add_input_trigger and the way to find the trigger_index that remove_input_trigger needs. Scoped to the binding: triggers living on the InputAction asset itself show up in get_input_action instead.

params.name: ctx_path
params.description: Asset path of the UInputMappingContext

params.name: mapping_index
params.description: 0-based index of the FEnhancedActionKeyMapping within Mappings[]

commands.returns: { count, triggers: [{index, class_name, display_name}] }

commands.name: map_input_action
commands.description: Bind a key to an InputAction in an Enhanced Input mapping context, both by full asset path (add_mapping_to_context takes short names), and save the context. A context that already maps that key to that action is left as it is (added false, already_mapped true, not saved); a new mapping succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Other actions on the same key are not checked: use find_free_input_key or list_all_input_mappings first.

params.name: context_path
params.description: Full path to the InputMappingContext asset.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Full path to the InputAction asset.

params.name: key_name
params.description: Key name to map (e.g., "SpaceBar", "LeftMouseButton").

params.name: key
params.description: Alias of key_name, read only when key_name is absent (same FKey names).

params.name: input_action_path
params.description: Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent.

commands.returns: { context_path, action_path, key_name, index, mapping_count, added, already_mapped, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: register_input_key_mapping
commands.description: Remaps a player input mapping to a new key at runtime via UEnhancedInputUserSettings::MapPlayerKey (EnhancedInputUserSettings.h). Wraps FMapPlayerKeyArgs with the supplied mapping name + new key + slot. The call fails when the engine refuses the remap, with its reasons in failure_tags.

params.name: mapping_name
params.description: FName of the source mapping inside an already-mapped IMC (required)

params.name: new_key
params.description: FKey name (e.g. "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom") (required)

params.name: player_controller_name
params.description: Optional editor-world APlayerController actor name (defaults to first local player)

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index used to resolve the PlayerController (default 0).

params.name: slot
params.description: "First" | "Second" | "Third" | "Fourth" (default "First"); EPlayerMappableKeySlot enum

commands.returns: { applied: bool, mapping_name: string, new_key: string, slot: string, failure_tags: [string] }

commands.name: remove_input_modifier
commands.description: Delete one modifier from a key mapping in an Enhanced Input mapping context, by mapping_index + modifier_index -- e.g. removing a Negate that flipped an axis the wrong way -- and save the context; the call succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Indices shift after a removal, so work from the highest down. add_input_modifier is the inverse.

params.name: ctx_path
params.description: Asset path of the UInputMappingContext

params.name: mapping_index
params.description: 0-based index of the FEnhancedActionKeyMapping

params.name: modifier_index
params.description: 0-based index of the modifier within Mapping.Modifiers

commands.returns: { applied, removed_class_name, remaining_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: remove_input_trigger
commands.description: Delete one trigger from a key mapping in an Enhanced Input mapping context, by mapping_index + trigger_index -- e.g. dropping a Hold so the key fires immediately again -- and save the context; the call succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Get the indices from list_input_triggers; they shift after a removal, so work from the highest down.

params.name: ctx_path
params.description: Asset path of the UInputMappingContext

params.name: mapping_index
params.description: 0-based index of the FEnhancedActionKeyMapping

params.name: trigger_index
params.description: 0-based index of the trigger within Mapping.Triggers

commands.returns: { applied, removed_class_name, remaining_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: remove_mapping_from_context
commands.description: Unbind a key from an InputAction in a saved Enhanced Input mapping context -- how you free a key that list_all_input_mappings flagged as conflicting, or retire a verb. Identified by context + action + key, so only the first mapping of that action to that key goes; the assets themselves survive. The engine moves the context's last mapping into the freed slot, so mapping indexes (add_input_trigger, list_input_triggers) can change. The context is saved, and a removal succeeds only when it reaches disk; a mapping that is not there succeeds with removed false and already_absent true, and saves nothing.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputMappingContext.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputAction.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name of the mapping to remove.

params.name: context_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Mapping Context

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: key_name
params.description: Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom)

commands.returns: { context_name, action_name, key, removed, already_absent, mapping_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_input_action_flags
commands.description: Set an InputAction's behaviour flags: consume_input, trigger_when_paused, consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, reserve_all_mappings, the legacy-key consume bitmask, accumulation behaviour and the editor description. Handle consume_input with care -- it is the flag that decides whether OTHER actions on the same key still fire, and turning it on can swallow the game's interaction key entirely, a failure that shows up in an unrelated system days later. Only the fields you pass change, and a call that passes none is an error; the action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Verify with get_input_action.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Input action name

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: consume_input
params.description: When set, updates the action's bConsumeInput flag.

params.name: trigger_when_paused
params.description: When set, updates the action's bTriggerWhenPaused flag.

params.name: consumes_action_and_axis_mappings
params.description: When set, updates bConsumesActionAndAxisMappings.

params.name: reserve_all_mappings
params.description: When set, updates bReserveAllMappings.

params.name: trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys
params.description: When set (int32 ETriggerEvent bitmask), updates TriggerEventsThatConsumeLegacyKeys.

params.name: accumulation_behavior
params.description: When set, one of "TakeHighestAbsoluteValue" or "Cumulative".

params.name: action_description
params.description: When set, updates the action's ActionDescription (FText) shown in the editor.

commands.returns: { action_name, action_path, b_consume_input, b_trigger_when_paused, b_consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, b_reserve_all_mappings, trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys, accumulation_behavior, action_description, flags_set, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_input_action_trigger_behavior
commands.description: Tune HOW an input trigger fires on an InputAction: actuation threshold, hold time and one-shot for Hold triggers, tap release window for Tap, time-dilation sensitivity for timed ones -- i.e. how long "hold E to interact" must be held. Address the trigger either by index or by trigger_class (first of that type). Only the fields you pass change; the action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Add the trigger first with add_input_trigger and re-read with get_input_action.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action (or short asset name).

params.name: action_name
params.description: Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent.

params.name: trigger_index
params.description: Index into the action's Triggers array to edit. Mutually exclusive with trigger_class.

params.name: trigger_class
params.description: Select the first trigger of this type (Down|Pressed|Released|Hold|Tap|Pulse|ChordAction) instead of an index.

params.name: actuation_threshold
params.description: When set, the base UInputTrigger::ActuationThreshold (float).

params.name: hold_time_threshold
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerHold::HoldTimeThreshold (float). Hold triggers only.

params.name: is_one_shot
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerHold::bIsOneShot (bool). Hold triggers only.

params.name: tap_release_time
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerTap::TapReleaseTimeThreshold (float). Tap triggers only.

params.name: affected_by_time_dilation
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerTimedBase::bAffectedByTimeDilation (bool). Timed triggers only.

commands.returns: { action_path, action_name, trigger_index, trigger_class, properties_set, trigger, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_input_action_value_type
commands.description: Change an InputAction's value type after the fact (button vs axis: Bool / Axis1D / Axis2D / Axis3D). Not cosmetic -- the type decides what shape of value the bound handlers receive and what trigger_input_action must inject, so switching it can break existing graph pins. Re-read with get_input_action and re-check the handlers. The action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path to the input action

params.name: value_type
params.description: One of "Bool", "Float", "Int", "Vector2D", "Vector", "Rotator", "String", etc.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent.

commands.returns: { action_name, action_path, value_type, value_type_set, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: trigger_input_action
commands.description: Inject a value for an Enhanced Input action into a local player's UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem in a running PIE or game session, so the real bound handlers run with the action's own modifiers and triggers (headless key injection never reaches Enhanced Input). dispatched true does not prove a handler fired: compare get_input_action_state before and after.

params.name: action
params.description: Full object path of a UInputAction, or its short asset name (required).

params.name: value_json
params.description: The value to inject, coerced to the action's ValueType: bool (Boolean), number (Axis1D), or a [x,y]/[x,y,z] array or {x,y,z} object (Axis2D/Axis3D). If omitted, Boolean actions default to true (pressed) and axis actions default to zero.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Local player index used to resolve the PlayerController (default 0).

params.name: hold_seconds
params.description: Optional float. When > 0, the value is re-injected every tick for this many seconds (so a movement AXIS actually moves the pawn), then a final neutral/zero value is injected to release. Fire-and-forget: the command returns immediately and the hold runs across the next hold_seconds of PIE. Omit (or 0) for a single one-shot sample.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). With 2+ players the default may drive the OTHER player's pawn.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Alias of action, read when action is absent or empty: InputAction object path or short asset name.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Alias of action, read only when action is absent or empty and action_path is absent: InputAction object path or short asset name.

commands.returns: { dispatched: bool, note: string, action_path: string, value_type: string, injected_value: [x,y,z], player_index: number, hold_seconds: number, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: unregister_input_key_mapping
commands.description: Resets a player input mapping back to its default key at runtime via UEnhancedInputUserSettings::UnMapPlayerKey (EnhancedInputUserSettings.h). Inverse of register_input_key_mapping; locates the mapping by name + slot and clears the player override (does not need new_key, does not delete the row). The call fails when the engine refuses it, with its reasons in failure_tags.

params.name: mapping_name
params.description: FName of the source mapping inside an already-mapped IMC (required)

params.name: player_controller_name
params.description: Optional editor-world APlayerController actor name (defaults to first local player)

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index used to resolve the PlayerController (default 0).

params.name: slot
params.description: "First" | "Second" | "Third" | "Fourth" (default "First"); EPlayerMappableKeySlot enum

commands.returns: { applied: bool, mapping_name: string, slot: string, failure_tags: [string] }

commands.name: interchange_can_reset_actor
commands.description: Report, read-only, whether Interchange can reset an actor of the editor world (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::CanResetActor, which needs a bound UInterchangeSceneImportAsset); returns actor_path and can_reset. The actor is found by full object path or by object name in the persistent level, not by label.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full object path of the actor (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap:PersistentLevel.ActorName_0") or its object name in the persistent level of the editor world (e.g. "StaticMeshActor_3"); labels are not matched.

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, can_reset: bool }

commands.name: interchange_can_reset_world
commands.description: Report, read-only, whether Interchange can reset a world (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::CanResetWorld): the map asset world_path names, loaded if needed, or the current editor world. Returns can_reset, is_editor_world and resolved_world_path. Run the reset with interchange_reset_level_asset.

params.name: world_path
params.description: World asset path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap") or fully-qualified object path. Empty = current editor world.

commands.returns: { world_path: string, can_reset: bool, is_editor_world: bool }

commands.name: interchange_can_translate_source_data
commands.description: Whether a registered Interchange translator can read a source file (a path on disk or an asset path). Read-only.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path of the source file to test on disk (e.g. "C:/Assets/Mesh.fbx"), or an Unreal asset path. Passed to UInterchangeManager::CreateSourceData.

params.name: scene_only
params.description: When true, restrict the check to scene translators (bSceneOnly). Defaults to false (any translator type).

commands.returns: { file_path: string, scene_only: bool, can_translate: bool }

commands.name: interchange_create_pipeline_asset
commands.description: Create an Interchange pipeline asset of a concrete pipeline class (the generic texture, mesh, material, animation, audio, scenes, groom or assets pipelines, glTF, sparse volume texture, MaterialX). Idempotent: an object of that name already in package_path is returned with already_existed:true.

params.name: pipeline_class_path
params.description: Class path of the concrete (non-abstract) UInterchangePipelineBase subclass to instantiate (e.g. "/Script/InterchangePipelines.InterchangeGenericAssetsPipeline"), loaded via LoadClass.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Name of the new pipeline asset (the object/package name under package_path).

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination UE content folder for the new pipeline asset (e.g. "/Game/Pipelines"). Defaults to "/Game".

commands.returns: { pipeline_path: string, class: string, already_existed: bool, note: string }

commands.name: interchange_get_asset_import_data
commands.description: Read the UInterchangeAssetImportData of an asset.  Loads the asset via LoadObject<UObject> and calls UInterchangeManager::GetAssetImportData(Asset) (InterchangeManager.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API). For assets imported via the legacy factory path the returned data is null — that is reported as ``present:false`` (a normal state, not an error). When present, also calls ScriptExtractFilenames / ScriptExtractDisplayLabels (UFUNCTION inline, InterchangeAssetImportData.h/65).

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo") or fully-qualified object path ("/Game/Foo/Foo.Foo")

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, present: bool, pipelines_count: number, has_node_container: bool, source_filenames: [string], display_labels: [string] }

commands.name: interchange_get_node_container
commands.description: Read the UInterchangeBaseNodeContainer of an asset's UInterchangeAssetImportData.  Loads the asset + ID, then iterates factory nodes via IterateNodesOfType<UInterchangeFactoryBaseNode> (InterchangeBaseNodeContainer.h, template header-only) and reads class via GetObjectClass() (InterchangeFactoryBaseNode.h, INTERCHANGECORE_API), UniqueID + DisplayLabel from UInterchangeBaseNode (InterchangeBaseNode.h, INTERCHANGECORE_API).

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo")

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, present: bool, root_uids: [string], factory_node_count: number, factory_nodes: [object] }

commands.name: interchange_get_pipeline_properties
commands.description: Read the properties of an Interchange pipeline asset by reflection; class_only lists only their names and types.

params.name: pipeline_path
params.description: Object path of the pipeline asset to read (loaded via LoadObject, must be a UInterchangePipelineBase).

params.name: class_only
params.description: When true, return only the EditAnywhere property NAMES and types (no values) for discovery. Defaults to false (includes current values).

commands.returns: { pipeline_path: string, class: string, properties: [object], property_count: number }

commands.name: interchange_get_pipelines
commands.description: List the UInterchangePipelineBase instances stored on an asset's UInterchangeAssetImportData.  Loads the asset, retrieves its UInterchangeAssetImportData via UInterchangeManager::GetAssetImportData (InterchangeManager.h), then calls ID->GetPipelines() (InterchangeAssetImportData.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API). Returns the class, name, and full object path of each pipeline.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo") or fully-qualified object path

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, present: bool, pipeline_count: number, pipelines: [object] }

commands.name: interchange_get_project_settings
commands.description: Read the project's Interchange settings (UInterchangeProjectSettings): the content and scene import settings (pipeline stacks, default stack and its per-asset-type overrides, import dialog class and flags, per-translator dialog overrides), the file picker and generic pipeline classes, the converter default pipeline and the Interchange groups.

commands.name: interchange_get_supported_formats
commands.description: List file extensions supported by registered Interchange translators of a given type.  Calls UInterchangeManager::GetSupportedFormats(EInterchangeTranslatorType) (InterchangeManager.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API). The 5.8 enum has Invalid / Assets / Actors / Scenes (Scenes = Assets|Actors). Accepts aliases "Assets", "Actors", "Scenes", and "AssetsAndScene" (mapped to Scenes).

params.name: translator_type
params.description: Translator type: "Assets" [default], "Actors", "Scenes", or the spec alias "AssetsAndScene"

commands.returns: { translator_type: string, format_count: number, formats: [string] }

commands.name: interchange_import_asset
commands.description: Import a source file synchronously through the Interchange manager: unattended, no dialogs, replacing existing assets unless replace_existing is false. When the InterchangeImport plugin is not loaded the note says so.

params.description: Path of the source file to import on disk (e.g. "C:/Assets/Mesh.fbx"). Passed to UInterchangeManager::CreateSourceData.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: Destination UE content folder for the imported asset(s) (e.g. "/Game/Meshes"). Defaults to "/Game/Imported".

params.name: replace_existing
params.description: When true, overwrite an existing asset at the destination (bReplaceExisting). Defaults to true.

commands.returns: { file_path: string, destination_path: string, imported: bool, count: number, imported_objects: [string], note: string }

commands.name: interchange_module_status
commands.description: Report Interchange framework availability.  Reads UInterchangeManager::IsInterchangeImportEnabled() (InterchangeManager.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API) and counts the supported file extensions reported by GetSupportedFormats(Assets) (InterchangeManager.h). Translator count itself is derived because UInterchangeManager's RegisteredTranslatorsClass set is private in 5.8 (InterchangeManager.h) — we surface ``enabled`` (= import enabled AND at least one supported format) which carries the same operational signal.
commands.returns: { enabled: bool, import_enabled: bool, asset_format_count: number, actor_format_count: number, scene_format_count: number, asset_formats: [string], translator_type_queried: string }

commands.name: interchange_register_factory
commands.description: Load a factory class and register it with the Interchange manager. Idempotent: a class already registered is a no-op.

params.name: factory_class_path
params.description: Class path of the factory UClass to instantiate and register (e.g. "/Script/InterchangeEngine.InterchangeTextureFactory"), loaded via LoadClass.

commands.returns: { factory_class_path: string, class: string, registered: bool, note: string }

commands.name: interchange_register_translator
commands.description: Load a translator class (e.g. /Script/InterchangeEngine.InterchangeTextureTranslator) and register it with the Interchange manager. Idempotent: a class already registered is a no-op.

params.name: translator_class_path
params.description: Class path of the translator UClass to instantiate and register (e.g. "/Script/InterchangeEngine.InterchangeTextureTranslator"), loaded via LoadClass.

commands.returns: { translator_class_path: string, class: string, registered: bool, note: string }

commands.name: interchange_reimport_asset
commands.description: Reimport an existing asset from its stored UInterchangeAssetImportData (UInterchangeManager::ReimportAsset). An asset without Interchange import data (a legacy factory import, or one never imported) gets an error.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo") or fully-qualified object path ("/Game/Foo/Foo.Foo")

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, reimported: bool, count: number, note: string }

commands.name: interchange_reset_actors
commands.description: Run an Interchange reset (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetActors) on the editor-world actors listed by object path or persistent-level object name; the library skips actors that fail CanResetActor, and the reply does not say which were reset. Returns count, resolved and unresolved_paths. Check first with interchange_can_reset_actor.

params.name: actor_paths
params.description: Actors to reset, each a full object path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap:PersistentLevel.ActorName_0") or an object name in the persistent level; labels are not matched, and empty or unknown entries land in unresolved_paths.

commands.returns: { count: number, resolved: number, unresolved_paths: [string], note: string }

commands.name: interchange_reset_level_asset
commands.description: Run an Interchange reset on a level (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetLevelAsset), the map world_path names or the current editor world, only when the Interchange.FeatureFlags.InterchangeReset CVar is on and CanResetWorld is true; otherwise it does nothing and the call fails (reset false, with the reason in note). It does not save. Returns reset, can_reset, cvar_enabled and a note.

params.name: world_path
params.description: World asset path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap") or fully-qualified object path. Empty = current editor world.

commands.returns: { world_path: string, resolved_world_path: string, reset: bool, can_reset: bool, cvar_enabled: bool, note: string }

commands.name: interchange_reset_scene_import_asset
commands.description: Call the Interchange reset of a UInterchangeSceneImportAsset (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetSceneImportAsset); other asset classes are refused. The engine only resets while the Interchange.FeatureFlags.InterchangeReset CVar is 1: with it at 0 the call does nothing and fails (reset false).
