params.name: slot_index
params.description: 0-based index into LandscapeProxy::RuntimeVirtualTextures (default 0)

params.name: propagate_to_proxies
params.description: Optional bool, default TRUE. Opt-out that writes the landscape actor alone. NOTE: with it false the proxies stay empty and nothing writes to the RVT cache, so `applied` will still report false (plus a `warning`) unless the proxies already carried the RVT -- the opt-out exists to reproduce that write, not to bless its result.

commands.returns: { applied, slot_index, rvt_asset_path, landscape, landscape_has_rvt, propagate_to_proxies, proxies_total, proxies_updated, proxies_with_rvt, proxies_missing: [string], proxies_missing_truncated: bool, proxy_enumeration, warning?, requested: {...} }

commands.name: bookmark
commands.description: Emit a TRACE_BOOKMARK into the active .utrace at the current frame. The bookmark channel must be enabled in the trace (default start_trace channels include it). The text is dynamic via printf-style formatting, but the Format token itself is a TEXT() literal as required by the macro's static_assert.

params.name: text
params.description: The bookmark text. Becomes the bookmark label in UnrealInsights.

commands.returns: { bookmarked: bool, text: string, frame: int, note: string }

commands.name: create_rvt_asset
commands.description: Create a URuntimeVirtualTexture asset at directory_path/asset_name with the given material type, tile count and tile size (both exponents, clamped silently), and save it; the save result is not checked. Returns asset_path, tile_count, tile_size and size in texels. Then use create_rvt_volume and assign_rvt_to_landscape.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Name of the new RVT asset (e.g. "RVT_Landscape"), without a folder.

params.name: directory_path
params.description: Content folder as a long package path (e.g. "/Game/VirtualTextures"), not a relative one (default /Game).

params.name: material_type
params.description: One of "BaseColor_Normal_Specular", "BaseColor_Normal_Roughness" or "WorldHeight", case-insensitive (default "BaseColor_Normal_Specular"); any other value, BaseColor_YCoCg included, is refused.

params.name: tile_count
params.description: Exponent of the size in tiles: 2^n tiles, clamped to 0..12 (default 8 = 256 tiles); a texel value such as 256 is clamped to 12.

params.name: tile_size
params.description: Exponent of the tile size: 2^(n+6) texels, clamped to 0..4 (default 2 = 256 texels).

params.name: continuous_update
params.description: When true, already mapped pages are re-rendered round-robin (bContinuousUpdate); default false.

commands.returns: { asset_path, material_type, tile_count, tile_size, size }

commands.name: create_rvt_volume
commands.description: Spawn an ARuntimeVirtualTextureVolume (the RVT producer that registers the runtime virtual texture into the scene and defines its world-space region) bound to an RVT asset. Without a volume, assign_rvt_to_landscape only wires the landscape as a writer -- nothing produces the RVT. Optionally fits the volume bounds to an actor (usually the landscape) in the same call. Headless-safe: spawns with a null VirtualTexture (no render-state) then binds a valid RVT. Idempotent: returns the existing volume if one already targets this RVT.

params.name: rvt_asset_path
params.description: Required. /Game path to the URuntimeVirtualTexture asset (create_rvt_asset).

params.name: bounds_align_actor
params.description: Optional. Name/label of an actor (usually the ALandscape) to fit the volume bounds to; runs the engine "Set Bounds" after binding.

params.name: volume_name
params.description: Optional. Actor label for the spawned volume.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x,y,z] spawn location (default [0,0,0]; overridden by the bounds-align when bounds_align_actor is given).

commands.returns: { volume_name, rvt_asset_path, bounds_aligned, bounds_align_actor?, already_existed }

commands.name: frame_timing
commands.description: Read the current frame's Game/Render/GPU/RHI thread times plus a CPU-vs-GPU bottleneck verdict with an actionable hint.
commands.returns: { frame_ms: float, game_thread_ms: float, render_thread_ms: float, rhi_thread_ms: float, game_thread_wait_ms: float, render_thread_wait_ms: float, gpu_ms: float, cpu_busy_ms: float, verdict: "GPU-bound"|"CPU-bound (game thread)"|"CPU-bound (render thread)"|"VSync/present bound"|"balanced"|"no-data", hint: string, null_rhi: bool, note: string } -- cpu_busy_ms is game + render + rhi; null_rhi is true with -nullrhi or in a commandlet, where the timings read 0 (verdict "no-data" when they all do) and note warns of it; otherwise note is empty.

commands.name: get_fps_info
commands.description: Retrieves current and target FPS along with performance settings and world network mode.
commands.returns: { current_fps: float, target_fps: float, fps_variance: float, engine_version: string, is_editor: bool, is_dedicated_server: bool, performance_settings: {vsync_enabled (r.VSync), smooth_frame_rate, max_fps (0 = uncapped), min_fps (lower bound of frame-rate smoothing; 0 without it)}, world_name: string, net_mode: string }

commands.name: get_frame_count
commands.description: Read the engine frame counters without side effects: frame_count (GFrameCounter, game thread) and frame_count_render_thread (GFrameCounterRenderThread). Read it before and after another call to measure how many frames ticked; for frame times use frame_timing or get_fps_info.
commands.returns: { frame_count: uint64, frame_count_render_thread: uint64 }

commands.name: get_memory_usage
commands.description: Retrieves detailed memory usage including process, scene, GPU, and system information.
commands.returns: { process_memory: {used_physical_memory_mb, peak_used_physical_memory_mb, available_physical_memory_mb, total_physical_memory_mb, used_virtual_memory_mb, peak_used_virtual_memory_mb}, scene_memory: {actor_count, component_count, static_mesh_count, material_count (distinct), material_slot_count, texture_count (distinct textures the scene's materials use), resident_texture_count (every UTexture2D in memory)}, gpu_memory: {gpu_memory_available, gpu_memory_status, rhi_name, dedicated_video_memory_mb?, shared_system_memory_mb?, total_graphics_memory_mb?, streaming_texture_memory_mb, non_streaming_texture_memory_mb}, system_info: {platform, cpu_brand, cpu_cores, cpu_threads} }

commands.name: get_rvt_info
commands.description: Read a URuntimeVirtualTexture asset without changing it: material_type (full enum name, e.g. "ERuntimeVirtualTextureMaterialType::WorldHeight"), tile_count in tiles, tile_size and size in texels (not the exponents create_rvt_asset takes), and continuous_update.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object or package path of the RVT asset (e.g. "/Game/VirtualTextures/RVT_Landscape").

commands.returns: { asset_path, material_type, tile_count, tile_size, size, continuous_update }

commands.name: get_trace_status
commands.description: Report whether Unreal Insights tracing is compiled in, currently connected, and to what destination.
commands.returns: { system_status: "not_available"|"available"|"tracing_to_file"|"tracing_to_server"|"tracing_to_secure_network"|"tracing_to_custom_relay"|"unknown", compile_time_enabled: bool, connected: bool, destination: string, elapsed_s: float } -- compile_time_enabled is false only when system_status is not_available (tracing compiled out, as in Shipping); destination is empty and elapsed_s 0 when not connected, and elapsed_s is also 0 for a trace start_trace did not start.

commands.name: list_active_regions
commands.description: Read-side of region_start: the named timing regions still OPEN in this bridge instance, each with how long it has been running. Use it to spot a region you forgot to close, or to read an elapsed time without ending the region. Entries disappear when region_end closes them, one name at a time; the state is per bridge instance and does not survive a restart.
commands.returns: { total, regions:[{ name, started_at_s, elapsed_s }] }

commands.name: list_traces
commands.description: Enumerate .utrace files in <ProjectDir>/Saved/Profiling/, returning their path, size and modification time.
commands.returns: { directory: string, count: int, traces: [{ path, name, size_bytes, modified_iso }] } -- directory is the resolved profiling folder; only its own files are listed, not subfolders.

commands.name: region_end
commands.description: Close an open named region and return its duration in ms. Removes the region from the active set; subsequent region_end with the same name returns an error.

params.name: name
params.description: Region identifier. Must match an open region.

commands.returns: { ended: bool, name: string, duration_ms: float, duration_s: float }

commands.name: region_start
commands.description: Begin tracking an in-process named region. Region start time is stored in this bridge instance and matched by region_end for duration calculation. Idempotent — calling region_start twice with the same name returns already_started:true.

params.name: name
params.description: Region identifier. Required.

commands.returns: { started: bool, already_started: bool, name: string, started_at_s: float }

commands.name: remove_rvt_asset
commands.description: Destroy a URuntimeVirtualTexture asset (mirror of create_rvt_asset). Typed-delete: it loads the asset and REFUSES to delete it if it is not a URuntimeVirtualTexture, so it cannot wipe the wrong asset the way the generic delete_asset can. Idempotent on missing assets. It deletes the ASSET, not any binding: unassign_rvt_from_landscape is what detaches it from a landscape first.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full /Game/... asset path of the RVT.

commands.returns: { asset_path, deleted, already_existed, asset_class?, note? }

commands.name: set_rvt_volume_bounds
commands.description: Fit an existing ARuntimeVirtualTextureVolume's bounds to an actor -- the engine "Set Bounds" button (RuntimeVirtualTexture::SetBounds). Sets the volume's BoundsAlignActor and recomputes its transform to cover that actor (a landscape uses its complete bounds) plus any primitives writing to the volume's RVT. The volume must already have its RVT bound (create_rvt_volume). Optional landscape texel-snap + bounds expansion.

params.name: volume_name
params.description: Required. Actor name/label of the ARuntimeVirtualTextureVolume.

params.name: bounds_align_actor
params.description: Required. Name/label of the actor (usually the ALandscape) to fit the bounds to.

params.name: snap_to_landscape
params.description: Optional bool. Snap virtual-texture texels to landscape vertices (only meaningful when the align actor is a landscape).

params.name: expand_bounds
params.description: Optional float >= 0. Amount to expand the computed bounds.

commands.returns: { volume_name, bounds_align_actor, snap_to_landscape, expand_bounds, applied }

commands.name: start_trace
commands.description: Start an Unreal Insights trace recording to a .utrace file. Idempotent — if a trace is already active, returns already_tracing:true with the current destination instead of failing.

params.name: channels
params.description: Comma-separated channel list (default "cpu,frame,bookmark"; also: gpu, region, memtag, counters, log, screenshot)

params.name: output_path
params.description: Absolute .utrace path. If empty, defaults to <ProjectDir>/Saved/Profiling/MCP_<timestamp>.utrace

commands.returns: { tracing: bool, already_tracing: bool, destination: string, channels: string, note: string }

commands.name: stop_trace
commands.description: Stop the active Unreal Insights trace and return its destination, duration and file size. Idempotent — calling stop_trace when no trace is active returns was_tracing:false with a note instead of failing.
commands.returns: { stopped: bool, was_tracing: bool, destination?: string, duration_s?: float, size_bytes?: int, note: string } -- with no trace running only stopped:false, was_tracing:false and note; when the engine's Stop() refuses because the trace is already stopping, stopped is false and size_bytes is absent; after a stop, note says to open the .utrace in Unreal Insights. duration_s is 0 for a trace start_trace did not start.

commands.name: unassign_rvt_from_landscape
commands.description: Inverse of assign_rvt_to_landscape: clears ONE slot of a landscape's RuntimeVirtualTextures array, breaking the binding without leaving a dangling entry behind. It unbinds only -- the RVT asset itself survives (remove_rvt_asset destroys that). Reports the asset path that was in the slot, so the operation is reversible.

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Actor name (or label) of the ALandscape actor (omit for first landscape in world)

params.name: slot_index
params.description: 0-based index to clear (default 0)

commands.returns: { cleared, slot_index, previous_rvt_asset_path?, landscape }

commands.name: add_field_node
commands.description: Author a field command node into a UFieldSystem and persist it.  Builds a transient authoring field U-node (selected by node_type), resolves the physics target to an EFieldPhysicsType, constructs the runtime FFieldSystemCommand via FFieldObjectCommands::CreateFieldCommand, appends it to UFieldSystem.Commands, and saves the asset.  node_type accepts "RadialFalloff", "PlaneFalloff", "BoxFalloff", "WaveScalar", "UniformScalar", "NoiseField", "UniformInteger", "RadialIntMask", "UniformVector", "RadialVector", "RotatedRadialVector", "RandomVector". Vector nodes pair with vector targets (LinearVelocity/LinearForce); scalar with strain/threshold; integer with state (DynamicState).  target is a physics target attribute name like "LinearVelocity", "ExternalClusterStrain", "DynamicState".  falloff_type accepts "Inverse", "Squared", "Logarithmic", or "None". Defaults to "Linear".

params.name: field_system_path
params.description: Asset path of the UFieldSystem (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/FS_Example")

params.name: node_type
params.description: One of "RadialFalloff", "PlaneFalloff", "BoxFalloff", "WaveScalar", "UniformScalar", "NoiseField", "UniformInteger", "RadialIntMask", "UniformVector", "RadialVector", "RotatedRadialVector", "RandomVector"

params.name: target
params.description: Physics target attribute name, e.g. "LinearForce", "LinearVelocity", "ExternalClusterStrain", "DynamicState"

params.name: magnitude
params.description: Optional scalar magnitude; defaults to 1.0

params.name: radius
params.description: Optional falloff / mask radius; defaults to 100.0

params.name: position
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world / center position

params.name: direction
params.description: Optional [x, y, z]; uniform-vector direction, plane normal (PlaneFalloff), or rotation axis (RotatedRadialVector)

params.name: falloff_type
params.description: Optional EFieldFalloffType; defaults to "Linear"

params.name: min_range
params.description: Optional remap lower bound for falloff/noise nodes; defaults to 0.0

params.name: max_range
params.description: Optional remap upper bound for falloff/noise nodes; defaults to 1.0

params.name: default_value
params.description: Optional out-of-range value for falloff nodes; defaults to 0.0

params.name: distance
params.description: Optional plane distance limit for PlaneFalloff; defaults to 0.0

params.name: wavelength
params.description: Optional WaveScalar wavelength; defaults to 10000.0

params.name: period
params.description: Optional WaveScalar period; defaults to 1.0

params.name: wave_function
params.description: Optional WaveScalar function "Cosine", "Gaussian", "Falloff", "Decay"; defaults to "Cosine"

params.name: interior_value
params.description: Optional RadialIntMask interior integer; defaults to 1

params.name: exterior_value
params.description: Optional RadialIntMask exterior integer; defaults to 0

params.name: mask_condition
params.description: Optional RadialIntMask condition "Always", "MergeInterior", "MergeExterior"; defaults to "Always"

params.name: angle
params.description: Optional RotatedRadialVector rotation angle in degrees; defaults to 0.0

commands.returns: { field_system_path: string, node_type: string, target: string, physics_type_name: string, command_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_geometry_collection_source
commands.description: Append an additional StaticMesh source to an existing geometry collection, then save it. Succeeds only when the package reaches disk; a failed save leaves the change in memory only (saved false, save_error).

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UGeometryCollection

params.name: source_mesh_path
params.description: Asset path to the UStaticMesh to append

params.name: transform
params.description: Optional {location, rotation, scale} for the source mesh placement

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, source_mesh_path: string, num_sources: int, num_materials: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: add_impulse_to_actor
commands.description: Kick a physics body: apply an impulse (or, with vel_change, a mass-independent velocity change) to an actor's primitive component, optionally at a world location for torque via AddImpulseAtLocation, or on a named skeletal bone. Acts on the EDITOR world, where nothing is simulating unless the component has simulate_physics on -- so on a resting editor actor this is a no-op that still reports applied:true; verify with a transform re-read, and for gameplay-time forces drive it in PIE.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional primitive component name (defaults to the actor's RootComponent)

params.name: impulse
params.description: [x, y, z] impulse vector in world units (required)

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location for AddImpulseAtLocation (omit to use AddImpulse)

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Optional skeletal bone name to apply the impulse to

params.name: vel_change
params.description: Optional; if true, impulse is treated as a velocity change (mass-independent)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, applied: bool }

commands.name: add_instanced_static_mesh_component
commands.description: Attach an InstancedStaticMeshComponent (ISM) to a placed editor-world actor so you can then scatter many copies of one static mesh through it with add_ism_instance. Idempotent: if the actor already has an ISM it returns that one with already_existed=true instead of adding a second. This is the working alternative to the foliage scatter tools, which crash the editor in this build.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor (required)

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Optional /Game/... path to a UStaticMesh asset (defaults to engine cube if absent)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, num_instances: int, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: add_ism_instance
commands.description: Place one more instance of an InstancedStaticMeshComponent's mesh at a world transform -- the cheap way to scatter many copies of a mesh (rocks, props, vegetation) without spawning an actor each. Pair it with add_instanced_static_mesh_component to create the component first. Prefer this route over the foliage tools: scatter_foliage_in_box and add_foliage_instances both CRASH the editor in this build, and an ISM is the same code path a foliage actor and PCG use anyway.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the actor carrying the ISM component (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional ISM component name (defaults to the first one on the actor)

params.name: location
params.description: [x, y, z] world-space translation (required)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation (defaults to zero)

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] scale (defaults to [1,1,1])

params.name: world_space
params.description: Optional; if true, transform is interpreted in world space (default true)

commands.returns: { instance_index: int, num_instances: int }

commands.name: add_physics_asset_constraint
commands.description: Author a ragdoll constraint (joint) inside a UPhysicsAsset between two bones.  Creates a UPhysicsConstraintTemplate via FPhysicsAssetUtils::CreateNewConstraint (idempotent by name — re-using a name returns the existing joint), sets the child/parent bones and a Limited swing+twist cone, and snaps the joint frames to the bones' default relative transform when BOTH bones exist in the preview-mesh skeleton (skipped honestly otherwise, since the engine fatal-checks an unknown bone).  Refine motions/limits afterwards with set_physics_asset_constraint_limits.

params.name: physics_asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the UPhysicsAsset to add the constraint to.

params.name: child_bone
params.description: Name of the child bone/body (ConstraintBone1, the moving end).

params.name: parent_bone
params.description: Name of the parent bone/body (ConstraintBone2, the anchor end).

params.name: constraint_name
params.description: Optional joint name (defaults to child_bone); re-using an existing name is idempotent (no duplicate).

commands.returns: { physics_asset_path: string, constraint_name: string, constraint_index: int, child_bone: string, parent_bone: string, already_existed: bool, child_in_skeleton: bool, parent_in_skeleton: bool, child_body_index: int, parent_body_index: int, frames_snapped: bool, collision_disabled: bool, constraint_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string, constraint: object }

commands.name: add_simple_collision_to_static_mesh
commands.description: Appends one simple collision primitive (Box, Sphere or Capsule) sized to the bounds of a UStaticMesh to its BodySetup and saves the mesh; a mesh outside /Game is first duplicated to dest_path. Not idempotent: each call adds one more (clear them with remove_static_mesh_collision).

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Path to the source UStaticMesh.

params.name: dest_path
params.description: Path under /Game to copy a mesh that is not under /Game into before editing (required then; an existing mesh there is reused and edited)

params.name: shape
params.description: Box, Sphere or Capsule, case-insensitive, sized from the mesh bounds (default Box; any other value also adds a Box)

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, shape, box_count, sphere_count, capsule_count, element_count, collision_added, duplicated_to_game, saved, save_error }

commands.name: clear_ism_instances
commands.description: Wipe ALL instances from an InstancedStaticMeshComponent in one call (the component itself stays). Use it to reset a scatter before re-running it, rather than looping remove_ism_instance. Returns the post-clear num_instances, which should be 0.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the actor carrying the ISM component (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional ISM component name

commands.returns: { cleared: bool, num_instances: int }

commands.name: cluster_geometry_collection
commands.description: Runs auto-clustering on all transforms of a UGeometryCollection asset, targeting site_count clusters ("Small" doubles it, "Large" halves it, any other method keeps it) with connectivity enforced, then saves it. Returns the cluster count used and the transform counts before and after; the call fails when no cluster was added (a collection that is not fractured into several pieces has nothing to group) or when the save fails.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UGeometryCollection

params.name: cluster_size_method
params.description: Small, Medium, or Large, default Medium

params.name: site_count
params.description: Target cluster count before cluster_size_method scales it, minimum 1, default 10

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, cluster_size_method: string, site_count: int, num_transforms_before: int, num_transforms_after: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: compute_gc_proximity
commands.description: Rebuilds the proximity (adjacency) graph of a UGeometryCollection asset in place and saves it; undoable. Returns proximity_pairs (unordered pairs of neighboring pieces, from a precise proximity pass), transform_count, success and saved; fails when the save fails. Afterwards get_gc_hierarchy_info reports proximity_computed true.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the UGeometryCollection

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, proximity_pairs: int, transform_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_field_system_asset
commands.description: Create (or load) a saved UFieldSystem asset on /Game.  Idempotent: if the asset already exists it is loaded and the same payload shape is returned. Otherwise a new UFieldSystem is created, registered with the asset registry, and saved to disk.

params.name: field_system_name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. "FS_Example")

params.name: package_path
params.description: Optional content folder; defaults to /Game/MCP

commands.returns: { field_system_path: string, field_system_name: string, command_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_geometry_collection
commands.description: Creates a UGeometryCollection asset at package_path/name, optionally filled from one StaticMesh, and saves it. An existing collection there is RESET first (all geometry and sources discarded; created false, rebuilt true). A source_mesh_path that does not load as a StaticMesh is an error, checked before anything is touched. Succeeds only when the package reaches disk; a failed save leaves the collection in memory only (saved false, save_error).

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. /Game/Chaos/Collections; a path without a leading slash is placed under /Game/

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the geometry collection asset, e.g. GC_Wall

params.name: source_mesh_path
params.description: Optional StaticMesh to convert and append, e.g. /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, geometry_collection_name: string, num_materials: int, num_transforms: int, created: bool, rebuilt: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: create_physical_material
commands.description: Create and save a UPhysicalMaterial asset, optionally setting surface/object properties.  Idempotent: if the asset already exists it is loaded, any provided values are re-applied, and a stable payload is returned.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. 'PM_Rubber').

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/Physics")

params.name: friction
params.description: Optional Friction value to set on creation

params.name: restitution
params.description: Optional Restitution value to set on creation

params.name: density
params.description: Optional Density value (g/cm^3) to set on creation

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, package_path: string, friction: number, restitution: number, density: number, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: create_physics_asset
commands.description: Creates a UPhysicsAsset at package_path/name, generating bodies and constraints from a skeletal mesh, sets that mesh as its preview mesh and saves it; the mesh is not pointed at the new asset. An existing one there is returned unchanged. Returns bodies, constraints, skeleton_bones, bodies_generated, saved.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. 'PA_Cube').

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the new asset (default /Game/Physics; an empty string also uses it)

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Skeletal mesh to generate the bodies from (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube); the call fails when it does not load

commands.returns: { package_path, already_existed, created, saved, bodies_generated, generation_message, save_error }

commands.name: fracture_geometry_collection
commands.description: Applies Voronoi fracturing to all transforms of a UGeometryCollection asset, using num_sites random sites in its bounds, then saves it. num_fractures is the number of new pieces, measured as the transforms the fracture added; the call fails when it added none (an empty collection, or a chance_to_fracture that skipped every piece) or when the save fails. Re-fracturing grows a collection geometrically and can stall the editor; fracture a fresh one from create_geometry_collection.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UGeometryCollection

params.name: num_sites
params.description: Number of random Voronoi sites to generate, minimum 1, default 20

params.name: random_seed
params.description: Seed for the random site positions and the per-transform fracture chance, default 0

params.name: chance_to_fracture
params.description: Chance from 0 to 1 that each selected transform is fractured, default 1

params.name: grout
params.description: Width of the gap left between cut pieces, in cm (default 0)

params.name: split_islands
params.description: Optional, split resulting islands, default false

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, num_fractures: int, transform_count: int, num_sites: int, random_seed: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: get_actor_bounds
commands.description: Measure how BIG an actor really is: its aggregate world-space bounding box (origin, half-extent, min, max) in the EDITOR world. The size oracle for placement and footprint questions, and the honest test for "did that volume/brush actually get built" -- a spawned volume whose extent comes back (0,0,0) has no geometry no matter what the spawning tool reported. Its `components` filter is the reason to prefer it over reading a component property: "all" (default, AActor::GetActorBounds -- inflated by interaction/trigger shapes), "colliding" (only collision-enabled components) or "mesh"/"rendered" (UMeshComponent geometry ONLY, so trigger spheres/boxes are excluded and the box hugs what you actually see). Editor world only -- for a PIE-world footprint use overlap_scene/raycast_scene with a `world` selector.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor name or editor label

params.name: components
params.description: Which components contribute: "all" (default; everything, trigger shapes included) | "colliding" (collision-enabled only) | "mesh" | "rendered" (UMeshComponent geometry only)

params.name: include_child_actors
params.description: Include child-actor components' bounds. Defaults to false.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, components: string, valid: bool, component_count: int, origin: {x,y,z}, extent: {x,y,z}, min: {x,y,z}, max: {x,y,z} } -- valid=false with a zero extent means no contributing geometry was found

commands.name: get_collision_info
commands.description: Read ONE placed primitive component's collision setup and physics state: collision enabled mode, per-channel responses (WorldStatic / WorldDynamic / Pawn / PhysicsBody), overlap and hit event flags, simulate-physics, mobility, and the physical material with its friction / restitution / density. The tool to answer "why does this not block / not overlap" without writing Python. Two limits from the code: it searches by component NAME across the world's actors but only inspects each actor's FIRST primitive component, so a secondary component (a second collider, a trigger next to a mesh) reports "not found" even though it exists; and it reads the component's live responses, NOT the profile definition -- for the profile itself use get_collision_profile (which is blind to +EditProfiles overrides), and prove a channel really blocks with raycast_scene.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the primitive component to query (must be its actor's first primitive component to be findable).

commands.returns: { component_name: string, collision_info_found: bool, collision_info_message: string, collision_enabled: string, collision_type: string, collision_response: string, collision_enabled_state: string, collision_generate_overlap_events: bool, collision_generate_hit_events: bool, collision_simulate_physics: bool, collision_mobility: string, collision_response_world_static: string, collision_response_world_dynamic: string, collision_response_pawn: string, collision_response_physics_body: string, physics_material_is_default: bool, physics_material_name: string, physics_material_path: string, physics_material_surface_type: string, physics_material_friction: float, physics_material_restitution: float, physics_material_density: float, physics_material_raise_mass_to_power: float, physics_material_linear_damping: float (body), physics_material_angular_damping: float (body), physics_material_mass_scale: float (body) }

commands.name: get_field_system_info
commands.description: Read the field commands authored in a UFieldSystem asset, in order: each with physics_type, target_attribute, command_name and max_magnitude (not its node graph), plus command_count. Read-only; the array index is what remove_field_node takes, and add_field_node authors new commands.

params.name: field_system_path
params.description: Asset path of the UFieldSystem, e.g. "/Game/MyGame/FS_Example" or "/Game/MyGame/FS_Example.FS_Example".

commands.returns: { field_system_path: string, command_count: int, commands: [{ physics_type, target_attribute, command_name, max_magnitude }], success: bool }

commands.name: get_gc_hierarchy_info
commands.description: Reads the bone hierarchy of a UGeometryCollection asset: transform_count, root_indices, and per bone its level, name and simulation type ("Rigid", "Clustered" or "None"), plus proximity_computed. Generates the Level attribute in memory if needed, without saving. For parent indices use list_geometry_collection_bones.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the UGeometryCollection

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, transform_count: int, root_indices: [int], levels: [int], bone_names: [string], simulation_types: [string], proximity_computed: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: get_geometry_collection_info
commands.description: Reads a UGeometryCollection asset without changing it: material, source and damage-threshold counts, damage model ("Threshold", "MaterialStrength" or "Unknown"), mass settings and element counts (transforms, vertices, faces, geometry; 0 without collection data). Use get_gc_hierarchy_info for the bone tree.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path, e.g. /Game/Chaos/GC_Wall

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, num_materials: int, num_geometry_sources: int, damage_model: string, num_damage_thresholds: int, is_empty: bool, num_transforms: int, num_vertices: int, num_faces: int, num_geometry: int, mass: float, mass_as_density: bool, minimum_mass_clamp: float, density_from_physics_material: bool, has_physics_material: bool }

commands.name: get_ism_instance_info
commands.description: Count the instances in an InstancedStaticMeshComponent, or read one instance's transform (location / rotation / scale) and per-instance custom data floats. Two modes from one call: omit instance_index for COUNT mode (num_instances + num_custom_data_floats -- the oracle for "did my scatter actually place anything"), pass it for per-instance mode. Reads the component in the editor world, so it needs no PIE.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the actor carrying the ISM component (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional ISM component name (defaults to the first one on the actor)

params.name: instance_index
params.description: Optional; absent -> count mode; present and >=0 -> per-instance mode (must be a valid index)

params.name: world_space
params.description: Optional; if true, transform is returned in world space (default true)

commands.returns: count mode { num_instances: int, num_custom_data_floats: int } or instance mode { instance_index: int, num_instances: int, world_space: bool, location: [x,y,z], rotation: [pitch,yaw,roll], scale: [x,y,z], custom_data: [float], num_custom_data_floats: int }

commands.description: Read a UPhysicsAsset's body count, constraint count, and bound skeletal mesh.

params.name: physics_asset_path

commands.returns: success or error payload

commands.description: Read the full authored configuration of a world APhysicsConstraintActor's UPhysicsConstraintComponent: identity + wired bodies/bones, linear/angular limits (with motion types), linear/angular drives (motors) with targets, breakable thresholds, projection, and collision/dominance flags.  Read-only complement of spawn_physics_constraint / set_constraint_limits / set_physics_constraint_drives; returns the serialized template, not live simulation state (no motor torque/broken/force values, which are 0 outside PIE).

params.name: constraint_actor_name
params.description: Label/name of the APhysicsConstraintActor.

commands.name: get_physics_settings
commands.description: One-shot physics census of the current world: UPhysicsSettings substepping/delta-time values, world gravity_z, and a walk of every actor counting collision-enabled vs disabled, simulating bodies, mobility split and mass totals, plus a heuristic quality label and a recommendations list. Use it for a broad "what is the physics state of this level" sweep instead of hand-writing the actor loop in Python; for ONE component's collision use get_collision_info, and to change gravity use set_world_gravity / set_physics_gravity. Read the numbers with three caveats visible in the code: physics_engine is a hardcoded "PhysX" literal (UE5 actually runs Chaos), the walk takes only the FIRST primitive component per actor so multi-component actors are undercounted, and generate_hit_events is always 0 (never populated).
commands.returns: { physics_settings_found: bool, physics_engine: string (hardcoded "PhysX"), physics_quality: string (heuristic from max_physics_delta_time), max_physics_delta_time, max_substep_delta_time, max_substeps, world_name, world_gravity_z, world_gravity_enabled, per-component counts (collision enabled/disabled, simulating, static/stationary/movable, overlap events), mass totals (only simulating bodies contribute), recommendations: [string], complexity score }

commands.name: get_scene_bounds
commands.description: How big is the LEVEL: one world-space bounding box aggregated over every level-bounds-relevant actor in the editor world (persistent level plus any loaded streamed levels), or over an explicit subset if you pass actor_names. Use it for map extents / where-is-everything questions; use get_actor_bounds for a single actor. Note it only sees LOADED actors, so on a World-Partition map an unloaded region contributes nothing and the box reads smaller than the map.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Optional subset of actor names/labels; omit for every loaded actor in the world

commands.returns: { valid: bool, origin: {x,y,z}, extent: {x,y,z}, min: {x,y,z}, max: {x,y,z}, actor_count: int }

commands.name: list_geometry_collection_bones
commands.description: List every bone (transform) of a UGeometryCollection asset in index order with its name, parent index (-1 for a root) and simulation type ("Rigid", "Clustered" or "None"), plus transform_count and root_count. Read-only: nothing is generated or saved. A path that does not load or a collection without geometry data is an error. For levels, root indices and whether proximity is computed use get_gc_hierarchy_info; for damage, mass and source settings use get_geometry_collection_info.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the UGeometryCollection, as a package path (/Game/Chaos/GC_Rock) or an object path (/Game/Chaos/GC_Rock.GC_Rock); required.

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path, transform_count, root_count, bones: [{name, parent, sim_type}] }

commands.name: overlap_scene
commands.description: Sphere / box / capsule overlap query against the world: "what is inside this volume?", returning one JSON entry per overlapping actor+component instead of export-text, so no Python is needed to parse it. Use it over raycast_scene when the question is proximity/containment rather than line of sight -- e.g. is the pawn actually inside a water body's real collision, is anything blocking a build spot. Accepts the same `world` selector (editor / server / client / pie:N): an editor-world query does NOT see World-Partition/OFPA actor collision, so pass a live PIE world, and in co-op say WHICH one or an empty result is uninterpretable.

params.name: shape
params.description: "sphere" | "box" | "capsule"

params.name: location
params.description: World-space [x, y, z] shape center

params.name: radius
params.description: Sphere/capsule radius (required for those shapes)

params.name: half_height
params.description: Capsule half-height (required for capsule)

params.name: half_extent
params.description: Box HALF-extent [x, y, z], not the full size (required for box)

params.name: trace_channel
params.description: Collision channel, canonical ("ECC_Visibility") or friendly ("Visibility"). Defaults to "Visibility".

params.name: ignore_actors
params.description: Actor names/labels to exclude from the overlap.

params.name: world
params.description: Which world to query: absent/"editor" (default) | "server" (the PIE world with authority) | "client" | "pie:N" | "pie" (ambiguous) | "game" (alias of "pie"). Pass a live world to hit World-Partition/OFPA actor collision (only cooked in the PIE physics scene).

commands.returns: { overlaps: [{actor_path, actor_name, component_name, item_index, blocking}], count: int, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: plane_cut_fracture
commands.description: Cuts all transforms of a UGeometryCollection asset with num_planes random planes inside its bounds (no noise, islands split by default), then saves it. new_fracture_count is the number of new pieces, measured as the transforms the cut added; the call fails when it added none (an empty collection, or planes that miss every piece) or when the save fails.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the UGeometryCollection

params.name: num_planes
params.description: Number of random cutting planes to generate, minimum 1, default 3

params.name: random_seed
params.description: Optional seed for plane generation, default 1337

params.name: grout
params.description: Width of the gap left between cut pieces, in cm (default 0)

params.name: split_islands
params.description: Optional, split resulting islands, default true

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, num_planes: int, new_fracture_count: int, transform_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: raycast_scene
commands.description: Line trace / raycast the world and get a REAL JSON hit result -- what actor and component was hit, impact point, normal and distance -- instead of the UE export-text FHitResult blob that call_function on a line-trace UFUNCTION returns, so no Python parsing is needed. Accepts a `world` selector (editor / server / client / pie:N), which matters twice: an EDITOR-world trace does not hit World-Partition/OFPA actor collision (only cooked in the PIE physics scene) and reads as a clean miss, and in co-op a miss on the client world looks identical to a missing collider -- pass "server" or "pie:N" so a hit:false is interpretable. Also the honest way to prove a custom collision CHANNEL blocks: trace the same segment on a known-good channel (Visibility) and on the new one and compare actor/component/Z/distance, because get_collision_profile does not see +EditProfiles overrides.

params.name: start
params.description: World-space [x, y, z] trace start

params.name: end
params.description: World-space [x, y, z] trace end

params.name: trace_channel
params.description: Collision channel, canonical ("ECC_Visibility") or friendly ("Visibility", "Camera", or a custom channel name). Defaults to "Visibility". A channel created THIS session is not in the live profile table yet -- restart the editor before trusting a trace on it.

params.name: trace_complex
params.description: Test against complex (per-poly) collision instead of simple. Defaults to false.

params.name: ignore_actors
params.description: Actor names/labels to exclude from the trace.

params.name: return_physical_material
params.description: Populate physical_material in the result. Defaults to false.

params.name: world
params.description: Which world to trace: absent/"editor" (default) | "server" (the PIE world with authority) | "client" | "pie:N" | "pie" (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | "game" (alias of "pie"). Editor-world traces do NOT hit World-Partition/OFPA actors, so pass a live world to verify obstacle collision; with 2+ PIE instances prefer "server"/"pie:N".

commands.returns: { hit: bool, blocking_hit: bool, actor_path: string, actor_name: string, component_name: string, location: {x,y,z}, impact_point: {x,y,z}, normal: {x,y,z}, impact_normal: {x,y,z}, distance: float, bone_name: string, physical_material: string, face_index: int, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: remove_field_node
commands.description: Remove a field command node from a UFieldSystem by index and persist.  Inverse of add_field_node: selects the FFieldSystemCommand at the given index in UFieldSystem.Commands, removes it (RemoveAt frees the command's owned RootNode graph), and saves the asset.  Idempotent: an out-of-range index is a clean no-op (removed:false, note:"index out of range") so re-running after the node is already gone is safe.

params.name: field_system_path
params.description: Asset path of the UFieldSystem (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/FS_Example")

params.name: index
params.description: Zero-based index of the field command to remove

commands.returns: { field_system_path: string, removed: bool, removed_index?: int, removed_target?: string, command_count: int, success: bool, saved?: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_geometry_collection_source
commands.description: Remove a StaticMesh source reference from an existing geometry collection (inverse of add_geometry_collection_source; drops the GeometrySource entry only, does NOT re-fracture the core geometry)

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UGeometryCollection

params.name: index
params.description: Optional 0-based index into the GeometrySource array (exactly one of index / source_mesh_path)

params.name: source_mesh_path
params.description: Optional asset path of the source mesh to match against SourceGeometryObject (exactly one of index / source_mesh_path)

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, removed_index: int, removed_source_object: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, num_sources: int, success: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_ism_instance
commands.description: Delete ONE instance from an InstancedStaticMeshComponent by index. Indices shift after a removal, so remove from the highest index down when deleting several; to empty the component entirely use clear_ism_instances instead. Re-read num_instances from the reply (or get_ism_instance_info) as the oracle -- removed:true alone is not proof of the final count.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the actor carrying the ISM component (required)

params.name: instance_index
params.description: Index of the instance to remove (required, >=0)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional ISM component name

commands.returns: { removed: bool, num_instances: int }

commands.name: remove_physics_asset_constraint
commands.description: Remove a ragdoll constraint (joint) from a UPhysicsAsset — the inverse of add_physics_asset_constraint.  Resolves the joint by constraint_name (preferred) or constraint_index and deletes it via FPhysicsAssetUtils::DestroyConstraint (the same ConstraintSetup.RemoveAt the PhAT editor runs).  Idempotent: an already-absent constraint returns removed:false/already_absent:true with success (no mutation, no save).

params.name: physics_asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the UPhysicsAsset to remove the constraint from.

params.name: constraint_name
params.description: Optional joint name (JointName) of the constraint to remove; preferred over constraint_index when both are given (see get_physics_asset_info).

params.name: constraint_index
params.description: Optional constraint index to remove (used when constraint_name is absent).

commands.returns: { physics_asset_path: string, constraint_name: string, constraint_index: int, child_bone: string, parent_bone: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, constraint_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_static_mesh_collision
commands.description: Clear ALL simple/convex collision primitives from a UStaticMesh's BodySetup (the 'clear' half of the collision CRUD).  Calls UBodySetup::RemoveSimpleCollision (InvalidatePhysicsData + AggGeom.EmptyElements), rebuilds the physics meshes and saves.  Reuses the same duplicate-first logic as add_simple_collision_to_static_mesh so a read-only /Engine source is copied into dest_path first.  Idempotent: clearing an already-empty BodySetup (or a mesh with no BodySetup) is a no-op reported via already_empty:true.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Path to the source UStaticMesh.

params.name: dest_path
params.description: /Game path to duplicate a read-only /Engine source mesh into first (required only when the source is not under /Game).

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, removed_count, element_count, collision_removed, already_empty, duplicated_to_game, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_gc_connection_settings
commands.description: Write the five clustering and connection-graph properties of a UGeometryCollection asset (cluster connection type, EnableClustering, ClusterGroupIndex, MaxClusterLevel, bounds filtering margin) in an undo transaction, invalidate it and save it; a failed save makes success false. Every field is written on each call, so an omitted one goes back to its listed default, and an unrecognized connection type becomes PointImplicit. The bone hierarchy is not rebuilt: cluster_geometry_collection builds clusters and compute_gc_proximity the proximity graph. The reply reads back the type, enable_clustering and max_cluster_level.

params.name: bounds_filtering_margin
params.description: Connection graph bounds filtering margin, default 0

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, cluster_connection_type: string, enable_clustering: bool, max_cluster_level: int, success: bool, saved: bool }

The reply reads back damage_model ("Threshold", "MaterialStrength" or "Unknown") and num_thresholds; get_geometry_collection_info shows them later. params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)

params.name: force

The real check is the actor's spawned components (get_pcg_generated_data / get_components_by_class), after cleanup_pcg_component + generate_pcg_component.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)
