params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name, has_component, output_data_count, data:[{index, pin, data_class, tags:[...]}], note? }

commands.name: get_pcg_graph_info
commands.description: Reads the structure of a UPCGGraph: node count, per-node titles and pin labels, and every directed edge.  Pin labels and the input_node_name/output_node_name feed connect_pcg_nodes / disconnect_pcg_nodes; the implicit graph endpoints are also addressable by the tokens "Input"/"Output".

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_count: int, nodes: [{node_name, title, settings_class, input_pins: [string], output_pins: [string]}], has_input_node: bool, has_output_node: bool, input_node_name: string, output_node_name: string, edges: [{from_node, from_pin, to_node, to_pin}], edge_count: int }

commands.name: get_pcg_graph_parameters
commands.description: List a PCG graph's user parameters with name, type and current value -- and the read that decides whether a THIRD-PARTY graph can be reused without editing it. An empty list means nothing is exposed: meshes, densities and exclusions are welded inside, so the only way to change them is to edit the asset, which is not an option for a read-only library graph. Read-only. Note it accepts a PCGGraph asset, not a PCGGraphInstance -- overriding a parameter on an instance has no headless route and must be ticked in the details panel.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UPCGGraph (required)

commands.returns: { pcg_graph_path, parameter_count, parameters:[{name, type, value}] }

commands.name: get_pcg_node_properties
commands.description: Reads every editable property of a PCG node's settings object via reflection.  The node is resolved by name from get_pcg_graph_info (or the "Input"/"Output" tokens); its UPCGSettings is serialized to JSON. Read-only.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

params.name: node_name
params.description: The node_name from get_pcg_graph_info of the node to read (the tokens "Input"/"Output" address the implicit endpoints).

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_name: string, settings_class: string, properties: object }

commands.name: list_pcg_node_types
commands.description: Enumerate every PCG node type available in this build (all concrete PCGSettings subclasses, including plugin- and project-added ones), with class names and paths. Run it before add_pcg_node so you pass a class that exists instead of guessing a name from documentation that may not match this engine version. Read-only reflection.
commands.returns: { base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }

commands.name: remove_pcg_node
commands.description: Removes a user-added node from a PCG graph by name.  Uses UPCGGraph::RemoveNode, which auto-breaks the node's edges and notifies its neighbours; the graph is re-saved after the mutation. The implicit Input/Output endpoint nodes cannot be removed (doing so would silently corrupt the graph) and are rejected with an honest error. Idempotent: a node that is not present reports already_removed without error.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

params.name: node_name
params.description: The node_name from get_pcg_graph_info of the node to remove. The tokens "Input"/"Output" (and the endpoints' real names) are rejected: the implicit graph endpoints cannot be removed.

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_name: string, removed: bool, already_removed: bool, node_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: set_pcg_component_properties
commands.description: Sets properties on an actor's UPCGComponent by reflection (Seed, bActivated, bIsComponentPartitioned, GenerationTrigger, ...). Reads the stored values back into the response.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)

params.name: properties
params.description: JSON object { PropertyName: value, ... } applied to the component

commands.returns: { actor_name, set:[name], failed:[{name, error}], applied:{name: stored_value_text} }

commands.name: set_pcg_graph_parameter
commands.description: Write the value of an existing PCG graph user parameter (bool / int / float / double) and read the stored value back, so the reply is its own oracle -- how you tune scatter density or a rule threshold without opening the graph. The parameter must already exist (add_pcg_graph_parameter) and the value type must match. IMPORTANT: it accepts a PCGGraph ASSET only and answers "PCG graph not found" for a PCGGraphInstance -- per-instance overrides have no headless route and must be ticked in the details panel. Changing a parameter does not update the world: cleanup_pcg_component then generate_pcg_component, or the cached output is reused.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UPCGGraph (required)

params.name: name
params.description: Parameter name (must already exist; add with add_pcg_graph_parameter) (required)

params.name: value
params.description: New value; its type must match the parameter's declared type (required)

commands.returns: { pcg_graph_path, name, type, set, value }

commands.name: set_pcg_node_properties
commands.description: Authors a PCG node's settings object via reflection (partial merge + clamp).  Only the keys present in ``properties`` are written; absent keys are untouched. After the merge, PostEditChange() invalidates the node's cached CRC and regenerates its pins. The graph is re-saved and the persisted settings are read back. Idempotent: re-applying the same values is a no-op.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

params.name: node_name
params.description: The node_name from get_pcg_graph_info of the node to author (the tokens "Input"/"Output" address the implicit endpoints).

params.name: properties
params.description: Object of UPCGSettings fields to merge (e.g. for a SurfaceSampler: bApplyDensityToPoints(bool), PointsPerSquaredMeter(float>=0), Looseness(float)); absent keys untouched.

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_name: string, settings_class: string, applied_keys: [string], properties: object, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: spawn_pcg_volume
commands.description: Spawns an APCGVolume in the editor world with a REAL cube brush (from ``extent``), optionally assigning a graph. Bounds, origin, scale and brush geometry are RE-READ from the spawned actor, never echoed. Without ``extent`` the volume is spawned brush-less (kept for compatibility) and the response says so explicitly, because a PCG component with null bounds generates 0 instances in total silence.

params.name: location
params.description: World location [X, Y, Z] for the volume.

params.name: extent
params.description: Cube HALF-size [x, y, z] in unreal units, each > 0 (same convention as spawn_box_volume / spawn_navmesh_bounds_volume). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: omitting it leaves the volume with extent (0,0,0) and the PCG component generates 0 instances with no error and no warning.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation for the volume (default 0,0,0).

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Optional content path of a UPCGGraph to assign to the spawned volume's PCG component.

params.name: name
params.description: Optional explicit name (skipped if already used in the current level to avoid Rename-onto-occupied crash).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_label: string, actor_class: string, has_pcg_component: bool, pcg_graph_path: string, graph_assigned: bool, location: [float], bounds_extent_actual: [float], bounds_origin_actual: [float], actor_scale: [float], has_brush_geometry: bool, brush_poly_count: int, brush_requested: bool, scale_normalized: bool, warning?: string, requested: {...} }

commands.name: add_component_event
commands.description: Checks an event of a level actor's component; it never creates a binding (success is always false). A binding made on a live level-actor component would not persist: a handler belongs in a Blueprint's event graph. When the actor comes from a Blueprint and the event is a bindable delegate, the reply carries suggested_call: the add_component_bound_event call that authors it, with its parameters filled in.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name of the actor containing the component

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the component

params.name: event_name
params.description: Name of the event to add (must be one of: BeginPlay, EndPlay, Tick, Activate, Deactivate, Register, Unregister, TransformUpdated, OnClicked, OnBeginCursorOver, OnEndCursorOver, OnInputTouchBegin, OnInputTouchEnd, OnInputTouchEnter, OnInputTouchLeave)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, event_name: string, event_category: string, event_description: string, event_function_signature: string, success: bool, binding_created: bool, is_bindable_delegate: bool, delegate_property_name: string, bound_handler_count: int, message: string, error: string, component_class: string, component_category: string, component_tooltip: string, component_display_name: string, component_is_active: bool, component_is_registered: bool, component_owner: string, component_creation_method: string, suggested_call?: { tool: string, params: { blueprint_name, component_name, delegate_name } } }

commands.name: call_component_function
commands.description: Drive a COMPONENT without ever building its object path: name the actor, name the component CLASS, and it resolves the actor (editor world or a live PIE world via `world`), runs FindComponentByClass, and invokes the UFUNCTION with JSON arguments — the one generalist reflection call that replaces bespoke per-feature helpers (attribute getters, inventory or equipment calls), since almost all gameplay state in a component-based framework lives on components rather than on the actor. Arguments go in a dict named `params` (call_function uses `parameters`, call_object_method uses `args_json`); marshals scalars, ENUM by entry name, STRUCT as a JSON object, ARRAY/set as a JSON array, FGameplayTag (validated) and FGuid, and returns return_value + out_params typed alongside the resolved component_path and the identity of the world that answered. WARNING: it uses the FIRST component of (or derived from) that class. An OBJECT/class argument IS passed by path — resolved in the target's own world first, then as an asset, and a path that resolves to nothing is a hard error, never a silent null. In co-op, world='server' is where authoritative component state lives.

params.name: actor
params.description: Actor name / path / (in PIE, editor) label to resolve. In world='editor' also accepts a full object path / CDO / archetype; in world='pie' resolves within the running PIE world (Actor[.Component[.Subobject]] by name/label).

params.name: component_class
params.description: Component CLASS name/path to locate on the actor (bare/native e.g. "AC_Storage", /Script path, or Blueprint asset path — resolved via ResolveClass). The FIRST component of (or derived from) this class is used.

params.name: function
params.description: Name of the UFUNCTION to call on the component (BlueprintCallable+Public or a BlueprintEvent).

params.name: params
params.description: Optional {param_name: value} dict. Same marshaling as call_function: scalars; ENUM by entry name string; STRUCT as a JSON object; ARRAY/set as a JSON array; FGameplayTag as {"TagName":"A.B"} (validated); FGuid as a hex/braced string.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Anything other than absent/'editor' resolves the actor in that live world (LIVE component instance).

params.name: transact
params.description: Optional (default false). Wrap the invocation in an FScopedTransaction and Modify() BOTH the component and its owner actor first (a component's authored state persists in the OWNER's package — the OFPA .uasset for a World Partition actor), so the write is undoable and actually gets saved. REFUSED for pure/const functions and whenever world='pie'.

commands.returns: { success: bool, actor: string, component_class: string, component_path: string, function: string, world: string, returns_json: object ({ return_value?: any, out_params?: object }), transaction?: { requested, modified: [path], saved_to_transaction_buffer, is_package_external, package_name, package_file, package_file_exists, package_dirty_before, package_dirty_after }, verification?: object (only when transact=true), world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: call_function
commands.description: Invoke a UFUNCTION on an object instance in the EDITOR world and get its return value and out-params back typed. Arguments go in a dict named `parameters` (each sibling uses a DIFFERENT key — call_object_method uses `args_json`, call_component_function uses `params` — and an unknown key is a hard error, so read the signature with get_function_info first). Marshals scalars, ENUM by entry name, Blueprint STRUCTs as JSON objects, ARRAY/set as JSON arrays, FGameplayTag (validated against the registry) and FGuid. Choose call_object_method to reach a CDO/archetype/live PIE subobject or to pass `world`, call_component_function to hit a component without hand-building its path, and call_library_function for a static/library call with no instance at all. Only BlueprintCallable+Public or BlueprintEvent functions are callable; pass transact=true to make the write undoable and actually dirty an OFPA package.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object instance, resolved in the EDITOR world: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" whose first segment is the actor's internal name. This command has NO `world` parameter — use call_object_method for a live PIE target.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function to call, exactly as declared (a Blueprint graph named "Add Item" keeps its spaces)

params.name: parameters
params.description: Optional {param_name: value} dict. Scalars map directly; pass an ENUM by its entry name as a string (e.g. "Harvest"); pass a STRUCT param as a JSON object {Field: val, ...} and an ARRAY/set as a JSON array (nativized via FJsonObjectConverter — nested structs + enum-by-name inside structs supported; JSON keys match the field's authored name). A UE-format text string (e.g. "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)") is also accepted for structs.

params.name: transact
params.description: Optional (default false). When true, wrap the invocation in an FScopedTransaction and Modify() the target (and, for a component, its owner) BEFORE calling, so whatever the function writes is undoable AND marks the owning package dirty. Without this, a CallInEditor-style function that fills state on a World Partition (OFPA) actor leaves the package clean and save_level reports success while writing nothing. REFUSED for pure/const functions and for PIE-world targets (both would only produce a false-positive dirty flag).

commands.returns: { object_path: string, function_name: string, success: bool, message: string, return_value: any (typed: bool/number/string natively, struct/map as object, array/set as array, object-ref as path string), out_params: object (same typed values), transaction?: { requested, modified: [path], saved_to_transaction_buffer, is_package_external, package_name, package_file, package_file_exists, package_dirty_before, package_dirty_after }, verification?: object (only when transact=true) }

commands.name: call_library_function
commands.description: Invoke a static / BlueprintCallable library function on a class's Class Default Object, addressing the class by NAME or by Blueprint asset path so you never have to hand-build a "Default__X_C" object path. This is the way to reach UKismetSystemLibrary, UGameplayStatics, UGameplayTagLibrary and any Blueprint Function Library when there is no instance to talk to. Arguments go in a dict named `parameters` (call_object_method uses `args_json`, call_component_function uses `params`), with the same marshaling: scalars, ENUM by entry name, STRUCT as a JSON object, ARRAY/set as a JSON array, FGameplayTag (validated) and FGuid. Note it always runs on the CDO and takes no `world` selector — use call_object_method(world=...) or call_component_function(world=...) for anything that must run inside a live PIE world.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Class NAME (bare/native e.g. "KismetSystemLibrary", /Script path, or a Blueprint asset path — resolved via ResolveClass; a Blueprint path yields its GeneratedClass). The function is invoked on this class's Class Default Object.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function to call (BlueprintCallable+Public or a BlueprintEvent). Static library functions and BlueprintPure getters work here.

params.name: parameters
params.description: Optional {param_name: value} dict. Same marshaling as call_function: scalars map directly; ENUM by entry name string; STRUCT param as a JSON object; ARRAY/set as a JSON array; FGameplayTag as {"TagName":"A.B"} (validated); FGuid as a hex/braced string.

commands.returns: { success: bool, class_name: string, class_path: string, function_name: string, returns_json: object ({ return_value?: any, out_params?: object }) }

commands.name: call_object_method
commands.description: Invoke a UFUNCTION on ANY UObject — component archetype, class default object, asset, or a LIVE PIE subobject — not just level actors, and unlike call_function it takes a `world` selector so the same method can be driven on the server or on a client and the response stamps which world ran it. Arguments go in a dict named `args_json` (call_function uses `parameters`, call_component_function uses `params`); it marshals scalars, ENUM by entry name, STRUCT as a JSON object, ARRAY/set as a JSON array, FGameplayTag (validated) and FGuid, and reports return_value plus out_params typed. Use call_component_function instead when the target is a component you would otherwise have to path by hand, and call_library_function for a static library call. transact=true makes an editor-world write undoable and dirties the owning (OFPA) package; it is refused for pure functions and for PIE targets.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object; resolved in the editor world by default, or in the PIE world when use_pie_world=true (full/PIE path, or dotted Actor[.Component[.Subobject]] by name/label).

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function to call.

params.name: args_json
params.description: Optional {param_name: value} dict. Same marshaling as call_function: scalars map directly; ENUM by entry name string; STRUCT param as a JSON object; ARRAY/set as a JSON array; FGameplayTag as {"TagName":"A.B"}.

params.name: use_pie_world
params.description: Optional (default false). Resolve object_path in the running PIE world instead of the editor world. Equivalent to world='pie'; `world` wins when both are given.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector (takes precedence over use_pie_world): absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

params.name: transact
params.description: Optional (default false). Wrap the invocation in an FScopedTransaction and Modify() the target (and, for a component, its owner) first, so the write is undoable AND dirties the owning package — without it a write into an OFPA actor is never saved even though save_level reports success. REFUSED for pure/const functions and for PIE-world targets.

commands.returns: { success: bool, object_path: string, function_name: string, world: string, returns_json: object ({ return_value?: any, out_params?: object }), transaction?: { requested, modified: [path], saved_to_transaction_buffer, is_package_external, package_name, package_file, package_file_exists, package_dirty_before, package_dirty_after }, verification?: object (only when transact=true), world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: compare_objects
commands.description: Diff TWO LIVE objects property by property at the same instant, using the ENGINE's own equality (FProperty::Identical + PPF_DeepComparison) rather than exported text, so FText localization identity and object-outer differences are classified as `noise` instead of being reported as real differences. Use it for "instance vs its CDO", "fork vs original", "this actor vs that one". Accepts `world`, which resolves BOTH paths in the SAME world (e.g. two live actors inside the server world); to compare the same actor ACROSS worlds — server vs client — use snapshot_object + diff_object_snapshots, which is what a replication check needs. list_instance_overrides diffs a placed actor against its archetype and also tells you which package carries the override; diff_blueprints diffs the AUTHORED graphs instead of live values.

params.name: object_path_1
params.description: Path or name of the first object (full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" by internal name; in a live world the first segment also matches the editor LABEL)

params.name: object_path_2
params.description: Path or name of the second object, same resolution as object_path_1 and in the SAME world

params.name: equality_predicate
params.description: Optional 'identical' (DEFAULT, FProperty::Identical + PPF_DeepComparison — what the engine itself calls equal) or 'export_text' (raw ExportTextItem_Direct(Defaults=nullptr, PPF_None) string compare, kept only for callers that depend on its over-reporting behavior).

params.name: include_noise
params.description: Optional (default false). With equality_predicate='identical', also emit under `noise[]` the properties the engine considers EQUAL but whose exported text differs (FText localization identity, object outer). They are ALWAYS counted in `noise_counts` whether or not this is set.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector applied to BOTH paths: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). It cannot straddle two worlds — one selector, both objects; an UNRECOGNIZED value is an error naming the worlds that exist, never a silent fallback.

commands.returns: { object_path_1: string, object_path_2: string, same_class: bool, same_type: bool, equality_predicate: string, differences: [{property, difference, kind, value_1?: typed_value, value_2?: typed_value, export_text_1?, export_text_2?, note?}], difference_count: int, noise_counts: object, noise_count: int, noise?: [...], world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: find_classes_implementing_interface
commands.description: Enumerate every loaded class that implements a given UInterface. No inverse index exists in the engine (confirmed against source) -- this is an O(loaded classes) sweep, same idiom as list_subsystem_classes.

params.name: interface
params.description: Name/path of the interface to search for (resolved via ResolveClass)

params.name: include_blueprints
params.description: Include Blueprint-generated (non-native) classes (default true)

commands.returns: { interface: string, classes: [{class_name, path, is_blueprint, implemented_by_k2}], count: int, scanned_class_count: int }

commands.name: get_actor_properties_by_class
commands.description: Enumerate ACTORS by CLASS (or by editor label) and read their PROPERTIES in one call, in the editor world or in a live one. Reads the EDITOR world too (world='editor', with no PIE running), not just a live one. Use it instead of an execute_python loop over GetAllActorsOfClass + get_editor_property: it returns { path, props } per instance and stamps the world that answered, which such a loop does not. Filter with class_name (IsA) and/or actor_label, drill into one `component`, pick which `properties` to read, and use world='server' vs 'client' to separate an authoritative reading from a replicated one.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Class filter: bare UClass name resolved with FindFirstObject (e.g. "BP_MyActor_C", "StaticMeshActor"), NOT an asset path. Matches every actor that IsA(class_name). REQUIRED unless actor_label is given.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor-label filter; matches actors whose GetActorLabel() equals this EXACTLY (no substring, no case-folding). REQUIRED unless class_name is given — the call errors when both are missing.

params.name: component
params.description: Optional component name to drill into on each matched actor (reads that component's props instead of the actor's). WARNING: actors that have no component with this name are DROPPED from `instances` entirely, so a short list can mean "wrong component name", not "no such actor".

params.name: properties
params.description: Optional property names to read. Names the target does not have are skipped SILENTLY (no not_found list — cross-check the spelling with list_object_properties or get_class_properties). Omit it to read every BlueprintVisible property, which on a Character is a very large payload.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default, ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'editor' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). THIS is the parameter that separates a server reading from a client one.

commands.returns: { instances: [{ path: string, props: object (typed values) }], instance_count: int, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_class_functions
commands.description: List every UFUNCTION a class exposes — the ones it DECLARES plus every inherited one, each tagged with owner_class and is_inherited, and counted separately in declared_function_count / inherited_function_count so "does this class add a function of its own?" is answerable WITHOUT reading the array (declared_only=true returns just those) — with its signature and the flags that decide whether MCP can call it: is_blueprint_callable, is_public, is_static, is_blueprint_pure, is_blueprint_event, is_call_in_editor, category, tooltip and the parameter names/types. This is the lookup to run BEFORE call_function / call_object_method / call_component_function, which refuse anything that is not BlueprintCallable+Public or a BlueprintEvent. WARNING: ZERO own functions is NOT "no Blueprint API": components and data classes usually expose theirs as PROPERTIES (get_class_properties), and a plugin's runtime API often lives in a separate static "*BlueprintLibrary" class rather than on the type itself — both traps show up on MetaHumanComponentBase, whose creator API is in MetaHumanCharacterInstanceBlueprintLibrary. get_function_info drills into ONE function (and separates return values from inputs); get_blueprint_functions_list lists the graphs a Blueprint AUTHORED rather than the compiled class surface.

params.name: class_name
params.description: UClass identifier, resolved with ResolveClass: bare FName ("Character"), /Script/Module.Class, a Blueprint asset path, or a generated class ("BP_MyActor_C"). WARNING: the REGISTERED FName can differ from the C++ type name and from the name the Python bindings expose — UMetaHumanCharacterInstance is registered as "MetaHumanInstance" — so a failure here is NOT evidence the class is absent; the error names the near misses instead. The response echoes what it resolved to in resolved_class_name / resolved_class_path.

params.name: declared_only
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true = ONLY the UFUNCTIONs this class declares, skipping every inherited one.

commands.returns: { class_name: string, resolved_class_name: string, resolved_class_path: string, declared_only: bool, functions: [{name, owner_class, is_inherited, is_blueprint_callable, is_blueprint_event, is_public, is_static, is_blueprint_pure, is_call_in_editor, category?, tooltip?, parameters: [{name, type}]}], function_count: int, declared_function_count: int, inherited_function_count: int }

commands.name: get_class_hierarchy
commands.description: Walk the full inheritance chain of a class from itself up to UObject, one record per level with its path, is_native flag, class flags/metadata and implemented interfaces — the answer to "is X a Y?" and "where does the native code stop and the Blueprint chain start?". get_blueprint_parent returns only the IMMEDIATE parent of a Blueprint ASSET; this returns every ancestor of a compiled CLASS. get_blueprint_children goes the other direction (descendants).

params.name: class_name
params.description: UClass identifier, resolved with ResolveClass: bare FName ("Character"), /Script/Module.Class, a Blueprint asset path, or a generated class ("BP_MyActor_C"). WARNING: the REGISTERED FName can differ from the C++ type name and from the name the Python bindings expose — UMetaHumanCharacterInstance is registered as "MetaHumanInstance" — so a failure here is NOT evidence the class is absent; the error names the near misses instead. The response echoes what it resolved to in resolved_class_name / resolved_class_path.

commands.name: get_class_properties
commands.description: List every property VISIBLE on a class — the ones it DECLARES plus every inherited one, each tagged with owner_class and is_inherited so "does this class add anything of its own?" is a FIELD (declared_property_count) and not an eyeball diff against a remembered list of engine members. declared_only=true returns just this class's own. WARNING: a component or data class usually exposes its Blueprint API as PROPERTIES, not functions: get_class_functions coming back with nothing of its own does NOT mean the class has no API — ask here too (e.g. MetaHumanComponentBase: 0 own functions, 12 own properties). Full typed descriptor per property — kind, cpp_type, editable, edit_const, blueprint_visible, replicated, save_game, config, clamp min/max, enum entries, struct fields, tooltip, edit_condition — plus the class's own flags, config name and implemented interfaces. Schema only: NO instance values. Use list_object_properties for the same descriptors WITH the current values of a live object, get_properties when you already know the names, and get_blueprint_variables_list for just the variables a Blueprint itself authored.

params.name: class_name
params.description: UClass identifier, resolved with ResolveClass: bare FName ("Character"), /Script/Module.Class, a Blueprint asset path, or a generated class ("BP_MyActor_C"). WARNING: the REGISTERED FName can differ from the C++ type name and from the name the Python bindings expose — UMetaHumanCharacterInstance is registered as "MetaHumanInstance" — so a failure here is NOT evidence the class is absent; the error names the near misses instead. The response echoes what it resolved to in resolved_class_name / resolved_class_path.

params.name: declared_only
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true = ONLY the properties this class declares, skipping every inherited one. The cheap way to ask "what does this class add?", and what keeps a big class's response from being offloaded for size (get_class_properties("MetaHumanComponentBase") is 44 KB inherited-heavy, 12 properties declared).

commands.name: get_object_class
commands.description: Resolve an object instance and report just its type: class name, class path, is_native and immediate super class. The one-line "what IS this thing?" probe before spending a call on inspect_object or list_object_properties; get_class_hierarchy expands the same answer into the whole ancestor chain. Accepts `world`, so the same name can be typed in the editor world or in a LIVE PIE world (server vs client) — useful when a class is swapped at runtime — and the response stamps which world answered.

In the editor world: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" whose first segment is the actor's INTERNAL name. Answers "what actually lives inside this .uasset, besides the asset named after it?" and "does this package have unsaved changes?". WARNING: it resolves with FindFirstObject over loaded UPackages — a package that is on disk but not loaded is reported as not found; use get_asset_by_name / resolve_asset_by_name for on-disk existence, and list_dirty_packages to sweep every dirty package at once.

Use it instead of N calls to get_property_value; use list_object_properties when you do not know the names yet. Accepts `world`, so the SAME batch can be read on the server and on the client — the cheapest way to prove a value replicated — and the response stamps which world answered.

params.name: object_path

In a live world: a fully-qualified PIE path or the same dotted form (first segment matches internal name OR editor label).

params.name: world

commands.description: Read ONE property off ONE object you can already name (full object path, on-disk asset, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]"), typed rather than stringified. Cheapest of the property readers: use it for a single value, get_properties to batch several names off the same object, list_object_properties to dump every property with its editor metadata, and get_actor_properties_by_class when you do NOT have a path and want to find instances BY CLASS or LABEL instead. params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object instance. In the editor world: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" where the first segment is the actor's INTERNAL name (editor labels are not matched here — get_actor_properties_by_class's actor_label is). In a live world: a fully-qualified PIE path or the same dotted form (first segment matches internal name OR label).

params.name: property_name
params.description: Name of the property to read

params.name: world

Anything other than absent/'editor' resolves the object in that live world.

commands.name: get_struct_info
commands.description: Read the definition of a UScriptStruct (native or Blueprint-authored): its path and every member property as a typed descriptor. Use it to learn the FIELD NAMES before passing a struct as a JSON object to call_function / set_property_value, or to read the row layout behind a DataTable. get_struct_members is the Blueprint-struct-authoring view of the same asset; get_enum_info is the enum equivalent.

commands.name: inspect_object
commands.description: One-shot portrait of an object instance: identity (name, class, class path, is_valid), the class-level flags/metadata/implemented interfaces, EVERY reflected property as a { name: typed_value } map, and — when it is an actor — the list of its live components with their classes. The "I know nothing about this object yet" entry point; once you know what you want, get_property_value / get_properties are far cheaper, list_object_properties adds per-property editor metadata the map here omits, and get_actor_components lists components alone. Accepts `world`, so the portrait can be taken of the LIVE server instance or of the client one, and the response stamps which world answered.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to inspect. In the editor world: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" whose first segment is the actor's INTERNAL name. params.name: world

Anything other than absent/'editor' portrays the LIVE instance in that world; an UNRECOGNIZED value is an error naming the worlds that exist, never a silent fallback to another world.

commands.name: list_instance_overrides
commands.description: Audit a PLACED ACTOR (and every one of its components) against its ARCHETYPE and list the property values that were authored as per-instance overrides in the level, each with its archetype baseline, plus the physical package that carries them (the rotating-hash OFPA .uasset for a World Partition actor) and whether that package is dirty. The tool that answers "did my write actually land on this instance, or only look like it?" — it catches set_property_value reporting success on an FGameplayTag while storing an empty "()" override. Component baselines are the SCS TEMPLATE, not the Blueprint CDO (a CDO carries no SCS components at all). Resolves in the EDITOR world by design: an instance override is an on-disk concept, not a runtime one.

params.name: actor
params.description: Actor to audit: internal object name, editor label, or full object path. Resolved in the EDITOR world — a per-instance override is an editor/on-disk concept, not a runtime one.

params.name: include_components

params.name: require_edit
params.description: Optional (default true). Only consider properties flagged CPF_Edit, i.e. what a human could actually have authored in the details panel. false widens to every reflected property.

params.name: include_transient

params.name: include_noise

commands.description: Dump EVERY reflected property of one object instance with its current value AND its full editor metadata (type, editable, edit_const, blueprint_visible, replicated, save_game, clamp, tooltip, enum entries...). The discovery tool of the property family: use it when you do not yet know the property NAMES, then switch to get_property_value (one name) or get_properties (several names) which are far cheaper. get_class_properties gives the same descriptors WITHOUT values for a class you cannot instantiate; get_actor_properties_by_class finds instances by class/label when you have no object path. Accepts `world`, so it can dump the live server instance or the client one.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object instance. In the editor world: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" whose first segment is the actor's INTERNAL name (not its editor label). In a live world: a fully-qualified PIE path or the same dotted form (first segment matches internal name OR label).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default: the editor/asset instance) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Anything other than absent/'editor' resolves the object in that live world (LIVE per-instance state).

commands.returns: { object_path: string, class_name: string, properties: [<typed descriptor (see get_class_properties) + typed value>], property_count: int, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

The response stamps the world that answered, so count:0 means "not in THIS world" instead of "does not exist".

commands.name: get_actor_replication_info
commands.description: Read replication settings for an editor-world actor (replicates, replicate_movement via reflection, frequencies, dormancy, role).

commands.name: serialize_actor_state
commands.description: Save an actor's transform plus an EXPLICIT set of properties into a SaveGame slot, keyed by an identity YOU choose (stable_key, defaulting to actor_name). Nothing is captured implicitly: name the properties you want in property_names or you get the transform and only the transform. Idempotent -- re-serializing the same key overwrites that slot, it never duplicates. Pair with restore_actor_state, which takes the same key.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Required. Object name or editor label of the actor to serialize (resolved via mcp_common::FindActorByName).

params.description: Optional array of UPROPERTY names to capture in addition to the transform. If omitted, ONLY the transform is saved -- it never silently saves "everything" via CPF_SaveGame, which no native property here sets and which, on a Blueprint variable, depends on whether that Blueprint ticked the SaveGame checkbox (get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info reports it): a filter this command cannot assume for you.

commands.name: add_consideration
commands.description: Attach a utility-AI consideration (any struct deriving from FStateTreeConsiderationBase) to a state's Considerations array on a UStateTree. Considerations rank selectable children by score (0..1) when the state's selection behavior is utility-driven (e.g. TrySelectChildrenWithHighestUtility). Friendlier aliases are accepted in addition to the full struct name: "Constant" -> StateTreeConstantConsideration, "FloatInput"/"Float Input" -> StateTreeFloatInputConsideration, "EnumInput"/"Enum Input" -> StateTreeEnumInputConsideration. Use set_consideration_property to set initial values like Constant.Constant or FloatInput.Input. Idempotent: re-adding the same struct-type appends another consideration (engine semantics; considerations of the same type are valid).

params.name: tree_path
params.description: Asset path of the UStateTree

params.name: state_name
params.description: Name of the state to attach the consideration to

params.name: consideration_class
params.description: Struct name (FStateTreeConstantConsideration / StateTreeConstantConsideration) or alias (Constant|FloatInput|Enum Input|...)

commands.returns: { tree_path, state_name, consideration_class, consideration_count, added, saved }

commands.name: add_state
commands.description: Add a top-level state (a new SubTree, never a child of another state) to a StateTree asset, then compile and save it. Idempotent: if any state already has that name nothing changes and already_existed is true. Returns state_count, added and saved.

params.name: tree_path
params.description: Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard".

params.name: state_name
params.description: Name of the new state, e.g. "Patrol"; the other state commands find states by this name.

commands.returns: { tree_path, state_name, state_count, already_existed, added, saved }

params.name: condition_struct

commands.returns: { tree_path, state_name, condition_struct, enter_condition_count, added, saved }

commands.name: add_state_evaluator
commands.description: Attach an evaluator node (by struct name, via reflection) to a UStateTree; evaluators are TREE-scoped (they live on UStateTreeEditorData::Evaluators, not on a state) and tick for the whole tree, so this command takes no state_name.  Idempotent: an evaluator of the same struct already present is not appended again.

commands.name: add_state_transition
commands.description: Append a transition from from_state to to_state on a StateTree asset (trigger OnStateCompleted, type GotoState), then compile and save it; each call adds another one. event_name only fills RequiredEvent, which matters with an OnEvent trigger: set that with set_transition_properties. Returns transition_count and saved.

params.name: tree_path
params.description: Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard".

params.name: from_state

params.name: to_state

commands.name: add_state_tree_binding
commands.description: Bind a UStateTree root parameter (source) to a target node's input property (target), so the node reads the parameter at runtime.  The target defaults to a state Task, but target_kind selects any FStateTreeEditorNode list: enter_condition/consideration (on the state) or global_task/evaluator (on the tree) — the binding anchor (FStateTreeEditorNode::ID) is identical for every kind. Authors an FStateTreePropertyPathBinding in the editor data's property bindings (idempotent per target path — re-binding the same target replaces it); validate it resolves with compile_state_tree.

params.name: tree_path
params.description: Asset path to the UStateTree.

params.name: target_property
params.description: Name of the target node's input property to bind (the binding target), e.g. "BindableText".

params.name: source_parameter
params.description: Name of the root parameter to bind from (the binding source; add it with add_tree_parameter first).

params.name: state_name
params.description: Name of the state owning the target node (required for target_kind task|enter_condition|consideration; ignored for global_task|evaluator, which live on the tree).

params.name: target_kind
params.description: Which node list holds the target: "task" (default) | "enter_condition" | "consideration" | "global_task" | "evaluator".

params.name: target_index
params.description: Optional index into the selected node list (default 0).

commands.returns: { tree_path: string, state_name: string?, target_kind: string, target_index: int, target_property: string, source_parameter: string, source_struct_id: string, target_struct_id: string, bound: bool, binding_count: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_component_parameter_override
commands.description: Override a single UStateTree root parameter on a UStateTreeComponent living on a placed actor. CRITICAL: the implementation calls UStateTreeStateTreeReference::SetPropertyOverridden(ParamGuid, true) — without this, the runtime reads from the asset default and the per-instance value is silently dropped. The value is written via FInstancedPropertyBag::SetValueSerializedString so the engine parses the string into the parameter's actual type (Bool/Int/Float/Vector/Struct/...). The tree must already declare the parameter; add it with add_tree_parameter first. Use clear_overrides=true to remove the override (asset default takes over again) without writing a value. If the component has no bound tree, pass state_tree_path to auto-bind before overriding (cold-start convenience); the public UStateTreeComponent::SetStateTree(UStateTree*) handles the bind through reflection on the protected StateTreeRef member.

params.name: value
params.description: Optional string-encoded value; type-driven by the parameter's FPropertyBagPropertyDesc

params.name: state_tree_path
params.description: Optional path to a UStateTree to bind the component to if no tree is already bound

params.name: clear_overrides
params.description: If true, drop all per-instance overrides on the component (asset defaults take over); value is ignored

commands.returns: { actor_label, component_class, parameter_name, parameter_id, value, was_overridden, cleared, saved, bound_tree }

Newly-created colors get a fresh UUID; the caller is responsible for re-binding any state ColorRefs that referenced an orphaned previous UUID. r/g/b default to 1.0; a defaults to 1.0. The engine stores Colors as a TSet<FStateTreeEditorColor> keyed on ColorRef (display name uniqueness is the caller's responsibility — duplicate names are allowed by the engine but produce ambiguous lookups downstream).

commands.name: inspect_subsystem_instance

commands.name: watch_pie_property
commands.description: Sample one or SEVERAL properties across a PIE session, arming BEFORE PIE starts so a write that happens in BeginPlay is still observable. Answers "what did this value do during play", NOT "who wrote it": it SAMPLES rather than intercepting writes, so `identifies_writer` is always false and a transient A->B->A between two samples is invisible. THE ORDER MATTERS: action="start" arms and returns immediately (it cannot block the game thread), THEN you start PIE, and afterwards action="status" returns the recorded samples. Arming while PIE is ALREADY running is honoured but flagged (`armed_while_pie_running`) -- the BeginPlay window has already passed for that session, which is precisely the failure this tool exists to avoid, so stop PIE, arm, then start PIE. It self-disarms on duration_seconds or max_samples (it can never leak a ticker) and the recorded samples survive until action="clear".

params.name: action
params.description: Optional: "start" (default) | "status" | "stop" | "clear" | "list".

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property to sample on the matched object. Required for "start" unless `properties` is given.

params.name: properties
params.description: Optional array of property names sampled TOGETHER, in the SAME tick, as one ROW. This is what answers correlation questions ("movement_mode changed in the same tick immersion crossed the threshold"), which N separate watches cannot: each would dedupe on its own clock and the columns would not line up. The row is the dedup unit -- if ANY field changes the whole row is recorded -- and each sample carries a `values` object with the per-property breakdown. With one property there is no `values` object.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Optional actor class filter (exact UClass name; a Blueprint class needs the "_C" suffix). At least one of class_name / actor_label is required for "start".

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Optional actor filter, matched against the editor label OR the object name.

params.name: component
params.description: Optional component name: sample the property on that component of the matched actor instead of on the actor.

params.name: sample_interval_seconds
params.description: Optional periodic sampling interval (default 0.1, min 0.01).

params.name: duration_seconds
params.description: Optional auto-disarm after this many real seconds (default 300; 0 = no time cap, disarms only on max_samples or an explicit stop).

params.name: max_samples
params.description: Optional hard cap on recorded samples (default 400).

params.name: watch_id
params.description: Target watch for "status" / "stop" / "clear" (omit = all of them).

commands.returns: { action: string, watch_id?: int, armed?: bool, watches: [{ watch_id, property_name, class_name, actor_label, component, sample_interval_seconds, duration_seconds, max_samples, active, saw_pie_world, armed_while_pie_running, sample_count, elapsed_real_seconds, stop_reason, distinct_objects_seen, samples?: [{ phase, object_path, actor_label, value_text, value, elapsed_real_seconds, world_time_seconds, world, changed_from_previous }] }], identifies_writer: bool, sampling_only: bool, armed_pre_pie?: bool, pie_running?: bool, class_resolved?: bool, hint?: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }. The five world_* / net_mode / pie_instance fields identify the PIE world the ticker is sampling AT THE MOMENT OF THE CALL (all null / pie_instance -1 when no PIE session is running, which is the normal state right after arming).

A 0 value means "no roll" (clears the roll window). The values are written via the inline SetPreRollFrames / SetPostRollFrames setters and read back through the section's public FFrameNumber fields.

Frames are tick-resolution frames, rounded; keys are not moved or rescaled. range_set is false when the stored range differs from the request. Read a section's range with get_section_info; for the whole sequence use set_sequence_playback_range.

commands.name: set_sequence_display_rate
commands.description: Set the display frame rate of a Level Sequence.  The display rate is the asset-level "play rate" (frames per second of the timeline). Changing it rescales how existing frame numbers map to time. Backed by UMovieScene::SetDisplayRate(FFrameRate).  Note: The numerator/denominator are integers (FFrameRate), so the fps argument is rounded to the nearest whole-number fps. For non-integer rates (e.g. 23.976) the caller should still pass the closest whole number; the engine does not support fractional FFrameRate numerators without a custom non-integer tick resolution.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the Level Sequence.

params.name: fps
params.description: New display rate in frames per second. Must be > 0.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, fps: float, numerator: int, denominator: int, verified: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_sequence_duration
commands.description: Sets the playback range of a Level Sequence (found by asset name under /Game) to [0, duration) and marks the package dirty without saving; not undoable. Returns previous_duration, actual_duration, duration_set (within 0.01 s), and start_frame and end_frame in tick-resolution frames.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path (e.g. "LS_Intro"); the first match under /Game is used

params.name: duration
params.description: New length in seconds, greater than 0 and at most 3600 (0 is refused)

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, requested_duration: number, previous_duration: number, actual_duration: number, duration_set: bool, start_frame: int, end_frame: int }

commands.name: set_sequence_frame_rate
commands.description: Change the frame rate of a Level Sequence: its tick resolution AND its display rate, as create_level_sequence sets them (one tick per frame). Every key, section and range is migrated to the new rate, so nothing moves in time. To change only the display rate, use set_sequence_display_rate.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the sequence to modify

params.name: frame_rate
params.description: New frame rate in fps, must be greater than 0; NTSC rates (23.976, 29.97, 59.94) become N*1000/1001

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, frame_rate: number, numerator: int, denominator: int, previous_frame_rate: number, frame_rate_set: bool } -- read back from the movie scene

commands.name: set_sequence_playback_range
commands.description: Sets the playback range of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, in tick-resolution frames (start inclusive, end exclusive, rounded), in an undo transaction, and saves the sequence. Tracks, sections and keys are not moved or clipped, and the Sequencer's playback-range lock does not block it. range_set compares the stored range with the request. To set a length in seconds from 0 use set_sequence_duration; the editor-only timeline windows are set_sequence_view_range and set_sequence_working_range.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence (found by AssetName under /Game).

params.name: start_frame
params.description: Inclusive lower bound of the playback range, in tick frames.

params.name: end_frame
params.description: Exclusive upper bound of the playback range (must be > start_frame).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, requested_start_frame: int, requested_end_frame: int, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, range_set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_sequence_view_range
commands.description: Sets the editor view range of a Level Sequence (path or bare asset name), in seconds: the visible window of the Sequencer timeline. Editor UI state only, it changes neither playback nor the playback range. The engine keeps it in a transient field, so it lasts for this editor session and is not saved (persisted is always false); a Sequencer showing the sequence follows it on its next tick. Undoable, and the package is not marked dirty. verified compares the stored range with the request. For the scrollable bounds use set_sequence_working_range; for what plays use set_sequence_playback_range.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the Level Sequence.

params.name: start_seconds
params.description: Start of the view range, in seconds.

params.name: end_seconds
params.description: End of the view range, in seconds. Must be > start_seconds.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, start_seconds: float, end_seconds: float, verified: bool, persisted: bool (always false: the field is transient) }

commands.name: set_sequence_working_range
commands.description: Sets the working range of a Level Sequence (path or bare asset name): the scrollable bounds of the Sequencer timeline, in seconds. Editor UI state only, it changes neither playback nor evaluation. The engine keeps it in a transient field, so it lasts for this editor session and is not saved (persisted is always false): after a reload the working range is recomputed from the playback range. Undoable, and the package is not marked dirty. verified compares the stored range with the request. For the visible window use set_sequence_view_range; for what plays use set_sequence_playback_range.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the Level Sequence.

params.name: start_seconds
params.description: Start of the working range, in seconds.

params.name: end_seconds
params.description: End of the working range, in seconds. Must be > start_seconds.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, start_seconds: float, end_seconds: float, verified: bool, persisted: bool (always false: the field is transient) }

commands.name: spawn_box_volume
commands.description: USE THIS, NOT the plain actor spawners, for ANY AVolume-derived actor: it spawns the actor AND builds a real cube brush for it from a half-extent, so the volume actually encloses space. The generic spawners leave an EMPTY UModel brush -- zero bounds, which means 0 nav tiles and no overlap, an actor that looks spawned and does nothing. It then normalizes the residual scale some actor factories stamp on placement and RE-READS the resulting world bounds, so `success` means "the volume you got matches the volume you asked for", not "the call returned".

params.name: volume_class
params.description: Volume class: short reflected name ('NavMeshBoundsVolume', 'PhysicsVolume', 'TriggerVolume', 'BlockingVolume', 'PCGVolume', with or without a leading 'A') or a full object path ('/Script/Engine.TriggerVolume'). Must derive from AVolume (required).

params.name: location
params.description: World [x, y, z] location to spawn the volume (default 0,0,0)

params.name: extent
params.description: Required [x, y, z] in unreal units, each component > 0. !!! THIS IS THE SEMI-AXIS (HALF-size), NOT the full edge length !!! extent=[500,500,200] builds a 1000 x 1000 x 400 cube and, with the scale normalized, gives world bounds of +/-500 / +/-200 around `location`. Check `bounds_extent_actual` against what you asked for.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Optional editor label for the spawned actor

params.name: is_spatially_loaded
params.description: World Partition spatial-loading flag (default true; only applied when the actor allows changing it). Reported RE-READ from the actor.

params.name: normalize_scale
params.description: Default TRUE: resets the actor scale to (1,1,1) after building the brush, so the world bounds equal the requested `extent`. It matters because some actor factories stamp a default scale during placement -- APCGVolume is spawned at (25, 25, 10) -- and since brush polys are authored in LOCAL space that scale MULTIPLIES your extent. Set it false only if you deliberately want the factory's scale; `spawn_scale` always reports what it was. Be aware that with normalize_scale=false and a factory scale != 1 the real bounds are NOT the requested extent, so `extent_matches_request` and therefore `success` come back FALSE -- that is the honest answer, not a bug, and `actor_scale` says why they differ.

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_path, actor_class, volume_class, world_bounds_extent: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, GetActorBounds -- kept for compatibility), bounds_extent_actual: [x,y,z] (RE-READ from the BRUSH component's world bounds; this is the volume itself, with no stray editor sprite in the box), bounds_origin_actual: [x,y,z], actor_scale: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, after normalization), spawn_scale: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, as the actor factory left it), scale_normalized: bool (true only when a correction was actually needed), extent_matches_request: bool, bounds_tolerance_uu: number, has_brush_geometry, brush_built, is_spatially_loaded (RE-READ), spatial_flag_applied, success, requested: { volume_class, location, extent, actor_label, is_spatially_loaded, normalize_scale } }

commands.name: add_widget_property_binding
commands.description: Bind a widget PROPERTY to a function of the Widget Blueprint -- the Designer's "Bind" dropdown, headless. The property then recomputes every frame from that function instead of holding a fixed value (a health bar's Percent, a label's Text, a panel's Visibility). TWO RULES, both enforced by the ENGINE'S OWN validator (FDelegateEditorBinding::IsBindingValid, the same code the UMG compiler runs -- this tool does not second-guess it): the property is bindable only if its widget declares a companion delegate named "<Property>Delegate" (Text -> TextDelegate), and the function must have a COMPATIBLE SIGNATURE (same return type, NO parameters) and be PURE (BlueprintPure or const), because it is called while painting. A refusal names which of the two failed and, when the property is not bindable at all, lists the ones that are. Create the function first with add_blueprint_function + set its return type; one property can hold only ONE binding, so re-binding the same property REPLACES it (reported in replaced_existing).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget in the tree whose property gets bound (must be a direct variable of the UserWidget)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property to bind, e.g. "Text" on a TextBlock, "Percent" on a ProgressBar, "Visibility" on any widget. Must have a companion "<property_name>Delegate" on the widget's class.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function ON THIS Widget Blueprint that supplies the value. Must be pure and take no parameters, returning the property's type.

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true). The compile is what turns the editor binding into the runtime one, so a false here leaves the binding authored but not live.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, property_name: string, function_name: string, bound: bool, valid: bool, replaced_existing: bool, member_guid: string, validation_messages: [string], bindable_properties?: [string], saved: bool, save_error: string }

Idempotent by name: a widget already called widget_name with the same class is returned as is (already_existed true), and the blueprint is compiled and saved only when it has unsaved changes; a widget of another class under that name is an error. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error. add_widget_extended takes the larger palette of list_widget_types.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_type
params.description: one of TextBlock, Button, Image, VerticalBox, CanvasPanel (the curated basic names; see list_widget_types), OR any native widget class path (e.g. /Script/UMG.Throbber), OR a UserWidget-derived Widget Blueprint to embed as a nested instance, by its /Game asset path (e.g. /Game/UI/WBP_HealthBar) or generated-class path (/Game/UI/WBP_HealthBar.WBP_HealthBar_C)

params.name: widget_name
params.description: unique name for the new widget

params.description: Optional name of a panel widget to host the new child; defaults to the root widget.

commands.name: apply_widget_style_preset
commands.description: Apply ONE block of style properties to EVERY widget of a Widget Blueprint that matches a filter, in a single pass with ONE compile + ONE save -- the multi-widget companion to set_widget_property's multi-path form. Selection is target_widgets (explicit names, wins over everything) OR target_class (matched with IsA, so subclasses count) AND/OR name_pattern (wildcard). At least one selector is required: to hit every widget in the tree say so explicitly with name_pattern="*". Every value goes through the same honest applier, so the per-widget report distinguishes what landed from what was ignored; dry_run=true resolves the match and reports it WITHOUT writing, which is the cheap way to check a filter before it touches 40 widgets.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: preset
params.description: Dict of {"<property or dotted path>": <value>} applied to each matched widget, e.g. {"WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor":"#1B1B1BFF"}. Optional when the source_* params are used; when both are given the inline values WIN, so you can say "the theme, but this one in red". A path that does not exist on a given matched widget lands in that widget's ignored[] instead of failing the whole call.

params.name: source_bp_path
params.description: THEME MODE: /Game path of a Widget Blueprint holding a REFERENCE widget to copy the style from, instead of writing the values inline. This is what makes one widget the single source of truth rather than scattering the same colour across 40 calls.

params.name: source_widget_name
params.description: Name of the reference widget inside source_bp_path. Required with source_bp_path.

params.name: source_property_paths
params.description: Which paths to copy off the reference widget, e.g. ["WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor","WidgetStyle.NormalPadding"]. A path that does not resolve on the REFERENCE is an error, not a silent skip: an incomplete theme that says nothing is worse than a refusal. Use audit_widget_style with the same reference + paths to find what has drifted before fixing it.

params.name: target_class
params.description: Class filter matched with IsA: a curated name (Button, TextBlock), a native class path (/Script/UMG.Button) or a Widget Blueprint asset path. Subclasses match too.

params.name: name_pattern
params.description: Wildcard on the widget's name (Btn_*, *_Title, or * for every widget). Combined with target_class as AND.

params.name: target_widgets
params.description: Explicit widget names. When present, target_class and name_pattern are IGNORED and only these are touched (reported in selector_used).

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Resolve the match and report it without writing anything (default false).

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true; a dry run never saves).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, selector_used: string, matched: [string], matched_count: int, dry_run: bool, results: [{widget_name, widget_class, applied, ignored, errors, failed_paths, applied_count, all_applied}], widgets_fully_applied: int, widgets_with_failures: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

Unlike read_pie_widgets (read-only) this MUTATES runtime state -- it runs the exact bound handlers a real click would, including the client->server RPC path, so equip/inventory/craft UI flows can be driven headless instead of by a human (driving them via call_function bypasses that RPC path and yields false negatives). commands.description: Create a runtime UUserWidget instance of a concrete UserWidget class in a running PIE world (the default while PIE runs) or the editor world, owned by that world's first local PlayerController when there is one, and optionally AddToViewport it. Nothing is saved, and an unreferenced widget is garbage-collected. In the editor world add_to_viewport never adds (no PlayerController): read added_to_viewport. A taken name gets a unique variant, reported in widget_name; a class that does not load, is abstract or is not a UserWidget is an error. To change the asset use add_widget_to_blueprint; remove_widget searches the same worlds.

params.description: Full path to widget class, e.g. '/Game/UI/MyWidget.MyWidget_C'
