commands.name: create_widget_blueprint
commands.description: Create (and save) a new UWidgetBlueprint asset with a CanvasPanel root.

params.name: package_path
params.description: /Game folder to create the asset in (e.g. /Game/UI)

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (no extension)

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Parent UUserWidget subclass (default "UUserWidget").

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, root_created: bool, root_widget: string, root_widget_class: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: duplicate_widget
commands.description: Duplicate a widget (DuplicateObject<UWidget> outered to the WidgetTree) and add the clone under a target parent panel, copying the source's slot property values onto the new slot when the slot classes match. Refuses (clear error, no partial/broken result) to duplicate a panel widget that currently has children -- UE's object duplication would leave the clone's slots aliasing the SAME original child widgets rather than deep-copying them (see FDuplicateDataWriter); duplicate leaf widgets, or rebuild the panel's children individually with add_widget_extended. Name collisions on new_name are a clear error (not a silent alias of the pre-existing widget at that name).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget to duplicate (must not be a panel widget with children)

params.name: new_name
params.description: unique name for the duplicate

params.name: target_parent_name
params.description: Optional name of the panel widget to host the duplicate; defaults to the source widget's own current parent (sibling placement).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, source_widget_name: string, new_widget_name: string, widget_class: string, target_parent_name: string, slot_class: string, slot_class_matched_source: bool, slot_properties_copied: int, duplicated: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: get_pie_focused_widget
commands.description: Report which UMG widget currently has FOCUS in the running PIE session -- the assertion that makes gamepad navigation testable instead of eyeballed. Resolves FSlateApplication's focused SWidget and maps it back to the UMG UWidget that created it, by walking up to the owning SObjectWidget and matching cached widgets: the same route the engine's own navigation component uses, and it has to walk up because the widget holding focus is usually an internal SButton, not the one that maps 1:1 to a UWidget. Pair it with inject_key_input route="slate", the only input path that moves focus at all: press Down, read this, assert. Returns has_focus:false as an honest success (not an error) when nothing is focused -- which is itself the finding when a menu opens with no focus and every navigation key then appears to do nothing.

params.name: user_index
params.description: Optional Slate user index (default 0). Local co-op players are separate Slate users, so player 2 is user 1.

commands.returns: { has_focus: bool, slate_widget_type: string, widget_name: string, widget_class: string, owning_user_widget: string, owning_user_widget_class: string, resolved_to_umg: bool, note? } -- resolved_to_umg:false together with has_focus:true means something in Slate holds focus but it is not a UMG widget (the viewport, a native Slate panel); slate_widget_type still names it.

commands.name: get_widget_animations
commands.description: List the UWidgetAnimations of a Widget Blueprint asset, each with its object name, display_name and has_movie_scene, plus animation_count and the resolved asset_path. Read-only; add_widget_animation creates one and remove_widget_animation accepts either name.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: Asset path of the Widget Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu"; it must exist.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, asset_path: string, animations: [{name, display_name, has_movie_scene}], animation_count: int }

commands.name: get_widget_blueprint_tree
commands.description: Return a Widget Blueprint's widget tree as nested {name, class, children[]} AND, on request, the actual VALUES of its widgets and slots -- which is what makes verifying a style a cheap read instead of a PIE session. Off by default (a bare tree is what name-only callers want); three switches turn it on: property_paths reads exact dotted paths ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor") on every node whether or not they still hold the default -- this is the oracle that closes a set_widget_property; include_properties reports only what DIFFERS from each widget's archetype, i.e. what this Widget Blueprint actually changed, instead of the ~120 inherited properties nobody reads; include_slot adds each widget's UPanelSlot class plus its own non-default values (position, anchors, padding, row/column). Values come back as TYPED JSON, not UE export-text. widget_name dumps one subtree instead of the whole asset.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Optional: dump only this widget and its descendants instead of the whole tree.

params.name: property_paths
params.description: Optional list of property names or dotted paths read on EVERY node, emitted under "properties" even when the value is still the default. A path that does not exist on a given widget is listed in that node's "unresolved_property_paths" (normal: a WidgetStyle has no meaning on a TextBlock), never silently dropped.

params.name: include_properties
params.description: Emit each widget's editable properties that DIFFER from its archetype, under "non_default_properties" (default false).

params.name: include_slot
params.description: Emit each widget's UPanelSlot class and its non-default slot values under "slot" (default false).

params.name: include_navigation
params.description: Emit each widget's six gamepad/keyboard navigation directions under "navigation" (default false). A widget with no authored navigation reports all six as Escape with has_authored_navigation:false -- which is what it will actually do in game, rather than an empty object the caller has to interpret. Author them with set_widget_navigation.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Optional recursion limit (-1 = unlimited, the default). A panel cut off by the limit reports "children_omitted" instead of passing for a leaf.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, asset_path: string, widget_count: int, root_widget: string, dumped_root: string, include_properties: bool, include_slot: bool, include_navigation: bool, property_paths: [string], tree: {name, class, properties?, unresolved_property_paths?, non_default_properties?, slot?, children: [...], children_omitted?} }

commands.name: get_widget_hierarchy
commands.description: Retrieve the widget hierarchy tree including parent, children, and nested structure information.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget to query

commands.returns: { widget_name: string, hierarchy: { name: string, class: string, depth: number, valid: bool, enabled: bool, visibility: string, size?: { width, height }, position?: { x, y, z }, children: [object], child_count: number }, widget_valid: bool }

commands.name: get_widget_properties
commands.description: Retrieve detailed properties and state information for a widget by name.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget to query

commands.returns: { widget_name: string, widget_class: string, widget_valid: bool, widget_visible: bool, visibility: string, size?: { width: number, height: number }, position?: { x: number, y: number, z: number }, rotation?: { pitch: number, yaw: number, roll: number }, scale?: { x: number, y: number, z: number }, parent_widget?: string, parent_class?: string, child_count: number, is_enabled: bool, has_focus: bool }

commands.name: list_level_widget_components
commands.description: CALL THIS FIRST to discover valid widget_name values instead of guessing: it enumerates ALL UWidgetComponents on ALL actors of the current EDITOR level, which is the EXACT population that get_widget_properties / set_widget_visibility / get_widget_hierarchy search by widget_name (remove_widget searches it too). It reads GEditor's world and never a running PIE session (use read_pie_widgets for that), and it lists every widget component on an actor, not just the first. WARNING: THIS POPULATION IS NOT WIDGET BLUEPRINTS, and that is the trap the name does not warn you about: these are world-space UWidgetComponents hosted on actors. To author the CONTENT of a Widget Blueprint asset -- its tree, styles or layout -- you want get_widget_blueprint_tree / set_widget_property / set_widget_slot_properties instead. In particular ANCHORS live on a UCanvasPanelSlot inside a Widget Blueprint's tree and have no meaning at all on a level UWidgetComponent: set them with set_widget_slot_properties(widget_bp_path, widget_name, anchors=[min_x,min_y,max_x,max_y]).

params.name: actor_name_filter
params.description: Optional substring filter on the owning actor's name (Contains match)

commands.returns: { components: [{ actor_name: string, widget_component_name: string, widget_name: string|null, widget_class: string|null }], component_count: number, actor_name_filter: string|null }

commands.name: list_widget_property_bindings
commands.description: List the UMG PROPERTY BINDINGS of a Widget Blueprint -- the "Bind" dropdown next to a property in the Designer's details panel, which makes that property recompute every frame by calling a function instead of holding a fixed value. These live in UWidgetBlueprint::Bindings, NOT in the widget tree and NOT in the event graph, so no other reader sees them; and UWidgetBlueprint::Bindings is NOT exposed to Python either (get_editor_property("bindings") throws), so this is the only headless way to read them. Each entry is re-validated live with the engine's own FDelegateEditorBinding::IsBindingValid, so a binding whose function was renamed or made non-pure comes back valid:false WITH the compiler's reason -- that is the difference between "there is a binding" and "there is a binding that works".

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: include_bindable_properties
params.description: Also list, per widget in the tree, which properties ACCEPT a binding at all (default false). A property is bindable only if its widget declares a companion delegate named "<Property>Delegate" -- this saves guessing.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, binding_count: int, bindings: [{ widget_name, property_name, function_name, kind, member_guid, source_property, valid, validation_messages: [string] }], bindable_properties?: {widget_name: [string]} }

commands.name: list_widget_types
commands.description: List the CURATED widget_type names accepted by add_widget_to_blueprint (family="basic") / add_widget_extended (family="extended", the default -- a strict superset of basic), with each entry's resolved /Script/UMG.<Name> class path and whether LoadObject actually resolves it in this build (should always be true; reported for honesty rather than assumed). This list is a convenience shortlist, NOT the full set of accepted values -- both tools also accept any native widget class path (/Script/Module.ClassName) and any UserWidget-derived Widget Blueprint's /Game asset path (embeds a nested instance); see custom_class_note in the response.

params.name: family
params.description: Optional "basic" | "extended" (default "extended")

commands.returns: { family: string, widget_types: [{ widget_type: string, class_path: string, resolvable: bool }], count: int, custom_class_note: string }

commands.name: play_widget_animation
commands.description: Play a widget animation. REAL playback (UUserWidget::PlayAnimation) when a live PIE instance of this WidgetBP is found in the viewport's active UUserWidgets; falls back to an honest headless gate (played:false, headless:true, requires_pie:true) when no PIE session is running or no live instance is found.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the animation to play

params.name: start_at_time
params.description: Optional float seconds to start playback at (default 0).

params.name: num_loops
params.description: Optional int number of loops (default 1).

params.name: play_mode
params.description: Optional Forward | Reverse | PingPong (default Forward).

params.name: playback_speed
params.description: Optional float speed multiplier (default 1.0).

params.name: restore_state
params.description: Optional bool: restore the pre-animation state on finish (default false).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, animation_exists: bool, played: bool, headless: bool, requires_pie: bool, note: string, saved: bool, live_widget_name?: string, live_animation_name?: string, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: pop_common_ui_widget
commands.description: Pop the ACTIVE screen off a live CommonUI stack, or clear the whole stack -- the inverse of push_common_ui_widget and the other half of driving a menu state machine headless (open, go deeper, come back, assert what is on top). WARNING: RUNTIME ONLY, same as the push: with no PIE session there is nothing on any stack. Popping an empty stack is an honest success with popped:false, not an error.

params.name: stack_widget_name
params.description: Name of the live activatable container in the running session.

params.name: clear_all
params.description: Remove EVERY widget instead of just the active one (default false).

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index whose viewport widgets are searched (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N'.

commands.returns: { stack_widget_name, popped: bool, popped_widget: string, cleared_all: bool, widget_count: int, active_widget: string } -- widget_count and active_widget are read AFTER the operation; popped:false with widget_count:0 means the stack was already empty.

commands.name: push_common_ui_widget
commands.description: Push a screen onto a LIVE CommonUI activatable stack in the running PIE session -- the operation that lets a menu state machine be driven to a specific state and then asserted. create_common_ui_stack only puts the stack in place; its contents are populated at runtime with AddWidget, which this calls headless, so "open the pause menu, then the options page, now check the back button" is reproducible. WARNING: RUNTIME ONLY: the container's widget list and its widget pool are Transient, so with no PIE session there is genuinely nothing to push onto and this says so rather than pretending. The pushed widget is activated by the stack itself; read the result with get_common_ui_stack or read_pie_widgets, and move focus into it with set_pie_widget_focus.

params.name: stack_widget_name
params.description: Name of the live UCommonActivatableWidgetStack (or any activatable container) in the running session. Resolved like click_pie_widget, nested Widget Blueprints included.

params.name: widget_class
params.description: The UCommonActivatableWidget class to push: a /Game Widget Blueprint path, its generated-class path, or a native class path.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index whose viewport widgets are searched (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N'.

commands.returns: { stack_widget_name, pushed_class, pushed_widget: string, widget_count: int, active_widget: string } -- widget_count and active_widget are read off the stack AFTER the push, so they are evidence rather than an echo.

commands.name: read_pie_widgets
commands.description: Read LIVE UMG from the running PIE session (game thread): enumerate the active UUserWidgets added to the viewport and walk each widget tree, emitting name/class plus optional visibility/hover/text/value/geometry as a parent/child tree.  Reads only game-thread-safe widget-tree state (never the render thread). Errors clearly if no Play-In-Editor session is running.  DESCENDS INTO NESTED WIDGET BLUEPRINTS: an AAA screen is a Widget Blueprint composed of Widget Blueprints, so everything interesting sits one level below the first. Cycles are handled with a visited set plus max_depth, and a subtree that IS cut says so in subtree_omitted instead of looking like a leaf. Rich text is read too (URichTextBlock does not derive from UTextBlock). Not implemented: include_bindings, which is accepted and flagged in bindings_note.

params.name: root_filter
params.description: Optional case-sensitive substring; only top-level UserWidgets whose object name contains it are returned.

params.name: include_text
params.description: Optional bool (default true): include UTextBlock text.

params.name: include_visibility
params.description: Optional bool (default true): include visibility, is_hovered and has_keyboard_focus per widget. has_keyboard_focus is what tells you whether a navigation key will do anything at all: with nothing focused every key is a no-op, which reads exactly like broken navigation.

params.name: include_bindings
params.description: Optional bool (default false): NOT implemented in this subset; sets bindings_note when true.

params.name: include_values
params.description: Optional bool (default false): include is_enabled + widget-type-specific value (Slider.value / ProgressBar.percent / CheckBox.is_checked / ComboBoxString.selected_option).

params.name: include_geometry
params.description: Optional bool (default false): include GetCachedGeometry()-derived absolute_position/absolute_size, render_opacity, and render_transform.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Optional recursion limit (-1 = unlimited, the default). Counts every level including the descent into a nested Widget Blueprint's own tree. A subtree cut by the limit reports subtree_omitted rather than passing for a leaf.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.returns: { widgets: [{ widget_name, class, is_any_animation_playing, visibility?, is_hovered?, children: [{ widget_name, class, visibility?, is_hovered?, text?, is_enabled?, value?, percent?, is_checked?, selected_option?, geometry?, children: [...] }] }], widget_count: int, scanned_viewport_widgets: int, include_text: bool, include_visibility: bool, include_bindings: bool, include_values: bool, include_geometry: bool, bindings_note?: string, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: remove_viewmodel
commands.description: Remove a UMVVMViewModelContext (by context name) from a Widget BP's MVVM authoring state. Inverse of add_viewmodel; idempotent (already-absent is an honest success).

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset (string)

params.name: context_name
params.description: FName identifying the context to remove (idempotency key)

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, context_name, already_existed, removed, view_model_count, has_mvvm_extension, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: remove_widget
commands.description: Detach a runtime UserWidget, found by object name, from the viewport or panel holding it with RemoveFromParent. It searches the worlds create_widget uses: the one target_world names, or without it the running PIE world first and then the editor world; in each, the first widget hosted by a level UWidgetComponent, then any other UserWidget of that world. The object is not deleted, no asset changes and there is no undo. was_in_viewport and had_parent are measured before the call: both false means nothing was detached, as for a component-hosted widget. It never edits a Widget Blueprint asset.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Object name of the runtime widget to detach (case-insensitive), as list_level_widget_components or create_widget report it

params.name: target_world
params.description: Optional world to search, with the values create_widget takes (editor, pie, server, client, pie:N, game). Omitted: the PIE world while PIE runs, then the editor world.

commands.returns: { widget_name: string, target_world: string, was_in_viewport: bool, had_parent: bool, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: remove_widget_animation
commands.description: Remove a UWidgetAnimation from a Widget Blueprint.  Inverse of add_widget_animation: finds the animation by object name or display label, removes it from WidgetBP->Animations, unregisters it as a blueprint variable (OnVariableRemoved), then compiles and saves. If no such animation exists it is an honest no-op (removed:false, already_existed:false, no save).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the animation to remove

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, object_name: string, removed: bool, already_existed: bool, animation_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: remove_widget_property_binding
commands.description: Remove a UMG property binding (the Designer's "Bind" dropdown set back to none), so the property goes back to holding its authored fixed value. Inverse of add_widget_property_binding and idempotent: a property that was not bound is an honest success with removed:false, never an error.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget whose binding to drop

params.name: property_name
params.description: The bound property, e.g. "Text". Matching is on widget_name + property_name, which is exactly how UMG identifies a binding (one binding per property, max).

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, property_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, remaining_binding_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: rename_widget
commands.description: Rename a widget in a Widget Blueprint's tree (WidgetTree membership, blueprint variable map, bindings, and animation bindings all updated in one call -- the same path as the Designer's F2).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: old_name
params.description: current name of the widget in the tree

params.name: new_name
params.description: desired new name

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, old_name: string, new_name: string, resolved_name: string, renamed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: render_widget_preview
commands.description: Render a Widget Blueprint to a PNG on disk WITHOUT running the game: builds the widget with the editor's own designer flags, draws it through FWidgetRenderer into a render target and writes the file. This is what turns "does this style look right?" from a PIE session someone has to watch into a static read plus one image to LOOK at. HONEST SCOPE: it is a DESIGN preview, the same thing the UMG Designer shows -- not the live HUD. Anything that only exists while the game runs (text filled in NativeConstruct, property bindings, ViewModel data, anything behind an IsDesignTime() guard) renders at its default/empty value. Use read_pie_widgets or capture_pie_screenshot for the running session. Returns rendered:false with a reason (never a blank image) when the editor has no RHI (-nullrhi/headless), because FWidgetRenderer cannot draw there.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset to render

params.name: output_path
params.description: Optional output file. A bare name lands under <ProjectSaved>/MCP/WidgetPreviews/, an absolute path is used verbatim, and .png is appended when missing. Defaults to the asset's name.

params.name: width
params.description: Optional render width in pixels. Omit BOTH width and height to render at the widget's own desired size (a Slate prepass measures it).

params.name: height
params.description: Optional render height in pixels. Omit BOTH width and height to render at the widget's own desired size.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional draw scale applied by the renderer (default 1.0), the equivalent of DPI scaling in the Designer.

params.name: opaque_background
params.description: Optional (default false). Force every pixel's alpha to 255 so the PNG is not transparent where the widget did not paint -- the same trick capture_viewport uses. Leave false to keep real transparency.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, rendered: bool, file_path: string, width: int, height: int, scale: number, drew_at_desired_size: bool, byte_size: int, designer_flags: string, preview_note: string, error?: string }

commands.name: reorder_widget_child
commands.description: Change a widget's index among its parent panel's children via UPanelWidget::ShiftChild (clamps new_index internally; safe with any int). For a CanvasPanel parent, visual stacking is governed by each child's CanvasPanelSlot ZOrder (set_widget_slot_properties z_order), NOT child index -- the index shift is still applied and reported honestly, with a note.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget to reorder

params.name: new_index
params.description: desired index among its parent's children (clamped to [0, child_count])

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, parent_name: string, old_index: int, requested_index: int, resolved_index: int, child_count: int, reordered: bool, parent_is_canvas_panel: bool, note?: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: reparent_widget
commands.description: Move a widget to a new parent panel (optionally at a specific child index), via FWidgetBlueprintOperationUtils::MoveWidget -- the same primitive backing the Designer's drag-and-drop reparent. Validates the new parent is a panel widget and refuses to create a cycle. Optional slot_properties are applied to the widget's NEW slot afterward via the shared reflection setter (e.g. {"Row":1,"Column":2} for a GridSlot). THIS IS ALSO HOW YOU FILL A NAMED SLOT: a UNamedSlot is a UContentWidget (hence a panel), so add one with add_widget_extended widget_type="NamedSlot" and reparent the content into it -- there is no separate SetContentForSlot tool and none is needed (it answers reparented:true, new_slot_class:PanelSlot).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget to move

params.name: new_parent_name
params.description: name of the panel widget to become the new parent

params.name: target_index
params.description: Optional int child index to insert at (default: append at the end)

params.name: slot_properties
params.description: Optional object of {PropertyName: value} applied to the resulting slot via reflection (best-effort; per-field errors are reported, not fatal)

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, old_parent_name: string, new_parent_name: string, new_slot_class: string, resolved_child_index: int, reparented: bool, slot_properties_applied: int, slot_property_errors?: [string], saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: scaffold_menu_screen
commands.description: Build a styled menu screen: create or reuse the Widget Blueprint at package_path/name with a centred panel, optional title and one button per entry bound to an event-graph OnClicked handler, then compile and save. Re-runs reuse widgets and bindings. Returns contrast_ratio_normal_text; the default colors pass audit_widget_accessibility. Layout is not measured (long labels can clip) and text is inline, not String Table.

params.name: package_path
params.description: /Game folder for the new Widget Blueprint (e.g. /Game/MyGame/UI).

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. WBP_OptionsMenu.

params.name: entries
params.description: REQUIRED, the buttons top to bottom. Each item is either a plain string (the label) or an object {label, handler_name?}. handler_name names the generated event-graph function; omitted, it becomes On<Label>Clicked. Order is preserved.

params.name: title
params.description: Optional heading text above the buttons. Omitted or empty = no title widget at all (not an empty one).

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Parent UUserWidget subclass (default "UUserWidget"). Pass a CommonUI activatable class here to scaffold a screen for a CommonUI stack.

params.name: background
params.description: Draw the background panel (default true). false leaves the buttons floating on nothing -- which is what makes contrast unjudgeable, so it also drops contrast_ratio_normal_text from the payload.

params.name: panel_color
params.description: Background panel colour. "#RRGGBBAA", [r,g,b,a] (LINEAR 0..1) or {R,G,B,A}. Default is a near-black panel.

params.name: button_color
params.description: Button resting colour, same formats. If you override this, you own the contrast: the returned ratio tells you what you got.

params.name: text_color
params.description: Label colour for title and buttons, same formats. Default white.

params.name: title_font_size
params.description: Title text size in Slate font points, truncated to a whole number; default 36. Unused when title is empty.

commands.name: set_named_slot_content
commands.description: Put a widget into a NAMED SLOT of a NESTED Widget Blueprint instance -- the "template screen with holes" pattern. reparent_widget already fills a UNamedSlot that belongs to your own tree (it is a UContentWidget, so it is just a panel), but the slot of an embedded instance is not a panel in your tree at all: it is an entry in that instance's NamedSlotBindings, and no other tool writes it. WARNING: the engine's SetContentForSlot returns nothing and SILENTLY DROPS the binding when the slot name does not exist, so this re-reads it with GetContentForSlot afterwards and reports the RE-READ, never the call. List what a given instance offers with available_slots in the response, or pass no slot_name at all to just enumerate them.

params.description: /Game path of the OUTER Widget Blueprint (the one that owns both the nested instance and the content).

params.name: clear
params.description: Empty the slot instead of filling it (default false). Mutually exclusive with content_widget_name.

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true).

Companion to add_list_view/add_tile_view, which only construct an EMPTY view.

params.description: Required. Name of the target UListView/UTileView in the live tree (as reported by read_pie_widgets), resolved the same way click_pie_widget resolves widget_name.

params.name: items

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional: after resolving widget_name, drill into a descendant widget with this name and populate THAT widget instead.

params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default) | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session each client owns its own widgets.

commands.name: set_pie_widget_focus
commands.description: Give keyboard/gamepad FOCUS to a live UMG widget in the running PIE session, so navigation has somewhere to start from. Menus routinely open with nothing focused, and then every navigation key does nothing -- which reads exactly like broken navigation and sends you to debug rules that were fine. Resolves the widget the same way click_pie_widget does (widget_name, optionally drilling in with child_name, nested Widget Blueprints included), then calls UWidget::SetKeyboardFocus. Verify with get_pie_focused_widget and drive from there with inject_key_input route="slate".

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of a live UserWidget added to the viewport, or of a widget inside one.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional: after resolving widget_name, drill into this descendant by name (nested Widget Blueprints included).

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index whose viewport widgets are searched (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector, same rules as read_pie_widgets: absent/'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N'.

commands.returns: { focused: bool, widget_name: string, widget_class: string, has_keyboard_focus: bool } -- has_keyboard_focus is RE-READ off the widget after the call, so it is evidence and not an echo: false means Slate refused the focus, and the usual cause is that the widget is not focusable (check IsFocusable and its Visibility -- a HitTestInvisible widget cannot take focus).

commands.name: set_pie_widget_value
commands.description: Set a LIVE PIE input widget's REAL value (companion to click_pie_widget, which only broadcasts a delegate with zero-init params and never touches Slider/CheckBox/EditableTextBox/ComboBoxString state first). Resolves the widget exactly like click_pie_widget (same widget_name/child_name/player_index rules), then calls the widget's real setter: USlider::SetValue, UCheckBox::SetIsChecked, UEditableTextBox::SetText/UEditableText::SetText, UComboBoxString::SetSelectedOption, or UProgressBar::SetPercent. fire_event genuinely gates a manual OnCheckStateChanged/OnTextChanged(+OnTextCommitted) broadcast for CheckBox/EditableText(Box); Slider/ComboBoxString auto-broadcast on the engine side whenever the value actually changes (fire_event cannot suppress that -- see event_fired_note); ProgressBar has no change event at all. Errors clearly if no PIE session is running, the widget is not found, or its class is not one of the supported input types.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Required. Name of the target UWidget in the live tree (as reported by read_pie_widgets).

params.name: value
params.description: Required object: {"type":"float"|"bool"|"string", "value": <matching JSON type>}.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional: drill into a descendant widget with this name after resolving widget_name.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional (default 0): filter to viewport UserWidgets owned by this local player index.

params.name: fire_event
params.description: Optional bool (default true): broadcast the widget's change event where the engine does not already do so unconditionally (CheckBox / EditableTextBox / EditableText).

params.name: commit_type
params.description: Optional "Default" | "OnEnter" | "OnUserMovedFocus": when present (EditableTextBox/EditableText only, and fire_event is true), also broadcasts OnTextCommitted with this commit type.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.name: set_slot_properties
commands.description: Set ANY property of a widget's UPanelSlot BY REFLECTION, whatever the concrete slot class is -- including the 9 of UMG's 17 slot types that no shortcut covers (UButtonSlot, which is every widget inside a Button; UUniformGridSlot, UWrapBoxSlot, UStackBoxSlot, UWidgetSwitcherSlot, USafeZoneSlot, UScaleBoxSlot, UBackgroundBlurSlot, UWindowTitleBarAreaSlot) and any slot type a future engine version adds. Accepts dotted paths into nested slot structs ("Padding.Left", "Size.SizeRule") and reports field by field what landed, same honest contract as set_widget_property: the oracle is applied[]/ignored[]/errors[], not success. For the common cases prefer the validated shortcuts, which also normalise formats this does not guess: set_widget_slot_properties (CanvasPanel anchors/offsets/z-order), set_box_slot_properties (HorizontalBox/VerticalBox/Overlay/Border/SizeBox/ScrollBox alignment+padding+size) and set_grid_slot_properties (GridPanel row/column/spans).

params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget whose slot to edit (its PARENT panel decides the slot class; read it from get_widget_blueprint_tree include_slot=true)

commands.name: set_widget_navigation
commands.description: Author a widget's GAMEPAD/KEYBOARD navigation rules -- what gets focus when the player pushes up, down, left, right, Tab or Shift+Tab off this widget. Without this a menu cannot be driven with a pad, and it is NOT reachable through set_widget_property: UWidget::Navigation is an Instanced SUBOBJECT that starts null, so there is no asset path a reflection setter could point at and a dotted path fails on a null segment. Follows the editor's own flow, including the two details that matter: the subobject is created RF_Transactional with template flags propagated, and if all six directions end up on Escape the subobject is DISCARDED (that is what tells "no navigation authored" apart from "navigation authored that happens to be the default", and it is what the Designer does). Read the result back with get_widget_blueprint_tree include_navigation=true.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget in the tree whose navigation to author

params.name: rules
params.description: Dict of {direction: rule}. Direction is Up|Down|Left|Right|Next|Previous (Next/Previous are Tab/Shift+Tab). The value is either a rule name string ("Wrap", "Stop", "Escape") or an object {"rule":"Explicit","widget_to_focus":"Btn_Confirm"} when the rule needs a target. Rules: Escape (default -- let the search continue outward), Stop (movement dies here), Wrap (cycle inside the container), Explicit (jump to widget_to_focus).

params.name: all_directions
params.description: Optional rule name applied to ALL SIX directions before `rules` is processed, so you can say "Stop everywhere, except Down" in one call. Explicit is refused here: it would need six different targets.

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path, widget_name, applied: [{direction, rule, widget_to_focus}], current_navigation: {Up:{rule,widget_to_focus}, ...}, navigation_discarded: bool, saved, save_error } -- navigation_discarded:true means every direction ended on Escape so the subobject was dropped, exactly as the Designer does; current_navigation is then all-Escape.

commands.name: set_widget_property
commands.description: Set ONE or MANY reflected properties on a widget of a Widget Blueprint, addressing NESTED STYLE FIELDS by dotted path ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor", "WidgetStyle.Hovered.OutlineSettings.CornerRadii") and reporting FIELD BY FIELD what actually landed.  Two calling shapes over one write path: property_name+value writes a single path; `properties` writes a whole map with ONE Modify + ONE compile + ONE save (a FButtonStyle is ~30 leaf fields -- one call, not 30 recompiles). WARNING: The oracle is `applied[]`/`ignored[]`/`errors[]`, NOT success: a JSON key that matches no reflected field lands in `ignored[]` and `all_applied` goes false instead of the silent no-op the engine's converter reports as success. Read the result back with get_widget_blueprint_tree(property_paths=[...]).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget in the tree (get_widget_blueprint_tree lists them)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Single reflected property name ("Text") OR a dotted path into nested structs ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor"); array indices are supported ("Items[0].Label"). Requires `value`. Omit when using `properties`.

params.name: value
params.description: New value for property_name: string, number, bool, JSON object (struct, applied field by field) or JSON array. Colors accept {"R":1,"G":0,"B":0,"A":1}, [r,g,b,a] or "#RRGGBBAA"; FMargin accepts a scalar, [h,v] or [l,t,r,b]; an FSlateBrush accepts a texture/material path string; enums accept the short name ("Box").

params.name: properties
params.description: Batch form: {"<dotted path>": <value>, ...}. Every path is written against the SAME widget under one Modify/compile/save. Combinable with property_name+value (both end up in the same map).

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true). Pass false to chain several calls and save once at the end -- the asset stays dirty in memory until something saves it.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, widget_class: string, requested_paths: [string], applied: [string], ignored: [string], errors: [{path, error}], failed_paths: [string], applied_count: int, all_applied: bool, current_values: object, saved: bool, save_error: string }

params.description: Schema identifier (not the C++ class name), e.g. "MaterialBindingAPI", "GeomModelAPI"

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { applied: bool, schema_name: string, why_not?: string }

commands.name: clear_usd_attribute
commands.description: Clear authored values of a USD attribute on a prim of an open stage: with time, only the sample at that time code; without it, the default value and every time sample. Edits the stage in memory; save_usd_stage writes it. Returns present and cleared, present false when the attribute is missing.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Name of the attribute to clear, e.g. "size".

params.name: time
params.description: Time code of the single sample to clear (ClearAtTime); omit it to clear the default value and all samples (Clear).

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, cleared: bool, present: bool, time: number? }

commands.name: clear_usd_references
commands.description: Remove every reference from a prim's reference list (irreversible — there is no "undo" in USD composition authoring).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Prim whose references should be cleared.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, prim_path: string, cleared: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: clear_usd_variant_selection
commands.description: Clear the active variant selection on a variant set (leaves the set and its variants intact — only the selection arc is removed); HasVariantSet guard

params.name: stage_name

commands.name: close_usd_stage
commands.description: Close a USD stage by its LLM-facing stage_name.  Removes the stage from the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache AND calls UnrealUSDWrapper::EraseStageFromCache on it — this is the ONLY way to release a memory stage (memory stages are never closed automatically, even on editor shutdown). If stage_name is not in the cache the call returns success with a note rather than an error (idempotent — closing an already-closed stage is a no-op). The 'removed_from_cache' field reports whether the stage was actually present in the UnrealUSDWrapper stage cache at close time.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under via open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, closed: bool, was_in_cache: bool, removed_from_cache: bool, note: string? }

commands.name: create_usd_attribute
commands.description: Create an attribute of a given USD type on a prim of an open stage, or return the existing one with created false. Edits the stage in memory; save_usd_stage writes it. Returns name, type_name, cpp_type and created; author its value with set_usd_attribute_value.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Attribute name (e.g. "size", "displayColor")

params.name: type_name
params.description: USD type name (e.g. "float", "float3", "token", "asset")

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, name: string, type_name: string, cpp_type: string, created: bool }

commands.name: create_usd_stage
commands.description: Create a new USD stage (either on-disk or in-memory).  When file_path is provided, UnrealUSDWrapper::NewStage(FilePath) creates a root layer file at that path and opens it as a stage. When file_path is omitted or empty, NewStage() (no args) creates a memory-only stage — this is the only way to author a USD stage that is NOT persisted to disk; the only way to clean it up is close_usd_stage. The new stage is always added to the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache under stage_name (default "Untitled"), so subsequent calls can refer to it by name. The returned identifier is the root layer's USD identifier (real path for on-disk; an anonymous "anon:0x..." handle for memory stages).

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute path for the new USD root layer file (.usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz). Omit or empty for a memory-only stage (optional).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: LLM-facing name to register the new stage under (optional, default "Untitled").

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, file_path: string, memory: bool, identifier: string, real_path: string, dirty: bool, is_valid: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: create_usd_stage_actor
commands.description: Spawn an AUsdStageActor into the editor's current world (or return the existing one).  Each editor world has at most one AUsdStageActor (USDStage is single-instance per world); when one already exists the tool returns already_existed:true with its current actor_path instead of failing. Spawn uses a uniquely-named FName based on the user-supplied name parameter so re-runs with the same name pick up the existing actor cleanly. Requires a live editor world — honest-gated.

params.name: name
params.description: Desired actor name (default "UsdStageActor"). Used only on first spawn; ignored on subsequent calls that pick up the existing actor.

params.name: location
params.description: World [x, y, z] location for the new actor (optional, default [0, 0, 0]).

params.name: rotation
params.description: World [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees for the new actor (optional, default [0, 0, 0]).

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, already_existed: bool, name: string }

commands.name: define_usd_prim
commands.description: Define a prim (specifier def) of type_name at prim_path on a registered USD stage, at its current edit target, defining missing ancestors as typeless prims. On an existing prim of another type it replaces the type, so leaving type_name out retypes it to Xform. The requested specifier is then authored at the edit target (specifier_set_ok); specifier reports it only when that write succeeded, and a failed write fails the call. An unknown specifier is refused before anything is authored. In memory only: save_usd_stage writes it. override_usd_prim authors an over instead; set_usd_prim_type changes only the type.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath, e.g. /World/Cube

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under

params.name: type_name
params.description: USD type name (Xform, Mesh, Cube, Scope, Camera, DistantLight...). Default: Xform

params.name: specifier
params.description: "Def" | "Over" | "Class", case-insensitive; anything else is refused. Default: Def

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, type_name: string, specifier?: string, is_valid: bool, specifier_set_ok: bool, requested?: object }

commands.name: flatten_usd_stage
commands.description: Export a flattened copy of the stage to a .usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz file (the file writer is chosen by the extension).  Wraps UE::FUsdStage::Export(OutputPath, bAddSourceFileComment, FileFormatArguments) — does NOT alter the in-memory stage. When add_source_file_comment is true (default) the flattened file includes a comment header noting the source file (useful for provenance). The returned 'exported' field reports pxr::'s bool return — false means the file writer could not write the requested path (e.g. invalid extension, permission denied). Realistic gotcha: stage.Export() requires the stage NOT be in a restricted-edit state — under headless cov this is not an issue, but in-editor it can be during PIE.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under, OR an absolute file path to auto-open.

params.name: output_path
params.description: Absolute path of the flattened file to write. The file extension picks the writer (.usda=text, .usdc=binary, .usdz=archive).

params.name: add_source_file_comment
params.description: Include the source-file comment header in the flattened file (default true).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, resolution: string, output_path: string, exported: bool, add_source_file_comment: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: get_usd_attribute_time_samples
commands.description: List the time codes at which a USD attribute on a prim of an open stage has authored time samples, without changing the stage. Returns time_samples, count and present; a missing attribute is not an error but present false with an empty list.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Name of the attribute to inspect, e.g. "xformOp:translate".

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, time_samples: [number], count: int }

commands.name: get_usd_attribute_value
commands.description: Read a USD attribute's value at a time code

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Stage cache key

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Target prim path

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Attribute name to read

params.name: time
params.description: Optional time code (default: unset = static default)

commands.returns: { present: bool, has_value: bool, has_authored_value: bool, type: string, type_name: string, value: object }

commands.name: get_usd_generated_assets
commands.description: Resolve the transient assets (UStaticMesh, USkeletalMesh, UMaterial, etc.) generated by the stage actor for a given prim path.  Wraps AUsdStageActor::GetGeneratedAssets(prim_path). Returns an empty assets array (count:0) when the prim has no generated assets — NOT an error. A prim may produce multiple assets (e.g. a skinned mesh produces USkeletalMesh + USkeleton + UPhysicsAsset).

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full actor path (or short name) of the AUsdStageActor.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Full prim path, e.g. "/root_prim/my_mesh".

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, prim_path: string, assets: [string], count: int }

commands.name: get_usd_generated_component
commands.description: Resolve a transient USceneComponent generated by the stage actor for a given prim path.  Wraps AUsdStageActor::GetGeneratedComponent(prim_path). Returns present:false (NOT an error) when the path is invalid or the prim has no generated component — the LLM can pivot on this cleanly. When present, also returns component_class (the runtime UClass name).

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full actor path (or short name) of the AUsdStageActor.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Full prim path, e.g. "/root_prim/my_prim".

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, prim_path: string, present: bool, component_path?: string, component_class?: string }

commands.name: get_usd_layer_info
commands.description: Read metadata for a single layer in the stage's stack (identifier, real path, dirty/muted flags, sublayer paths).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

params.name: layer_index
params.description: 0-based index into the layer stack (root layer is 0; session layers follow). Defaults to 0. Out-of-range returns an error rather than a synthetic empty payload.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, layer_index: int, identifier: string, real_path: string, dirty: bool, is_muted: bool, sub_layer_paths: [string], sub_layer_count: int, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: get_usd_prim_info
commands.description: Read one prim of a registered USD stage: name, type_name, active, parent_path, direct children_count, applied_schemas, variant_sets and an is_a map for nine common types (Xform, Mesh, Cube, Scope, Camera, four lights). A missing prim returns is_valid=false with a note, not an error. Read-only.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the prim to read, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { name: string, prim_path: string, type_name: string, active: bool, is_valid: bool, is_pseudo_root: bool, parent_path: string, children_count: number, applied_schemas: [string], variant_sets: [string], is_a: { Xform, Mesh, Cube, Scope, Camera, DistantLight, SphereLight, RectLight, MeshLight: bool } }, or { prim_path, is_valid: false, note } when the prim does not exist

commands.name: get_usd_prim_metadata
commands.description: Read the metadata of a prim on a registered USD stage: one key (present plus value as {type, value}) or, with no key, all entries (authored and fallback) plus count. Above 100 entries only count and a note return; unsupported value types become a placeholder string. Read-only.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: stage_name

params.name: key

commands.returns: { present: bool, key: string, value: object, metadata: object, count: number, note?: string }

commands.name: get_usd_stage_actor_info
commands.description: Read live metadata from an AUsdStageActor.  Returns the root layer identifier + real path from the actor's currently-open UE::FUsdStage (via GetUsdStage()), the integer EUsdStageState (0=Closed, 1=Opened, 2=OpenedAndLoaded), the presence of a generated ULevelSequence (a non-null GetLevelSequence()), and the count of USceneComponents the actor has spawned (via GetComponents()). All read-only.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full actor path (or short name) of the AUsdStageActor.

commands.name: get_usd_stage_info
commands.description: Read metadata about a USD stage: root layer identifier, real path, dirty flag, timecode range (start/end), frames-per-second, total prim count (recursive) and layer-stack depth (includes session layers when include_session_layers is true).  Resolves stage_name via the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache first, then falls back to treating stage_name as a file path and auto-opening it (LoadAll, use cache). Returns 'resolution' as one of "cache_hit" / "auto_opened" so the caller knows which path served the stage.

params.description: Name the stage was registered under, OR an absolute file path to auto-open.

params.name: include_session_layers
params.description: Include session layers when computing the layer-stack depth (default true).

commands.name: get_usd_variant_set_info
commands.description: Read the variant names and current selection for a single variant set on a prim

params.description: Stage cache key

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, variant_set_name: string, variants: [string], current_selection: string, variant_count: int }

commands.name: insert_usd_sublayer
commands.description: Add a sublayer path to the stage's root layer's composition stack (idempotent — re-running with the same path returns already_present without erroring).

params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

commands.description: Enter isolated mode by replacing the actor's displayed stage with a new stage rooted at one of the sublayers of the current layer stack.  Wraps AUsdStageActor::IsolateLayer(Layer, b_load_usd_stage). The layer_index selects into Stage.GetLayerStack(true) — index 0 is the root layer, >0 are sublayers. When b_load_usd_stage is true (default) assets, actors and components are regenerated from the isolated stage; when false the isolation is structural only.

params.description: Load assets/components from the isolated stage (default true).

commands.name: list_usd_file_formats
commands.description: List the USD file format extensions the engine supports, with optional human-readable descriptions.  Always returns the native set ("usd"/"usda"/"usdc"/"usdz") and the full supported set (native + third-party USD plugin extensions like "abc" from usdAbc). When include_descriptions is true, also calls AddUsdImportFileFormatDescriptions to populate the human-readable per-extension description strings (e.g. "usdc; Universal Scene Description binary files").

params.name: include_descriptions
params.description: Also return the per-extension import description strings from UnrealUSDWrapper::AddUsdImportFileFormatDescriptions (optional, default false).

commands.returns: { native_formats: [string], supported_formats: [string], native_count: int, supported_count: int, descriptions: [{format: string, description: string}]? }

commands.name: list_usd_prim_attributes
commands.description: List every attribute of a prim on an open USD stage without changing it. Returns count and attributes [{name, type_name, cpp_type, has_value, has_authored_value, time_sample_count}]; has_value also counts fallback values, has_authored_value only authored opinions.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attributes: [{name, type_name, cpp_type, has_value, has_authored_value, time_sample_count}], count: int }

commands.name: list_usd_prims
commands.description: List the prims under one prim (default the pseudo root "/") on a registered USD stage, each with prim_path, type_name and active, plus count: its direct children, or with recursive=true its whole subtree in depth-first order. Only active, loaded, defined, non-abstract prims appear, and instance proxies are not traversed. Read-only.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

params.name: prim_path_prefix
params.description: SdfPath of the prim whose children are listed; it must exist. Default "/" (the pseudo root).

params.name: recursive
params.description: false (default) lists the direct children only; true lists every descendant, each parent before its children.

commands.returns: { prims: [{ prim_path, type_name, active }], count: number }

commands.name: list_usd_stage_layers
commands.description: List the layer stack of a USD stage opened with open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage, read-only: each layer identifier, real_path, is_muted and dirty, plus count and any captured USD errors. An unregistered stage_name is an error; get_usd_layer_info details one layer by index.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, include_session_layers: bool, count: int, layers: [{ identifier: string, real_path: string, is_muted: bool, dirty: bool }], errors: [string]? }

commands.description: Enumerate every stage currently in the UnrealUSDWrapper stage cache (shared across C++ + Python).  Returns one entry per cached stage with the root layer identifier, real path and dirty flag. Each entry's 'stage_name' is the name the stage was opened under through these tools; it is empty for a stage they did not open.

params.description: SdfPath of the prim to inspect

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Stage cache key

commands.name: mute_usd_layer
commands.description: Toggle mute state on a set of layers by their identifiers (mute + unmute are passed in the same call — pxr:: applies them atomically).

params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, muted: [string], unmuted: [string], errors: [string]? }

commands.name: open_usd_stage
commands.description: Open an existing USD stage from a file path.  Wraps UnrealUSDWrapper::OpenStage with caching and force-reload controls. When use_stage_cache is true (default) and the file is already open in the UnrealUSDWrapper stage cache, the existing stage is returned. When force_reload is true, all local layers are forced-reloaded from disk (useful when the file was modified by another tool since the last open). The opened stage is added to the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache under either the explicit stage_name or a derived one (basename without extension). The stage_id returned is the root layer's USD identifier — a stable string handle useful as a unique reference across follow-up commands.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute path to the .usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz file (or a USD layer identifier).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: LLM-facing name to register the opened stage under. Defaults to the file basename without extension (optional).

params.name: initial_load_set
params.description: "LoadAll" (default; loads payloads) or "LoadNone" (faster; inspect without loading payloads).

params.name: use_stage_cache
params.description: Use UnrealUSDWrapper's stage cache (default true). When false the stage is re-read and not added to the cache.

params.name: force_reload
params.description: Force-reload all local layers from disk, bypassing the layer registry (default false).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, stage_id: string, identifier: string, real_path: string, from_cache: bool, file_path: string, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: override_usd_prim
commands.description: Author an over (specifier over, no type) at prim_path on a registered USD stage, at its current edit target, with overs for missing ancestors, to add opinions to a prim without defining it. A prim that already exists there is returned untouched (already_existed true, no specifier reported, since nothing was authored); specifier Over comes back only for an over this call authored. is_valid=false means USD refused; a missing stage or a bad path is an error. In memory only: save_usd_stage writes it. define_usd_prim creates a typed def; set_usd_prim_specifier changes the specifier of an existing prim.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath to author the over at, e.g. "/World/Cube"

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, is_valid: bool, already_existed: bool, specifier?: string }

commands.name: remove_usd_attribute
commands.description: Remove one attribute from a prim on a registered USD stage by deleting its scene description in the current edit target layer only, so opinions from other layers or references can keep it composed. Idempotent: an absent attribute gives present=false and removed=false, not an error, and a relationship of that name counts as absent. A stage not registered under stage_name or a missing prim is an error. In memory only: save_usd_stage writes it. To keep the attribute and drop its values use clear_usd_attribute.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Name of the attribute to remove, e.g. "size"

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, removed: bool, present: bool }

commands.name: remove_usd_prim
commands.description: Remove a prim and its subtree from the current edit target layer of a registered USD stage, returning removed. Opinions in other layers or references can keep it composed; set_usd_prim_active with active=false is the reversible way to hide a prim. Not saved to disk.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the prim to remove, e.g. "/World/Cube"; its descendants go with it.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { removed: bool, prim_path: string }

commands.description: Remove an applied API schema (e.g. "MaterialBindingAPI") from an existing prim of a registered USD stage, on the current edit target. A schema the prim does not have returns removed=false and was_applied=false instead of an error. Not saved to disk; inverse of apply_usd_prim_schema.

params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: schema_name

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { removed: bool, schema_name: string }

commands.name: remove_usd_sublayer
commands.description: Remove a sublayer by index from the stage's root layer's composition stack.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

params.name: sublayer_index
params.description: 0-based index into GetSubLayerPaths() of the root layer.

params.name: max_wavelength
params.description: Optional maximum wavelength in uu

params.name: min_amplitude
params.description: Optional minimum wave amplitude in uu

params.name: max_amplitude
params.description: Optional maximum wave amplitude in uu

params.name: wind_angle
params.description: Optional dominant wind angle in degrees

params.name: small_wave_steepness
params.description: Optional steepness of the smallest wave (generator default 0.4)

params.name: large_wave_steepness
params.description: Optional steepness of the largest wave (generator default 0.2)

params.name: steepness_falloff
params.description: Optional exponent shaping the small->large steepness ramp (generator default 1.0)

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, wave_supported: bool, has_waves: bool, num_waves: int, max_wave_height: number, total_steepness: number, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_water_body_gerstner_waves_spectrum
commands.description: Build a Gerstner wave set using the oceanology spectrum generator (octaves of a known wave spectrum) and apply it to a wave-supporting water body (Lake/Ocean).

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBody actor (Lake/Ocean)

params.name: spectrum_type
params.description: Wave spectrum: Phillips (default), PiersonMoskowitz, or JONSWAP

params.name: octaves
params.description: Optional array of octaves, each { num_waves?, amplitude_scale?, main_direction?, spread_angle?, uniform_spread? }; one default octave is used if omitted

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, wave_supported: bool, has_waves: bool, num_waves: int, max_wave_height: number, spectrum_type: string, octave_count: int, applied: bool, note: string }

commands.name: set_water_body_material
commands.description: Set the surface water material on a water body (resolved by asset path).

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBody actor

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface to assign

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, material: string, set: bool }

commands.name: set_water_body_properties
commands.description: Partial-update a water body's properties (only the keys present are applied); each applied field is read back with already_set when it already matched.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBody actor (Lake/Ocean/River)

params.name: input_key
params.description: Spline input key for water_velocity/audio_intensity (required only when either is set)

params.name: water_velocity
params.description: River/spline water velocity to set at input_key (requires input_key)

params.name: audio_intensity
params.description: Spline audio intensity to set at input_key (requires input_key)

params.name: target_wave_mask_depth
params.description: Water depth at which waves start being attenuated

params.name: max_wave_height_offset
params.description: Offset added to the automatically calculated max wave height bounds

params.name: collision_height_offset
params.description: Distance above the water surface where collision checks still occur

params.name: shape_dilation
params.description: Shape dilation in uu

params.name: affects_landscape
params.description: Whether the landscape is deformed by this water body

params.name: post_process_blend_weight
params.description: Underwater post-process blend weight (0..1)

params.name: water_height_offset
params.description: Ocean-only additional water height (errors on non-ocean bodies)

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, body_type: string, applied: [string], fields: { <name>: { value, already_set } } }
